description:
Pulau Besar, just off the coast of Malacca, is widely know as the 'most mysterious island in Asia' thanks to it's heavy religious connotations and local legends of black magic and forest elves.

What's crazy is it's largely ignored by tourists, despite it's beautiful white sand beaches, clear swimming waters, and lusciously green rain forest.

Pulau Besar is also home to an abandoned 5-star resort that was being developed in the 1990s, until clashes with the locals halted the project, leaving it to decay over the past 3 decades.

Today we're making our way to Pulau Besar via speedboat to see if it's an overlooked tropical getaway from Malacca and mainland Malaysia.

title: Southern most point of mainland Asia ✅ (Full route in description)
tags: malaysia|malaysia road trip|malaysia travel|johor|johor road trip|johor travel|pontian|southernmost tip of asia|tanjung piai|batu pahat|muar|parit jawa|melaka|malacca|backpacking|backpacking malaysia|backpacking asia|southeast asia
description:
Send this to the person you’d take the hidden route with 🚌💨

👉 Check out the full YouTube video linked to this! 🍿🎥

We could’ve travelled straight from Johor Bahru to Melaka. But we’re here for adventures, so we took buses between smaller towns and gave ourselves time to see what was there.

Here’s the route we’d do again 👇

Stop 1 | Johor Bahru
Start with a proper food day! For Ryan’s birthday, I planned a day around the city, and lunch at Restoran Hua Mui got the birthday boy’s approval 😂

Stop 2 | Pontian
Use Pontian as a base for Tanjung Piai, the southernmost point of mainland Asia. We literally had the whole mangrove park to ourselves!!

Stop 3 | Batu Pahat
We found colourful alleys and visited Si Hai Long Wang Temple, where the manager gave us a suuuper warm welcome. Keep an eye on the river beside it too… 🐊

Stop 4 | Parit Jawa
Come hungry for asam pedas stingray! We needed a little help from the locals to work out which bits to eat, and it ended up being one of our favourite meals. P.S. It’s a small town, so we’d recommend stopping just for lunch!

Stop 5 | Muar
Walk the colourful alleys, try satay for breakfast and see if you can spot a crocodile by the river. We looked, but no promises you’ll find one lol. There’s also a river cruise, which we didn’t manage to do, but it was recommended by our community!

Stop 6 | Melaka
Finish somewhere we’d happily spend more time. After all those quieter stops, we loved wandering Melaka’s streets, cafés & little shops (and ofc, the crazy Jonker Street market!)

Melaka will prolly already be on your itinerary. The stops before it might not be, but we’re sooo glad we didn’t skip them ❤️

Which one would you make time for? 👀

Johor Bahru is the border city next to Singapore, and for some reason it always flies beneath the radar when it comes to the backpacker trail.

So today we're giving Johor Bahru the attention it deserves!

To begin, we'll head from Singapore to Malaysia by crossing the land border alongside a multitude of Malaysians and Singaporeans. And all the while showing you how to cross the border too.

And then for Ryan's birthday, we'll take on Johor Bahru with a vengeance. Sara's planned a wild day out starting at KotaJail, an old city jail that's been renovated into a cultural hub.

Then we'll explore Ta Hiok Nee heritage street and eat some local food at a decades old Haianese restaurant. 

Finally, we'll wrap up with a street food tour in Johor Bahru's monday night market, trying some familiar things, as well as some more... interesting delicacies.

title: The PERFECT 24 hours in Singapore 🇸🇬
description:
One tip that makes exploring cheaper AND easier👇

👉 Before we start, don’t forget to subscribe and come backpacking around Asia with us! 🎒✈️

⚠️ You don’t need to buy a separate transport card! Simply tap in & out of Singapore’s MRT and buses using the same contactless bank card or mobile wallet 🚇 Just make sure you use the SAME one at both ends! We used public transport every day and were charged around S$3–4 per day.

This was our 3rd time in Singapore, and here’s the one-day itinerary we’d recommend to our friends:

🕌 7am: Sultan Mosque
Visit at sunrise before the streets around Kampong Glam get busy and get those photos without loads of people in the background! 💸 Free

🚲 8am: Cycle to Little India
Unlock an Anywheel bike and cycle towards Little India. Just remember to leave it inside a designated parking area when you finish! 💸 We paid S$4 each for 2h

🌈 9am: Former House of Tan Teng Niah
Explore Little India and stop at this incredibly colourful building, the last surviving Chinese villa in the neighbourhood! 💸 Free

🥘 11:30am: Sakunthala’s Restaurant
We shared a couple of dishes and ordered mango lassis, which were hands down the BEST we’ve ever had 🤤 💸 We paid S$32 for two

🌉 1:30pm: Cavenagh Bridge
Take the MRT towards the river and begin your walk at one of Singapore’s oldest bridges. 💸 Free

🦁 2pm: Merlion and Marina Bay
I only just realized that Merlion is a mix of mermaid and lion (sorry, lost in translation lol)! It gets busy, but you can’t skip it or the opportunity to take some ridiculous photos 😂 💸 Free

🌿 4pm: Gardens by the Bay
Leave a few hours to explore because this place is HUGE! There’s even a McDonald’s if you fancy stopping for a cheeky one lol. The outdoor gardens are free, while some attractions require tickets.

✨ 7:45pm: Garden Rhapsody
End the day underneath the Supertrees for the free light and music show. If you don’t make the first one, there’s another show at 8:45pm!

Save this Singapore itinerary and send it to the person you’d explore the city with! 📌

title: Pack with us for 20-months backpacking in Asia 🎒
description:
Here’s everything WE learned from packing for Asia FIVE times 🎒👇

👉 Before we dive in, don’t forget to follow @acrosseveryborder for more travel! ✈️

We’ve both packed for long trips around Asia before, but this is our first time doing it together… for 20 MONTHS… in our 30s loool. No pressure 😂

Here are the packing rules we swear by:

🎒 Comfort over smallest backpack
I use the Decathlon Travel 100 Easyfit Women’s backpack, while Ryan uses the Osprey Farpoint 70L. We like having enough space without needing to fight the zip every time we move!

🌧️ Bring a waterproof bag
You might not use it every day, but when the tropical rain arrives, you’ll be VERY happy you packed one. Ours also becomes a day bag for rainy adventures.

👕 Pack one week of clothes
Laundry is easy to find around Asia, and fewer clothes mean more room to buy cute things along the way. They’ll prolly cost less than at home too, so technically we’re saving money… girl travel maths 😂

🛫 We prefer checking our backpacks
Carry-on luggage often costs extra anyway, we don’t have to drag the big bags around the airport and I can keep my full-size body creams.

🧳 Use simple packing cubes
They make packing and unpacking sooo much faster, and we can immediately see where everything is. We’ve tried compression cubes, but once filled, they can still become bulky little bricks!

💡 Bonus tip: My (Sara) backpack comes with a rain cover, and I also use it to protect the straps whenever I check the bag at the airport.

Tbh, packing for 20 months is basically the same as packing for two weeks. You’re going to wash everything anyway, so don’t bring your entire wardrobe!

With the help of Visit Toulouse, we followed an itinerary designed to show a more local, modern side of the city. From creative food halls and busy markets to space exploration and giant mechanical art, this day turned into one of the most unexpected city experiences we’ve had in France.

We start at Halles de la Cartoucherie, a huge cultural and food space where locals actually spend time, before heading to Cité de l’Espace, where Toulouse’s deep connection to aerospace suddenly makes a lot of sense.

Back in the city centre, we take a food-focused wander around Marché Victor Hugo, tasting classic dishes and getting a feel for everyday life in Toulouse. We finish off at Halle de la Machine, home to some of the most impressive and unusual mechanical creations we’ve ever seen.

Rather than trying to “see everything,” this video is about what it actually feels like to explore Toulouse for a weekend. We experienced the food, the creativity, the culture, and the little surprises that make a place memorable.

If you’re planning a trip to southern France, or you’re curious about lesser-known French cities, we hope this gives you a genuine sense of why Toulouse deserves a spot on your itinerary.

description:
Hiking to Mist Mountain Hot Spring. This is hands down my longest day vlog yet, but I promise you, it's worth the watch! Such an EPIC DAY! description:
Our journey through Vietnam continues as we explore Ninh Binh, Vietnam, and experience some of the most popular things to do in this incredible destination! 🇻🇳

In this video, we're exploring Ninh Binh, a destination known for its towering limestone mountains, beautiful rice fields, hidden caves, and scenic boat tours. With so much to see, we wanted to experience some of the best activities Ninh Binh has to offer and find out if they're worth visiting.

We start bright and early at 7 AM with the famous Hang Mua (Lying Dragon) hike. After climbing nearly 500 steps to the top, we're rewarded with incredible panoramic views of Ninh Binh's limestone mountains and surrounding countryside. We also explore Tiger Cave and visit a massive lotus pond at the base of the mountain.

After the hike, we stop at Sister Fields, one of Ninh Binh's popular brunch spots. We try Vietnamese salted coffee alongside an English breakfast and a pesto chicken sandwich before heading out for our next adventure.

Next, we take the Tam Coc Discovery Tour, exploring Ninh Binh's incredible landscape by boat and shuttle. We cruise along the river surrounded by towering limestone cliffs, rice fields, and beautiful scenery. Along the way, we see local boat operators rowing with their feet, something Tam Coc is famous for!

Our boat tour also takes us through a stunning wet cave, where we learn about how these limestone caves formed over millions of years. The views throughout the journey are some of the most incredible we've experienced in Vietnam.

After finishing the boat portion of the tour, we continue exploring Tam Coc by shuttle, stopping at local temples and discovering a hidden cave called Fairy Cave. What starts as a quick visit turns into another unexpected adventure underground.

From the famous Hang Mua viewpoint to the incredible Tam Coc boat tour, Ninh Binh quickly became one of our favourite destinations in Vietnam.

If you're planning a trip to Ninh Binh, Vietnam, or wondering whether the Hang Mua hike and Tam Coc boat tour are worth it, hopefully this video gives you a look at what these experiences are really like!

description:
Today we're exploring Ninh Binh, Vietnam, a beautiful region just two hours south of Hanoi, filled with limestone mountains, ancient temples, and incredible scenery! 🇻🇳

In this video, we're visiting the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Trang An Landscape Complex, cycling through the rice fields of Tam Coc, and enjoying one of the most affordable massages we've ever had.

We start our morning at Trang An, where we board a traditional rowboat for a 2–3 hour journey through the limestone mountains. We choose Route 3, which takes us through three caves and three temples surrounded by incredible scenery.

Our first stop is an ancient temple before heading into Dot Cave, an underground river cave stretching approximately 1,000 metres! With ceilings so low we have to duck our heads, it's one of the most unique cave experiences we've had in Vietnam.

As we continue through Trang An, we're surrounded by towering limestone cliffs rising straight out of the water. The scenery feels like something out of Jurassic World!

Next, we explore Cloud Cave, a 400-metre-long cave with much higher ceilings, before visiting another beautiful temple hidden among the mountains. We also discover lily ponds, a floating pagoda, and incredible golden temple decorations.

After finishing our Trang An boat tour, we head to Tam Coc to explore Ninh Binh by bicycle. We ride around the lake before following a quiet countryside path through the rice fields, surrounded by beautiful scenery.

Next, we visit Tam Spa, where we find an incredible deal: a 90-minute massage for just $26 CAD per person! After being welcomed with tea, biscuits, and a foot soak, we settle in for a relaxing afternoon.

Finally, we finish our day with some delicious Vietnamese food, including fresh spring rolls, bun cha, beef pho, and banh mi.

If you're planning a trip to Vietnam and wondering what to do in Ninh Binh, whether the Trang An boat tour is worth it, or how to explore Tam Coc, hopefully this video gives you a look at what the experience is really like!

description:
Our journey through Vietnam continues as we spend 24 hours aboard a luxury cruise in Ha Long Bay, Vietnam! 🇻🇳

In this video, we're exploring Ha Long Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its incredible limestone islands and beautiful scenery. But with so many cruises to choose from, we wanted to find out if a luxury overnight cruise is actually worth the money.

We start with a transfer from Hanoi to Ha Long Bay, where we're surprised to find what looks like a ghost town. Despite the empty buildings, we're excited to board our cruise ship and see what the next 24 hours have in store.

Once onboard, we're welcomed with watermelon juice before our first buffet lunch. We try Vietnamese foods, including green mango salad, fried oysters, and fish soup, while cruising past Ha Long Bay's famous limestone formations.

After lunch, it's time to check into our luxury cabin. Our room has a queen-sized bed, a private balcony overlooking Ha Long Bay, and a bathtub with an incredible view. We also discover local vendors selling drinks and snacks directly from small boats, so naturally, we have to give that a try.

Next, we head out kayaking through Ha Long Bay's Dark and Light Cave. While the caves aren't exactly what we expected, the surrounding scenery is incredible, and we explore parts of the bay larger cruise ships can't reach.

Back onboard, we give you a tour of our luxury cruise ship, including the rooftop jacuzzi, swimming pool, gym, dining room, bar, and outdoor lounges.

As evening arrives, we sit down for a multi-course dinner featuring duck salad, pumpkin soup, sea bass, steak, and dessert. Then we try something unexpected on a luxury cruise, squid fishing in Ha Long Bay!

The next morning starts with a 6:30 AM Tai Chi class, followed by breakfast and time enjoying the views from our balcony. Before leaving, we have one final buffet meal and reflect on our experience.

So, how much did our luxury Ha Long Bay cruise cost? We paid **$240 CAD per person for 24 hours**, including accommodation, meals, and activities. Was it worth the price?

If you're planning a trip to Vietnam or wondering whether an overnight Ha Long Bay cruise is worth it, hopefully this video gives you a look at what the experience is really like.

description:
Today we're taking on one of Vietnam's MOST INCREDIBLE adventures, the HA GIANG LOOP! 🇻🇳 Over 4 days, we're riding motorcycles through the mountains of northern Vietnam, exploring massive caves, visiting the China border, cruising through incredible valleys and experiencing some of the BEST views in Vietnam!

Our adventure starts in Hanoi, where we take a 6-hour sleeper bus to Ha Giang before beginning our 4-day motorcycle tour with Jasmine Tours! 🏍️ We've booked easy riders, meaning we get to enjoy the scenery while our experienced drivers navigate the winding mountain roads.

On DAY ONE, we ride through breathtaking mountain passes, stop at incredible viewpoints and explore a MASSIVE cave with a hidden well of fortune! After a full day of riding, we check into our first homestay and experience a traditional Ha Giang Loop happy water party!

DAY TWO takes us all the way to the CHINA BORDER! 🇨🇳 We stop at the famous Tham Ma Pass, climb hundreds of steps to a giant Vietnamese flag overlooking China and take on a terrifying skywalk high above the mountains. The views are absolutely unreal!

On DAY THREE, we experience one of the most beautiful parts of the Ha Giang Loop: a boat cruise surrounded by towering limestone cliffs and bright blue water! 🚤 After more incredible mountain roads, Vietnamese salt coffees and delicious food, we arrive at our favourite homestay of the trip, complete with mountain views and a swimming pool!

For our FINAL DAY, we visit a waterfall, learn how traditional Vietnamese textiles are made in a local village and take in one last mountain viewpoint before finishing our incredible 4-day adventure!

After spending 4 days exploring northern Vietnam, we can confidently say the Ha Giang Loop was one of the BEST experiences of our entire Vietnam trip! 🇻🇳 But is the Ha Giang Loop actually worth it? Watch to find out!

description:
Today we're spending our FINAL DAY in Hanoi, Vietnam! 🇻🇳 From the famous Hanoi Train Street and Vietnamese salt coffee to incredible bánh mì, the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology, a traditional water puppet show and Hanoi Beer Street, we're trying some of the BEST things to do in Hanoi!

We start our day at the famous Hanoi Train Street, where we grab Vietnamese salt coffees and wait for a train to pass just feet away from our table! 🚂 Hanoi Train Street has become one of the most popular attractions in the city, but is it actually worth visiting?

After watching the train pass, we head out for one of Vietnam's most famous foods: BÁNH MÌ! 🥖 We visit Bánh Mì 25, one of the most popular bánh mì restaurants in Hanoi with thousands of Google reviews. We try beef and cheese and honey grilled chicken bánh mì, with some of the crispiest bread we've had in Vietnam!

Next, we visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology to learn more about the different ethnic groups, cultures and traditional homes found throughout Vietnam. 🇻🇳 The museum even has full-size recreations of traditional Vietnamese houses that you can walk inside and explore!

After a quick snack, we experience one of Hanoi's most unique traditions: a Vietnamese WATER PUPPET SHOW! 🎭 We watch traditional Vietnamese folktales and scenes from everyday life performed over water alongside live Vietnamese musicians.

For dinner, we're back to eating some of our favourite Vietnamese foods, including a crispy Vietnamese pancake (bánh xèo) and bún chả, before ending our final night in Hanoi with a beer on the famous Hanoi Beer Street! 🍺

After spending so much time exploring Hanoi, this was the perfect way to finish our time in Vietnam's capital. 🇻🇳

description:
Today we're going on a FREE FOOD TOUR in Hanoi, Vietnam! 🇻🇳 From Michelin Guide Vietnamese pancakes to local duck dishes and delicious Vietnamese desserts, we're exploring Hanoi's incredible food scene with two local student guides from Hanoi Kids!

Hanoi Kids is a student-run organization offering free tours led by local Vietnamese students. It's an amazing way to discover authentic local restaurants, learn about Vietnamese culture and experience Hanoi through the eyes of locals.

Our first stop is a Michelin Guide restaurant, where we try crispy Vietnamese pancakes filled with beef and fresh herbs, along with grilled pork skewers wrapped in rice paper and dipped in a delicious peanut sauce. These might be some of our FAVOURITE Vietnamese pancakes yet!

Next, our guides take us to a local duck restaurant that we probably would have walked right past. 🦆 We try fried duck with garlic, black pepper duck, spicy fermented bamboo and a traditional noodle soup with one ingredient we weren't expecting...

DUCK BLOOD! 😳

Finally, we finish the evening with our first taste of Vietnamese sweet soup (chè). 🍨 From coconut milk and condensed milk to tapioca, pandan jelly, caramel flan and jackfruit, these desserts are unlike anything we've tried in Vietnam so far!

One of the best parts of this experience was getting to know our two local guides, hearing about their daily lives and discovering restaurants we never would have found ourselves.

And the best part? The tour itself is completely FREE! You simply cover your guides' food expenses and can make an optional donation to the organization afterwards.

This was easily one of our favourite food experiences in Hanoi so far! 🇻🇳

description:
Today we're exploring some of the OLDEST and most historic places in Hanoi, Vietnam! 🇻🇳 From Vietnam's first university to Hanoi's oldest Buddhist temple, we're spending our second day in the city diving into its history, culture, and, of course, eating some incredible Vietnamese food along the way.

We start our day at the Temple of Literature, which was founded in 1070 and later became home to Vietnam's first national university. Walking through the courtyards, gates, gardens and historic buildings, we learn about the scholars who studied here hundreds of years ago and see the famous stone stelae sitting on top of carved turtles.

This ended up being one of our favourite historical sites we've visited in Vietnam so far, and we even met a group of local students who wanted to take photos with us!

After exploring the Temple of Literature, we're hungry, so we make our way into Hanoi's Old Quarter for BÁNH MÌ. 🥖🇻🇳 We try a barbecue chicken bánh mì and a char siu pork bánh mì, both served on perfectly crispy Vietnamese baguettes.

But one Vietnamese treat isn't enough...

On our way to the next historical stop, we grab another Hanoi favourite: SALT COFFEE! ☕ Made with cream, condensed milk and salt, this has quickly become one of our favourite coffee discoveries in Vietnam.

Next, we visit Trấn Quốc Pagoda, the oldest Buddhist temple in Hanoi, with a history dating back around 1,500 years. We explore the temple grounds, learn more about Buddhism and karma, and have a slightly interesting encounter outside involving someone trying to sell us scarves. 😂

Finally, there's only one way to finish a day exploring Hanoi: MORE FOOD.

We head to Bún Chả Hương Liên, the famous Hanoi restaurant where Anthony Bourdain and Barack Obama shared a meal together in 2016. Their table has even been preserved inside the restaurant!

We order bún chả with grilled pork, vermicelli noodles, fresh herbs and dipping broth, along with giant seafood spring rolls. And after trying everything, we might have discovered one of our NEW favourite Vietnamese foods. 🇻🇳

Hanoi continues to surprise us with just how much history, culture and incredible food is packed into the city. From buildings that are nearly 1,000 years old to some of the best food we've eaten in Vietnam, this was easily one of our favourite days in Hanoi so far.

And tomorrow (3 videos from now), we're leaving Hanoi for something we've been told could be LIFE-CHANGING... 👀

tags: Hanoi Vietnam|Hanoi Travel|Hanoi Travel Vlog|Hanoi Vlog|Hanoi 2026|Vietnam Travel|Vietnam Travel Vlog|Vietnam Vlog|Vietnam 2026|Hanoi Old Quarter|Exploring Hanoi|First Time in Hanoi|Things to Do in Hanoi|Hanoi Food Tour|Hanoi Street Food|Vietnamese Food|Banh Mi Hanoi|Vietnamese Coffee|Egg Coffee Hanoi|Cafe Giang|Pho Hanoi|Pho 10 Hanoi|Michelin Food Hanoi|Hoan Kiem Lake|Ngoc Son Temple|Hanoi Shopping|Northern Vietnam|Tanner and Sierra
description:
We’re officially back in VIETNAM and exploring HANOI for the first time! 🇻🇳 Today, we’re spending the day in Hanoi’s Old Quarter, trying some of the city’s most famous food and coffee, visiting historic landmarks, and searching for jackets before our upcoming Ha Giang Loop adventure.

We start our morning with two freshly toasted bánh mì sandwiches from Bánh Mì Mama. Tanner tries the classic pork bánh mì, while Sierra orders chicken with cheese. With crispy bread, generous fillings, and plenty of sauce, it’s the perfect way to begin our first day back in Vietnam!

Just around the corner, we visit St. Joseph’s Cathedral, one of Hanoi’s most recognizable landmarks. Built in 1886, its European Gothic architecture feels completely different from the busy streets surrounding it.

Next, we head into an unassuming building to find Loading T Café, where we try two of the most unusual coffee combinations we’ve ever seen: BANANA COFFEE and LIME COFFEE. 🍌🍋☕ One tastes like a banana milkshake with espresso, while the other combines lime, cinnamon, and coffee into a drink we still aren’t entirely sure how to describe. 😂

Once we’re caffeinated, we begin searching Hanoi’s Old Quarter for power banks and affordable rain jackets for the Ha Giang Loop. We visit multiple stores looking for jackets, but the prices are much higher than expected, with one shop asking 2.4 million Vietnamese dong!

After striking out on the jackets, we walk across the bright red Huc Bridge to Ngoc Son Temple on Hoan Kiem Lake. Inside, we learn about Hanoi’s famous giant turtles and the local legend of a magical sword being returned to the Golden Turtle God.

Of course, we couldn’t explore Hanoi without visiting Café Giảng, which is widely credited with inventing Vietnamese egg coffee in 1946. Tanner loves the thick whipped egg yolk and coffee mixture, while Sierra has a slightly harder time getting past the strong egg flavour. ☕🥚

Finally, we end our food adventure at Phở 10, a restaurant featured in the Michelin Guide. We try traditional northern Vietnamese phở with a light, clean broth, plenty of chili sauce, and fried dough sticks given to us by the friendly people sitting beside us.

description:
It's our FINAL DAY in China, and we're spending it exploring some of the most historic places in Beijing! 🇨🇳 From walking through Tiananmen Square and the massive Forbidden City to exploring historic streets and eating our final dumplings in China, we're packing as much as possible into our last day.

We start bright and early at Tiananmen Square, arriving before 7:00 a.m. to get through security before the lines get too long. After figuring out the reservation and security process, we make it inside one of the largest public squares in the world and take some time to learn about its significance in Chinese history.

From Tiananmen Square, we make our way toward the Forbidden City, where we discover something we weren't expecting: despite reading online that tickets needed to be reserved days in advance, we're able to buy ours SAME DAY!

Once inside, we quickly realize just how enormous the Forbidden City is. We walk through seemingly endless gates, courtyards and palaces while learning about the emperors who once lived here, including why it's called the "Forbidden City," the significance of its yellow rooftops, and how the complex was designed around symmetry.

We eventually reach the Hall of Supreme Harmony, explore the former living quarters of China's emperors, and finish our journey through the Forbidden City in the beautiful Imperial Garden. 🏯🇨🇳

After a morning packed with history, it's time for a change of pace! We explore some of Beijing's historic streets, starting with South Lu Lane, where we grab bubble tea before continuing to Qianmen Street, a pedestrian street with more than 500 years of history.

And because this is our LAST DAY in China, we're not leaving without eating a few more things. 😂 We try an incredibly crispy scallion pancake before sitting down for our final dumplings of the trip, complete with chili oil and vinegar.

Finally, after traveling through Shanghai and Beijing, riding China's bullet train, visiting the Great Wall, eating Peking duck and exploring some of the country's most famous sites, we share our final thoughts on Beijing and China. While we enjoyed Beijing and think you can experience many of its highlights in 3–4 days, Shanghai ended up being the highlight of our trip and somewhere we already know we want to return to!

If you're planning a trip to Beijing or wondering what it's like visiting Tiananmen Square and the Forbidden City, hopefully this video gives you a look at the experience, from navigating security and buying Forbidden City tickets to exploring historic Beijing and trying some final Chinese food before leaving the country.

title: You Can SLIDE Down the Great Wall of China?! 🇨🇳
tags: Great Wall of China|Great Wall China|Mutianyu Great Wall|Great Wall of China 2026|Great Wall of China vlog|Great Wall on a budget|Great Wall of China budget|Beijing Great Wall|Beijing to Great Wall|Mutianyu China|Mutianyu Toboggan|Great Wall Toboggan|Mutianyu Chairlift|China travel|China vlog|Beijing travel|Beijing vlog|China 2026|Great Wall travel guide|things to do in Beijing|Great Wall day trip|Tanner and Sierra
description:
We're visiting the GREAT WALL OF CHINA for the first time! 🇨🇳 But instead of booking an expensive private tour, we're seeing just how cheaply we can visit one of the most famous landmarks in the world.

Today we're heading from Beijing to the Mutianyu section of the Great Wall, taking public transportation, riding a chairlift up, hiking from Watchtower 5 to Watchtower 1, and finishing by TOBOGGANING down the mountain! 🛝🇨🇳

We start by taking a bus from Beijing to Mutianyu for around $15 CAD per person roundtrip. After nearly two hours, we arrive at the tourist village and take the included shuttle toward the entrance.

Once there, we have an important decision to make: EAST or WEST?

The west side is the more popular route, taking visitors toward Watchtowers 14–20 by cable car. Instead, we choose the EAST side, where we've heard there are significantly fewer people. It also means taking an open-air chairlift up and, more importantly, a TOBOGGAN back down!

The chairlift and toboggan cost approximately $75 CAD for the two of us, bringing our total to around $115 CAD — roughly $60 each.

But there's one thing we weren't prepared for: the LINES. 😂

Between transportation and waiting, it takes us about FOUR HOURS to finally reach the Great Wall. Even on a weekday, Mutianyu is incredibly busy.

Thankfully, once we reach the east side, everything changes.

Starting at Watchtower 5, we hike toward Watchtower 1 through some surprisingly steep sections. Along the way, we explore the watchtowers, learn how they were used for communication and defence, and get incredible views across the surrounding mountains.

And the farther east we hike, the fewer people we see.

After reaching Watchtower 1, we make our way back toward something we've been looking forward to all day: riding the famous Mutianyu TOBOGGAN down from the Great Wall of China!

For around $115 CAD total, we travelled from Beijing to Mutianyu, visited the Great Wall, rode the chairlift, hiked the east section and took the toboggan back down.

If you're planning a trip to Beijing or wondering how to visit the Great Wall of China on a budget, hopefully this gives you a realistic look at the experience — including transportation, prices, crowds, which side of Mutianyu to visit, and whether saving money is worth the extra waiting.

description:
We're leaving Shanghai and taking China's famous bullet train to Beijing for the first time! 🇨🇳 

From navigating the Shanghai metro with Alipay and racing to catch our train to ordering food directly to our train car, this ended up being quite the travel day.

We start the morning in Shanghai using Alipay for the metro before noticing something that is a constant every time you use the metro: X-ray security machines. After talking about some of the security and surveillance we've noticed while traveling through China, we realize we're running late and need to hurry if we're going to make our train to Beijing.

Thankfully, we make it!

We board the high-speed bullet train from Shanghai to Beijing and quickly realize how different the train system is from what we're used to. There are no physical train tickets. Instead, our passports are essentially our tickets, which Sierra explains once we're onboard.

Then we attempt something even more interesting: ordering lunch to be delivered DIRECTLY to our train car while traveling through China. After struggling our way through the ordering process, we explore the food car and pick up some crab crackers for the journey.

A few hours later, we officially arrive in Beijing for the FIRST TIME... although our introduction to the city doesn't go exactly as planned. 😂

From the train station, we make our way to the China World Hotel, Beijing, a Shangri-La hotel, where we'll be staying during our time in the city. We check out our room and hotel before heading out for one of the foods we've been most excited to try in Beijing.

PEKING DUCK! 🦆🇨🇳

For our first proper meal in Beijing, we visit Xiheyayuan to try the city's famous Peking duck and see if it lives up to the hype.

Finally, after a massive travel day from Shanghai to Beijing and already eating one dinner, we somehow end up having a SECOND dinner in the business lounge back at our hotel.

This is officially the beginning of our Beijing adventure!

If you're planning a trip to China or wondering what it's actually like taking the bullet train from Shanghai to Beijing, hopefully this video gives you a look at the entire experience, from using the Shanghai metro and navigating China's train stations to riding the high-speed rail, arriving in Beijing, staying at a luxury hotel, and trying authentic Peking duck.

Our first full day exploring Shanghai, China is packed with amazing food, beautiful streets, hidden cafes, shopping, and our first look at the famous Shanghai skyline!

We start the morning with one of Shanghai's most popular breakfast foods, a Shanghai egg pancake for only $2. After breakfast, we head to Wukang Road to explore the beautiful French-style buildings and historic streets of the area.

Next, we stumble across a Harry Potter-style cafe where we try a strawberry tiramisu before continuing our walk through Shanghai. We make a quick stop at To Summer, a popular Chinese perfume brand, before heading over to Anfu Road to do some shopping and check out an Adidas store.

By lunchtime, we're on the hunt for a hidden food spot and eventually find Yang's Dumplings tucked away in the basement of a shopping mall. We try some of their famous dumplings before continuing our Shanghai food tour.

We finish our first full day in Shanghai with dinner at Lai Lai Xiao Long, getting one more taste of authentic Chinese food before calling it a night.

description:
We spend the day exploring Seoul, South Korea, from the famous cherry blossoms at Seokchon Lake to Starfield Library, Gangnam, Garosu-gil, Korean fashion, viral desserts, and an incredible dakgalbi dinner.

Our day starts at Seokchon Lake, one of the most famous places to see cherry blossoms in Seoul. We happened to be visiting South Korea during cherry blossom season, so we couldn't pass up the chance to see one of Seoul's most popular spring destinations in full bloom.

From there, we head across Seoul to Starfield Library, the massive library inside COEX Mall that has become one of the city's most recognizable attractions.

After exploring the library, it was time for coffee, and we stumbled across ORDER Cafe, where we tried a peach coffee that sounded slightly questionable but ended up completely blowing us away.

Next, we visit one of the most iconic landmarks in Gangnam, the giant Gangnam Style hands statue, dedicated to PSY's song that basically introduced our entire generation to Gangnam.

Then we head to Garosu-gil, one of Seoul's most popular shopping streets, to explore Korean fashion and see what makes shopping in Seoul so different from back home.

This leads us down a rabbit hole we weren't expecting...

Why is Discovery Channel a clothing brand in Korea?!

Apparently, turning TV networks and other unexpected brands into fashion labels is actually a thing here, and Discovery Expedition is WAY bigger in South Korea than we ever realized.

We continue exploring Garosu-gil, stop to smell some ridiculously expensive Le Labo perfume, and eventually hunt down one of the most viral desserts in Korea right now, the famous Dubai chewy cookie.

We've seen this thing everywhere, but is the Dubai chewy cookie actually worth the hype?

Finally, after a full day exploring Seoul, we head to Jangin Dakgalbi for dinner to try Korean dakgalbi, a spicy stir-fried chicken dish cooked right at the table and the perfect way to end another day in South Korea.

If you're planning a trip to Seoul, South Korea and wondering what to do in Seoul, where to see cherry blossoms, what to see in Gangnam, where to shop, or what Korean food to try, hopefully this video gives you a few ideas!

description:
We spend the day eating our way through Seoul, South Korea, trying some of the city's most famous Korean street food, exploring local markets, hunting for vintage watches, and enjoying a Michelin-recognized Korean meal.

Our Seoul food tour starts at Gwangjang Market, one of the most famous traditional markets in South Korea and an absolute paradise for Korean food.

First up is tteokbokki, one of Korea's most popular street foods. These spicy rice cakes are everywhere in Seoul, but we weren't prepared for just how massive the portion would be.

Next, we try mayak gimbap, the famous mini Korean seaweed rice rolls that Gwangjang Market is known for, before hunting down one of the foods we were most excited to try, Garlic Boy.

After seeing Garlic Boy all over social media, we needed to find out if it actually deserved the hype. Spoiler... it did.

Of course, a Korean street food tour wouldn't be complete without trying a Korean corn dog. They're definitely not the same corn dogs we're used to back home.

For our final stop at Gwangjang Market, we grab a freshly made glutinous rice donut for something sweet before escaping the crowds and walking along Cheonggyecheon, the stream that runs through the middle of Seoul.

From there, we head to Dongmyo Flea Market, one of Seoul's best spots for vintage shopping, where we were on the hunt for watches.

Our shopping continues at MIMILINE, a massive accessories store that is almost impossible to describe until you see it. There is SO much stuff inside that it quickly becomes overwhelming.

Naturally, we find more food along the way and try Korean salt bread chips before heading for one of our biggest meals of the day.

We visit Mokmyeoksanbang, a Michelin-recognized restaurant in Seoul, where we try bulgogi bibimbap alongside cheese and kimchi pancakes.

Finally, we explore the busy streets of Myeongdong and end our Seoul food tour with one last Korean dessert, a sweet fish-shaped pastry.

If you're planning a trip to Seoul, South Korea, and wondering what Korean street food to try, where to eat in Seoul, or what to do around Gwangjang Market, Dongmyo, Cheonggyecheon, and Myeongdong, this video is for you!

description:
We explore Seoul, South Korea for the first time, spending the day eating our way through some of the city's most famous neighborhoods, traditional markets, historic sites, and incredible Korean food.

Our first full day in Seoul starts at Bukchon Hanok Village, one of the city's most famous historic neighborhoods. We wander through the traditional Korean hanoks (houses), take in some incredible views of Seoul, and stop for a black sesame coffee before continuing our food tour.

Next, we try hotteok for the first time. Traditionally, it’s a sweet Korean pancake filled with brown sugar and nuts, but we switch things up and order one stuffed with japchae and another with honey butter and cheese. They might genuinely be some of the best Korean street food we’ve ever had.

From there, we visit Gyeongbokgung Palace, one of Seoul's most iconic landmarks. The palace is beautiful, but we quickly discover just how busy some of Seoul's biggest attractions can get. Yes, we complain about the tourists while also being tourists ourselves 😂

After escaping the crowds, it's straight back to the food. We stop at Jayeondo Salt Bread to try their famous Korean salt bread before making our way into Insadong, one of Seoul's best neighborhoods for traditional culture, shops, cafés, and Korean food.

For dinner, we visit Jongno Halmeoni Kalguksu (종로할머니칼국수 종로본점), where we try traditional, and delicious, Korean knife-cut noodles and dumplings. We finish the day exploring more of Seoul and jumping into a retro photo booth for a souvenir from our first full day in the city.

description:
One of the most interesting things about bamboo is that it’s the fastest-growing plant on Earth. 

During the peak growing season, some species can grow up to 1 metre (3 feet) in a single day. That rapid growth is so extreme that, in a quiet forest, you can sometimes hear faint pops and cracks as the bamboo expands and pushes upward. This is actually such a cool sound to hear!

Combined with the stalks gently swaying and knocking together in the wind, it creates one of the most unique natural soundscapes you’ll ever experience.

The bamboo in Kyoto’s Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is primarily Moso bamboo, with many stalks reaching 25 to 30 metres (80 to 100 feet) tall. 

Although each stalk looks like its own plant, many are actually connected underground through a massive network of rhizomes (a version of roots), meaning entire sections of the forest are part of the same living organism.

The grove itself sits beside Tenryu-ji Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site dating back to 1339, and has become one of Kyoto’s most iconic landmarks. Visiting early in the morning is the best way to experience it, when the crowds are smaller and the sounds of the forest become just as memorable as the towering bamboo itself.

description:
We spend our first full day exploring Okinawa, Japan, often called the Hawaii of Japan, to find out if it's really worth visiting. From ancient castle ruins and hidden beaches to one of the world's most unique salt factories, famous Okinawan taco rice, and surprisingly empty tourist attractions, this island completely caught us off guard.

Our adventure starts with an unexpected breakfast... Vietnamese bánh mì. After spending months traveling through Vietnam, we couldn't resist one more taste before diving into everything Okinawa has to offer.

Our first stop is Zakimi Castle Ruins, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with incredible views over Okinawa. Along the way, we quickly realize something else makes Okinawa unique... there are butterflies everywhere, in every colour imaginable.

One thing we learned the hard way? Rent a car before you arrive. Finding a same-day rental in Okinawa isn't as easy as we expected, and having a car makes exploring the island so much easier.

Next, we visit the beautiful Yomitan Pottery Village, home to traditional Okinawan ceramics, before heading to one of Okinawa's most fascinating attractions, Nuchi Masu Salt Factory, where some of the world's most unique sea salt is produced using a process unlike anything we've seen before.

Of course, we couldn't leave without trying Okinawa's famous salt ice cream, and it turned out to be one of the most surprisingly delicious treats we've had in Japan.

One of the biggest surprises of the day? It feels like nobody is visiting Okinawa. Many of the places we explored felt like private tours, giving us an entirely different experience compared to cities like Tokyo, Kyoto, and Osaka.

After learning how Okinawan salt is made, we stop at the stunning Happy Cliff lookout before relaxing on the crystal-clear shores of Ukun Beach, one of the island's beautiful hidden beaches.

To finish the day, we try one of Okinawa's most famous local dishes, authentic Okinawan Taco Rice, and share one final piece of advice that could save your trip.

To finish the day, we grab a comforting bowl of authentic Japanese chicken ramen before sharing our biggest tips for anyone planning to spend a day exploring Kyoto.

Join us for a full day exploring the Marble Mountains in Da Nang, Vietnam 🇻🇳

We start the morning in Da Nang with one of Sierra’s absolute favourites, Vietnamese Salt Coffee, while talking about the crazy weather we’ve been having lately. Even though it’s not supposed to be rainy season, Da Nang has been hit with nonstop storms and grey skies.

Still, we decide to take the chance and head to the famous Marble Mountains, hoping the rain finally clears up.

After arriving, we begin exploring the caves hidden inside the mountain… and quickly realise this place feels absolutely unreal. Deep inside the cave system, the atmosphere starts feeling more like an entrance to hell than a tourist attraction 😳 before we eventually climb what feels like a staircase to heaven out onto the mountain itself.

From there, we debate whether to take the elevator or hike to the top (we choose the harder option), snack on the true breakfast of champions — Peanut M&M’s — and make our way through the mountain paths and viewpoints overlooking Da Nang.

After reaching the highest peak of the Marble Mountains, we head back into the city for one of Da Nang’s most famous local dishes, Bánh Xèo at Ba Duong Pancake House, where Tanner encounters one mysterious vegetable that instantly removes every bit of moisture from his mouth 😂 You NEED to tell us what it was in the comments.

To finish the night, we grab 30 cent milk pops from Vinamilk and hope we finally get a blue hour sunrise tomorrow morning.

description:
Join us for a full day exploring Da Nang, Vietnam 🇻🇳

We start the morning with a massive Western-style breakfast at Bikini Bottom Express before heading to one of Da Nang’s most famous attractions, the incredible Lady Buddha statue.

When we arrive, the weather quickly turns and dark storm clouds begin rolling in over the mountains. Along the way we run into monkeys roaming freely around the grounds (one almost jumps on Tanner), explore the massive temple complex, and learn the story behind why it’s called the “Lady” Buddha.

Just as we’re getting comfortable, the rain absolutely pours down and everyone scrambles for cover.

Later that night, we head back into Da Nang to meet up with a friend for dinner at Bep Cuon, where we try some amazing Vietnamese food and talk about why meeting people while travelling can make trips so much better.

If you’re planning a trip to Vietnam and looking for things to do in Da Nang, this travel vlog is for you.

description:
Join us for a beautiful (and slightly chaotic) day exploring the Vietnamese countryside 🌾🇻🇳

We start our morning at a peaceful coffee shop hidden in the rice paddies, one of the most relaxing and scenic spots you can find. After soaking in the views, we hop on our bikes and cycle through endless green rice fields, experiencing the quiet charm of rural Vietnam.

But the weather has other plans… 🌧️  
A sudden downpour and thunder turns our ride into a race against the rain!

We wrap up the vlog with cozy snacks and a rainy ending that perfectly captures the unpredictability of travel.

If you love travel vlogs, countryside adventures, and real, unfiltered experiences... this one’s for you.

description:
What’s really worth doing on a Mekong Delta tour… and what isn’t? 🤔

In this Vietnam travel vlog, we leave Ho Chi Minh City for a full-day adventure into the Mekong Delta, cruising through narrow jungle waterways that feel completely different from the chaos of the city 🌿

Our first stop takes us to Coconut Island, where we see how coconut candy is made completely by hand, and quickly realize just how many different ways coconuts are used out here 🥥

But things get weird fast.

We’re offered “happy water” (Vietnamese rice wine)… infused with actual snakes and geckos 🐍 yeah, not exactly what we expected signing up for this tour.

After that, we head to a local bee farm where we try fresh honey straight from the comb, while the bees are still crawling on it 😳 and even sample royal jelly, something we’d never even heard of before.

Then comes one of the most relaxing parts of the day, drifting through the Mekong Delta in a small boat, surrounded by palm trees and quiet canals… before things take another unexpected turn when we get the chance to hold a real snake.

From unique foods to strange traditions to moments we definitely didn’t see coming, this Mekong Delta tour turned out to be way more unpredictable than we expected.

If you’re thinking about visiting the Mekong Delta, this is what the experience actually looks like.

description:
Join us on an exciting full day in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam! 🇻🇳
After the Lunar New Year holiday, the city is buzzing with life and we start our morning with
one of Vietnam’s most famous drinks – the legendary Vietnamese Egg Coffee.
We visit a local café to try this unique drink made with egg yolk, sugar, and coffee. Then it’s
time for a delicious Vietnamese breakfast with the iconic Banh Mi sandwich, packed with
chicken, pork, pate, and fresh vegetables.
Our day continues with a meaningful visit to the War Remnants Museum, where we learn
about the history of the Vietnam War from a different perspective. After that, we explore the
charming Book Street and send postcards from the historic Saigon Post Office.
Later, we grab some snacks from 7-Eleven before ending the day at the famous Four Peas
Pizza, known for serving some of the best pizza in Vietnam.
If you love travel, street food, and exploring new cultures, this Ho Chi Minh City travel vlog is
for you!

Our journey through Thailand continues as we arrive in Chiang Rai, Thailand, and check into a $15 hostel to see what budget accommodation in Southeast Asia is really like! 🇹🇭

In this video, we're staying at Baan Mai Kradan Hostel in Chiang Rai, a beautiful budget-friendly hostel with modern facilities, spacious common areas, and comfortable dorm rooms. After staying in several hostels throughout Thailand, we wanted to show you exactly what $15 a night can get you and share what we've learned about choosing a good hostel while backpacking.

We start with a full hostel tour, exploring the beautiful outdoor courtyard, welcoming reception area, and shared living spaces. From comfortable lounges and a TV room to complimentary breakfast, free drinking water, and places to work, this hostel has plenty to offer for its affordable price.

Next, we head upstairs to check out our dorm room. We show you the bunk beds, privacy curtains, personal lighting, and small workspaces before exploring the shared bathrooms. After spending the previous week using wet bathrooms, having separate showers feels like a huge upgrade!

We also discover a quiet balcony overlooking the courtyard and an unexpected rooftop with views of a nearby temple. Although the rooftop could use some furniture, it's another interesting feature of this Chiang Rai hostel.

After finishing our tour, we settle into one of the common areas to get some work done and discuss what makes a hostel worth staying in. From location and cleanliness to bathrooms, social spaces, and the people you share a room with, we share our biggest tips for choosing hostels while travelling Southeast Asia.

For just $15 a night, Baan Mai Kradan Hostel surprised us with how much it offers. If you're planning to visit Chiang Rai, Thailand, or wondering what budget hostels in Southeast Asia are actually like, hopefully this video gives you a better idea of what to expect!

description:
Our journey through Thailand continues as we explore Chiang Mai, Thailand, and visit a local artist village to try traditional Khao Soi, one of Northern Thailand's most famous dishes! 🇹🇭

In this video, we're visiting an artist village in Chiang Mai, known for its local crafts, handmade souvenirs, creative workshops, and traditional Northern Thai food. With so much to explore, we wanted to experience some of the village's unique activities and find out if its famous Khao Soi is worth the hype!

We start by exploring the artist village, where we discover a workshop that lets visitors create personalized leather notebooks. Sierra decides to make one of our own, choosing the leather, stamping letters, and decorating the pages to create a unique souvenir from our time in Thailand.

After finishing our notebook, we head out to find one of the village's popular Khao Soi restaurants. With a massive lineup and a 40-minute wait, we're hoping this traditional Northern Thai dish lives up to its reputation!

Khao Soi is a famous Northern Thai noodle soup made with egg noodles, crispy noodles, tender chicken, and a rich coconut curry broth. It's typically served with pickled vegetables, lime, onions, and chili, creating an incredible combination of flavours.

While waiting for our food, we grab some refreshing drinks before finally getting to watch our Khao Soi being prepared using traditional cooking methods.

Once our bowls arrive, we add all the toppings and dig in! The chicken is incredibly tender, the broth is rich and flavourful, and the crispy noodles add the perfect crunch. But after trying Khao Soi at several restaurants around Chiang Mai, we're left wondering whether this popular spot is actually worth the higher price.

From making personalized souvenirs to trying traditional Khao Soi, Chiang Mai's artist village is a fun destination for anyone interested in local food, art, and Thai culture.

If you're planning a trip to Chiang Mai, Thailand, or wondering where to try authentic Khao Soi, hopefully this video gives you a look at what this unique experience is really like!

With steep climbs, jungle scenery, and incredible viewpoints, we wanted to find out if hiking to Doi Suthep is worth the effort!

We begin our adventure near Chiang Mai University, making our way past Chiang Mai Zoo to find the entrance to the Monk's Trail. This historic route has been used by Buddhist monks for generations, and today we're following in their footsteps through the mountains.

Our first stop is Wat Pha Lat, a peaceful Buddhist temple hidden in the jungle. Along the way, we pass Mindfulness Hill, colourful trail markers, and beautiful forest scenery before arriving at this incredible temple surrounded by nature.

After exploring Wat Pha Lat, we continue hiking toward Wat Phra That Doi Suthep, one of Chiang Mai's most famous temples. The second part of the hike is much more challenging than we expected, with steep inclines, difficult trails, and what feels like endless climbing!

Eventually, we reach Doi Suthep and make our way up the famous Naga staircase to explore the temple grounds. After an exhausting day of hiking, we're rewarded with incredible panoramic views overlooking Chiang Mai.

From the peaceful jungle temple of Wat Pha Lat to the breathtaking views at Doi Suthep, this turned out to be one of our most challenging adventures in Thailand!

description:
Our adventures in Thailand continue as we explore the famous Sticky Waterfalls in Chiang Mai, one of the most unique things to do in Northern Thailand! 🇹🇭

In this video, we're visiting Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls, located in Si Lanna National Park just outside Chiang Mai, Thailand. Unlike most waterfalls, these have a unique limestone surface that allows visitors to climb directly up the rushing water without slipping! With this being one of Chiang Mai's most popular attractions, we wanted to experience it ourselves and find out if it's actually worth visiting.

We start by making our way down to the bottom of the waterfalls, taking in the beautiful jungle scenery along the way. Rather than starting halfway up like many visitors, we decide to climb the entire waterfall from bottom to top!

Once we reach the water, we quickly discover why these waterfalls are called "sticky." Thanks to the natural calcium carbonate deposits, the rocks provide an incredible amount of grip, even with water rushing over them. It's a strange feeling being able to walk straight up a waterfall without slipping!

As we continue climbing, we encounter steep sections, slippery patches, and some incredible views of the surrounding forest. Along the way, we learn more about the unique geological phenomenon known as tufa, which creates the waterfall's unusual surface.

After reaching the top, we explore more of Si Lanna National Park, following a peaceful nature trail to a beautiful natural spring with incredibly blue water. It's a completely different experience from the busy waterfalls and a great way to see more of the park.

From climbing the famous Sticky Waterfalls to exploring the surrounding jungle and natural springs, this quickly became one of our favourite activities in Chiang Mai!

If you're planning a trip to Chiang Mai, Thailand, or wondering whether the Bua Tong Sticky Waterfalls are worth visiting, hopefully this video gives you a look at what the experience is really like!

description:
Our journey through Thailand continues as we spend a day exploring Chiang Mai, Thailand, experiencing what everyday life is like while backpacking through Southeast Asia! 🇹🇭

In this video, we're taking you along for a typical day in Chiang Mai, a city known for its beautiful Buddhist temples, incredible street food, affordable accommodation, and relaxed atmosphere. From checking into our first hostel to exploring the Old City and trying delicious Thai food, we're showing you what backpacking in Chiang Mai is really like.

We start the morning by checking out of our hotel and heading to our first hostel of the trip. At just $16 CAD per night, we're surprised by how beautiful it is, complete with a swimming pool, breakfast area, and comfortable shared rooms.

After dropping off our bags, we head to Thailand's famous 7-Eleven to grab some food. We pick up iced coffee, green tea, ham and cheese croissants, steamed pork buns, cheesy fried chicken rolls, yogurt, and salmon onigiri. With everything costing around $10 CAD, we're excited to see whether Thailand's 7-Eleven lives up to the hype!

Next, we explore Chiang Mai's historic Old City, surrounded by ancient walls and a moat. With Buddhist temples around nearly every corner, we spend the afternoon discovering beautiful architecture, golden decorations, massive Buddha statues, and historic chedis.

Along the way, we visit a temple that only allows men to enter, learn about local Buddhist traditions, and explore one of Chiang Mai's most impressive historic temple complexes.

After a full afternoon of exploring, we finish our day at Lanna Square Market, where we try beef Khao Soi, one of Northern Thailand's most famous dishes. With its rich coconut curry broth, tender beef, and crispy noodles, it's the perfect way to end our day!

From affordable hostels and 7-Eleven food to beautiful temples and traditional Thai cuisine, Chiang Mai is quickly becoming one of our favourite places in Thailand.

If you're planning a trip to Chiang Mai or wondering what backpacking through Southeast Asia is really like, hopefully this video gives you a look at an average day in Chiang Mai!

description:
Our adventures in Thailand continue as we head into the mountains of Chiang Mai to visit Joy Elephant Sanctuary and experience one of our biggest bucket list activities in Southeast Asia! 🇹🇭🐘

In this video, we're exploring Joy Elephant Sanctuary, located about two hours outside downtown Chiang Mai, Thailand. With so many elephant sanctuaries to choose from, we wanted to find an ethical experience where we could observe these incredible animals in a natural environment while learning more about their care and conservation.

Our adventure starts with a winding drive through the mountains of northern Thailand. After making our way up some incredibly steep roads, we arrive at the sanctuary surrounded by beautiful jungle scenery.

Before meeting the elephants, our guide teaches us about the sanctuary's approach to elephant welfare, including the importance of providing enough food, time to eat, and space to roam freely. We also learn why visitors aren't allowed to touch the elephants and how the sanctuary works to prioritize their well-being.

Next, we get to feed the elephants fresh fruit before heading out on a jungle hike alongside them! Along the way, we meet several elephants, including a 64-year-old elephant with limited vision and a younger elephant named Ellie. Getting this close to these incredible animals was easily one of the highlights of our time in Thailand.

After our jungle adventure, we head to a beautiful waterfall for a swim before returning to enjoy a traditional Thai lunch. We're treated to vegetarian Pad Thai, fresh pineapple, watermelon, and other delicious food while surrounded by the mountains.

To finish the day, we take part in a unique Thai cultural activity, making traditional herbal inhalers using local ingredients and menthol!

From feeding elephants and hiking through the jungle to swimming at a waterfall and enjoying delicious Thai food, this was one of our most memorable experiences in Chiang Mai.

If you're planning a trip to Chiang Mai, Thailand, or wondering whether visiting an elephant sanctuary is worth it, hopefully this video gives you a look at what the experience is really like!

description:
Our six-month backpacking adventure through Southeast Asia begins with a 30-hour travel day from Vancouver, Canada, to Chiang Mai, Thailand! 🇹🇭✈️

In this video, we're flying across the world on three different airlines: Air Canada, Emirates, and Thai Airways. Along the way, we're comparing the economy-class experience, airplane food, entertainment, comfort, and service to find out which airline offers the best experience.

We start our journey at Vancouver International Airport (YVR), where we have a few hours to explore, pick up snacks, and prepare for our first flight. After grabbing some essentials, we board our 13-hour Air Canada flight to Hong Kong.

On Air Canada, we experience everything from a full dinner service with beef and mashed potatoes to a late-night tuna sandwich and pork noodles for breakfast. We share our thoughts on the food, seating, entertainment, and overall experience of flying long-haul in economy class.

After arriving in Hong Kong, we board our second flight with Emirates, flying on the massive double-decker Airbus A380 to Bangkok, Thailand. Even though the flight is only two hours, we're impressed by the comfortable blankets, entertainment system, onboard cameras, and overall experience. Is Emirates really that much better than Air Canada?

Once we arrive in Bangkok, our travel plans hit a small problem when we discover that our airport lounge booking is for the international terminal, but our next flight is domestic. Instead, we spend the night at a 24-hour airport cafe, drinking coffee, trying Thai green tea, and attempting to stay awake.

Finally, we board our third and final flight with Thai Airways from Bangkok to Chiang Mai. Despite being our shortest flight, Thai Airways surprises us with some of the best airplane food we've had throughout the entire journey!

After 30 hours of traveling, three airlines, very little sleep, and plenty of airplane meals, we finally arrive in Chiang Mai, Thailand, where our Southeast Asia backpacking adventure officially begins.

If you're planning to fly from Canada to Thailand, comparing Air Canada vs Emirates vs Thai Airways, or wondering what a 30-hour economy-class travel day looks like, hopefully this video gives you a look at what these airlines are really like!

Finally, we finish our Vancouver Chinatown food tour at Phnom Penh, one of our favourite Michelin Guide restaurants in Vancouver. Our entire dinner costs just $51 CAD!

After living in Chinatown for so long, these are some of the restaurants we're going to miss the most. Whether you're visiting Vancouver for the first time or looking for some of the best places to eat in Chinatown, hopefully this video helps you discover a few new favourites!

tags: International Village Mall Vancouver|Vancouver’s strangest mall|Vancouver strange mall|Vancouver food court|Vancouver food tour|Vancouver food vlog|Vancouver cheap eats|cheap food Vancouver|Vancouver hidden gems|Vancouver Chinatown food|downtown Vancouver food|Vancouver restaurants|Vancouver food guide|Uzbek food Vancouver|Uzbek pilaf|Thai food Vancouver|Pad Thai Vancouver|Mexican food Vancouver|carnitas tacos|Vancouver travel vlog|Tanner and Sierra
description:
We’re exploring Vancouver’s STRANGEST shopping mall! 🇨🇦 International Village Mall once had dreams of becoming a luxury shopping destination, but today it feels unusually quiet, slightly spooky, and almost frozen in the 1990s.

Despite its empty storefronts and lack of foot traffic, one part of the mall is still thriving: its surprisingly diverse FOOD COURT! 🍜🌮

Today, we’re trying three different cuisines from around the world to find out whether International Village Mall deserves another chance.

Our first stop is for Uzbek cuisine, where we order pilaf and a pickled carrot salad for only around $13 CAD. The pilaf is packed with rice, chickpeas, carrots, raisins and tender braised beef, making it one of the best-value meals we’ve found in downtown Vancouver.

Next, we try a classic Pad Thai with medium spice. It starts sweet, sour and tangy, but the heat continues building with every bite! 🌶️

For our final meal, we visit Don José Authentic Mexican Carnitas for traditional carnitas tacos served with pico de gallo, avocado cream and smoky red pepper sauce. We also try a sweet bun similar to a concha and an unexpected Mexican dessert called chongos zamoranos, which is made from curdled milk.

After trying food from Uzbekistan, Thailand and Mexico, we have to decide: Does Vancouver’s strangest mall deserve a resurgence?

description:
I’m spending 36 HOURS in Victoria, BC with my best friend Ali! 🇨🇦 I haven’t seen her in a few months, so we’re making the most of our time together by revisiting some of our favorite places, trying new cafés and eating plenty of amazing food.

My adventure begins with a ferry ride over to Vancouver Island. After arriving in Victoria, Ali and I kick off our reunion with drinks at Rabbit Rabbit before officially beginning our first full day in the city.

Day one starts with strawberry iced matchas from Wairua. They may not have looked quite as pretty by the time we drank them, but they were some of the best matchas I’ve ever had!

Next, we head to Duo Cafe and Bakery for breakfast, where we try a carrot cake latte and a twice-baked almond croissant. The latte has the perfect balance of sweetness and spice, and the croissant is just as delicious.

After breakfast, we spend some time exploring downtown Victoria, shopping and visiting Munro’s Books, one of the city’s most famous independent bookstores. We continue window shopping before heading toward the water for a walk along the breakwater.

We stop at the Breakwater Cafe before getting ready for dinner at Cera, a Korean fusion restaurant in Victoria. Our table quickly fills up with spicy cucumber salad, fried dumplings, bulgogi and an incredible kimchi ragù pasta.

The food spread is absolutely crazy! 😂

On day two, we start our morning with coffee from Routine Coffee. Neither of us has visited before, so we’re excited to try somewhere new.

For our final meal of the trip, we head to the Morning People food truck for breakfast. We both order bacon breakfast sandwiches and share crispy potatoes with garlic aioli and a side of fruit.

After 36 hours of incredible food, coffee, shopping and exploring Victoria, it’s time to say goodbye. This trip was such a fun opportunity to catch up with my best friend and revisit some of our favorite places in the city!

description:
We're taking on the famous Richmond Night Market just outside Vancouver, Canada, trying and ranking some of the CRAZIEST foods we can find! 🇨🇦🍜

From massive BBQ skewers and birria grilled cheese to giant squid and a Nutella strawberry bao bun, we came hungry and decided to find out which Richmond Night Market foods are actually worth trying.

After waiting in a massive line to get into the market, we're absolutely starving and start searching for our first meal of the night.

Our goal is simple: try a bunch of different foods, rank everything we eat, and make sure we try at least ONE food we've never had before.

We start with ramen before making our way to one of the market's popular skewer stalls. We grab Angus beef, sweet garlic chicken, shrimp, and even honey garlic CHICKEN SKIN — something Sierra has never tried before.

Next, we find what ends up being one of the biggest surprises of the entire night: BIRRIA GRILLED CHEESE.

It combines everything you'd want from a grilled cheese with birria, and it immediately shoots toward the top of our rankings. Sierra even gives it a 10/10!

But then it's time for the food we've been putting off...

Neither of us really knows what to expect, and between the seasoning and texture, this one definitely doesn't perform quite as well as the birria grilled cheese.

Finally, we finish the night with dessert and try a Nutella strawberry bao bun with ice cream before revealing which foods were our favourites.

There were some amazing foods, some questionable ones, and a few things we probably wouldn't order again — but that's part of the fun of visiting the Richmond Night Market!

tags: New Brunswick Canada|New Brunswick travel|New Brunswick road trip|Bay of Fundy|Bay of Fundy tides|Hopewell Rocks|Hopewell Rocks Canada|Hopewell Rocks kayaking|Fundy National Park|St Andrews New Brunswick|Saint John New Brunswick|Ministers Island|St Martins Sea Caves|East Coast Canada|Eastern Canada road trip|Canada road trip|Canada travel vlog|New Brunswick vlog|things to do New Brunswick|Bay of Fundy Canada|Canada travel|Tanner and Sierra
description:
We're finishing our Eastern Canada road trip with four days exploring New Brunswick and the incredible Bay of Fundy! 🇨🇦

In Part 3 of this 3-part series, Sierra travels through St. Andrews, Saint John, Fundy National Park, Hopewell Rocks, and more — experiencing some of the biggest tidal changes in the world along the way.

The adventure begins with the drive from Prince Edward Island to New Brunswick, crossing the Confederation Bridge before arriving in the beautiful seaside town of St. Andrews.

After exploring Kingsbrae Garden and Water Street, we spend another morning in St. Andrews before heading somewhere completely unique: Ministers Island. The only way to drive onto the island is across the ocean floor at low tide — an area that becomes covered by around 14 feet of water when the tide comes back in!

Next, we're heading toward one of the biggest highlights of the entire East Coast road trip: the Bay of Fundy.

We explore Fundy National Park before visiting the famous Hopewell Rocks at low tide, where Sierra can literally walk along the ocean floor beneath the massive rock formations.

A few hours later, everything changes.

We return as the tide rises and kayak through Hopewell Rocks in water covering the exact same places Sierra had been standing earlier. Seeing how dramatically the landscape transforms in just a few hours was easily one of the coolest experiences of the trip.
For the final full day, we explore Saint John, check out the Reversing Rapids, visit the Saint John City Market and historic Uptown, and make our way to the waterfront.

Then it's off to the massive St. Martins Sea Caves before finishing our final night in New Brunswick with some deep-dish pizza.

Finally, we make our way to Fredericton to return the rental car and fly home, officially bringing this 2-week Eastern Canada road trip through Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and New Brunswick to an end! 🇨🇦

If you're planning a trip to New Brunswick or the Bay of Fundy, hopefully this video gives you some ideas for your own East Coast Canada road trip — from St. Andrews and Ministers Island to Fundy National Park, Hopewell Rocks, Saint John, and the St. Martins Sea Caves.

description:
Welcome to Part 2 of my Eastern Canada road trip! 🇨🇦 This time, I've made it to Prince Edward Island for a few days of exploring beaches, lighthouses, seafood, Anne of Green Gables, and some of the most beautiful coastal scenery in Canada.

After taking the ferry over to PEI, we arrive in Charlottetown and start exploring Water Street and the waterfront before checking into The Arts Hotel. And, of course, my first night on the island had to include my first lobster roll of the trip! 🦞

The next morning, we spend a full day exploring Charlottetown. We grab brunch, walk along the waterfront, visit Founders Food Hall, explore downtown, and make our way toward Victoria Park and Beaconsfield Historic House. Along the way, we stumble across a hidden garden that ends up being one of my favourite unexpected finds in Charlottetown.

Next, we're heading to Cavendish for an entire day dedicated to Anne of Green Gables! We explore the places that inspired L.M. Montgomery's famous story, visit the Anne of Green Gables Museum, and then make our way into PEI National Park to see the island's famous red cliffs and beaches.

And the food somehow keeps getting better. We stop at Richard's Seafood for a hot lobster roll and fish and chips, which might just be the BEST meal of the entire trip. 🦞

For our next day, we explore the eastern side of Prince Edward Island, starting at Greenwich Beach before continuing to Basin Head Beach, Souris, and Point Prim Lighthouse. Basin Head seriously felt like we'd somehow been transported to Hawaii!

Finally, we're road-tripping across the western side of PEI. We explore the famous red sand at Argyle Shore Provincial Park, visit West Point Lighthouse, see houses made from thousands of glass bottles, and eventually make our way to Summerside for our final night.

Prince Edward Island ended up being one of the places I was most excited to visit on this entire Eastern Canada road trip, and it definitely didn't disappoint.

If you're planning a trip to PEI or wondering what to do in Prince Edward Island, hopefully this video gives you some ideas for your own road trip, from Charlottetown and Cavendish to PEI's beaches, lighthouses, seafood, and coastal drives.

We're kicking off an EPIC road trip through Atlantic Canada, starting with 4 days exploring Nova Scotia! 🇨🇦

After flying from Vancouver to Halifax, Sierra and her mom begin a two-week road trip through Canada's East Coast. This is Part 1 of a 3-part series taking us through Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and New Brunswick!

We start in Halifax, exploring the Public Gardens, Halifax Citadel, waterfront, local shops, restaurants, and Fisherman's Cove.

The next day, we head outside the city to explore some of Nova Scotia's most famous coastal towns, including Peggy's Cove, Mahone Bay, and colourful Lunenburg.

Then it's time for Cape Breton! We drive the famous Cabot Trail, stopping at beaches, waterfalls, small towns, and Cape Breton Highlands National Park before hiking the Skyline Trail at golden hour.

For our final day, we explore more of Cape Breton, hike the Middle Head Trail, visit Ingonish, follow parts of the local Artisan Trail, and finish our Nova Scotia road trip in Baddeck.

Next stop: Prince Edward Island! 🦞🇨🇦

If you're planning a Nova Scotia road trip, hopefully this video gives you some ideas for your own trip and some of the best things to do in Halifax, Peggy's Cove, Lunenburg, Cape Breton, and along the Cabot Trail.

description:
Join us for an intense day of hiking near Vancouver, Canada 🇨🇦
What started as a casual morning hike quickly turned into a 12-hour adventure across two incredible trails.

We begin at Shannon Falls, just outside of Squamish, where we take on a steep hike to a beautiful waterfall and hidden swimming spot. After a quick polar plunge and some amazing views, we head to our second hike of the day… and this is where things get real.

Echo Lake and Falls is a 17km round trip hike that took us about 8 hours to complete at a steady pace. Along the way, we deal with steep climbs, unexpected distances, and the pressure of trying to make it back in time for our boat pickup. With only a couple hours left and a long way down, things got a little stressful.

If you’re looking for epic hikes near Vancouver or planning a trip to Squamish, these trails offer some of the best views in British Columbia, just make sure you come prepared.

We start the day at El Cafecito with a beef and bean burrito and a horchata coffee, then head into the famous Granville Island Public Market to explore everything from fresh bagels to local desserts. Along the way, we try a rosemary rock salt bagel from Siegel’s Bagels (until a seagull literally steals half of it), sample a lemon square, and taste a passion fruit canelé from La Bise Bakery.

The food tour continues with a pickle tasting at Hobb’s Pickles, fresh cookies from A Bread Affair, and ends with a nostalgic stop for perogies at Kaisereck.

description:
Hi Friends & Family, in this video today we are going to explore Korea’s War Memorial. The War Memorial of Korea is a museum located in Yongsan-dong, Yongsan-gu, Seoul, South Korea. It opened in 1994 on the former site of the army headquarters to exhibit and memorialize the military history of Korea.
The War Memorial of Korea is divided into indoor and outdoor exhibitions. Exhibits amount to 6,300 pieces. The 14,000㎡ indoor exhibition area consists of The Memorial Hall, The War History Room, The Korean War Room, The Expeditionary Forces Room, The ROK Armed Forces Room, The Exhibition Hall for Donated Artifacts, and The Exhibition of Large Military Equipments. Various materials related to wars fought to protect the nation, from the distant prehistoric times to the present day, and the merits of those who dedicated themselves to the country are displayed dynamically and three-dimensionally through various exhibition materials

In the country of Philippines you would find most of the population (around 82 percent) are Roman Catholics, while around 5 percent of people practice Islam. The rest 13 percent consists of people from mixed faith.

Boracay is a small island in the Central Philippines. It's known for its resorts and beaches. Along the west coast, White Beach is backed by palm trees, bars and restaurants. On the east coast, strong winds make Bulabog Beach a hub for water sports. Nearby, the observation deck on Mount Luho offers panoramic views over the island. Offshore, coral reefs and shipwrecks are home to diverse marine life.

Caticlan Airport is the nearest airport to Boracay, located just off the island's southern tip in nearby Caticlan. On the other hand, Kalibo Airport is located in the capital city of Aklan and is the bigger airport between the two gateways as it can accommodate larger aircraft.

Popular for its beaches and blessed with a long stretch of powdery white sand, crystal clear and azure waters, and a stunning sunset. Boracay is the most iconic island in the Philipines and has won multiple awards in previous years.

Located in Sivagangai district, the Keezhadi museum has been constructed as a testament to the lives led by people in the Sangam era. Carbon dating of the artefacts showed that the Vaigai riverbed was urbanised during the early 6th century BCE, around the same time that the Ganges civilisation was urbanised, according to the Tamil Nadu government. More than 1000 symbols and 60 pot shells with lettering in Thamizhi, an ancient Tamil script, have been found during the excavations. Earlier, the Sangam era was calculated to have been between 3rd century BCE and 3rd century CE, but with these findings, the estimated period has now been pushed back to 6th century BCE, the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology has said. The findings also establish extensive commercial networks between Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, the Ganges civilisation, as well as Rome.
