It's one of Sri Lanka's most mysterious abandoned ruins, perched on a rock monolith 500ft above the valley. There is a clear proof of advanced ancient technology in King Ravana's Palace which is located in SIGIRIYA. The Ancient Builders not only used Chisels and Hammers for Construction and Carvings but also some other Advanced Machines to create Marvelous Construction & Carvings. Sigiriya (Lion Rock) "is famous for its palace ruins on top of a massive 200 meter high rock surrounded by the remains of an extensive network of gardens, reservoirs and other structures. description:
🇳🇵 Pokhara to Manang Road Trip | Dangerous Cliffs, Beautiful Waterfalls & Drone Rescue! 😱

Welcome back to our Nepal Expedition 2026! ❤️🏔️

In this episode, we continue our adventurous journey from Jagat towards Manang, Nepal. The route is filled with breathtaking mountain views, beautiful waterfalls, deep valleys and massive cliffs that make this Himalayan road trip truly unforgettable!

On the way, we meet an inspiring cyclist riding all the way to Manang, enjoy some incredible natural views and capture cinematic drone shots of the dramatic Himalayan landscape.

But things get a little scary when our drone loses track of our car and starts returning towards its previous home point! 😰 We have to turn back and rescue our drone before something goes wrong. Thankfully, we manage to recover it safely!

Join us on this beautiful yet adventurous journey as we explore the stunning landscapes on the way to Manang, Nepal. 🇳🇵

✨ In this vlog:

Jagat to Manang road trip

Beautiful waterfalls along the Himalayan highway

Massive cliffs and breathtaking mountain views

Meeting an inspiring bicycle rider

Cinematic drone shots of the Himalayan landscape

A scary drone incident and our drone rescue

Exploring the adventurous roads of Nepal

If you love travel vlogs, mountain adventures and road trips, make sure to LIKE, COMMENT, SHARE & SUBSCRIBE to our channel for more episodes from Nepal Expedition 2026! ❤️

In this episode of our Nepal Road Trip, we explore the beautiful and historic village of Kagbeni, the Gateway to Upper Mustang. Hidden in the Himalayas, Kagbeni is one of Nepal's oldest villages, known for its ancient stone houses, narrow alleys, Tibetan Buddhist culture, and breathtaking mountain landscapes.

We visit the famous Kag Chode Monastery, walk through centuries-old streets, discover the unique Shaligram Stones found in the sacred Kali Gandaki River, and experience the peaceful atmosphere that makes Kagbeni truly unforgettable.

If you're planning a Nepal road trip or visiting Muktinath, don't miss this incredible Himalayan village.

💰 Currency Exchange

We exchanged Indian Rupees (INR) for Nepalese Rupees (NPR) near the border.

• Official Exchange Rate: 1 INR = 1.60 NPR
• Local exchange rates may vary depending on the exchange counter.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📱 Nepal SIM Card

We purchased Ncell SIM card after entering Nepal.
• Cost: NPR 600 (Approx. ₹400 INR)
• Useful for Internet, Google Maps, Hotel Booking, and Communication during your Nepal road trip.

description:
Welcome to one of the most sacred and breathtaking journeys in the Indian Himalayas — Gunji to Adi Kailash. This vlog captures every step, emotion, and view from this life-changing pilgrimage that takes you to Adi Kailash (Chhota Kailash), a place where Lord Shiva is believed to reside in eternal peace.
Starting from the small, beautiful border village of Gunji, we traverse through remote Himalayan terrain toward Kuti, Jyolingkong, and finally reach Adi Kailash— sacred destinations nestled near the Indo-Tibetan border in Uttarakhand.
The route is raw, rugged, and extremely remote. No mobile network, no luxuries — just pure nature, devotion, and faith. 
Also Known as Chhota Kailash, Adi Kailash is considered the twin of Mount Kailash in Tibet. It holds great significance in Hindu mythology and is believed to be a place where Lord Shiva meditates. Unlike the main Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, this route lies entirely within Indian territory — yet remains vastly unexplored.
Gunji → Kuti → Jyolingkong → Adi Kailash
🚗 Remote mountain roads
💨 Thin air, high altitude
🙏 Stronger faith with every step

In this video, you'll witness:

The destination—Dharchula—is a peaceful border town split by the Kali River, where India and Nepal exist almost side by side..

🧭 Highlights Along the Way:
Askot Wildlife Sanctuary : famous for its natural beauty

Jauljibi: a small but historic village where India-Nepal trade thrives

Bridge connecting India and Nepal at Dharchula (a unique scene!)

Scenic entry into Dharchula town, full of colours, culture, and calm

1. Valid Photo Id (Adhaar card, Voter Id card or Passport )
2. 2 Passport sized photos
3. Medical certificate
4. Address Proof
5. Police verification form
6. ILP form

And then submit to the SDM Office in Dharchula.

description:
So, finally we allowed to go to Zojila pass from the check post. And In this video, we are excited to cross and conquer Zojila Pass. Zojila pass is a high altitude mountain pass which separates kashmir valley from ladakh region. Its considered as a gateway to Ladakh. 
Zojila is the most important and strategic route as most of the supplies of ladakh region passes through this route for six month in summer as in winters this region gets totally isolated from the outer world due to snowfall and closing of zojila pass.
Due to its strategic importance this area had seen some wars. Also, major of those are zojila war, when this was captured by pakistani based tribals and was recaptured by Indian army through operation Bison.

🌋 ACATENANGO HIKE — COMPLETE GUIDE (Malayalam Travellers)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Acatenango volcano hike is one of the most epic overnight hikes in the world. Here's everything you need to know before you go:

🧭 Trailhead: Acatenango village, Chimaltenango, Guatemala
📏 Elevation: Start 7,500 ft → Summit 13,045 ft (nearly 6,000 ft gain!)
🕐 Hike up: 5–7 hours | Hike down: 3 hours
🏕️ Camp: Base camp at ~12,300 ft overnight
🌡️ Night temp: Near freezing — pack warm layers
🌋 Fuego eruptions: Every 15–20 minutes on average
💰 Tour cost: ~$35–50 USD (guide + tent + sleeping bag + meals included)
📅 Best season: November–April (dry season, clearest views)
👟 Fitness level: Challenging — steep trail, high altitude, loose volcanic gravel
⚠️ Altitude sickness is real — acclimatize 1 day in Antigua first

The payoff: watching an active volcano shoot lava and ash into the sky from your campsite at night is something no photo or video can fully capture. You have to be there.

🏛️ ANTIGUA GUATEMALA — MUST VISIT
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Antigua is a UNESCO World Heritage city — one of the best-preserved Spanish colonial cities in all of Latin America. Cobblestone streets, colourful buildings, volcano views from every corner.

📍 La Merced Church — the iconic yellow baroque church
📍 Convento Santa Clara Ruins — hauntingly beautiful
📍 Parque Central — the heart of the city
📍 Mercado Central — local food, fresh produce, crafts
🍵 Guatemala has some of the best coffee in the world — don't skip it
🌮 Try pepián (national dish) and chuchitos (local tamales)

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🚤 LAKE ATITLÁN — THE WORLD'S MOST BEAUTIFUL LAKE
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Aldous Huxley called Lake Atitlán "the most beautiful lake in the world." Three volcanoes ring the lake, and indigenous Maya villages dot its shores. We took a lancha (boat) across, rode tuk-tuks through the streets, explored local handicraft markets, and yes — got tattoos. 😂

📍 Panajachel → San Juan La Laguna → Santiago Atitlán
🚤 Lancha boat rides between villages: ~25–50 GTQ
🛺 Tuk-tuks everywhere — negotiate the price first!

description:
ഈജിപ്തിലെ ലക്സറിലുള്ള വെസ്റ്റ് ബാങ്കിലെ വിസ്മയിപ്പിക്കുന്ന കാഴ്ചകളാണ് ഈ വീഡിയോയിൽ നമ്മൾ കാണുന്നത്. പുരാതന ഈജിപ്ഷ്യൻ രാജാക്കന്മാരുടെ അന്ത്യവിശ്രമസ്ഥലമായ വാലി ഓഫ് ദി കിങ്‌സ് (Valley of the Kings) മുതൽ മമ്മികളെ നേരിട്ട് കാണുന്ന നിമിഷങ്ങൾ വരെ ഇതിൽ ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തിയിട്ടുണ്ട്.

ഈ വീഡിയോയിൽ നമ്മൾ കാണുന്ന പ്രധാന സ്ഥലങ്ങൾ:

⚰️ രാജാക്കന്മാരുടെ ശവകുടീരങ്ങൾ: ഫറവോമാരുടെ മനോഹരമായി അലങ്കരിച്ച കല്ലറകളിലേക്കുള്ള സാഹസിക യാത്ര.

🏺 അലബാസ്റ്റർ കരകൗശലം: ഹത്ഷെപ്സുത് ക്ഷേത്രത്തിലേക്കുള്ള വഴിയിൽ ഒരു തെരുവോരത്തെ കരകൗശല ശാല സന്ദർശിക്കുന്നു. തലമുറകളായി കൈമാറിവരുന്ന രീതിയിൽ അലബാസ്റ്റർ കല്ലുകൾ കൊണ്ട് വിസ്മയങ്ങൾ തീർക്കുന്ന അവിടുത്തെ കലാകാരന്മാരെ നമുക്ക് പരിചയപ്പെടാം.

🏛️ ഹത്ഷെപ്സുത് ക്ഷേത്രം (Hatshepsut Temple): ഈജിപ്തിലെ കരുത്തുറ്റ വനിതാ ഫറവോ ആയിരുന്ന ഹത്ഷെപ്സുത്തിന്റെ വിസ്മയിപ്പിക്കുന്ന ജീവിതകഥയും അവരുടെ അതിമനോഹരമായ ക്ഷേത്രവും.

🎨 മെഡിനറ്റ് ഹബു (Medinat Habu): റാംസെസ് മൂന്നാമന്റെ ഭരണകാലത്തെ അതിശയിപ്പിക്കുന്ന കൊത്തുപണികൾ നിറഞ്ഞ ക്ഷേത്രം.

ഈജിപ്ഷ്യൻ ചരിത്രത്തിലെ വിസ്മയങ്ങളും അവർ മരണാനന്തര ജീവിതത്തിൽ വിശ്വസിച്ചിരുന്ന രഹസ്യങ്ങളും ഈ വീഡിയോയിലൂടെ നമുക്ക് അടുത്തറിയാം.

Welcome to the West Bank of Luxor, famously known as the "Land of the Dead." In today’s episode, we cross the Nile to explore the sacred ground where ancient Egypt’s greatest Pharaohs were laid to rest.

The Finger Lakes is a region of New York State. It's named for its series of long, thin lakes, and known for its vineyards. The surrounding area is marked by high gorges, many with dramatic waterfalls, including Taughannock Falls and Buttermilk Falls.

If you are looking to get outdoors, the Finger Lakes are a must-see destination. From hiking and biking, to boating and fishing or even, there's something for everyone to enjoy. There are also a number of state parks with scenic beauty to behold including a number of waterfalls; visit Watkins Glen State Park to see the gorge trail complete with 19 waterfalls. 

Watkins Glen State Park is in the village of Watkins Glen, south of Seneca Lake in Schuyler County in New York's Finger Lakes region. The park's lower part is near the village, while the upper part is open woodland. It was opened to the public in 1863 

Seneca Lake is the largest of the glacial Finger Lakes of the U.S. state of New York, and the deepest lake entirely within the state.

Ithaca Falls is a waterfall located within the city of Ithaca, New York. It is the last of a series of waterfalls along the hanging valley formed where Fall Creek intersects the glacial trough of Cayuga Lake. The falls are in an amphitheater formed by freezing and thawing of the weak shale which makes up most of the gorge walls.

description:
London, city, capital of the United Kingdom. It is among the oldest of the world’s great cities—its history spanning nearly two millennia—and one of the most cosmopolitan. By far Britain’s largest metropolis, it is also the country’s economic, transportation, and cultural center.

Tower of London-
The Tower of London, officially Her Majesty's Royal Palace and Fortress of the Tower of London is a historic castle located on the north bank of the River Thames in central London. It lies within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, which is separated from the eastern edge of the square mile of the City of London by the open space known as Tower Hill. It was founded towards the end of 1066 as part of the Norman Conquest of England. The White Tower, which gives the entire castle its name, was built by William the Conqueror in 1078 and was a resented symbol of oppression, inflicted upon London by the new ruling elite. The castle was used as a prison from 1100 until 1952, although that was not its primary purpose. A grand palace early in its history, it served as a royal residence. As a whole, the Tower is a complex of several buildings set within two concentric rings of defensive walls and a moat. There were several phases of expansion, mainly under kings Richard I, Henry III, and Edward I in the 12th and 13th centuries. The general layout established by the late 13th century remains despite later activity on the site.

We aimed to see the sunset of Kumarakom to its waters would be the best things to see. 
We started from Angamaly around 9.30 Am in the morning and reached Kumarakom around 11.30 am with a couple of stops on the way. 
The village of Kumarakom is a cluster of little islands on the Vembanad Lake and is part of the Kuttanad region. The bird sanctuary here, which is spread across 14 acres is a favorite haunt of migratory birds and an ornithologist's paradise. Egrets, Darters, Herons, Teals, Waterfowls, Cuckoo, Wild Duck and migratory birds like the Siberian Stork visit here in flocks and fascinate all visitors.
An enchanting backwater destination, Kumarakom offers visitors many other leisure options. One of them is The Zuri Kumarakom, Kerala Resort & Spa. We had our lunch from the Lime restaurant there. Pretty good with lots of options, though it gets crowded after a while, we were treated well. 

The boat ride in  Vembanad Lake is just relaxed and refined feeling, featuring lush flowery landscapes and a multicolored plethora of bird species, best enjoyed the best sunset.

The day well ended with an authentic dinner from the Kottayam club overlooking the Lake. Must see !!!

description:
What should we say - Dramatic Landscapes !!

Yellowstone National Park should be in anyone’s bucket list who loves the bond between nature & wildlife. Dramatic landscape, Alpine Forest, Gushing Geyser,Fuming Hot Spring, Volcanic Caldera, Bubbling Basin,Colourful pool,Scenic Lake,Hiking trail what all what not. 

This topography is the perfect choice for photography & a traveler's stop. The whole area is atop of a volcano & the vesicles give a rough & porous texture on the earth’s outer crust. It exactly looks like a painful blister on earth’s skin.

Yellowstone National Park is a nearly 3,500-sq.-mile wilderness recreation area atop a volcanic hot spot. Mostly in Wyoming, the park spreads into parts of Montana and Idaho too. Yellowstone features dramatic canyons, alpine rivers, lush forests, hot springs and gushing geysers, including its most famous, Old Faithful. It's also home to hundreds of animal species, including bears, wolves, bison, elk and antelope.

Old Faithful is a cone geyser. It was named in 1870 during the Washburn-Langford-Doane Expedition and was the first geyser in the park to receive a name. It is a highly predictable geothermal feature, and has erupted every 44 minutes to two hours since 2000.

The Grand Prismatic Spring - It is located in the Midway Geyser Basin.

ഹെർഷേയ്‌സ് ചോക്ലേറ്റ് വേൾഡിന്റെ ആസ്ഥാനവും പെൻസിൽവാനിയയിലെ ഹെർഷേയിലാണ് ഇതിന്റെ ആസ്ഥാനം.

ഹെർഷേയ്‌സ് ചോക്ലേറ്റ് കമ്പനി എന്ന പേരിൽ 1894-ൽ മിൽട്ടൺ എസ്. ഹെർഷേയ്‌ ഇത് സ്ഥാപിച്ചു. ലോകമെമ്പാടുമായി 60-ലധികം രാജ്യങ്ങളിൽ ഹെർഷേയ്‌യുടെ ഉൽപ്പന്നങ്ങൾ വിൽക്കപ്പെടുന്നു

Grand Canyon was at the top of our bucket list from ever since we imagined! Such an incredible landscape! Mind blown by this Natural World Wonder!

The Grand Canyon is a steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, United States. The Grand Canyon is 277 miles (446 km) long, up to 18 miles (29 km) wide and attains a depth of over a mile (6,093 feet or 1,857 meters).

The canyon and adjacent rim are contained within Grand Canyon National Park, the Kaibab National Forest, Grand Canyon-Parashant National Monument, the Hualapai Indian Reservation, the Havasupai Indian Reservation and the Navajo Nation. President Theodore Roosevelt was a major proponent of preservation of the Grand Canyon area, and visited it on numerous occasions to hunt and enjoy the scenery.

Nearly two billion years of Earth's geological history have been exposed as the Colorado River and its tributaries cut their channels through layer after layer of rock while the Colorado Plateau was uplifted.[4] While some aspects about the history of incision of the canyon are debated by geologists, several recent studies support the hypothesis that the Colorado River established its course through the area about 5 to 6 million years ago. Since that time, the Colorado River has driven the down-cutting of the tributaries and retreat of the cliffs, simultaneously deepening and widening the canyon.

For thousands of years, the area has been continuously inhabited by Native Americans, who built settlements within the canyon and its many caves. The Pueblo people considered the Grand Canyon a holy site, and made pilgrimages to it. The first European known to have viewed the Grand Canyon was García López de Cárdenas from Spain, who arrived in 1540.

Antelope Canyon

Antelope Canyon is a slot canyon in the American Southwest. It is on Navajo land east of Page, Arizona. 
Antelope Canyon includes two separate, scenic slot canyon sections, referred to individually as "Upper Antelope Canyon" or "The Crack"; and "Lower Antelope Canyon" or "The Corkscrew".We visited the Lower Canyon. You have to take reservation with the tour company before visiting. Tickets will cost you  40$ per person.

Antelope Canyon was formed by erosion of Navajo Sandstone, primarily due to flash flooding and secondarily due to other sub-aerial processes. Rainwater, especially during monsoon season, runs into the extensive basin above the slot canyon sections, picking up speed and sand as it rushes into the narrow passageways. Over time the passageways eroded away, making the corridors deeper and smoothing hard edges in such a way as to form characteristic "flowing" shapes in the rock.

Horse Shoe Bend 

Horseshoe Bend is a horseshoe-shaped incised meander of the Colorado River located near the town of Page, Arizona, in the United States.

It is accessible via hiking a 1.5-mile (2.4 km) round trip from U.S. Route 89. Horseshoe Bend can be viewed from the steep cliff above.

The overlook is 4,200 feet (1,300 m) above sea level, and the Colorado River is at 3,200 feet (980 m) above sea level, making it a 1,000-foot (300 m) drop.

The World War II Memorial is a memorial of national significance dedicated to Americans who served in the armed forces and as civilians during World War II. The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is the largest of the many reflecting pools in Washington, D.C. It is a long and large rectangular pool located on the National Mall. The Lincoln Memorial is an American national monument built to honor the 16th President of the United States, Abraham Lincoln. It is located on the western end of the National Mall. The building is in the form of a Greek Doric temple and contains a large seated sculpture of Abraham Lincoln and inscriptions of two well-known speeches by Lincoln, "The Gettysburg Address" and his Second Inaugural Address.

Washington DC

Places to visit in Washington DC 

Washington, DC, the U.S. capital, is a compact city on the Potomac River, bordering the states of Maryland and Virginia. It's defined by imposing neoclassical monuments and buildings – including the iconic ones that house the federal government's 3 branches: the Capitol, White House, and Supreme Court. It's also home to iconic museums

Day 1

White House - 

The White House is the official residence and workplace of the President of the United States. It is located at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue NW in Washington, D.C. and has been the residence of every U.S. President since John Adams in 1800. 

Washington Monument - 

The Washington Monument is an obelisk on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., built to commemorate George Washington, once commander-in-chief of the Continental Army and the first President of the United States. Located almost due east of the Reflecting Pool and the Lincoln Memorial, the monument, made of marble, granite, and bluestone gneiss

The National Air and Space Museum 

The National Air and Space Museum of the Smithsonian Institution, also called the NASM, is a museum in Washington, D.C. In 2016, the museum saw approximately 7.5 million visitors, making it the second most visited museum in the world, and the most visited museum in the United States.  The museum contains the Apollo 11 command module, the Wright brothers' Plane, and many other interesting exhibits.

US Capitol 

The United States Capitol often called the Capitol Building, is the home of the United States Congress, and the seat of the legislative branch of the U.S. federal government. It is located on Capitol Hill at the eastern end of the National Mall in Washington, D.C.

The United States Botanic Garden 

The United States Botanic Garden (USBG) is a botanic garden on the grounds of the United States Capitol in Washington, D.C., near Garfield Circle. The U.S. Botanic Garden is supervised by the Congress through the Architect of the Capitol, who is responsible for maintaining the grounds of the United States Capitol. The USBG is open every day of the year, including federal holidays. It is the oldest continually operating botanic garden in the United States.

The Warf – Petalpalooza

The National Cherry Blossom Festival's Petalpalooza was on Saturday, April 7 from 1 – 9:30 PM at The Wharf. They had live music, games, fireworks, free product giveaways, and more. There are also lots of great restaurants along The Wharf where you can pop inside and grab a bite to eat.

The Statue of Liberty is a colossal neoclassical sculpture on Liberty Island in New York Harbor in New York City, in the United States. 
This copper statue, a gift from the people of France to the people of the United States, was designed by French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi and built by Gustave Eiffel.  
She holds a torch above her head with her right hand, and in her left hand carries a tabula ansata inscribed in Roman numerals with "JULY IV MDCCLXXVI" (July 4, 1776), the date of the U.S. Declaration of Independence. 
A broken chain lies at her feet. The statue became an icon of freedom and of the United States, and was a welcoming sight to immigrants arriving from abroad.

description:
The Adirondack Region features over 100 welcoming communities, mountains, lakes, verdant valleys and steep cliffs
Spanning more than six million acres with over 100 welcoming communities, the Adirondack Region is home to the largest protected natural area in the lower 48. Like a patchwork quilt, the Adirondacks are made up of twelve distinct regional destinations, each offering their own brand of Adirondack adventure. From the endless canoeing and kayaking in the Saranac Lake and Tupper Lake regions, to the extensive hiking trails of the High Peaks Wilderness in the Lake Placid Region - discover an area as diverse in geography as it is in activities and events. Bicycle between wineries on the Adirondack Coast, or dive to sunken shipwrecks in the Adirondack Seaway near the Canadian Border. 

High Gorge Waterfalls - High Falls Gorge is a 22 acre, privately owned nature park. We provide safe trail access for all ages to an otherwise inaccessible area, with four splendid Adirondack waterfalls cascading over rocks into a deep crevice carved a billion years ago. In the shadow of Whiteface Mountain Ski Resort, you can take a nature walk and hike to view the famous AuSable River as it cascades over ancient granite cliffs.
Sturdy bridges, walkways and groomed walking and hiking trails provide safe access to breathtaking Adirondack views and scenic photographic vantage points.

Lake Mirror 

Lake Placid - Lake Placid is a village near the lake of the same name, in New York State's Adirondack Mountains. It's known as a Winter Olympics venue and a hub for snow sports and other outdoor pursuits. In the center of town, Mirror Lake has a trail around the shoreline. The Lake Placid Olympic Museum exhibits artifacts including team uniforms and medals. The Historical Society Depot Museum is in the old train station.

Lake George - Lake George is a town in New York's vast, protected Adirondack region of mountains and old-growth forest. The town sits on the lake of the same name. On the shore, the Fort William Henry Museum & Restoration is a restored British fort, built in 1755. Nearby, Million Dollar Beach has picnic areas and a boat launch.Views was incredible .

Fort Ticonderoga - Fort Ticonderoga, formerly Fort Carillon, is a large 18th-century star fort built by the French at a narrows near the south end of Lake Champlain, in northern New York, in the United States.
Located on Lake Champlain in northeastern New York, Fort Ticonderoga served as a key point of access to both Canada and the Hudson River Valley during the French and Indian War. On May 10, 1775, Benedict Arnold of Massachusetts joined Ethan Allen and the Green Mountain Boys of Vermont in a dawn attack on the fort, surprising and capturing the sleeping British garrison. Although it was a small-scale conflict, the Battle of Fort Ticonderoga was the first American victory of the Revolutionary War, and would give the Continental Army much-needed artillery to be used in future battles.

description:
Niagara Falls is the collective name for three waterfalls that straddle the international border between Canada and the United States; more specifically, between the province of Ontario and the state of New York. They form the southern end of the Niagara Gorge.
From largest to smallest, the three waterfalls are the Horseshoe Falls, the American Falls and the Bridal Veil Falls. 

The Horseshoe Falls lies on the border of the United States and Canada with the American Falls entirely on the American side, separated by Goat Island. The smaller Bridal Veil Falls are also on the American side, separated from the other waterfalls by Luna Island. The international boundary line was originally drawn through Horseshoe Falls in 1819, but the boundary has long been in dispute due to natural erosion and construction.
Horseshoe Falls is the most powerful waterfall in North America, as measured by flow rate.

Peak visitor traffic occurs in the summertime, when Niagara Falls are both a daytime and evening attraction. From the Canadian side, floodlights illuminate both sides of the falls for several hours after dark (until midnight). The number of visitors in 2007 was expected to total 20 million, and by 2009 the annual rate was expected to top 28 million tourists. 
The oldest and best-known tourist attraction at Niagara Falls is the Maid of the Mist boat cruise, named for an ancient Ongiara Indian mythical character, which has carried passengers into the rapids immediately below the falls since 1846. Cruise boats operate from boat docks on both sides of the falls. 

American side

From the U.S. side, the American Falls can be viewed from walkways along Prospect Point Park, which also features the Prospect Point Observation Tower and a boat dock for the Maid of the Mist. Goat Island offers more views of the falls and is accessible by foot and automobile traffic by bridge above the American Falls. From Goat Island, the Cave of the Winds is accessible by elevator and leads hikers to a point beneath Bridal Veil Falls. Also on Goat Island are the Three Sisters Islands, the Power Portal where a huge statue of Nikola Tesla can be seen, and a walking path that enables views of the rapids, the Niagara River, the gorge, and all the falls. Most of these attractions lie within the Niagara Falls State Park.

description:
THOUSAND ISLANDS - 

The Thousand Islands constitute an archipelago of 1,864 islands[1] that straddles the Canada–US border in the Saint Lawrence River as it emerges from the northeast corner of Lake Ontario. They stretch for about 50 miles (80 km) downstream from Kingston, Ontario. The Canadian islands are in the province of Ontario and the U.S. islands in the state of New York.
The islands range in size from over 40 square miles (100 km2) to smaller islands occupied by a single residence, or uninhabited outcroppings of rocks. To count as one of the Thousand Islands, emergent land within the river channel must have at least one square foot (0.093 m2) of land above water level year-round, and support at least two living trees.

BOLDT CASTLE - 

Boldt Castle is a major landmark and tourist attraction in the Thousand Islands region of the U.S. state of New York. Open to guests seasonally between mid-May and mid-October. It is located on Heart Island in the Saint Lawrence River. Heart Island is part of the Town of Alexandria, in Jefferson County. Originally a private mansion built by an American millionaire, George Boldt, it is today maintained by the Thousand Islands Bridge Authority as a tourist attraction.

SINGER CASTLE - 

Dark Island, a prominent feature of the Saint Lawrence Seaway, is located in the lower (eastern) Thousand Islands region, near Chippewa Bay. It is a part of the Town of Hammond, in St. Lawrence County, New York.A historic landmark on the island, "The Towers", was long known as "Dark Island Castle" until recently renamed "Singer Castle". The island is situated only a few yards south of the Canada-United States border that runs along the river.
The south side of the island is only about one hundred feet from the shipping channel, and cargo ships frequently pass the island. Because of the depth of the channel on one side, and the relative shallowness on the other, it is very good for sports fishing of largemouth bass and northern pike.

 CAPE VINCENT – TIBBETS POINT LIGHTHOUSE-

Cape Vincent has a strong French heritage. After his brother, Joseph, established residence here in the early 1800s, the infamous Napoleon Bonaparte was to have settled in Cape Vincent, seeking refuge from the havoc he had wrought in Europe.
Located less than three miles west of Cape Vincent where the great Lake Ontario empties into the St. Lawrence River, this historic lighthouse shares Tibbets Point with an American Youth Hostel that is open from May to October. There is also a visitor's center, museum and gift shop on the grounds. A peaceful location to stop and enjoy the view.

Into the Caves

Stop 1 - Secret Caverns

Nestled in the hallowed halls of hollow earth, Secret Caverns is a small commercial cavern located in upstate New York. Founded by local civil engineer Roger Mallery, the caverns have hosted Americas roadside travelers and seekers of subterranean knowledge and adventure since its discovery by intrepid bovine explorers in 1928.
Tour- Visitors to the cave can expect a 45 minute to 1 hour guided walk through unsullied but accessible prehistoric passageway encrusted by the patient hand of time. Mother Nature’s handiwork can be easily viewed in the form of stalactites, stalagmites, and flowstone. Because visitors enter the cavern by use of the petrified escalator (the 103 stairs), the various layers of limestone deposited faithfully by the prehistoric ocean, which covered North America during the Silurian-Devonian eras, one can easily view Americas "first" settlers in the form of brachiopods, corals, and crinoids.
The tour culminates when one reaches the world famous 100 ft. underground waterfall. Truly a wonder of nature, this rare sight is unmatched among show caves. The caverns maintain a year-round temperature of 50 degrees F (~10 degrees C). As a result, we recommend a light jacket or sweater and comfortable walking shoes. Cameras, pictures, and touching of the formations are allowed, as is not the case with most other show caves in the US.
The complete trip of 1/2 mile takes about an hour. A guided group of generally no more than twenty enters the cave every 15-20 minutes throughout the day. The walking tour descends 103 steps to the lighted concrete walkway and gives an intimate view of ancient calcite formations, prehistoric fossils, and the spectacular 100-foot underground waterfall.

Stop 2 - Howe Caverns

The Howe Caverns is a cave in Howes Cave, Schoharie County, New York. Howe Caverns is a popular tourist attraction, providing cave-goers with a sense of caving or spelunking, without needing the advanced equipment and training usually associated with such adventures.

The Howe Caverns is named after Farmer Lester Howe, who discovered the cave on May 22, 1842. Noticing that his cows frequently gathered near some bushes at the bottom of a hill on sizzling summer days, Howe decided to investigate. Behind the bushes, Howe found a strong, cool breeze emanating from a hole in the Earth. Howe proceeded to dig out and explore the cave with his friend and neighbor, Henry Wetsel, on whose land the cave entrance was located. Even to this day, the cave is at a constant temperature of 52 degrees Fahrenheit, irrespective of the outside weather. 

Howe opened the cave to eight-hour public tours in 1843, and, as the business grew, a hotel was built over the entrance. The quarry's purchase included the hillside, which opened to the cave's natural entrance. Eventually, the cave was closed to the public, until an organization was formed in 1927 to reopen it. The organization spent the next two years undertaking development work to create another route into the cave. After completion of the work – including elevators, brick walkways, lighting, and handrails – the cave was reopened to visitors on Memorial Day, May 1929. 
The tour lasts about 80 minutes and shows most of, the cave. Visitors begin at the elevators and continue to the end of Lake of Venus, which marks the end of the property. Beyond this point lie about 2,100 feet (640 m) of unconditioned and destroyed caverns, which lead to the quarry and the natural entrance.

Places we are visiting:-

Cape Cod is a geographic cape extending into the Atlantic Ocean from the southeastern corner of mainland Massachusetts, in the northeastern United States. It's historic, maritime character and ample beaches attract heavy tourism during the summer months.

Nobska Light, originally called Nobsque Light, also known as Nobska Point Light is a lighthouse located at the division between Buzzards Bay and Vineyard Sound in Woods Hole, Massachusetts on the southwestern tip of Cape Cod, Massachusetts. It overlooks Martha's Vineyard and Nonamesset Island. The light station was established in 1826, with the tower protruding above the keeper's house, and was replaced in 1876 by the current 42-foot tall iron tower. The light station was added to the National Register of Historic Places as Nobska Point Light Station in 1987.

Boston (pronounced Listeni/ˈbɒstən/ boss-tən) is the capital and most populous city of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts in the United States. Boston is also the seat of Suffolk County, although the county government was disbanded on July 1, 1999. The city proper covers 48 square miles (124 km2) with an estimated population of 667,137 in 2015, making it the largest city in New England and the 23rd most populous city in the United States. The city is the economic and cultural anchor of a substantially larger metropolitan area known as Greater Boston, a Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA) home to a census-estimated 4.7 million people in 2014 and ranking as the tenth-largest such area in the country.

The Freedom Trail is a 2.5-mile-long (4.0 km) path through downtown Boston, Massachusetts that passes by 16 locations significant to the history of the United States. Marked largely with brick, it winds between Boston Common to the Bunker Hill Monument in Charlestown. Stops along the trail include simple explanatory ground markers, graveyards, notable churches and buildings, and a historic naval frigate.

Boston Common (also known as the Common) is a central public park in downtown Boston, Massachusetts. It is sometimes erroneously referred to as the "Boston Commons". Dating from 1634, it is the oldest city park in the United States. The Boston Common consists of 50 acres (20 ha) of land bounded by Tremont Street, Park Street, Beacon Street, Charles Street, and Boylston Street. The Common is part of the Emerald Necklace of parks and parkways that extend from the Common south to Franklin Park in Jamaica Plain, Roxbury, and Dorchester. A visitors' center for all of Boston is located on the Tremont Street side of the park.

The Massachusetts State House, also known as the Massachusetts Statehouse or the New State House, is the state capitol and seat of government for the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, located in the Beacon Hill/Downtown neighborhood of Boston.

Castle Island is located on Day Boulevard in South Boston on the shore of Boston Harbor. It has been the site of a fortification since 1634. Castle Island was connected to the mainland by a narrow strip of land in 1928 and is thus no longer an island. It is currently a 22-acre (8.9 ha) recreation site and the location of Fort Independence.

The Boston Marathon is an annual marathon hosted by several cities in greater Boston in eastern Massachusetts, United States. It is always held on Patriots' Day, the third Monday of April. Begun in 1897, inspired by the success of the first marathon competition in the 1896 Summer Olympics, the Boston Marathon is the world's oldest annual marathon and ranks as one of the world's best-known road racing events.

Stop No.1: Panoramic view of the Center City Philadelphia skyline, viewed from Camden, New Jersey, across the Delaware River. Comcast Center.

The main museum building was completed in 1928 on Fairmount, a hill located at the northwest end of the Benjamin Franklin Parkway at Eakins Oval. The museum administers collections containing over 240,000 objects including major holdings of European, American and Asian origin. The various classes of artwork include sculpture, paintings, prints, drawings, photographs, armor and decorative arts

1) Lombard Street is an east–west street in San Francisco, California that is famous for a steep, one-block section with eight hairpin turns. Stretching from The Presidio east to The Embarcadero (with a gap on Telegraph Hill), most of the street's western segment is a major thoroughfare designated as part of U.S. Route 101. The famous one-block section, claimed as "the most crooked street in the world", is located along the eastern segment in the Russian Hill neighborhood. The street was named after Lombard Street in Philadelphia by San Francisco surveyor Jasper O'Farrell. 

2) The Golden Gate Bridge is a suspension bridge spanning the Golden Gate strait, the one-mile-wide (1.6 km), three-mile-long (4.8 km) channel between San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean. The structure links the American city of San Francisco, California – the northern tip of the San Francisco Peninsula – to Marin County, carrying both U.S. Route 101 and California State Route 1 across the strait. The bridge is one of the most internationally recognized symbols of San Francisco, California, and the United States. It has been declared one of the Wonders of the Modern World by the American Society of Civil Engineers. 
The Frommer's travel guide describes the Golden Gate Bridge as "possibly the most beautiful, certainly the most photographed, bridge in the world." It opened in 1937 and was, until 1964, the longest suspension bridge main span in the world, at 4,200 feet (1,300 m).

3) Muir Woods National Monument is a unit of the National Park Service on Mount Tamalpais near the Pacific coast, in southwestern Marin County, California. It is part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area, and is 12 miles (19 km) north of San Francisco. It protects 554 acres (224 ha), of which 240 acres (97 ha) are old growth coast redwood (Sequoia sempervirens) forests, one of a few such stands remaining in the San Francisco Bay Area.

4) Muir Beach Overlook is part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area. People may visit this cliffside park when driving on State Route 1 (also known as Highway 1) north of San Francisco, California and south of Stinson Beach, California. It has views of Pacific oceanside cliffs and on clear days you can see San Francisco. You can also view migrating blue whales between November and June.

Exploring the Mysteries of Alcatraz

Alcatraz Island offers a close-up look at the site of the first lighthouse and US built fort on the West Coast, the infamous federal penitentiary long off-limits to the public, and the history making 18-month occupation by Indians of All Tribes. Rich in history, there is also a natural side to the Rock—gardens, tide pools, bird colonies, and bay views beyond compare.
Alcatraz Island is in the San Francisco Bay, 1.25 miles (2.01 km) offshore from San Francisco, California, United States. The small island was developed with facilities for a lighthouse, a military fortification, a military prison (1868), and a federal prison from 1933 until 1963. Beginning in November 1969, the island was occupied for more than 19 months by a group of aboriginal people from San Francisco who were part of a wave of Native activism across the nation with public protests through the 1970s. In 1972, Alcatraz became a national recreation area and received designation as a National Historic Landmark in 1986.

Today, the island's facilities are managed by the National Park Service as part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area; it is open to tours. Visitors can reach the island by ferry ride from Pier 33, near Fisherman's Wharf, San Francisco. Hornblower Cruises and Events, operating under the name Alcatraz Cruises, is the official ferry provider to and from the island.

It is home to the abandoned prison, the site of the oldest operating lighthouse on the West Coast of the United States, early military fortifications, and natural features such as rock pools and a seabird colony.

The Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary or United States Penitentiary, Alcatraz Island (often just referred to as Alcatraz) was a maximum high-security federal prison on Alcatraz Island, 1.25 miles (2.01 km) off the coast of San Francisco, California, which operated from 1934 to 1963. Alcatraz was designed to hold prisoners who continuously caused trouble at other federal prisons. One of the world's most notorious and best known prisons over the years, Alcatraz housed some 1,576 of America's most ruthless criminals

Landmarks on the island include the Main Cell house, Dining Hall, Library, Lighthouse, the ruins of the Warden's House and Officers' Club, Parade Grounds, building 64, Water Tower, New Industries Building, Model Industries Building, and the Recreation Yard.

A total of 36 prisoners made 14 escape attempts during the 29 years of the prison's existence, the most notable of which were the violent escape attempt of May 1946 known as the "Battle of Alcatraz", and the arguably successful "Escape from Alcatraz" by Frank Morris, John Anglin, and Clarence Anglin in June 1962 .

1) Fisherman's Wharf is a neighborhood and popular tourist attraction in San Francisco, California. It roughly encompasses the northern waterfront area of San Francisco from Ghirardelli Square or Van Ness Avenue east to Pier 35 or Kearny Street. The F Market streetcar runs through the area, the Powell-Hyde cable car lines runs to Aquatic Park, at the edge of Fisherman's Wharf, and the Powell-Mason cable car line runs a few blocks away.

2) Pier 39 is a shopping center and popular tourist attraction built on a pier in San Francisco, California. At Pier 39, there are shops, restaurants, a video arcade, street performances, the Aquarium of the Bay, virtual 3D rides, and views of California sea lions hauled out on docks on Pier 39's marina. The marina is also home to the floating Forbes Island restaurant. A two-story carousel is one of the pier's more dominant features, although it is not directly visible from the street and sits towards the end of the pier. The family-oriented entertainment and presence of marine mammals make this a popular tourist location for families with kids.
The pier is located at the edge of the Fisherman's Wharf district and is close to North Beach, Chinatown, and the Embarcadero. The area is easily accessible via the historic F Market streetcars.
From the pier one can see Angel Island, Alcatraz, the Golden Gate Bridge, and the Bay Bridge. Blue & Gold Fleet's bay cruises leave from Pier 39.
Pier 39 was first developed by entrepreneur Warren Simmons and opened October 4, 1978. 

3) The Palace of Fine Arts in the Marina District of San Francisco, California, is a monumental structure originally constructed for the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition in order to exhibit works of art presented there. One of only a few surviving structures from the Exposition, it is still situated on its original site. It was rebuilt in 1965, and renovation of the lagoon, walkways, and a seismic retrofit were completed in early 2009.
In addition to hosting art exhibitions, it remains a popular attraction for tourists and locals and is a favorite location for weddings and wedding party photographs for couples throughout the San Francisco Bay Area and such an icon that a miniature replica of it was built in Disney's California Adventure in Anaheim.

4) Union Square is a 2.6-acre (1.1 ha) public plaza bordered by Geary, Powell, Post and Stockton Streets in downtown San Francisco, California. "Union Square" also refers to the central shopping, hotel, and theater district that surrounds the plaza for several blocks. The area got its name because it was once used for rallies and support for the Union Army during the American Civil War, earning its designation as a California Historical Landmark. Today, this one-block plaza and surrounding area is one of the largest collections of department stores, upscale boutiques, gift shops, art galleries, and beauty salons in the United States, making Union Square a major tourist destination, a vital, cosmopolitan gathering place in downtown San Francisco, and one of the world's premier shopping districts. Grand hotels and small inns, as well as repertory, off-Broadway, and single-act theaters also contribute to the area's dynamic, 24-hour character.

Sponsored by Bank of America, Winter Village has transformed the park into a year-round destination. In September 2016, Bryant Park announced a new operator for Winter Village’s signature concession, Danny Meyer’s Union Square Hospitality Group (USHG), who will operate Public Fare, a fine-casual eatery. In addition, the Holiday Shops which grew from 80 stores in 2002 to over 125 in 2015, will be revamped by Urbanspace, NYC’s preeminent market makers, to offer a selection of local and homemade goods and a food market featuring some of the city’s hottest restaurants.

The Amityville Horror-
On November 13, 1974, Ronald DeFeo, Jr. shot and killed six members of his family at 112 Ocean Avenue, a large Dutch Colonial house situated in a suburban neighborhood in Amityville, on the south shore of Long Island, New York. 
In December 1975, George and Kathy Lutz and their three children moved into the house. After 28 days, the Lutzes left the house, claiming to have been terrorized by paranormal phenomena while living there.

Lake Ronkonkoma – 
Lake Ronkonkoma, Long Island's largest freshwater lake, is in Suffolk County, New York, United States, and has a circumference of about 2 miles (3.2 km), and is 0.65 miles (1.05 km) across on average. 
Lady of the Lake- A supposed Native American woman that committed suicide by drowning herself in the lake during the colonial era. There are several variations of the legend, most of which lead to the woman intentionally drowning herself. It is said that at least once a year, a virile and attractive male between the ages of 18 and 38 is "taken" by the lady to be her lover. Mysteriously, there is truth to the claims that at least one male within that age range drowns in the lake at regular intervals, but drownings are common in any lake that is open to the public. It is perhaps the accuracy that it is typically a male within that age range that makes the story more mysterious.
The most widely acknowledged interpretation of the legend is that a Native American woman fell in love with a European settler. Forbidden to pursue such love, the woman was forced into an arranged marriage but their love persisted. One evening, she tried to swim across the lake to her lover, suffered fatigue and drowned. She returns every year to claim a man to be with her at the bottom of the lake

Pilgrim Psychiatric Center-
Pilgrim Psychiatric Center, formerly known as Pilgrim State Hospital, is a state-run psychiatric hospital located in Brentwood, New York. At the time it opened, it was the largest hospital of any kind in the world.

Maine is a state in the New England region of the United States. It is bordered by New Hampshire to the west, the Atlantic Ocean to the south and east, and the Canadian provinces of New Brunswick and Quebec to the east and north, respectively. We Crossed New York, Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire to reach there and took around 5-6 hours with some intervals.

Acadia National Park is a 47,000-acre Atlantic coast recreation area primarily on Maine's Mount Desert Island. Its landscape is marked by woodland, rocky beaches and glacier-scoured granite peaks such as Cadillac Mountain, the highest point on the United States’ East Coast. Among the wildlife are moose, bear, whales and seabirds. The bayside town of Bar Harbor, with restaurants and shops, is a popular gateway.

Bar Harbor, a small seaside resort on the northeastern side of Mount Desert Island, has a unique symbiotic relationship with Acadia National Park. Together, they are like conjoined twins, both born of the same mother - and she is the land and ocean combined.

Cadillac Mountain in Acadia National Park, at 1,530 feet (466 meters), is the highest point along the North Atlantic seaboard and the first place to view sunrise in the United States from October 7 through March 6. 

Sunset -  Bass Harbor is a perfect example of a quaint little fishing village on what is called the “quiet” or “back” side of Mount Desert Island - home of a large portion of Acadia National Park. Bass Harbor is filled with coastal photo opportunities like lobster boats and other yachts, lobster traps and buoys, winding roads, and buildings characteristic of the area. The famous Bass Harbor Head Lights located here on park land a short distance southeast of the harbor. This is one of the most photographed and recognized lighthouses in America.

Sunrise - Portland Head Light is a historic lighthouse in Cape Elizabeth, Maine. The light station sits on a head of land at the entrance of the primary shipping channel into Portland Harbor, which is within Casco Bay in the Gulf of Maine. Completed in 1791, it is the oldest lighthouse in the state of Maine. The light station is automated, and the tower, beacon, and foghorn are maintained by the United States Coast Guard.

Atlantic City is a resort city in Atlantic County, New Jersey, the United States, known for its casinos, boardwalk, and beach. Atlantic City was the inspiration for the American version of the board game Monopoly, especially the street names.
Since 1921, Atlantic City has been the location for the Miss America pageant.
Activities -
Casinos and gambling
Atlantic City is considered as the "Gambling Capital of the East Coast", and currently, has eight large casinos and several smaller ones. In 2011, New Jersey's then 12 casinos employed approximately 33,000 employees, had 28.5 million visitors, made $3.3 billion in gaming revenue, and paid $278 million in taxes. They are regulated by the New Jersey Casino Control Commission and the New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement.
Boardwalk
The Atlantic City Boardwalk opened on June 26, 1870, as the first boardwalk in the United States.
The Boardwalk starts at Absecon Inlet in the north and runs along the beach south-west to the city limit 4 miles (6.4 km) away then continues 1 1⁄2 miles (2.4 km) into Ventnor City. Casino/hotels front the boardwalk, as well as retail stores, restaurants, and amusements. Notable attractions include the Boardwalk Hall, House of Blues, and the Ripley's Believe It or Not museum.
Shopping
Atlantic City has many different shopping districts and malls, many of which are located inside or adjacent to the casino resorts. Several smaller themed retail and dining areas in casino hotels include the Borgata Shops and The Shoppes at Water Club inside the Borgata, the Waterfront Shops inside of Harrah's, Spice Road inside the Trump Taj Mahal, while Resorts Casino Hotel has a small collection of stores and restaurants. Times Square is a major commercial intersection and neighborhood in Midtown Manhattan, New York City, at the junction of Broadway and Seventh Avenue, and stretching from West 42nd to West 47th Streets. Brightly adorned with billboards and advertisements, Times Square is sometimes referred to as The Crossroads of the World, The Center of the Universe, the heart of The Great White Way and the "heart of the world”. One of the world's busiest pedestrian intersections, it is also the hub of the Broadway Theater District] and a major center of the world's entertainment industry.

Times Square is one of the world's most visited tourist attractions, drawing an estimated 50 million visitors annually. Approximately 330,000 people pass through Times Square daily, many of them tourists, while over 460,000 pedestrians walk through Times Square on its busiest days.

Formerly Longacre Square, Times Square was renamed in 1904 after The New York Times moved its headquarters to the newly erected Times Building, the site of the annual ball drop which began on December 31, 1907, and continues today, attracting over a million visitors to Times Square every New Year's Eve.

India is celebrating it's 70th Independence Day this year. Though we are not in the country, we really respect and value this day and culture. Throughout this parade, you could see the pride of being an Indian and unity in diversity.

Independence Day, is observed annually on 15 August is a national holiday in India commemorating the nation's independence from the British Empire on 15 August 1947. India attained independence following an Independence Movement noted for largely nonviolent resistance and civil disobedience led by the Indian National Congress (INC). Independence coincided with the partition of India, in which the British Indian Empire was divided along religious lines into the Dominions of India and Pakistan; the partition was accompanied by violent riots and mass casualties, and the displacement of nearly 15 million people due to sectarian violence. On 15 August 1947, Jawaharlal Nehru, who had become the first Prime Minister of India that day, raised the Indian national flag above the Lahori Gate of the Red Fort in Delhi. On each subsequent Independence Day, the prime minister has raised the flag and given a speech.

Independence Day, one of the three national holidays in India (the other two being the Republic Day on 26 January and Mahatma Gandhi's birthday on 2 October), is observed in all Indian states and union territories. On the eve of Independence Day, the President of India delivers the "Address to the Nation".

The City of New York, often called New York City or simply New York, is the most populous city in the United States. Located at the southern tip of the state of New York, the city is the center of the New York metropolitan area, one of the most populous urban agglomerations in the world. With a U.S. Census Bureau-estimated 2015 population of 8,550,405 distributed over a land area of just 305 square miles (790 km2), New York is also the most densely populated major city in the United States. A global power city, New York City exerts a significant impact upon commerce, finance, media, art, fashion, research, technology, education, and entertainment, its fast pace defining the term New York minute.

One World Trade Center (also known as the Freedom Tower, 1 World Trade Center, One WTC and 1 WTC) is the main building of the rebuilt World Trade Center complex in Lower Manhattan, New York City. It is the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere, and the sixth-tallest in the world. The supertall structure has the same name as the North Tower of the original World Trade Center, which was completely destroyed in the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001. The new skyscraper stands on the northwest corner of the 16-acre (6.5 ha) World Trade Center site, on the site of the original 6 World Trade Center. The building is bounded by West Street to the west, Vesey Street to the north, Fulton Street to the south, and Washington Street to the east.

The National September 11 Memorial & Museum (known separately as the 9/11 Memorial and 9/11 Memorial Museum) are the principal memorial and museum, respectively. They commemorate the September 11, 2001 attacks, which killed 2,977 victims, and the World Trade Center bombing of 1993, which killed six. The memorial is located at the World Trade Center site, the former location of the Twin Towers, which were destroyed during the September 11 attacks. It is operated by a non-profit corporation whose mission is to raise funds for, program, own, and operate the memorial and museum at the World Trade Center site.

1. Dress Code: Proper attire is required. Visitors must wear long pants or skirts and cover their shoulders. Sleeveless shirts and shorts are not allowed, so be sure to dress conservatively. This is to show respect to the cultural and religious significance of the site.

2. Opening Hours: The Grand Palace is typically open every day from 8:30 AM to 3:30 PM, but hours can vary during holidays or special events, so it’s good to check ahead.

3. Ticket Purchase*: There is an entrance fee to the Grand Palace, and tickets can only be purchased at the official ticket booths near the entrance. Avoid buying tickets from street vendors as they might be scams.

4. Respect Royalty: The Grand Palace is a royal residence and an important cultural site. Always show respect when inside, which includes not taking photos in certain areas, especially in the temples and of the royal family’s images.

5. Shoes Off: When entering temples or sacred spaces within the Grand Palace, you will be required to remove your shoes.

6. No Smoking or Vaping: Smoking is prohibited in the Grand Palace and its surrounding areas, including the gardens and temples. Vaping is also restricted.

7. Photography Restrictions: While photography is allowed in some areas, be mindful of signs that restrict photography, especially inside temples. In certain areas, flash photography and tripods are not allowed.

8. Stay Quiet: As the Grand Palace is a place of religious and cultural significance, maintain a respectful and quiet demeanor, especially when in sacred areas like the Emerald Buddha Temple.

9. Don’t Point Your Feet: In Thai culture, pointing your feet at people or religious images is considered disrespectful. Be mindful of your posture, especially when sitting or standing near sacred objects.

10. Guided Tours Available: You can hire an official guide at the entrance or use audio guides to learn more about the history and significance of the Grand Palace, as it’s filled with rich cultural heritage.

Following these guidelines will help ensure a respectful and enriching experience when visiting this iconic landmark in Bangkok! About:

   Don’t limit yourself to just the European side of Istanbul. Take a ferry to the Asian side, particularly Kadiköy, to experience local markets, quieter streets, and a different cultural vibe.  
3. Use Public Transportation
   Istanbul’s public transportation system is extensive and affordable. Use the Istanbulkart, a reloadable card, for buses, trams, ferries, and metro lines. Avoid taxis during rush hours as traffic can be heavy.  
4. Dress Modestly for Religious Sites
   When visiting mosques or other religious sites, ensure your attire is modest. Women should bring a scarf to cover their hair, and both men and women should avoid shorts and sleeveless tops.  
5. Try Local Cuisine
   Indulge in Turkish delicacies like kebabs, baklava, simit, and Turkish tea. Don’t miss a traditional breakfast spread or street foods such as roasted chestnuts and stuffed mussels (midye dolma).  
6.Bargain at the Bazaars  
   The Grand Bazaar and Spice Bazaar are must-visit shopping spots. Bargaining is expected here, so negotiate politely to get a good deal on souvenirs, carpets, and spices.  
7.Take a Bosphorus Cruise 
   A Bosphorus cruise is a must-do to see Istanbul’s stunning skyline, palaces, and bridges from the water. Opt for a sunset cruise for the most magical views.  
8.Visit Neighborhoods Beyond Sultanahmet  
   While Sultanahmet is home to many of the city’s landmarks, explore vibrant neighborhoods like Balat for its colorful houses, Karaköy for its trendy cafes, and Beyoğlu for its lively nightlife and Istiklal Avenue.  
9.Respect Local Customs and Traditions
   Learn a few Turkish phrases like "Merhaba" (Hello) and "Teşekkür ederim" (Thank you). Respect prayer times in mosques and ask for permission before photographing locals.  
10. Prepare for Istanbul’s Weather
   Istanbul’s weather varies significantly by season. Bring a light jacket in spring and autumn, layer up in winter, and carry sunscreen and a hat during the summer months. Always check the forecast before heading out.

description:
The sunset in Istanbul, Turkey, is a mesmerizing experience, often described as magical and breathtaking. This city, straddling two continents—Europe and Asia—is blessed with stunning landscapes, where the sun sets over the Bosphorus Strait, casting vibrant colors across the water, historical landmarks, and the skyline.

Here’s what makes an Istanbul sunset so special:

1. Golden Hour: As the sun dips below the horizon, it creates a warm, golden hue that bathes Istanbul’s iconic landmarks, such as the Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque, Galata Tower, and the Topkapi Palace. The old city is particularly stunning during this time, with the blend of Ottoman and Byzantine architecture coming to life under the fading light.

2. Bosphorus Views: Watching the sunset from the Bosphorus Strait is a popular activity. The water reflects the sky's changing colors, and boats crisscrossing the strait add to the charm. The view from a boat, bridge, or nearby hilltop (like the Pierre Loti Cafe or Galata Tower) offers a perfect vantage point.

3. Colorful Skies: The skies over Istanbul during sunset often transition from golden yellows to fiery oranges, pinks, and purples, with the silhouettes of minarets and buildings adding drama. The contrast between the vibrant sky and the darkening city creates a striking scene.

4. Atmosphere: The energy of the city is palpable during sunset. People gather at rooftop cafes, along the Bosphorus promenade, or in the many parks to witness the beauty. The cool evening breeze, combined with the mesmerizing view, makes it a moment of collective reflection and awe.

5. Cultural Significance: In Istanbul, sunsets are an important part of daily life, marking the end of the workday, the call to prayer (adhan), and the beginning of the evening. The call to prayer can often be heard from the city's many mosques as the sun sets, adding to the spiritual atmosphere.

If you find yourself in Istanbul, witnessing the sunset from a viewpoint along the Bosphorus, a rooftop terrace, or a bridge is a must-do experience. The moment offers a perfect blend of natural beauty, cultural richness, and a sense of timelessness that defines this unique city.

Koh Samet Island, Thailand  
Koh Samet, located just 200 kilometers southeast of Bangkok in the Rayong Province, is a tropical paradise that offers a perfect escape from the bustle of city life. Known for its pristine beaches, crystal-clear waters, and relaxed vibe, Koh Samet is a favorite destination for both locals and international travelers seeking tranquility and natural beauty.  

The island is part of the Khao Laem Ya-Mu Ko Samet National Park, ensuring that much of its natural charm is protected and well-preserved. Its beaches range from lively and vibrant to serene and secluded, catering to all kinds of visitors. Hat Sai Kaew (Diamond Beach) is the largest and most popular, offering activities like jet skiing, beach volleyball, and parasailing. For those seeking a quieter retreat, Ao Prao Beach on the western side of the island provides breathtaking sunsets and an intimate ambiance.  

Adventure enthusiasts will love the opportunities for snorkeling and diving around Koh Samet’s reefs, where vibrant marine life awaits. Kayaking, paddleboarding, and hiking through the lush jungle trails are also popular activities that let you explore the island's varied landscapes.  

Koh Samet is also famous for its vibrant nightlife. Beachfront bars and restaurants come alive in the evening, offering fire shows, live music, and cocktails under the stars. Local cuisine, including fresh seafood and traditional Thai dishes, is a highlight, with options ranging from street food to upscale dining experiences.  

Access to Koh Samet is convenient, with regular ferries and speedboats departing from the Ban Phe Pier in Rayong. The journey takes just 30–45 minutes, making it an easy getaway for weekend travelers. Whether you’re planning a romantic escape, a family vacation, or a solo adventure, Koh Samet’s charm and accessibility make it a must-visit destination in Thailand.  

For those who value sustainability, the island has introduced eco-friendly practices to maintain its pristine environment. Visitors are encouraged to contribute by minimizing plastic waste and respecting local wildlife.  

Koh Samet offers something for everyone, from sun-soaked relaxation to thrilling activities, making it a gem in Thailand's roster of breathtaking islands. If you're dreaming of turquoise waters and golden sands, this island will not disappoint. About:

title: The AIDS monument in WeHo – the new LGBTQ+ monument in West Hollywood
tags: AIDS Monument|Couple of Men|West Hollywood|Living Monument|Visit WeHo|Queer Travel
description:
Fifteen years in the making, The AlDS Monument is about to become part of West Hollywood’s history. 

Located in West Hollywood Park, the new monument will officially open on November 16, 2025. Australian artist Daniel Tobin designed the monument to honor, educate, and connect generations of the LGBTQ+ community. The monument’s bronze pillars carry words like Pain, Pride, Family, Courage. They are all reminders of how deeply the AlDS crisis shaped queer life and activism.

For many who came of age two decades ago, HlV was still surrounded by fear and uncertainty. Before PrEP existed, protection meant condoms, and every test came with days of anxious waiting.Today, prevention and treatment have changed that reality. PrEP and modern medication save lives, but testing remains essential. In many countries, regular HlV tests are still required to access PrEP — a reminder that awareness and responsibility must continue. 

Yet access to medication is not equal everywhere, and AlDS remains incurable. Campaigns like End AlDS keep the focus on global health and equity, showing that remembrance is also about taking action and learning from the past.

This monument stands for exactly that: memory as movement, knowledge as protection, and community as hope. 

🌈📍 West Hollywood Park, 647 N San Vicente Blvd, Los Angeles CA
🎨 Artist: Daniel Tobin
📅 Opening: November 16, 2025

description:
Roze Zaterdag in Zaandam was a rainbow explosion of queer joy and community.

For the first time ever, Zaanstad hosted Roze Zaterdag (Pink Saturday). Celebrating our oldest Pride tradition (since 1977) on the 28th of June was not a coincidence since it marked the 56 anniversary of the Stonewall Riots.

The colorful Pride Parade through the heart of the city ended at Burcht where there was a big stage with performances and music.

We also dropped by the Zaantheater for the Queer Drag Party with fabulous drag performances and music by dj Heisa Jynx.

the Lego Pride Parade at city hall stole our hearts – proving Pride can be powerful in every shape and size.

Demonstrating with so many people felt really good, especially knowing that in many other cities people were doing the same thing. Especially Budapest Pride that had between 100,000 and 200,000 people dance from Pest to Buda, marching in an “illegal” Parade against the ban of portrayal or promotion of homosexuality in places where children might see it. It gives us hope when so many people show that they want to live in equality and will not let hate and fear rule our minds and live.

Happy Pride, happy Roze Zaterdag, and we will see you next year in Noordwijk!

The city of Malmö, the third biggest city in Sweden, is located in the southern part of the Scandinavian country. From the shoreline of the Öresund, a part of the Baltic Sea, you can spot the Danish capital city Copenhagen on the horizon. Since July 2001, the so-called Öresund Bridge which can be crossed by car or by train connects both cities conveniently and without long waiting times for a ferry boat. Over the years, this bridge became a symbol of the connection between both cities, their countries, and their LGBTQ+ communities. Now, in 2021, Malmö and Copenhagen will be the co-hosting cities for World Pride 2021, which is unique in the long history of World Pride events.

We visited the Swedish city Malmö twice in the past two years and fell in love with its strong and sustainable connection to nature as well as to the queer LGBTQ+ community. In 2020, we returned to Malmö with a mission, to dig deeper into the queer culture and history of Malmö by interviewing five queer voices of the local community. Thanks to their interviews which we planned at their favorite spots of the city, we learned about how queer-friendly the city of Malmö is, not only for World Pride 2021 but also beyond. description:
Done! And we are so proud of it! Daan finished the video about our gay summer adventure to the South Swedish county Skåne (Swedish for Scania). Thereby we are proud to finally show you the complete story of our road trip starting from Malmö. After the first night in Mölle exploring the Kullaberg Nature Reserve and meeting the gay couple Andi & Matti in their Café at the coast, we made our way south. The second stop was the city of Helsingborg where we stayed in the fantastic design hotel The Vault and enjoyed a Swedish skinny dipping sauna experience by sunset. That is also the place where this romantic photo was taken because the village of Kivik is known for its picturesque houses, flowers, and apple plantages. We spent our last day at the most beautiful beach of Sweden (that's at least what they say on the street) sunbathing in the dunes, naked swimming at the clothing-optional beach and enjoying the view of the blue Baltic Sea. The last night was planned in the beautiful apartments of Karnelund Krog & Rum where we could meet Janne and Peter, who own this place.

description:
We planned 3 days in Palakkad and stayed 5. Kollengode's paddy fields, a ₹3,500 heritage homestay, Kerala toddy and a ₹70 ropeway ride.

In this Palakkad trip vlog, we slow down in Kollengode, one of the most beautiful villages in Kerala, the "Rice Bowl of Kerala". We stay in an old heritage home in the middle of rice fields, try toddy for the first time, ride the Malampuzha ropeway, visit the Sarileru Neekevvaru shooting location at Muthalamada railway station, and eat our way through Palakkad, from Thattukada fish fry to the famous Ramassery idli. If you're looking for things to do in Palakkad or a peaceful Kerala village stay, this one's for you.

📍 Places Covered
• Kollengode village, paddy fields & viewpoints
• Kalavara restaurant & toddy shop
• Muthalamada, the Mango City of India
• Muthalamada railway station (Sarileru Neekevvaru & Hrudayam shoot)
• Rajendre Kada (Thattukada, since 1985)
• Malampuzha ropeway
• Vande Bharat train drone spot
• Kollengode's trending village tea shop
• Kollengode waterfall hill viewpoint & palm jaggery shop
• Kava dam / Kava lake & sunset viewpoint
• Kalpathy heritage village (agraharam)
• Ramassery idli shop

🏨 Stay
Mankav Heritage Home Stay, Kollengode: an old heritage home with 3 rooms, facing hills and rice fields. AC room ₹3,500/night (non-AC is cheaper). Homemade breakfast by the caretaker.
Booking link: [add link]

💰 Prices We Paid
• Heritage homestay (AC room): ₹3,500/night
• Malampuzha ropeway: ₹70 per person
• Toddy: sold by the half litre or litre

🚗 How to Reach
Fly into Coimbatore, then about 1.5 hours by road to Kollengode. You can also come via Thrissur. Self-drive cars and regular cabs are easy to find.

💡 Tips
• Best time to visit: June to August (monsoon). The hills turn into waterfalls.
• Kalpathy Ratholsavam (chariot festival) happens in November for 3 days.
• Muthalamada mangoes ripen by December–January, the first in India.
• Take home Palakkad matta rice and palm jaggery.

description:
Day 5 of our Iceland Camper Van Road Trip 🇮🇸🚐

After starting our journey from Reykjavik and exploring Iceland's incredible landscapes for the past few days, today we headed towards some of the most beautiful and unique locations in East Iceland.

Our first stop was the famous Hengifoss Waterfall. We initially thought it would be an easy walk, but reaching the waterfall required a medium trek in rainy weather. Even from a distance, the waterfall looked exactly like the photos, with its stunning red clay layers between basalt rock formations.

Next, we continued our road trip through Iceland's unreal landscapes. Endless roads, old lava fields, dramatic mountains, and scenery that looked like it belonged on another planet made the drive unforgettable.

We then visited Stuðlagil Canyon Main Access, one of Iceland's most famous canyon locations. After spending some time exploring the area, we continued our journey towards the highlight of the day — Dettifoss Waterfall.

Dettifoss is the most powerful waterfall in Europe, and honestly, it was one of the biggest waterfalls we have ever seen in our lives. The size, force, and sound of the waterfall were simply incredible.

We ended the day by driving to another campsite and getting ready for the next adventure on our Iceland Ring Road journey.

title: Finally reached the destination #bali #waterfall #travel
description:
Sekumpul Waterfalls, located in the northern part of Bali in the Singaraja region, is often regarded as one of the most beautiful waterfalls on the island. Surrounded by lush greenery, this hidden paradise is a must-visit destination for nature lovers and adventure seekers.

---

Why Visit Sekumpul Waterfalls?
Unlike many other waterfalls in Bali, Sekumpul consists of *seven cascading falls* in one area, making it a breathtaking sight. The tallest of these waterfalls reaches up to 80 meters, with crystal-clear water flowing down steep cliffs into natural pools below.

---

How to Reach Sekumpul Waterfalls
Reaching Sekumpul requires a bit of adventure. After a scenic drive through local villages and rice fields, visitors must trek for about 45 minutes. The trek involves descending steps, crossing rivers, and walking through dense forest paths. While the trek can be challenging, the reward is a stunning view of the waterfalls in all their glory.

---

What to Expect at Sekumpul Waterfalls
- **Trek Difficulty:** Moderate  
- **Best Time to Visit:** Dry season (April to October) for easier trekking and clear views  
- **Entrance Fee:** Around IDR 20,000-30,000 per person  
- **Guides Available:** Recommended for a safer trek  

---

Tips for Visiting Sekumpul Waterfalls
1. Wear comfortable shoes suitable for trekking.  
2. Bring a waterproof bag to protect your belongings.  
3. Don’t forget your swimsuit if you want to take a dip.  
4. Hire a local guide for a better experience and to learn about the area.

---

Why Sekumpul Stands Out
Unlike more crowded waterfalls in Bali, Sekumpul retains its natural charm and tranquility. The journey to the falls is as rewarding as the destination, offering glimpses of Bali's untouched beauty. The sound of rushing water, the cool mist in the air, and the serene atmosphere make it an unforgettable experience.

Whether you’re a photographer, a nature enthusiast, or an adventurer, Sekumpul Waterfalls is a destination that captures the essence of Bali’s natural wonders.

description:
The top 10 waterfalls in Coorg:

1. Abbey Falls: Located amidst lush greenery, Abbey Falls is a breathtaking sight as the water cascades down from a height of around 70 feet, creating a mesmerizing misty atmosphere around.

2. Iruppu Falls: Nestled in the Brahmagiri Range, Iruppu Falls offers a serene and picturesque setting. The waterfall plunges from about 170 feet, surrounded by dense forests and beautiful trekking trails.

3. Mallalli Falls: Situated in the foothills of the Pushpagiri Range, Mallalli Falls is renowned for its raw natural beauty. The water drops from a height of 200 feet, providing a picturesque view for nature enthusiasts.

4. Chelavara Falls: Also known as Embepare, Chelavara Falls boasts a striking drop of about 150 feet. It's an ideal spot for a peaceful day of relaxation amidst lush plantations and scenic surroundings.

5. Honnamana Falls: Honnamana Falls is celebrated for its spiritual significance and is dedicated to the goddess Honnamana. The waterfall plunges from about 60 feet, offering a spiritual and tranquil experience.

6. Burude Falls: Hidden away in the dense forests of Coorg, Burude Falls is a hidden gem. The cascading waters from a height of 80 feet create a soothing ambiance that attracts nature lovers.

7. Mallikarjuna Temple Falls: Located near the Mallikarjuna Temple, this waterfall is a divine spot offering stunning views and a spiritual atmosphere for visitors.

8. Chingara Falls: Chingara Falls is a relatively less explored waterfall, providing a tranquil escapade. The gushing water from a height of 66 feet amidst pristine surroundings is a delight for adventurers.

9. Sathodi Falls: Situated on the Yenne Hole River, Sathodi Falls is a multi-tiered beauty that drops from various heights. Surrounded by dense forests, it offers a surreal experience for those who venture to explore it.

10. Hattihole Falls: Tucked away in the remote regions of Coorg, Hattihole Falls charms visitors with its untamed beauty. The water plunges from a height of approximately 25 feet, making it an offbeat destination worth discovering.

These waterfalls showcase the natural splendor of Coorg and offer a perfect retreat for anyone seeking tranquility and enchanting views.
