Koh Chang, sometimes known as Ko Chang, is one of the largest islands in Thailand's Gulf of Thailand. Dense jungles, magnificent beaches, a lively nightlife, and, above all, a plethora of enjoyable activities and things to do. Elephant Island, so named because of its elephant-shaped head, retains its raw appeal and character thanks to the abundance of the environment surrounding it. So, whether you're visiting for two days or a week, here's a list of some of our favourite activities to do in Koh Chang.


(1) On a White Sands Beach, swing from a palm tree.
While nothing is usually a bad thing to do, it can occasionally be the nicest thing to do while relaxing on a Thai island. White Sands Beach, located in the north-western part of Koh Chang, is an excellent place to do so. There are beach bars and boats to rent, to be sure. But what's the harm in sunbathing? Choose your own sand place, preferably near one of the many swings suspended from the palm trees. Because the beach is on the west side of the island, it's also a great place to watch the sunset.


(2) Hike to the Kai Bae Waterfall, which is hidden.
On Koh Chang, there are various waterfalls to visit. The majority of them are located in a national park that costs 200 baht (£4.50) to enter, and many of them require the assistance of a guide to locate. However, there is one that is free and does not require a guide. A road leading inland is located just south of the 7-Eleven at the bottom of Kai Bae Beach. Drive or walk to the end of the road and turn left, then first right. This is just a gravel road that leads to a village. Find a parking spot, then follow the signs to the waterfall. It'll take you roughly ten minutes to hike. The final waterfall is secluded and serene. There's a good chance you won't run into anyone else on the trail. Ko Chang is one of Thailand's nicest islands, in our opinion, because of its remoteness.

(3) Embark on a Snorkelling Adventure
A snorkelling trip of the coral reefs and pristine waters abounding with fish is one of the more pleasurable activities on Koh Chang. Tickets are available for purchase across the island, however, it is preferable (and less expensive) to purchase them on the boat itself. Several old fishing ships have been adapted for snorkelling tours at the end of Bang Bao pier. They'll take you to five different locations, all within walking distance of one another, and several of them will offer you a complete lunch on the boat. Make sure you have enough of sunscreen and water with you. There are a few dive sites in Koh Chang that are worth visiting if you enjoy diving.

 
(4) Hike Salak Phet, Koh Chang's tallest mountain.
Hiking to waterfalls isn't the only thing to do on Koh Chang. Hiking through the jungles or climbing the mountains across the island are also options. Salak Phet is the island's highest point, but it's not simple to reach. While you can hire a tuk-tuk to drive you there, you should check with your hotel or hostel to see if they have any tours going that way. If not, simply ask around for recommendations for local hiking trails. There are also a number of local tour guides who are willing to rent their skills for the day.


(5) Bungalows on the Beach are a great way to spend the night.
On Koh Chang, there are a variety of accommodations to suit all budgets. The Habitat Hostel is just one of the island's cheap lodging, while White Sands Beach is lined with resorts. The ideal spot to stay is probably in a beach hut, with the sand right up to your doorstep. There are a few luxury rooms on Klong Prao Beach, but if you want peace and quiet, go to Hat Sai Noi at the bottom of the island and stay in one of the many bungalows. You'll also have access to a fantastic swimming pool with shallow water and many massage rooms just a few steps away.

After Phuket and Samui, Koh Chang is Thailand's third largest island. It is also known as "Elephant Island" because of its elephant-shaped promontory. It is located in Trat Province, in the Gulf of Thailand, near the Cambodian border, some 186 miles (300 km) east of Bangkok.

Koh Chang has something for everyone, from jungle-covered mountain peaks to vast bays, spectacular waterfalls to blooming coral reefs, beach huts to luxury resorts. The Mu Koh Chang National Park includes Koh Chang. Despite an increase in development and tourists over the last ten years or so, it has maintained its lonely and rugged nature.

70% of Koh Chang is covered with rainforests, mountains, and beaches, encompassing an area of around 82 sq. miles (212 sq.km.). The highest point on the island is Khao Salak Phet, which rises 2438 ft. (743 m.) above sea level, and the island's rugged nature means there are several waterfalls, the tallest of which, though not always the most accessible, is Klong Neung waterfall in the island's south-eastern corner.

Is there a good time to visit Ko Chang?
--------------------------------------------------------------

The cool season, which lasts from November to the end of February, is the longest on Koh Chang. This is the busiest time on the island, with assured everyday sunlight, beautiful blue skies, and calm waters. This is the best time to visit if you don't like crowds. The usual temperature during this season is between 27 and 30 ° C., with the occasional refreshing thunderstorm.  The cool season is followed by the hot season, which lasts three months from March to April. During these months, the temperature averages over 33°C on most days, which, combined with the excessive humidity, can be oppressive. Since its establishment on June 25, 1916, Bangkok Railway Station, commonly known as Hua Lamphong, had been the main transit for people touring Thailand before the introduction of low-cost air travel to Bangkok city.

Following King Rama V's orders, the building began in 1910. The King visited Germany in 1907 and was moved by the grandeur of the Frankfurt Train Station. Hua Lamphong station, as a result, includes classical features that embrace De Stijl Dutch inspirations, such as two-toned and patterned skylights and a curved roof with stained glass based on a Mario Tamagno design. Hua Lamphong is Thailand's principal gateway to the country's eastern, north-eastern, southern, and northern regions. It has a distinctive half-dome construction in an Italian neo-renaissance design that connects to the underground MRT system. It was built at the same time as the parliament building and the Bank of Thailand Museum, both designed by Mario Tamagno. It has a form that is typical of most government buildings and monuments.

The interior arrangement and appearance of the Bangkok Railway Station are similar to those of the Frankfurt Train Station. Both include a half-dome façade, a large clock, and open-air passenger galleries. Hua Lamphong has 26 ticket booths, two electric display booths, and 14 platforms, serving over 60,000 people per day on about 130 trains. Its entrance leads to the waiting and ticketing area, as well as the departures and arrivals electronic information display boards. Shops and quick food restaurants can be found on the mezzanine and lower floors. Travellers should familiarize themselves with the various types of trains and seats available before purchasing a ticket, as there are numerous possibilities. When you travel first-class, you'll have air conditioning and all seats convert to sleeping beds. Air conditioning is also available in second class, but not all seats can be converted to sleeping berths. Some seats in third class are air-conditioned, while others are not. The 103rd anniversary of the railway station was honoured in 2019.

In a city with a population of over 8 million people, life is always in motion. Hua Lamphong's historic station will hopefully be turned into a museum as Bangkok's new station, Bang Sue Grand Central station, opened at the end of 2021.

The 5 Cinque Terre villages, tucked away in a hilly bend at the eastern end of the Italian Riviera, were moulded by their deep isolation. These gorgeous, colourful towns, set amid some of the world's most stunning coastal scenery, can lift even the most jaded spirits. A 19th-century railway line carved through a series of coastal tunnels transports people from town to town, while sinuous footpaths traverse seemingly impregnable cliff slopes. Except for Corniglia, you can catch a boat from any of the villages. You may have to wait for the train or the boat, but wherever you are waiting, you may relax and take in the scenery. Except for the path connecting Vernazza and Corniglia, which leads away from the ocean over cliffs high above the sea, all of the main trails give wonderful views of the Mediterranean Sea. The colours are stunning on a sunny day. If you plan to walk more than one segment of the trail, save your ticket for the ticket booths at the start of each route.  Monterosso al Mare to Vernazza: This is a challenging 2.5 mile (4 km) trail with numerous ups and downs. Depending on how many stops you make to admire the scenery, it will take most people between 1.5 and 2 hours.  The trail from Vernazza to Corniglia is the most difficult of the four and offers the fewest views of the sea. Hiking this 2.5 mile (4 km) trail will take most people about 2 hours. Agrigento's enormous complex of temples and tombs dates back to 500 BCE and features Sicily's best surviving Doric temple (Tempio di Concordia), which is one of the most perfect to survive anywhere. In the eastern group, the Tempio di Juno Lacinia is nearly as large, while in the western group, the Temple of the Olympian Zeus is the largest at 131 ft. (40 m) but was damaged by an earthquake. Etna is a mystery; even its height fluctuates with each eruption, making it impossible to predict. However, with its often-smoking cone and height of over 9843 ft. (5) Cefalù 

Cefalù is a northern Sicilian beach city. It's famous for its Norman cathedral, a fortress-like structure with magnificent Byzantine mosaics and soaring twin towers dating from the 12th century. The Mandralisca Museum, located nearby, houses archaeological artefacts as well as a photo gallery featuring a portrait by Antonello da Messina. Trevi Fountain

Neuschwanstein Castle

Neuschwanstein, the crown gem of Europe's fairytale castles and Germany's best castle, is nestled on the edge of the mountains south of Munich. The castle was conceived in the mind of "Mad" King Ludwig of Bavaria, who commissioned it with his own personal wealth as a dream escape from the world. Neuschwanstein is so stunning that it was chosen as the inspiration for Sleeping Beauty's Castle by Walt Disney. It's an extravagant combination of spires, turrets, battlements, and pitched roofs built atop a rocky cliff surrounded by woodland.  It's a blend between neo-Romanesque and neo-Gothic mixed with a little fairytale. It is not just one of Germany's top castles to see, but it may also be the best fairytale castle in the world.


Hohenzollern Castle

Hohenzollern Castle is the ancestral home of the House of Hohenzollern, Germany's imperial family. It is one of Europe's most magnificent castles. Built in the early 1200s, the old fortress was destroyed in 1423. In 1454, a larger and more fortified successor was built, but by the beginning of the 19th century, it had fallen into disrepair. The current neo-Gothic fortified structure was built in 1850 by King Frederick William IV. The opulent residence is housed within a walled fortification with an amazing entrance. The Hohenzollerns still own and occupy the castle, and several members of the royal family are buried in the castle cemetery. Despite being private property, the castle is nevertheless open to the public.


Schwerin Castle

Unlike many other castles, which sit atop steep hills or perch on rocky crags for defence, this mega sized castle sits on an island in the middle of Schwerin Lake.  There has been a fortress here since AD 973 and In 1850, Grand Duke Friedrich Franz II ordered a complete reconstruction that retained only parts of the 16th and 17th century building. The results were the current somewhat fanciful castle with Its onion domed cupolas, tea caddy tower, and pointed spires. The opulent interior gleams once again and the highlight is the magnificent Throne Room. Seeing the castle over the lake and touring the vast gardens are amazing ways to spend part of a day.


Heidelberg Castle

The castle started in 1196 with the upper castle which was followed by the lower castle in 1212 which was completed in 1225.  The biggest expansion happened when Holy Roman Emperor Rupert III decided to make the small castle into his palace in 1410.  At its peak, Heidelberg Castle was considered the grandest palace of the Renaissance.  It fell victim to an enormous fire in 1764 that was caused by a freak lightning bolt which has left it uninhabitable but the most picturesque and largest castle ruin in Germany. The Romantic period of the 19th century brought about renewed interest in the ruins, and today the castle attracts many visitors.  Concert performances and festivals are held in the courtyard, and three times each summer there are huge fireworks displays. 


Wartburg Castle

At the turn of the 13th century, Wartburg was one of the most prominent castles in the region. The castle's most famous claim to fame occurred in 1521 when Frederick the Wise allowed religious icon Martin Luther asylum in the castle following his ex-communication by Pope Leo X. The entire Bible was translated from ancient Greek into German by Luther. In the next centuries, the castle fell into neglect and decay, but was renovated in the 19th century during the Romantic Period's ardour, and is now a popular tourist attraction. Gudauri

Gudauri is Georgia's most popular resort, located 90 minutes from Tbilisi, the country's capital. Even the parking area is higher than the peaks of most Alps slopes, at 7,200 ft (2.2 km). The 56 km (35 miles) of skiable terrain, which reaches a height of 10,750 ft (3.3 km), includes everything from long cruises for beginners to black slopes for speed demons. Beginner ski lessons are offered in English, and adrenaline addicts shouldn't miss out on the chance to Heli-ski down virgin slopes with Heliksir, an adventure firm with a decade of experience. Beyond the Jvari Pass, a new ski lift connects Gudauri and Kobi, making the resort much more accessible from Stepantsminda.

Bakuriani

This low-key resort, located two and a half hours west of Tbilisi in the centre of the Lower Caucasus range, attracts a primarily Georgian crowd. Bakuriani is still a favourite hideaway for elite skiers trying to get away from the masses, especially on weekdays when the tracks are nearly empty. Didveli, Kokhta, and Mitarbi are three interconnected ski regions with 18 km (11 miles) of downhill slopes. Didveli, which is popular with families and offers a variety of hotel and food options, as well as night skiing and an alpine rollercoaster, is smaller and more rugged than the latter two. Mitarbi, on the other hand, has no lodging and only one café. Bakuriani will host the FIS Freestyle Ski and Snowboard World Championships in 2023, a big coup for Georgia in the winter sports arena; new routes and ski lifts are now being built.


Mestia 

Mestia, a little village in the remote area of Svaneti noted for its millennium old tower homes and ancient, pagan influenced mountain culture, is only for those with a taste for adventure. Come here and select between Hatsvali and Tetnuldi, two tiny ski areas located less than 30 minutes by 4x4 from the village centre. Mestia is Georgia's wild west when it comes to skiing, so don't anticipate the creature conveniences of large resorts like hillside housing, English language signage, or full-service restaurants. The benefits include tranquil, crowd free runs that are shrouded in snow. Hatsvali is connected to the outskirts of Mestia by a ski lift that was erected in 2018, so ask for directions at the tourist office on Seti Square but double that it's working.

title: What is Martenitsa, exactly? Who is Baba Marta, by the way?

Who is Baba Marta|by the way?
description:
Martenitsa (Bulgarian red and white bracelet) is a little decoration made of white and red yarn that is worn from March 1 till the first blossoming tree or stork appears. As a result of this tradition, the 1st of March has become one of the most Bulgarian traditions ever.

Every year on March 1st, the holiday of "Grannie Marta" (Baba Marta - baba means 'Grandma' and Marta means 'March'), Bulgarians embellish themselves. This custom is regarded as a Bulgarian tradition unlike any other.

White is a beautiful colour that represents purity, innocence, and joy. The colour red represents vigour, health, and love, as well as victory, life, and courage, as well as the light of a rising or setting sun. According to common belief, this colour possesses the power of the sun and provides vigour to all living things.

Bulgarian Martenitsa is steeped in a plethora of fascinating rituals and traditions.

 •  Instead of white yarn, residents in some parts of Bulgaria use a variety of colours.
 • Every housewife in Razgrad hangs red fabric over one of the fruit trees in the garden at sunrise, "to make Baba Marta laugh."
 • Every house's mistress ties red wool locks on fruit trees and cattle horns on March 1st before sunrise in Troyan.
 • Grandmothers in Haskovo, who previously attached Martenitsa to the hands of youngsters, now dress totally in red.
 
Despite the widespread belief that Martenitsa is a Bulgarian "creation," Romania and Greece have something to say about it.

Romania

Martenitsa ("mărțișor" in Romanian) is an ancient emblem of a prehistoric scenario for nature's rebirth on the verge of spring. According to legend, this old ceremony is linked to the symbolic death and birth of a local female deity known as Baba Dokiya. In Romania, the month of March is known as Martsashor.

Greece

Ethnologists in Greece link this practice to the Balkan Peninsula's old pagan heritage, particularly agricultural fertility cults. Martenitsa's are exclusively found in high mountain places far from major metropolitan and cultural hubs in Greece.  Traditionally, grandmothers in small Greek villages tie Martenitsa on the hands of small children all year to keep them healthy and happy. In most big cities, this habit has been forgotten, but near universities and other gathering areas for young people, you can see cheerful lads and girls wearing red and white bangles around their wrists.

Macedonia

The majority of young individuals under the age of 22 had no idea what Martenitsa was. Some adults were told about it, and the majority of those over the age of 38/40 agreed that the custom has persisted in the past and that fewer people are aware of it now.

Symbolism of Martenitsa

The celebration represents the beginning of a new season - spring – as well as the natural cycle's rotation. Baba Marta represents nature in the early spring stage: chaotic, unexpected, and easily changing. Some of the ritual's distinctive elements, particularly the tying of the twisted white and red woollen threads, reflect Thracian Hellenic, possibly Roman origins.  Many trees in Bulgaria are adorned with red and white bracelets at the end of March. When a person wearing Martenitsa sees a blossoming tree, it is customary to tie it on a limb.

Baba Marta is a character from Bulgarian folklore.

Baba Marta is a mythological character in Bulgarian folklore who heralds the end of the cold winter and the arrival of spring. Baba Marta is thought to be a grouchy old lady whose emotions swing wildly, as evidenced by the fickle March weather. It was thought that when she smiled, the weather would be sunny and warm, but that if she became furious, the cold would last longer. Bulgarian forefathers begged Baba Marta for mercy by wearing the Martenitsa's red and white colours. They hoped it would speed up the passage of winter and usher in spring.

description:
Plovdiv (Bulgaria) at the historical crossroads of Europe, is a captivating city that easily transfers to culture and tradition. with a rich history and a blend of Eastern and Western influences, Plovdiv has something for everyone. The Bulgarian town of Plovdiv is located along the two sides of the river Maritza, which has a slow current, as well as on a number of scenic hills (locals call them tepe ) that add to the town's appeal and beauty. Plovdiv is a city in Bulgaria's southern and central regions. it has a population of around 350,000 people and is the country's second-largest metropolis. Plovdiv is separated into two sections: the old town of Stariyat Grad, which occupies three eastern hills, and the lower town, which is spread out across the plains below. the modern town provides amusement and exciting attractions, but the old town is best for the city's spirit and culture. The historic section of the three hill town is designated as an architectural reserve. The modern town serves as a commercial and cultural hub. It consists of a collection of museums, churches, banks, hotels, cafes, restaurants, cinemas, stores, bars, bazaars, music clubs, casinos, and other establishments. Several mosques and historic Turkish Baths may be seen here, as well as the ruins of a Roman Stadium and Vestiges of the Roman forum. The modern centre offers entertainment as well as a vibrant cultural life. Throughout the year, the fair camp hosts a variety of International exhibitions and expos. The Plovdiv International Fair is dedicated to putting on Bulgaria's largest and most famous fairs and special exhibitions. The International Fair Plovdiv hosts events that attract almost 4,700 firms from 50 countries each year. The fairgrounds attracts almost 600,000 visitors each year. These numbers demonstrate that the International Fair Plovdiv is not only the most active exposition centre in Bulgaria but also one of the largest in the Balkans. The Plovdiv International Fair is a gathering place for some major national and international firms in the domains of industry, trade, services, science, culture, and other fields of economics and development to build business contacts. The Plovdiv Valley flat terrain enables the creation of a complex road network. The "Thracian Highway" runs for 36 miles (59 km) across the region's boundaries; first-class roads are 80 miles long (129 km), second class roads are 141 miles long (227 km), and third-class roads are 405 miles long (652km). municipal roads make up the remaining 621 miles (1000 km).  Plovdiv has a certain allure in all seasons. The town is always interesting and unique. It is spectacularly snowy in the winter; green and flowers cover it in the spring; in the summer, it is almost unreal in the sweltering heat of Thracia; and in the autumn, it is quiet and serene, with ripe figs and luscious grapes falling into soft foliage... Plovdiv is difficult to convey in simple terms... to comprehend it, one must see it and feel its distinct aura.

title: Gili T to Nusa Penida travel guide, 3 days - A shock at the beach cliff…. 😳🇮🇩
tags: nusa penida|kelingking beach|broken beach|angel's billabong|Bali|Lombok|Indonesia|travel blog|travel
description:
Nusa Penida, home of turquoise waters, magnificent coves and lots of hills! We spent 3 days exploring the island and what it has to offer. 

Day 1, we arrived later in the afternoon after a long and misleading trip from Gili T... We were then greeted by a host of taxi drivers trying to over charge for taxi fare and port taxes. BE WARNED! Once we agreed to suitable price for our taxi ride, we made it to our accommodation which was situated at the top of Nusa Penida, giving us the most amazing views over the island. After collecting our scooter, we got refreshed and headed out for sunset on Crystal Bay Beach. This really was one of the most beautiful sunset's we have seen. We ate dinner on the beach and then headed back for some well needed rest. 

Day 2, Kelingking Beach. This is a must see while in Penida but be warned, its an extreme climb down to the beach and certainly not for everyone, including us. We attempted the climb down and halfway we decided would not take the risk being the only people there and we climbed back up and take in all of its beauty from the view points. While at the view point, using the drone we saw a squadron of Manta Ray!! AMAZING. 

Broken Beach and Angel's Billabong were next on our list. A trip around the West Coast of the island which took around 30 minutes we arrived at our destination. WOW! The beauty of mother nature and what crashing waves can create in the cliff sides is a must see. Amazing view points and some good little lunch spots located around the walk. We stopped off for a quick lunch which was very well priced with a view over the cliff side looking into the turquoise water.

In the evening we went to explore the local town near to where we were staying and tried our first MARTABAK MANIS! If you have a sweet tooth, this is for you. Indonesian version of sweet thick pancakes with toppings and fillings our your choice. We went for chocolate and milk. It’s soft but fluffy. And it has a little bit elastically chewiness that makes the pancake is just moreish with all those luscious fillings.

Day 3, We started our day with breakfast overlooking the mountains before heading to Pura Goa Giri Putri Temple. I can say this was one of the most magnificent temples we have seen. You enter via a small passage in the mountain side and there you are greeted by the inside of the cave which is now a temple dedicated to Shiva. We were so lucky to be greeted by locals who took us in and asked to watch their ceremony. 

And that was it, our time in Nusa Penida came to an end and we got a fast boat to Nusa Lembongan! 

See you next time. 

Emeline and Dean

description:
This is our 3 day itinerary of Gili Trawangan. 

From PadangBai to Gili Trawangan, we used Inami fast boat which this time was a treat as once the boat set off, we got lucky and ended up on the top deck by ourselves with just the sea air and a cold beer. 

Once the boat docked, we headed for our accomodation which was on the East side of the island. We were able to check in early as the room was ready, so we dropped off our bags and went straight for the beach! Almost immediately greeted by a Turtle! Then off to dinner on the Sunset beach before heading back for a well needed sleep. 

The next morning we went for a run and used the outdoor Jungle GYM. Once back and ready to start our day we rented two bikes from our accommodation which was really useful to explore the island and see much more than we could on foot. Back for breakfast on the beach and then some snorkeling. In the evening we took a bike ride over to sunset beach were we used the outdoor cinema and watched LaLa Land and had dinner and some drinks. Once the film was over, we attempted the notorious GILI T NIGHT LIFE!! Safe to say, it did not disappoint. We went to a few bars were they had live music and a DJ. In between the bars, we stopped off at the Night Market which was really cool to see all the night traders working away and providing locals and tourist with great food and drinks. 

Day 3 then quickly came around, so we started our morning with eggs and orange juice before heading out to our snorkeling boat tour which took us to 3 different spots, Bask Nest Underwater Sculpchers, Turtle Point and finally, Fish Garden. The boat then took us over to Gili Air for some lunch and then back to Gili T. Once back and changed, we took a walk across the seafront stopping off on the way for one of the best cinnamon rolls we have had (SO FAR!) Em then picked up a new fridge magnet to add to our collection. Over on sunset beach, we had our final evening watching the sunset on the beautiful beach. Rabbit Jump for dinner and then Gili YO frozen yogurt for dessert. The frozen yogurt tastes just like a place back home which was a nice touch.

At the end of the video we give our own opinions on Gili Trawangan and what we saw on our trip. Pro's and Con's of the island and whether or not we would rush back to visit again...

Thank you for watching!

title: Ubud Bali! 🇮🇩 4 day itinerary. Monkey Forest, ATV, Mount Batur, Jewellery Making, Waterfalls
tags: Ubud|Bali|Indonesia|MonkeyForest|ATV|MountBatur|Silversmith|AlasHarum|Jewellerymaking|Waterfall|Waterfalls|YouTubeShorts|Travel|Travelling|Jewellery|TravelVlog
description:
We spent 4 days roaming around the beautiful town that is Ubud! This is our full, 4 day itinerary showing you all that we saw and did along the way. 

From Monkey Forest, ATV, Mount Batur, Jewellery Making, Waterfalls and more! 

Monkey Forest- Well, we were pleasantly surprised by how amazing and big the forest was. Home to over 700 grey long-tailed Macaques, this place was beautiful. Just stay safe, and be cautious of your belongings when a monkey is close by... 

For our Mount Batur hike, we used Darma, an 18-year-old legend that kept us safe and entertained the whole time. He even took time to take lots of photos for us. His Instagram is @Darma6107. You can book direct via his IG and WhatsApp. 

ATV/Quad Biking- Well this one was not for the faint hearted! Our instructor at Beji ATV Ubud really gave us the best experience and allowed us to really push it to the limits around the only (So we were told) full off-road track in Ubud. We booked on WhatApp (+62 878-6623-2446).

Ahhh, Ubud Silversmith- This for us was a truly great experience where we got to craft something of our own. We both enjoy being hands on, so for us, this experience was great. We also enjoyed how friendly and kind the owners were. They have been open 1 year now but have been crafting jewellery for over 10 years!! We are so pleased with the rings. Again, we booked via WhatsApp (+62 857-3860-8782). As they are so busy, it's sometimes hard to reach them, so do feel free to ride out and book direct. 

Coffee plantation (By Tegenungan Waterfall)- If you're like Dean and really enjoy Coffee, this is a must try! The plantation is surrounded by rice fields and, in the evening sunshine, it is truly breathtaking. Our wonderful guide showed us how the Luwak Coffee and many Tea's are produced. (Disclaimer- DON'T put Luwak digested coffee beans into your mouth, they don't taste nice..) We then got to try 13 FREE Coffee/Tea's and then 50,000 IDR to try the Luwak Coffee. 

And finally, the waterfalls! Well Nature, there really isn't much to say about Mother Nature's beauty and wonder. Our only piece of advice is to get there as early as you can to avoid crowds.

Enjoy! 😊  🌴

Our third day in Paris starts with police barriers around Hotel Cambon, where we need ID and hotel confirmation just to get back through. With crowds gathering for the Pope’s visit, we head out for a light breakfast and a look at an extraordinary morning in the neighborhood.

Then it’s off to Le Marais—a lively mix of cafés, food shops, and streets we loved exploring. A chocolate and caramel stop recommended by our friend Lane turns out to be a delicious choice, followed by coffee, a Danish, and an outdoor market full of goodies for dogs.

Another Metro ride brings us to Pigalle, where the adult shops and atmosphere have me thinking of Nana Plaza and Soi Cowboy. Paris style, of course! We walk to Moulin Rouge for photos outside, then catch a band playing in front of a restaurant before heading off to our evening food tour.

description:
#Syros #Greece #GreekIslands

Join us as we explore the beautiful island of Syros, Greece 🇬🇷

On this 22-minute walking tour, Tikkie and I wander through the charming streets of Ermoupoli, the capital of the Cyclades. Along the way, we'll discover colorful architecture, waterfront promenades, scenic harbor views, local neighborhoods, and some of the most beautiful city views we found during our Greek island cruise.

Syros is unlike many of the other Greek islands. While famous destinations such as Mykonos and Santorini are known primarily for tourism, Syros has long served as the administrative and cultural capital of the Cyclades. Its elegant architecture, grand public buildings, and beautiful harbor reflect a rich maritime history that helped make Ermoupoli one of Greece's most important commercial centers during the 19th century. Today, visitors can still see that fascinating blend of history, culture, and island charm throughout the city.

One of the highlights of our visit was touring the historic Church of the Dormition of the Virgin. The beautiful interior, remarkable artwork, and peaceful atmosphere made it one of the most memorable churches we visited in Greece. Built in the early 19th century, the church remains one of Syros' most important landmarks and offers visitors a glimpse into the island's rich religious and cultural heritage.

Syros offers a different side of Greece—beautiful waterfront scenery, authentic local character, impressive architecture, fascinating history, and a relaxed atmosphere that invites you to slow down and enjoy the experience.

We hope you'll come along and explore this beautiful Greek island together with us.

Thanks for watching!

My friend Gene and I woke up at 4:30AM in Tokyo to experience the world-famous fish auction at Toyosu Market. From massive frozen tuna auctions to exploring the lively outer fish market, this turned into one unforgettable final day in Japan.
On our final day in Tokyo, Gene and I decided to do something most visitors never experience — wake up before dawn and head to the Toyosu Fish Market to watch the famous tuna auction from above.

Seeing hundreds of frozen tuna lined up on the auction floor was incredible, and watching the early-morning energy of the market was unforgettable.

Later in the morning, we explored the Tsukiji Outer Market, where the atmosphere completely changes — fresh seafood, street food, sushi stalls, and nonstop action everywhere you look.

From early mornings to great food and a fun final night in Japan, this was the perfect way to end our trip.

description:
#TokyoAtNight #ShibuyaCrossing #shinjuku 
Tokyo comes alive at night — and this was the perfect introduction.
From the iconic Shibuya Crossing to an unforgettable Shinjuku food tour, this night was pure energy.

Day 1, Part 2 of our Tokyo adventure — and this is where the city really starts to glow.

My friend Gene and I begin underground as an express train flies past us, then emerge into the organized chaos of Shibuya Crossing, one of the most famous intersections in the world. We walk with the crowd, soak in the atmosphere, and watch as everyone around us captures the moment — just like we are.

From there, we head up to Starbucks overlooking the crossing for coffee, hot chocolate, and a perfect bird’s-eye view of Shibuya in motion. After crossing again (because you have to), we make our way toward Shinjuku as night falls and the city transforms.

The evening continues with a guided Shinjuku food tour led by Sabina, where we visit four different restaurants and try 12–14 incredible dishes — including the best pork cutlet I’ve ever had. Along the way, we walk through the red-light district, take in the neon glow, pass Godzilla watching over the streets, and spot the famous 3D cat lighting up the night sky.

Tokyo is colorful, exciting, magnetic — and even if you’re not a “city person,” this is a city you feel.
I love Japan. I love Tokyo. And I hope this video makes you want to experience it for yourself.

Neon lights, street life, amazing food, and the pulse of Tokyo after dark.

Nakhon Phanom is calm, friendly, and beautifully located along the Mekong River — but is it right for long-term living or expats? This video shows what a real day in this lesser-known Thai city feels like, from morning coffee to nighttime walks along the river.

This isn’t a tourist highlight reel — it’s a real look at everyday life in one of Thailand’s quieter cities.

In this episode of Bangkok and Beyond with Tikkie and Jerry, we:
• Start the day with coffee at our hotel café  
• Visit the Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge and Mekong River  
• Explore riverside cafés and a unique vintage-style restaurant  
• Get a relaxing Thai massage  
• Share honest thoughts on living in Nakhon Phanom vs Bangkok  
• Experience a lively nighttime Chinese festival  
• End the day with dinner along the Mekong River walking street  

Nakhon Phanom surprised us with its charm, scenery, and relaxed pace — but slower life isn’t for everyone. If you’re curious about Isan Thailand, expat life outside Bangkok, or hidden cities along the Mekong, this video is for you.

Today I’m in Ari, one of my favorite neighborhoods in Bangkok, exploring one of the city’s most unusual and thought-provoking places: the Kid Mai Death Awareness Café. This café is part museum, part social experiment, and part immersive art installation designed to help people reflect on life, death, and the choices we make along the way.

I met up with friends Vance, Robert, and Noi, and together we walked through the full experience — the organ jars, the anatomical displays, the “final bed,” the pitch-black coffin reflection room, and even the unusual “birth tunnel.” Kid Mai goes far beyond being a café; it’s a surreal, philosophical, slightly bizarre journey through the cycle of life.

If you’re looking for hidden gems in Bangkok, unique experiences, or just something completely different to do in Bangkok, this place is unforgettable. Join me for a full walkthrough inside the Death Café and a look at what makes Ari one of the most interesting neighborhoods in the city.

description:

#MostBeautifulTemple

We drove up into the misty mountains of Phetchabun to visit what many call the most beautiful temple in Thailand — Wat Phra That Phasorn Kaew (วัดพระธาตุผาซ่อนแก้ว). Perched high in the clouds, this dazzling mountaintop sanctuary feels almost otherworldly. Five serene Buddhas sit in perfect alignment, surrounded by lotus-petal mosaics and golden arches that shimmer in the mountain light.

In this episode, we keep things simple — just a quiet walk, a bit of history, and time to take in the breathtaking scenery of Khao Kho, one of Thailand’s most stunning regions. Whether you come for the views, the architecture, or the peaceful energy, it’s easy to see why many travelers consider this Thailand’s most beautiful wat.

What makes this temple so special:
Perched on a mountain near Khao Kho, about 5–6 hours from Bangkok.
Famous for its five seated Buddhas and intricate mosaic-tile design that glitters in sunlight and mist.
Holds a sacred relic of a revered monk, adding deep spiritual meaning to its beauty.

Offers panoramic views, cool air, and tranquility rarely found elsewhere.

If you enjoyed this, please like and subscribe — it really helps our small channel keep exploring Thailand’s most beautiful places.

Gear & Credits: Filmed by Tikkie & Jerry • Bangkok & Beyond
Music: YouTube Audio Library

Travel notes (quick tips):

Dress respectfully (shoulders and knees covered).

Visit early or on weekdays for the best light and fewer crowds.

Weather changes quickly — clouds and mist make it even more magical.

description:
#KotorMontenegro #HiddenGemsOfEurope #TikkieAndJerry
Tucked deep within the Adriatic fjords lies a place that stunned us — the walled city of Kotor, Montenegro. With its medieval fortifications, Venetian alleys, and jaw-dropping mountain backdrop, Kotor might just be the most beautiful city you’ve never heard of.

🌊 The video begins with a serene cruise through the Bay of Kotor, a fjord-like inlet often called one of Europe’s best-kept secrets. As our ship glides into port, we’re greeted by fortified walls, medieval stone towers, and postcard-perfect views.

🏛️ Once ashore, we wander through Kotor’s UNESCO-listed Old Town, where 400 years of Venetian influence come to life in narrow alleys, Romanesque churches, and colorful flower boxes spilling from rustic stone windows. With Tikkie soaking in the beauty and Jerry capturing every moment, this walk through Kotor feels like traveling back in time.

🚤 After exploring the streets, we return to the ship and close the video with a final 5 minutes of sailing out through the fjord — a quiet, cinematic goodbye to one of the most beautiful places we've ever seen.

📸 This video is filled with unforgettable sights, heartfelt moments, and a deep appreciation for Kotor’s timeless beauty. Whether you’ve been here or are dreaming of going, we hope this episode leaves you inspired.

description:

Next, we head to the marina, where we take in the peaceful beauty of the sea, watch swimmers enjoy the warm water, and admire the elegant boats floating nearby.

Then it’s off to the Old Fortress, where Jerry climbs to the top for stunning panoramic views of Old Town Corfu. Tikkie takes a break while Jerry explores the fort and captures views you'll want to see.

We continue with a walk through Old Town Corfu, filled with colorful alleyways, Venetian charm, and historic churches. We visit two different churches—one in the fort and one in the heart of Old Town.

And of course, we wrap up with not just one, but two ice cream stops: a local favorite in town and a luxury premium dessert back on board the cruise ship!

description:
Join us for a perfect day in Chania, Crete, one of the most beautiful cities in all of Greece — maybe the most beautiful. This 23-minute episode is packed with stunning visuals, smooth pacing, and the kind of travel magic we’ll never forget.

☕ We started the day with a traditional Greek coffee at a café overlooking the city, taking in the peaceful views of Crete before heading out to explore.

🍷 Our first stop on land was a charming local shop where we joined a small group for an informative and fun Cretan wine tasting, sampling unique wines made only on the island.

🌊 From there, we took a relaxing walk along Chania’s scenic harbor — colorful buildings, clear blue water, and a view you won’t forget — followed by a stroll through Old Town Chania, a true Greek gem full of charm, color, and character.

🍽️ And then came one of our best meals of the trip: a lunch in the heart of Old Town featuring an array of authentic Cretan specialties —
• Creamy Cretan cheese drizzled with honey
• Flavorful moussaka
• Juicy pork and beef meatballs
• Savory dumpling-style bites
• A simple but perfect Greek salad (no vinegar, just olive oil and Cretan cheese)

🎵 The video opens and closes with sweeping views of Crete set to music, including our arrival into port from our stateroom balcony.

This may be our favorite video so far — beautiful, engaging, and a little mouthwatering too. Come with us and fall in love with Chania, Crete.

description:
In Episode 2 of our Rome and Mediterranean Cruise travel series, Jerry spends a busy Thursday solo in Rome, balancing Italian bureaucracy with historic discovery and a well-earned lunch.

The day begins with a visit to the Italian tax office, where Jerry takes the first step toward his dream of Italian dual citizenship by applying for a codice fiscale (Italian tax ID). From there, he enjoys a relaxing late lunch at a local Roman café, soaking in the atmosphere before heading to the U.S. Embassy in Rome to notarize a power of attorney—a process that goes smoothly, but with one unexpected twist: the document must be legalized at a separate office the next day (Friday), or it won’t be valid in Italy. Luckily, that timing works out, as Tikkie arrives just in time to join the next day’s adventure.

Between errands, Jerry explores the area near the embassy and steps inside the breathtaking Basilica of Santa Maria degli Angeli e dei Martiri, a former Roman bath transformed into a church by Michelangelo.

It's Thai New Year -- known as Songkran -- a tie when Bangkok usually turns into the biggest water fight in the world, and lots of fun! But this year, instead of getting soaked, we enjoyed a peaceful side of the city, spending quality time with friends and savoring great food. 

Our Songkran week started with lunch at Gordon Ramsay's Bread Street Kitchen in Emsphere, followed by a festive dinner at Tawandang German Brewery with our friend Ren and his family visiting from Peru. Along the way we got to enjoy some fun Songkran happenings in our neighborhood.

The next day we kept it local -- enjoying breakfast pancakes from our favorite local street food vendor and coffee at Cafe' Amazon on our soi. After that I joined my weekly Meetup group, and caught up for lunch with Dave, Vance and our good friend Jim, just in from the US. 

That evening Tikkie and I shared a cozy dinner at one of our favorite EmQuartier restaurants where the portions are so huge we took home enough food for two more meals. 

To wrap up the Songkron week, we strolled around Sukhumvit's Phrom Phong area, capturing the street scenes and showing what the city looks like during the Thai New Year without the usual splashy chaos.

title: We Found Devastating Termite Damage. Will Tikkie's Mom's House Survive?
tags: #ThailandLife|#IssanThailand|#TermiteProblem|#ThaiHouseTour|#EarthQuakeThailand|#BangkokCondo|#KalasinTrip|#ThaiCulture|#BangkokandBeyond|#TikkieandJerry|#RuralLivingThailand|#TermitesinThailand|#DinosaurBridgeThailand|#ThepsudaBridge
description:
Our three--day trip to Kalasin, Thailand started off peaceful--but on Day 3 things took a dramatic turn.

After enjoying a delicious Western-style breakfast at a just discovered restaurant in Kalasin City, we headed to Makro to buy supplies for mom, dad and grandma. On the way back we took a short detour to check out giant dinosaur statues near Thepsuda Bridge which crosses over a beautiful dam/lake which will be flooded with party goers soon for Songkran.

Then it was time to head to Tikkie's family home--and that's when the real surprise hit. We inspected the upper wooden floor of the house and discovered extensive termite damage. Just as we were discussing what to do next, we got news of an earthquake in Myanmar that was felt all the way in Bangkok!

The rest of the day was filled with questions: Should we stay overnight in Khon Kaen? Drive the rental car back to Bangkok? If we fly home will we be able to get back to the condo from the airport?

We finally made it back to Bangkok and discovered cracks in our condo walls and ceilings from the quake. It was a wild end to what started as a beautiful rural getaway.

Join us as we explore life in rural Thailand, deal with unexpected natural disasters, and share an authentic slice of life in Kalasin and beyond.

description:
Our last day in Hanoi, and a busy, fun one it was. We started by heading to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum which serves as the resting place of the Vietnamese revolutionary leader and President Ho Chi Minh. Next we visit the famous (infamous) Hanoi Hilton  (Hoa Lo Prison) where Senator McCain and many other American POW's were incarcerated during the Vietnam war. Next was a Banh Mi sandwich for lunch, and a visit to a beautiful temple that we lucked into finding. And it really is beautiful. Back to the Train Market for another close train pass by, and crazy traffic all around the area where you must be on your toes to keep from getting run over. Dinner followed, followed by a walk around beautiful Old Quarter Hanoi at night and a rooftop nightcap. The next day we went back to St Joseph Church and were able to go in and show you how beautiful it is.

description:
Join us on our first day in Hanoi, Vietnam, as we dive into the vibrant energy of this incredible city.

We start our day walking the wild and crazy streets looking for Blackbird Coffee for a much needed caffeine boost. Then we set out exploring the bustling Old Quarter, navigating through streets filled with chaotic motorcycles, cars, people, and the lively spirit of Hanoi.

Next we stumble upon a festive wonderland - a street filled with shops selling beautiful Christmas ornaments, trees, Santa's, reindeers and more. It's a magical site you don't want to miss.

Join us on our journey today into Singapore's Cultural Gems, the vibrant parts of the city that are a fun and must visit.  

We start in Chinatown where history and modernity blend seemlessly where we  wander thru the bustling streets lined with traditional shophouses, and newer vendors all doing their best to sell us something nice.  We meet a tailor whose been there for 35 years.  

Next we head to Little India a district bustling with colors, aromas and sounds. Explore the bustling markets of Serangoon Road where you can find everything from fresh flowers to amazing jewelry and delicious Indian snacks.

Our journey continues to Arab Street a cultural melting pot known for its rich history and unique charm.  Visit the majestic Sultan Mosque, an iconic symb ol of Singapore's Islamic heritage.  Stroll along the streets adorned with colorful textiles and unique boutiques.  Its also a haven for street art and trendy cafes and fantastic restaurants.  We finish the afternoon with a relaxing Starbucks that was much needed.

description:
#NanThailand #Thailand #Mountains #SaltMinesNan #ExploreNanMountains #jerrysneverboredinthailand #beautifulthailand #beautifulnan #northernthailand 
 Welcome to the enchanting province of Nan, Thailand, where every turn reveals a breathtaking surprise. Join us on a journey through stunning landscapes of these beautiful mountains.  

Nestled in the heart of Northern Thailand, Nan Province boasts some of the most awe-inspiring roads you'll ever encounter. Picture yourself cruising along twisty and winding paths, surrounded by lush greenery, as the gentle breeze caresses your face.

 And what better way to take in the beauty of Nan than from a cozy coffee shop with a panoramic view at our first stop of the journey. Sip on your favorite brew as you gaze out onto the rolling hills, admiring the majestic landscape that stretches as far as the eye can see. It's a tranquil oasis that will rejuvenate your soul.

Next stop the famous Street Number 3 road, and you will understand the name as soon as you see the road.  

Ten travel back in time and witness the legacy of Nan's 800-year-old salt mines. These historical treasures have been a cornerstone of the province's economy for centuries. As you explore the well-preserved remnants of this ancient industry, you'll gain a deeper appreciation for the resilience and ingenuity of the local people.

Finally a view from the awe inspiring 1715 Viewpoint on top of the mountain.  Sure to take your breath away.  

Day one of our Nan visit and already we are smitten.  Take a trip with us to this beautiful province

title: PETRA, Jordan, A World Marvel Vlog 47-23
tags: #Petra|#Jordan|#Nabataeans|#AncientHistory|#RomanEmpire|#UNESCO
description:
#Petra #PetraJordan #Ancient History #Nabataeans #Ancient Romans
This is our journey into the amazing Petra, Jordan.  It's longer than our other videos as I wanted you to see the beauty of Petra as we saw it during our walk.  Petra is truly an amazing and enchanting piece of history.
Petra was the capital city of the Nabataeans, nomadic Arabs who established it as a major trade route around 400 BC although evidence is only found from about 200 BC.

The Nabataeans became a client state of Rome in in the first century BC but lost it's independence in 106 AD.  Many structures were destroyed in a 363 AD earthquake and it's importance declined.  It was abandoned in the early Islamic era, and not discovered until 1812.

Petra is also called the "Rose City" decause of the colour of the stone from which it is carved.  It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985

title: Ancient Egypt, Inside The Tombs in Valley of the Kings, Luxor Vlog 33-23
tags: Tikkie and Jerry|Bangkok and Beyond|Egypt travel vlog|Nile River cruise|ancient Egypt|Egyptian temples|Luxor Egypt|Cairo Egypt|Valley of the Kings|Karnak Temple|Egyptian history|Egypt tourism|travel Egypt 2023|cruise vlog Egypt|bucket list travel|travel couple Egypt|Aswan Egypt|Abu Simbel|Egypt culture and history
description:
#valley of the kings #tikkieandjerry #bangkokandbeyond 
On our last day in Egypt we started the day by visiting the magnificent Valley of the Kings.  The Valley of the Kings, located on the west bank of the Nile River near Luxor in Egypt, is a remarkable archaeological site renowned for its rich historical and cultural significance.  

The Valley of the Kings served as the burial ground for many pharaohs and powerful nobles of the New Kingdom period (approximately 16th to 11th centuries BCE). It contains more than 60 tombs, including those of famous pharaohs like Tutankhamun, Ramesses II, and Hatshepsut. These tombs were constructed to preserve the bodies of the pharaohs and their belongings for the afterlife.

 The valley was chosen as the burial site for pharaohs due to its remote and isolated location, hidden among the towering cliffs and barren desert mountains. This choice was made to safeguard the tombs from grave robbers and ensure the pharaohs' eternal rest.

The tombs in the Valley of the Kings are adorned with intricate and detailed wall paintings, depicting scenes from Egyptian mythology, rituals, and the pharaoh's journey into the afterlife. These colorful frescoes provide valuable insights into ancient Egyptian beliefs and customs.

If you can, take a few minutes to enjoy these beautiful tombs.  And stay to the end as they get more beautiful along the way

On this day during our Egypt adventure, we visited the Edfu Temple, in Edfu Egypt.  It is famous for being one of the best-preserved ancient Egyptian Temples.

title: HOW DID THEY MOVE THIS? The incredible Abu Simbel Temple in Egypt.  WOW!
tags: #abu simbel|#ancient egypt|#temples|#nile river|#travel|#entertainment|#wonders of the world
description:
Abu Simbel is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in southern Egypt.  It contains two massive rock temples, the Great Temple of Ramses II, and the smaller Temple of Hathor.  They were built in the 13th Century BC and are famous for their impressive rock-cut architecture and intricate carvings.

The temple is well known for its four colossal statues of Ramses II, each over 20 meters tall.  The interior is adorned with carvings and hieroglyphics throughout.  Abu Simbel was relocated to it's current location due to rising waters from Lake Nasser, created by the construction of the Aswan High Dam.  The relocation was a monumental feat of engineering and stands as a testament to human ingenuity and preservation of cultural heritage.

The Temple of Philae is an ancient Egyptian temple complex located on an island in the Nile River near the city of Aswan.  Dedicated to the goddess of Isis it was one of the last built in the classical Egyptian style.

description:
We go inside the Great Pyramid of Giza — one of the most incredible experiences in Egypt.
Join us as we explore the pyramid’s passageways, visit the legendary Sphinx, and ride camels across the Giza plateau.
#GreatPyramidOfGiza #EgyptTravel #pyramidsofgiza 

Welcome to our visit to the Great Pyramid of Giza, the Sphinx, and a classic camel ride across the desert.

The Great Pyramid of Giza is the oldest and largest of the three pyramids on the Giza plateau, originally standing about 146 meters (481 feet) tall. Built more than 4,500 years ago, it remains one of the most extraordinary engineering achievements of the ancient world.

In this video we crawl and walk through the narrow passageways inside the pyramid until we reach the famous King’s Chamber, experiencing firsthand the incredible construction of this ancient wonder.

After exploring the pyramid interior, we visit the magnificent Sphinx, the iconic statue with the body of a lion and the head of a human that has guarded the Giza plateau for thousands of years.

To finish the adventure, we take a camel ride across the desert with the pyramids in the background — a classic Egypt experience that definitely got our attention (and maybe raised our heart rate a little!).

Giza is truly incredible, and visiting the pyramids is an experience of a lifetime.

title: Whale Sharks in Maldives ! Spectacular expiriance that you need to see. More in our full video
description:
Whale sharks in the Maldives are the gentle giants of the ocean.
Even though they can grow as long as a bus, they are completely harmless to people.
They glide slowly through the water, filtering tiny plankton and fish eggs with their wide mouths.
You’ll often see them near the surface, swimming calmly while hundreds of small fish follow in their shadow.
In the Maldives, they’re usually spotted in warm, clear waters, especially around South Ari Atoll.

description:
Loch Morlich – Beachfront Camping in the Heart of the Highlands
Tucked away in the Cairngorms National Park, Loch Morlich is a stunning freshwater loch with a golden sandy beach — one of the few in the UK surrounded by towering mountains and ancient pine forests. It feels like a slice of the Alps and the Scottish Highlands combined.

Just steps from the water, you can park your caravan or campervan at the Loch Morlich Campsite, which offers one of the most scenic overnight stays in Scotland. Wake up to the reflection of the Cairngorm mountains on the loch, breathe in the crisp pine-scented air, and fall asleep under a canopy of stars.

Perfect for swimming, paddleboarding, or just relaxing by the shore with a cup of coffee, Loch Morlich is a must-visit for anyone who loves wild beauty and peace. The sunsets here are unreal — and if you’re lucky, you might even spot red squirrels or deer in the forest nearby.

title: Transport in the Philippines Surprised Us...
description:

description:
What does a normal day in Makati actually look like? 🇵🇭 We spent the day living like locals in the Philippines — from silog breakfasts to mall hopping, Dunkin’, and 7-Eleven snacks.

In this video, we spend a full day living like locals in Makati, Philippines 🇵🇭 — exploring everyday Filipino life, food, and culture in one of the busiest areas of Metro Manila.

Instead of typical tourist activities, we wanted to experience what a normal day in Makati looks like, from local breakfasts to hanging out in malls, cafés, and convenience stores just like many Filipinos do every day.

We started our morning at Kanto Freestyle Breakfast, a popular local spot, where we tried classic Filipino breakfast dishes like silog meals 🍳 — one of the most iconic and loved meals in the Philippines.

After breakfast, we walked around Poblacion, Makati and along Makati Avenue, taking in the atmosphere of the city before heading to Ayala Triangle Gardens, a peaceful green space in the middle of the busy business district.

Of course, no day in the Philippines is complete without coffee and snacks, so we stopped by Pickup Coffee ☕ and Dunkin’ 🍩 (Dunkin’ Donuts) — two places that are hugely popular across the country.

We then explored Greenbelt, Makati, one of the most well-known shopping areas in Manila, and visited Fully Booked Bookstore 📚, a favourite spot for locals.

To keep things authentic, we also stopped at 7-Eleven Philippines to try some everyday Filipino favourites like calamansi juice and Tang Mango Juice (powder drink) — simple but iconic drinks you’ll find all over the country.

Along the way, we picked up a fresh coconut from a local street vendor 🥥, experiencing real street life in Manila and supporting small local businesses.

description:
What does a normal day in Makati actually look like? 🇵🇭 We spent the day living like locals in the Philippines — from silog breakfasts to mall hopping, Dunkin’, and 7-Eleven snacks.

In this video, we spend a full day living like locals in Makati, Philippines 🇵🇭 — exploring everyday Filipino life, food, and culture in one of the busiest areas of Metro Manila.

Instead of typical tourist activities, we wanted to experience what a normal day in Makati looks like, from local breakfasts to hanging out in malls, cafés, and convenience stores just like many Filipinos do every day.

We started our morning at Kanto Freestyle Breakfast, a popular local spot, where we tried classic Filipino breakfast dishes like silog meals 🍳 — one of the most iconic and loved meals in the Philippines.

After breakfast, we walked around Poblacion, Makati and along Makati Avenue, taking in the atmosphere of the city before heading to Ayala Triangle Gardens, a peaceful green space in the middle of the busy business district.

Of course, no day in the Philippines is complete without coffee and snacks, so we stopped by Pickup Coffee ☕ and Dunkin’ 🍩 (Dunkin’ Donuts) — two places that are hugely popular across the country.

We then explored Greenbelt, Makati, one of the most well-known shopping areas in Manila, and visited Fully Booked Bookstore 📚, a favourite spot for locals.

To keep things authentic, we also stopped at 7-Eleven Philippines to try some everyday Filipino favourites like calamansi juice and Tang Mango Juice (powder drink) — simple but iconic drinks you’ll find all over the country.

Along the way, we picked up a fresh coconut from a local street vendor 🥥, experiencing real street life in Manila and supporting small local businesses.

This video is all about:
👉 Filipino daily life
👉 Local food in Makati
👉 Places Filipinos actually go to
👉 Experiencing the Philippines beyond tourism

Whether you’re planning a trip or just curious about life in Manila and Makati, this vlog shows a real and relatable side of the Philippines.

🇵🇭🥐 British Couple Tries a Filipino Bakery in Makati!

title: A Full Day of Eating in the Philippines 🇵🇭 #philippines #filipino #travel #filipinofood #manila
tags: The Philippines|Philippines|filipino|filipino vlog|philippines Vlog|Travel vlog|travel vlog philippines|British Vloggers In The Philippines|Backpacker|Backpacker in The Philippines|Travel Vlog South East Asia|South East Asia Travel Videos|Travel Videos|Backpacking Vlog|Travel|Is the Philippines safe|holiday|bloggers in the philippines|vloggers in the philippines|filipino food|filipino food vlog|filipino foodie|foodie|24 hour food challenge|24 hour challenge
description:
Manila is a great place for foodies in the Philippines, and Makati is a great area in Manila to start a fun challenge. While traveling, we like to try new food, but after a while, we tend to stick to what we know. 

So, for the next 24 hours, we’re only going to be eating and drinking what the server last had.
The rules are simple: we go to a place, and when the server asks us what we want, we simply say, “What did you last eat/drink off this menu?” and we order that.

Restaurant - Kanto Freestyle
Meal - Breakfast
During the day of the challenge, we got to try some amazing Filipino food, including DanggitSilog (dried fish, garlic rice, and egg) and LongSilog (Filipino pork sausages, garlic rice, and egg). The fish was very powerful in taste, and Jason liked it, but it wasn’t to Erin’s taste.

Restaurant - Good Sh*t Coffee
Here, we ordered a Spanish latte (iced) and a hot latte. We didn’t do much after, so we enjoyed them in the comfort of our hotel room.

Bar - Booze & Brews
We were actually very full from breakfast and unknowingly skipped lunch (not something we normally do). So, we headed down to a bar that Erin had spotted the day before. There, we were greeted by some amazing staff and enjoyed what the server last had:
A peanut butter sour cocktail and another refreshing spritz-style cocktail.

Restaurant - 8 Cuts Burger
Meal - Dinner
We were actually going to go to CROSTA Pizza, but when we got there, it was mostly take-out only. So, we decided to go to another restaurant we had pinned on our map, which was right across the road. There, we (for the last time) ordered what our server last had.

This was not only amazing to film, but it was also really fun to do. We got to taste so much food and drink we normally wouldn’t have thought to order ourselves. We recommend you give it a try

title: Visiting Aristocrat For Sisig! #philippines #travel #filipino
description:
Filipino food is amazing, and Manila is a great place to eat it, with so many choices due to the vast number of restaurants. However, trying to find the best place can be tough. In this video, we are on the hunt for the best Sisig in Manila!

After a bit of research on Google and asking a few locals where their favorite place to eat Sisig was, we narrowed it down to the infamous “Aristocrat” Restaurant. It offers a blend of traditional and contemporary Filipino cuisine in an elegant setting. Known for dishes like lechon and adobo, it emphasizes quality and flavor. It's a popular choice for both casual dining and special occasions, celebrating local ingredients and culinary heritage.

We walked through the bustling streets of Makati at night to get to our nearest Aristocrat restaurant branch. Upon arrival, we were greeted by a friendly security guard and staff who showed us to our table.

Sisig is a popular Filipino dish made primarily from chopped, seasoned, and grilled or fried pork, often using the pig’s head and sometimes including the liver. The meat is typically crisped up and then mixed with onions, chili peppers, and a tangy sauce made from vinegar, calamansi (a citrus fruit), and sometimes soy sauce. The dish is often served sizzling on a hot plate, giving it a smoky aroma. It’s typically enjoyed as a pulutan (a snack or appetizer with drinks) but can also be eaten with rice as a main dish. The combination of savory, sour, and spicy flavors makes sisig a beloved and flavorful staple in Filipino cuisine.

We had a good feeling about this place. It was a chain, and we do try to avoid chains as much as possible while traveling, but it seemed wholesome.

We ordered one plate of Sisig, two garlic rice, and some Calamansi tea (Calamansi is a small citrus fruit popular in Filipino cuisine and beverages).

It tasted amazing—the pork was crispy in places, and the plate was sizzling. It was one of Jason’s favorite experiences with Sisig. It was a little expensive, but that was to be expected since we were in Makati and it was a chain restaurant.

On our way home, we found just enough room in our stomachs to try some Sisig from a street food vendor. This was only ₱85. Jason didn’t like this one as much as Erin did, though. It was three times cheaper than Aristocrat, so if you don’t mind sacrificing a bit on taste, you might enjoy this one just as much.

description:
We set ourselves the challenge of ONLY eating street food for 24 hours in Manila, just for fun—and we didn’t expect it to open our minds (and taste buds!) to such an incredible variety of flavours. Some of the tastiest food we've had in the Philippines came from street vendors, and we discovered just how safe and delicious it can be. Many tourists are wary of street food, associating it with food poisoning or poor hygiene, but we’re here to debunk that myth. In fact, you’re just as likely to get food poisoning from eating in a restaurant, and by avoiding street food, you’re missing out on so many budget-friendly, mouth-watering options.

We started the day at Salcedo Morning Market (we filmed a separate video on this market, so make sure to check that out too!), where we sampled a fantastic range of both Filipino and international foods. The weekend vibe was amazing, and we tried Hungarian sausage, empanadas, Filipino favourite chorizo pudpud, and fresh fruit juices. By mid-afternoon, we were still full, so we decided to find a light lunch or snack.

On the streets, we came across a stall serving cheesy bibingka, a delicious Filipino delicacy freshly cooked on coals. It was the perfect snack! We also grabbed some chilli and garlic peanuts to nibble on.

For dinner, we enjoyed a sizzling feast of pork skewers, another Hungarian sausage in a bun, and a Mexican birria taco—crispy and filled with marinated meat. As we sat on the street chatting about our love for street food, we got the chance to interact with some locals who were also grabbing their evening meals.

To finish our 24-hour street food adventure, we headed to Legazpi Sunday Market in Makati, where we had a final round of pork sisig, Korean dumplings, and sticky orange chicken with rice—all for a very reasonable price.

We absolutely loved doing this challenge, and it has definitely made us eager to try more! If you’ve made it this far, let us know in the comments what other food challenges you'd like us to take on. We’re ready for the next one!

title: BRITS vs Halo Halo, Did We Fail Again?🇵🇭
tags: The Philippines|Philippines|filipino|filipino vlog|philippines Vlog|Travel vlog|travel vlog philippines|British Vloggers In The Philippines|Backpacker|Backpacker in The Philippines|Travel Vlog South East Asia|South East Asia Travel Videos|Travel Videos|Backpacking Vlog|Travel|Is the Philippines safe|holiday|bloggers in the philippines|vloggers in the philippines|filipino food|filipino food vlog|filipino foodie|foodie|halo halo|filipino sweet treats
description:
Halo-halo is a popular Filipino dessert made from a mix of shaved ice, sweetened fruits (like jackfruit and banana), jellies, and beans, topped with leche flan, purple yam (ube), and a scoop of ice cream. It's a refreshing, colorful treat perfect for hot weather and festive occasions.

When we first came to the Philippines in 2024, we wanted to try this dessert, not only because everyone we spoke to said that we had to try it, but mainly because it sounded so crazy and different from the desserts we have back in the UK (the closest thing we could think of was a "Knickerbocker Glory." If you don't know what that is, just give it a Google, haha).
When we tried Halo Halo for the first time, we didn’t realize it, but we made a huge mistake… we forgot to mix the ingredients together and instead ate it layer by layer. For those of you who don’t know (like we didn’t), Halo Halo means "Mix Mix," so when we forgot to mix the ingredients, it was pretty funny for anyone watching who knew what we were doing wrong.
This is our first time in the Philippines, and we’re going to redeem ourselves. It was a hot day in Manila, and we could hear Halo Halo calling our names. It was the middle of the day, we skipped lunch, and went straight to dessert (it’s great being an adult).
As soon as the dish hit the table, we mixed that baby up and dug in. It was so much better than the first time we had it… probably because we mixed it!

description:
We’re in Tagaytay, located just a few hours from Manila. It’s a top travel destination in the Philippines, known for its cool climate, stunning views of Taal Volcano, and diverse dining options. It's a perfect spot for nature lovers, foodies, and those seeking a relaxing escape from the city hustle. Although we are here for all of the above, the main reason is Bulalo! 

Bulalo is a traditional Filipino beef stew made with tender beef shank, bone marrow, and a variety of vegetables such as corn, potatoes, and cabbage. Known for its rich, flavourful broth, it's a comforting dish often enjoyed on cold days or during family gatherings—perfect for those craving hearty, savoury comfort food. And we’ve been told, “If you go to Tagaytay, you have to have it!”

We arrived in the town after taking the local morning bus from Manila, and we quickly stretched our legs before hopping on a jeepney. We headed in the direction of the restaurant we had found, called “Bulalo Point,” which had some great reviews on Google.

We struggled with the menu slightly because we were unsure whether we needed to order one Bulalo each, but the staff told us that one bowl would serve 2-3 people.

It was honestly one of the best meals we had eaten in the Philippines. Even writing about it now, a few days later, is making our mouths water. We will definitely have it again, and if you haven’t tried it, you know what to do!

description:
During our first visit to the Philippines in May 2024, we were fascinated by the large steel buses we saw everywhere (we later found out they were called "jeepneys").

Now that we know what they are, for those of you who don't, a jeepney is a colorful and iconic Filipino public transport vehicle, known for its unique design and vibrant artwork. It's a cost-effective, open-air ride that can carry many passengers, often customized with local flair. Popular in the Philippines, jeepneys are a symbol of the country’s culture and heritage. One afternoon in Manila, with not much to do, we decided that today would be the day to finally hop on a jeepney. We stood around for a while, almost stalling. There was something intimidating about stepping into the unknown—we had no idea how it worked, where it went, or the cost.
When we finally plucked up the courage, we were greeted by smiling Filipino faces who were more than happy to help and even taught us the phrase “bayad po.”

If you’re ever in the Philippines, we highly recommend using this mode of transport. It costs only ₱13 and moves through traffic at the same speed as a Grab.

description:
Manila has almost become like a second home to us while traveling. The city has so many different parts: culture, crazy traffic, great food, high-rise buildings that tower over small, low-rise yet built-up communities, shopping malls, street food—you name it, and Manila has not only got it but they’ve got the best of it.

We’ve grown to love this city for many reasons. We’ve found our favorite spots and have started to return to them time and again, like our favorite breakfast spot, Kanto Freestyle, where we enjoyed some amazing spam and corned beef silog.

I (Jason) had to find a good place to get my haircut now that we’ve been in Manila for a while. When we return in the future, I’ll have a good barber to come back to. I found somewhere online that looked pretty cool and had great reviews. It was a little more expensive compared to other barbershops I had seen, but being a barber myself back in the UK, I don’t mind paying a bit more because I know where that extra money goes. Some people think, “A haircut is just a haircut” and ask, “Why pay more when you can get it for less?” But I know that more money usually means more experience. In the barbering world, unless you own your own shop, there tends to be very little room for development or moving up in management like in other industries. What you can do is work at a shop that pays its staff more, but that usually means they charge more for their haircuts, which in turn reflects higher standards of work. I know this seems obvious, but not everyone understands it... Anyway, I’m rambling.

The place I found did an amazing haircut for ₱350, and it was in a really friendly neighborhood of Manila. When we had a chance to walk around afterward, we were greeted with friendly faces and the famous Filipino hospitality.

description:
Are you ready for the ultimate Jollibee challenge? In this vlog, we take on a Jollibee 24-hour fast food challenge, where we eat nothing but Jollibee for an entire day! From breakfast to dinner, we'll be indulging in all of Jollibee's iconic menu items to see if we can survive a full day of Filipino fast food goodness.

Jollibee is the Philippines' most beloved fast food chain, renowned for its unique fusion of American fast food and Filipino flavors. Whether you're craving crispy fried chicken, sweet spaghetti, or juicy burgers, Jollibee offers a wide variety of delicious dishes that cater to all tastes.

We headed down Makati Avenue bright and early, making sure we were there before the breakfast menu ended at 10am. Jason went for the very traditional Filipino breakfast, fernsileg, while Erin opted for pancakes and maple syrup. We both enjoyed breakfast and were feeling positive about the day ahead.

As lunchtime rolled around, we went back to the Makati Avenue store and ordered our lunch. Jason had wanted to try the Aloha Burger for a long time, ever since he first saw it on the menu months ago. However, it was always out of stock when he went to try it. FINALLY, the stars aligned, and on a beautiful sunny day, he got to try the Aloha Burger.

It was one of our favorite things we've tried from Jellibee and tasted very similar to burgers from McDonald's. Erin went for the Chicken Crunch Burger and fries, which wasn't her favorite, especially compared to the Aloha Burger! We also got some chicken nuggets, purely because we wanted to try the ranch dip-something else that was always out of stock when we visited Jollibee.

The day flew by, and by the time we were ready for dinner, it was pretty late, and neither of us felt like venturing out to the Jollibee store. Luckily, Grab saved the day, and we ordered dinner through the app. Jason chose the Burger Steaks with rice and gravy, one of Jollikee's most famous menu items, while Erin went for her all-time favorite, Jollibee Spaghetti.

We both felt slightly sluggish after a full day of eating fast food, but the wide variety on the Jollibee menu made it a fairly easy challenge, and neither of us got bored with the options.

From breakfast to dinner, we'll be indulging in all of Jollibee's iconic menu items to see if we can survive a full day of Filipino fast food goodness.

Jollibee is the Philippines' most beloved fast food chain, renowned for its unique fusion of American fast food and Filipino flavors. Whether you're craving crispy fried chicken, sweet spaghetti, or juicy burgers, Jollibee offers a wide variety of delicious dishes that cater to all tastes.

We headed down Makati Avenue bright and early, making sure we were there before the breakfast menu ended at 10am. Jason went for the very traditional Filipino breakfast, fernsileg, while Erin opted for pancakes and maple syrup. We both enjoyed breakfast and were feeling positive about the day ahead.

As lunchtime rolled around, we went back to the Makati Avenue store and ordered our lunch. Jason had wanted to try the Aloha Burger for a long time, ever since he first saw it on the menu months ago. However, it was always out of stock when he went to try it. FINALLY, the stars aligned, and on a beautiful sunny day, he got to try the Aloha Burger.

It was one of our favorite things we've tried from Jellibee and tasted very similar to burgers from McDonald's. Erin went for the Chicken Crunch Burger and fries, which wasn't her favorite, especially compared to the Aloha Burger! We also got some chicken nuggets, purely because we wanted to try the ranch dip-something else that was always out of stock when we visited Jollibee.

The day flew by, and by the time we were ready for dinner, it was pretty late, and neither of us felt like venturing out to the Jollibee store. Luckily, Grab saved the day, and we ordered dinner through the app. Jason chose the Burger Steaks with rice and gravy, one of Jollikee's most famous menu items, while Erin went for her all-time favorite, Jollibee Spaghetti.

We both felt slightly sluggish after a full day of eating fast food, but the wide variety on the Jollibee menu made it a fairly easy challenge, and neither of us got bored with the options.
