description:
Tsukiji Fish Market is high on most tourists itineraries when visiting Tokyo, Japan. Before 2018, it was the largest seafood market in the world! In more recent times, it is more of a tourist attraction hotspot than an authentic fish market so we discuss whether we think it is still worth visiting or one to miss, along with the cost of the street food. 

We got ourselves a matcha latte before tasting some grilled tuna skewers with wasabi, despite it being so early in the morning! We paid 500 yen for one skewer which seemed pretty expensive compared to other places in Japan where we have tried fresh tuna. We then tried Japanese omelette skewers which were really sweet but not our favourite, it has a really distinct taste! 

We had a look at some of the fresh (and alive!) seafood they had for sale but it was definitely more aimed at tourist consumption and the prices reflected this so we decided to move onto somewhere a bit more backpacker budget friendly. 

Thank you for watching and please like this video and subscribe to our channel if you enjoyed it!

title: Do This Ride LAST At TOKYO DISNEYLAND! #tokyo #disneyland #beautyandthebeast #japan #japanese
tags: disneyland|disney|disney tokyo|disneyland tokyo|tokyo disney|tokyo disneyland|rides at tokyo disneyland|beauty and the beast ride|beauty and the beast|best rides tokyo disneyland|tokyo disneyland hacks|disney hacks|disneyland hacks|tokyo disneyland rides|best rides at tokyo disneyland|disneyworld|disney vlog|disney vlogger|travel vlog|japan vlog|tokyo vlog|disneyland in japan|disneyland in tokyo|beauty and the beast disney|disney vlog japan|travel
description:
We got to Tokyo Disneyland in Japan at 8.30am as the park opens at 9am. We headed straight to the Baymax Happy Ride which was our FAVOURITE and we were so shocked by how many people were on the side dancing to all Baymax's tunes! We hopped on the Star Tours ride before sorting out all of our fast passes and giving you a few tips and hacks on how to get free fast passes and skip all the queues. We managed to do 3 rides each with free fast passes saving us so much time! 

We walked through Cinderella's beautiful castle to the It's a Small World ride as our lunch settled (check out our previous video for EVERYTHING we ate at Disneyland, it will make you hungry!). We looked round the shops and were tempted by all the Baymax and Winnie the Pooh merch. We went on the Monsters Inc ride, Space Mountain (one of our favourites!) and Toy Story Mania in Tomorrowland where Jason absolutely smashed it and beat me by a mile. 

We got front row spaces for the Baymax Cooling Parade where we got absolutely SOAKED whilst dancing to the Happy Ride songs and cooling off in the hot Tokyo heat. We did some of the smaller rides in Adventureland and then queued up for Splash Mountain, our longest wait of the whole day but it was so worth it to get wet and cool down! 

We used our fast passes for the Winnie the Pooh ride  Pooh's Honey Hunt in Fantasyland before getting front row seats for the incredible night parade where we saw Mickey Mouse, the Disney princesses, Toy Story characters and more. On our way out of the park, we managed to get in the queue for the parks NEWEST RIDE Beauty and the Beast and we are so glad we did as it was absolutely incredible and the castle was beautiful, it just had such a long queue all day and you can't get free fast passes for this one. 

We had the BEST day at Tokyo Disneyland and hope you loved the video! If you did, please remember to like it and subscribe to our channel for more.

description:
We ate so much food at Tokyo Disneyland so we had to make a separate video as the food is completely different to any Disneyland we have been to before and we wanted to try it all! 

We started by heading to Center Street Coffeehouse to try out the famous Baymax curry - spicy beef and butter chicken with Baymax shaped rice separating the two. We also tried the Mickey tomato and seafood soup to start which was really tasty.

We then went to Pan Galactic Pizza Port and grabbed a cheese and salami pizza which was pretty good for a theme park pizza. Of course we HAD to try the Toy Story Alien Mochi balls which come in three flavours - custard, strawberry and chocolate and they tasted AMAZING, the perfect sweet snack and super affordable too. Whilst waiting for the Baymax parade, we swung by a popcorn stall to try the delicious caramel popcorn. We had no idea how big popcorn is at Disneyland Tokyo but we can see why!

For our dinner we tried the ginger, pork and egg Baymax burger with french fries and Mickey shaped nuggets from Tomorrowland Terrace! The burger was absolutely amazing and the fact that it's Baymax made it even better! Jason isn't a huge fan of ginger but it was subtle enough for him not to mind. 

We tried to find the Mickey bao glove but either they've stopped serving it or it was closed on the day we visited as we couldn't find it anywhere! So we had a quick look round the bakery, confectionary store and bought some Winnie the Pooh madeleines which were honey flavoured and a perfect snack to end the day. The food at Tokyo Disneyland was surprisingly affordable and equally delicious. Our favourites were definitely all the Baymax themed items!

description:

The next morning, the first stop was a coffee shop as we were both very tired from a few fast weeks of travel but the coffee perked us up and the okonomiyaki muffin was the strangest thing we ate in Japan! With new found energy, we sought out GiGo the MEGA games arcade (rebranded from Sega) in the Akihabara area. We had fun playing Mario Kart, Pac-Man and retro games we grew up with before we stopped off for some ramen and gyoza. 

The Uniqlo 12 floor flagship store was incredible so we had a quick shop before checking out 'Piss Alley' in the Shinjuku area, also known as Omoide Yokocho. Streets of small bars reminiscent of the good old days serving beers and meat skewers, definitely a place to add to your travel itinerary. 

We ended the vlog by visiting Tokyo's oldest bakery Ginza Kimuraya to test out their melon bread which was tasted so good, we've been thinking about it ever since! We then went back to the Shibuya crossing to view it from above and we share a budget friendly (free!) way of observing this iconic sight.

description:
Osaka is famously known as Japan's Kitchen so trying good food was top of our itinerary. We visited Izakaya Toyo, home to a hilarious flamethrower chef who cooks the most delicious tuna with a blowtorch. This stand-up street food restaurant featured on Netflix's hit documentary so he has gained a huge amount of global attention and his story is so beautiful, it is really worth the watch. 

Despite the popularity, we easily got a table and were able to sample all of his culinary delights whilst watching Toyo get to work with his blowtorch, indestructible hands and a cigarette hanging from his mouth. An izakaya in Japan is an establishment that serves alcohol and snacks so despite the boiling hot weather, we of course we had to indulge in a few beers and lemon sours alongside the freshest fatty tuna, lean tuna, broiled tuna, sushi and sashimi. We had the best afternoon trying all the seafood, drinking beers and getting to know the locals - we even learnt a few new Japanese words!

description:
A must-do for any Hiroshima itinerary has got to be trying Okonomiyaki, a Japanese savory pancake that’s a true local specialty. Packed with flavor and layers of goodness, Hiroshima-style Okonomiyaki includes noodles, fried egg, pork belly, cabbage, and a rich savory sauce that ties everything together. If you’re a food lover, this dish is an absolute must!

In this video, we visit the iconic Okonomi-mura (literally "Okonomiyaki Village"), a 7-story building in Hiroshima filled with 23 different Okonomiyaki restaurants, each serving up their own unique take on the famous dish. With so many choices, we had no idea which restaurant to pick! So, we decided to choose a spot based on the number of customers already seated—always a good sign when you’re looking for the best food, right?

We were not disappointed! The Okonomiyaki was absolutely incredible. From the perfectly crispy bottom to the mouth-watering layers of noodles, pork belly, and egg, every bite was better than the last. It was so good, in fact, that we went back the very next day for seconds! Hiroshima’s Okonomiyaki lived up to the hype and then some.

Whether you're a first-time visitor or a seasoned traveler, Hiroshima’s Okonomiyaki is an experience you won’t want to miss. If you're planning a trip to Japan, be sure to add Okonomi-mura to your itinerary. It's a foodie paradise!

We then headed down to Haeundae to ride the beach train and take in all the breathtaking views of the coast. After that, we headed high up in the sky at Busan X The Sky to see Busan and the beach from the 100th floor and even braved walking on the glass floor! 

On Day 2, we were up early to experience the cable car in Songdo, Korea's first ever cable car! A big bonus of arriving for opening is that we had our very own cable car, something you usually have to pay extra for. Another good activity for those rainy days is MUSEUM 1. Although not our favourite thing we did, it's nice to wander round and get out of the bad weather! We rounded up the day with a visit to Club D Oasis Spa and couldn't believe that this was included in the price of the 48 hour pass. It was our first experience of a Korean spa so certain elements definitely shocked us but it was nice to relax after cramming in all of the above in just 48 hours!

description:
Travelling down South Korea, we arrived in Suncheon and after a few drinks at a local brewery, decided to try Korean BBQ for the very first time. We had no idea what anything cost, what to do or what to eat but these very kind strangers helped us straight away, getting us beer and showing us how to cook the meat. 

We ended up chatting to them for a while and they bought us two Korean dishes to try - cold noodles (apparently a summer staple in Korea!) and kimchi strew. We drank more, chatted more and nearly ended up at karaoke! When we went to pay the bill, we found out that not only did they guide us through the dining experience but also surprised us by generously paying for the entire bill. 

This vlog shows the power of human connection and the beauty of unexpected acts of kindness. If you liked it, please remember to like the video and subscribe to the channel, it really helps us out. See you in the next one ✌🏼

description:
Visiting the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) of South Korea felt like a ‘must do’ when in Seoul to learn about the history of Korea, the war and the struggles people still face. And with hundreds of trips being advertised daily, it’s not hard to find yourself a bus to hop onto to partake in this day trip. In this video, we show you what it’s like to visit one of the most heavily militarized borders in the world, spanning 160 miles long. We were also allowed to use binoculars to look across the DMZ strip into North Korea and could even see people walking in the fields. It was a surreal experience to see this border that was established 71 years ago and to learn how things have changed since then. 
Thank you for watching our video! Please comment, like and subscribe for more 😄🇰🇷

title: How To See Tarsiers in Bohol! #bohol #philippines #tarsier #filipino #cordelia #travelshorts #monkey
tags: Philippines|Filipino|Bohol|Bohol Philippines|Philippines travel|Philippines travel vlog|Philippines travel vlog 2024|Filipino vlog|Filipino travel vlog|Filipino vlogger|Backpacking Philippines|Tarsier|Tarsier sanctuary Bohol|Philippine tarsier|Things to do Bohol|Must do Bohol|Panglao|Panglao things to do|Philippines travelling|Bohol itinerary|Bohol travel itinerary
description:
We rented a motorbike from a lovely lady in Panglao for 400 pesos (£5.35 GBP) and headed across the bridge to Bohol to see how much we could see in one day! We started with the attraction furthest away from Panglao - The Chocolate Hills. It took us about 2 hours to reach the main viewpoint for the chocolate hills as we navigated the twisty, broken roads up the mountains. We also passed the man made forest along the way so slowed down for the hundreds of people in the road taking selfies! We were so happy to visit this fascinating geological formation and lucky that half the mounds still had their chocolate brown colour and had not yet turned green. 
We then drove back down to Corella to visit the Philippine Tarsier Sanctuary, a non profit sanctuary saving the world’s smallest primate the Philippine Tarsier. It was only 150 pesos (£2 GBP) to have a tour round the sanctuary and we were lucky enough to see 3 tarsiers in their sanctuary, and one that was pregnant! 
Our day ended at the Hinagdanan Cave back in Panglao where it was too late in the day to swim in the cave but we enjoyed the cool temperature and watching other people swim! 
We loved exploring Bohol by motorbikes as it gave us the flexibility and freedom to spend as much or as little time at each place that we wanted.

description:
Moalboal in Cebu, Philippines is most well known for snorkelling or diving to see the famous sardine run at Panagsama Beach. Although you can see the sardines (and other marine life!) if you snorkel, we found that diving was a better option as you can swim amongst and underneath the sardines instead of just seeing them from the surface. 
The dive was absolutely beautiful as there is a stunning reef drop just meters from the shore and even though the visibility wasn’t that great on the day we did the dive, we still saw thousands of sardines and a few nudibranch and sea snakes. 
Diving in Moalboal is also pretty budget friendly and we were really impressed with the dive centre we chose for friendliness, cost and safety. 
Moalboal is a great place to travel too as there are so many options for accommodation, coffee shops and restaurants. We loved it!

We spent our days in the sea spotting the famous thresher sharks, laying on the beach, trying delicious Filipino food and playing with the cutest puppies.

Malapascua, Philippines, is a hidden paradise known for its stunning white-sand beaches, crystal-clear waters, and vibrant marine life. Famous for thresher shark diving 🦈, it’s a must-visit for adventure seekers. Enjoy swimming with friendly dogs, breathtaking drone shots, and exploring hidden spots. The island's welcoming locals and serene atmosphere make it perfect for relaxation and exploration.

We were blown away with how friendly everyone on this island was. We felt so safe and loved - same as everywhere we have visited in the Philippines! Some amazing children stopped us from getting lost and directed us to the hidden lighthouse on the north side of the island on our first day which made us feel so welcome straight away. We enjoyed the north beach and finding hidden coves along the coast line. 

Although Malapascua is fairly difficult to get to (5 hour minivan from Cebu City and then a 45 minute ferry from Maya port), it’s definitely worth the trip if you’re looking for somewhere a bit quieter to spend your days relaxing and exploring such a beautiful island. It was one of our favourite destinations whilst island hopping in the Philippines and we definitely recommend adding it to your Philippines travel itinerary!

We spent 5 nights in Malapascua and we fell in love with the natural, unspoilt, magical charm of the island. Although not much infrastructure and limited roads on the island, it’s easy to get around and explore. We spent our days in the sea, laying on the beach, trying delicious Filipino food and playing with the cutest puppies.
We were blown away with how friendly everyone on this island was. We felt so safe and loved - same as everywhere we have visited in the Philippines! Some amazing children stopped us from getting lost and directed us to the hidden lighthouse on the north side of the island on our first day which made us feel so welcome straight away. We enjoyed the north beach and finding hidden coves along the coast line. 
Although Malapascua is fairly difficult to get to (5 hour minivan from Cebu City and then a 45 minute ferry from Maya port), it’s definitely worth the trip if you’re looking for somewhere a bit quieter to spend your days relaxing and exploring such a beautiful island.

title: Holding RATS That Can Locate LANDMINES in Cambodia ?! 🐀🇰🇭 #travelshorts #cambodia #siemreap #rats
tags: Cambodia|Cambodia 2024|Cambodia travel vlog|Siem reap travel vlog|Siem reap travel itinerary|Cambodia travel itinerary|Backpacking Cambodia video|Rats in Cambodia|APOPO rats Cambodia|Hero rats|Landmine disposal rats|Landmines rats Cambodia|Giant African pouch rats|Things to do in siem reap|Things to see in Cambodia|Landmines in Cambodia|Siem reap things to do|Siem reap itinerary 2024|Siem reap vlog 2024
description:
We visited APOPO in Siem Reap Cambodia where African Giant Pouched Rats have been trained to detect landmines in the ground, helping to clear explosives leftover from the many wars Cambodia has suffered. Left in the ground, these landmines are causing a huge number of fatalities and injuries across Cambodia. These rats sniff out the landmines as they can detect TNT, scratch on the surface to alert their trainer and the landmines can then be carefully removed. One HeroRAT can search an area the size of a tennis court in 30 minutes which would take humans days and at a much higher cost! We were able to watch a demonstration showing how these rats detect landmines and were even able to hold one afterwards! This is definitely a must do if you are visiting Siem Reap 🐀 🇰🇭 

APOPO - https://apopo.org/

description:
We crossed the border from Laos into Cambodia and had been warned about the scams that can take place at both immigration offices (by officials). Admittedly, we didn’t have the right cash but even if we did, they were asking for more and were charging everybody a minimum of $38 dollars which is significantly more than the price advertised online. We had to pay $5 for a departure card leaving Laos as we had no idea we had to keep hold of these. After paying this fee, we were waved through and still not given a departure card to fill out. We ended up paying $87 for 2 Cambodian visas when the cost should have been approximately $70.

title: Kayaking with NEAR EXTINCT IRRAWADDY DOLPHIN!🐬 #travelshorts #dolphin #irrawaddydolphin #cambodia
tags: Near extinct animal|Extinct animal|Irrawaddy dolphin|Near extinct dolphin|Rare dolphin species|Wildlife encounter|Where to see Irrawaddy dolphins|Cambodia travel itinerary|Travel shorts|Rare wildlife encounter|Incredible dolphin jump|Dolphins in the wild|Kratie Cambodia|What to do in Cambodia|Should I visit Cambodia|Rare dolphin|Unseen before animal|South east Asia travel|Cambodia travel vlog|Backpacking Cambodia vlog
description: We were so incredibly FORTUNATE to spend time with the nearly extinct, elusive and struggling population of the Irrawaddy dolphins in Kratié, Cambodia. These dolphins are now extinct in most of the places they used to thrive, including Laos, and the last place you can see them today is in the Mekong River that runs through the village of Kampi, just north of Kratie. The dolphins have been driven to near extinction by by catch fishing and fishing net entanglement and although there are many laws in place now to protect them, they are still a tiny population and will struggle to fight extinction. We saw the dolphins from a kayak so no boat engines were used 🐬

Scattered across the hills are hundreds of massive stone jars, some believed to be over 2,000 years old. But who built them… and why?

Historians and archaeologists still debate their true purpose. Were they ancient burial sites? Part of complex funeral rituals? Or something else entirely? Local legends even say the jars were once used by giants to brew rice wine after a great victory.

Is it worth the trip? And what do you think these mysterious jars were used for?

In this video, and on our last full day in Vietnam, we go to Ninh Binh! About a 2 hour drive from central Hanoi, it's a beautiful area famous for its "earthly acne" type landscape with limestone mountains and a lot of grottos. We went on a 3 hour boat tour in Trang An that was being paddled by a Vietnamese lady who was very strong! Luckily there were paddles on board so we could help out as well. We stopped at a couple temples and went through 3 grottos, of which 1 was over a kilometer long! An epic day in Ninh Binh. We later also hiked up to a viewpoint to see the mountains at Tam Coc which is a bit more famous for this type of boat tour, but Trang An was a bit more relaxed. Then we drove back and ate Bun Rieu in Hanoi!

description:
This is a bit of a different video, and it's definitely NOT for the weak-stomached! In this video, I show the video coverage I did from Cap Goh Meh festival, also known as Tatung, in Singkawang, West Borneo, Indonesia. It's a festival that has its roots in Chinese culture as well as local tribal traditions. Under loud drums and smells of Chinese incents, people get into a certain "trance" in which they can stick needles or knives in their faces, necks, cheeks etc, without seeing any blood. I don't have a scientific explanation for it, my girlfriend explains it like "a ghost will enter the body" and then they can perform these things.

It was definitely very interesting to experience this and see the over 1000 people performing this in this parade. But yes this video is definitely not for people who are sensitive to graphic imagery or spiritual disturbing footage!

title: Stuck in a WATERFALL! Hiking the Most BEAUTIFUL HIKE of Taiwan! The Golden Grotto Trail!
tags: TravelingTice|East Taiwan|Hualien|Golden Grotto Trail|Trailhiking|Waterhiking|Waterrafting|Water adventure|River hike|Canyon hike|Waterfalls|Waterfall hike|Climb waterfall|Taiwan|Eastcoast Taiwan|Travel Vlog|Taiwan Travel|Travel Taiwan|Taiwan nature|花蓮
description:
On this day I do the most epic hike I ever did in my life. I had a full day in Hualien and from a contact back home I heard about this hike called the "Golden Grotto Hike". I cycled there, passing by some military places which felt a bit weird as I was cycling here during the Pelosi visit. After buying a waterproof bag (I didn't have one, terrible preparation) I started hiking. At first there was a path, but soon it disappeared and I had to start following the river by climbing, swimming and wading through the water. It was an absolute thrill! At some point the river came to a crosspoint where I had to climb up rocks to end up in a canyon type place. There it was proper climbing rocks and climbing through waterfalls! At some point I was stuck, but I knew I was almost at the end, and luckily I saw an alternative way to get up. So in the end I got up to another level where there was another waterfall.... and did I get up that one? You'll have to watch the video for that! All in all, a really epic day in Hualien!

description:
In this vlog, I start the longest part of my bike tour through Taiwan: the Eastcoast. I left from Taipei, after a quick visit to the enormous tower of Taipei 101. After this I cycled to the eastern coastline and followed it along. I had a very long day planned, over 130 kilometers, but it wasn't going as smooth as I wanted. At some point I hit a small town where I met a lady who dives for rockweed. It's a kind of seaweed and then she makes pudding out of it, which I tasted, and which was really good! Then I kept cycling, found some pizza and chicken as well, had a nice sunset ride, and then cycled for a bit into the night. It was getting late so I decided to take a train for the last stretch to my small apartment I had for the night in the town of Suao.

description:
In this mega episode, we go back in time to the summer of 2021. The world was still in the grips with the pandemic but my urge for travel couldn't be stopped, so I rented a car and made an epic 1.5 week road trip through Europe, visiting various places in Belgium, France, Switzerland and Luxembourg. The highlight of the trip was for sure the epic 3 days I spent in the town of Grindelwald in Switzerland. I did awesome mountain biking there on an electric mountain bike, as well as lots of hiking through the beautiful mountains. Visiting various places like Gletscherschlucht (Glacier canyon), Cliff walk up on First mountain, taking a cable cart to Kleine Scheidegg, overlooking mount Eiger and walking down to the town of Wengen, from which I took a train back to Grindelwald.

I also visited other places, like the Belgian Ardennes, Geneva, Strasbourg and Luxembourg. So overall this was an epic trip through West-Central Europe and a great reminder that I loved travel after being at home for 1.5 years due to the pandemic. More travels to come!

description:
The video of me working as a digital nomad in Las Palmas 👉 https://youtu.be/amP0CVZJR5U

After an amazing trip and experience to the arctic, I still had a couple days left on my holiday, so I decided to take that time to go to a place much further south 😅 basically as far south as you could easily travel to as a European citizen in Covid time! After an easy 4.5 hour flight with Easyjet I landed in Las Palmas, Gran Canaria! The main island of the Canary islands, an island chain belonging to Spain but geographically located off the coast of Africa. The weather here in December is a nice 20 - 30 degrees, so it was definitely a welcome change after spending over a week in the Arctic! My plan is to relax on this holiday, as well as do remote work as I'll be working again for my company which is a 9 - 5 job, but it is possible for me to work remotely, so I took that opportunity to try that out from here!

title: Seeing the NORTHERN LIGHTS in Svalbard!!
tags: TravelingTice|travel vlogger|Northern Lights|Aurora Borealis|Svalbard|winter wonderland|arctic|Camp Barentz|whale meat|sauna|Longyearbyen|travel vlog|nature lovers|outdoor adventures|magical lights|night sky|camera footage|saami dinner|saami food|saami|Willem Barentz
description:
Check out my interactive map of the Svalbard trip 🗺️ 👉  https://view.mapmytours.app/8l9g3jgqqoosyuh7uvxuuayewu5yjkys?lat=78.221661&lng=15.635396&zoom=11

Create your own interactive map using my application Map My Tours 🗺️ 👉 https://mapmytours.app

Watch the video of me exploring Tromsø here 👉 https://youtu.be/gud9W2u-IgE

On my final full day in Svalbard I finally got to see the Northern Lights! The famous Aurora Borealis. I was so happy to have seen them in Svalbard, which at this point had become one my most blown away expectations type trip! I was just chilling in the hostel when suddenly people were starting to run outside and I heard the Auroras were out, so I ran outside with just my jacket on and camera in hand (it was -17C at the time) and ran to a darker spot so I could see the northern lights better. And it seemed like the light show just got started because they became bigger and bigger, until it was so clear to see with my own eyes it was so beautiful and magical seeing these lights dancing in the night sky.

After seeing the auroras, I got on my last activity for the trip which was a local dinner at Camp Barentz, named after the famous Dutch explorer who was the first person to lay his eyes on Svalbard. And after this I concluded the trip with some nice footage I shot on other days I was there, including some experiences that didn't make it into a vlog. For example eating whale meat with a hostel friend and jumping in the freezing sea water at the Longyearbyen harbor after a nice and warm sauna experience. At the end of the video I fly to Tromsø where I conclude the whole Svalbard trip from my hotel there and talk a little bit about how I want to do these videos going forward.

Join on this guided day bike tour on Svalbard! We did a bike tour during the brightest hours of the polar night of November in -19C weather. I got picked up from my hostel and we prepared the gear and bikes at the Hurtigruten Svalbard headquarters in the harbor area of town. Then we put some batteries in the electric mountain bikes (with spike tires) and got on our way. We cycled across the town of Longyearbyen to some famous and interesting sights in the town. First up a hill where you had a really good view of the town, then past a very interesting building which was used during the mining days. Then we continued on to the harbour and coastal area where we had a break for some tea and biscuits at a little hut. After this we made our way back to the Hurtigruten place.

Thank you Hurtigruten Svalbard for organising the bike tour. It's great fun!

description:

 Cycling Ukraine is very different from the rest of Europe. Highway is kind of dangerous, found some tracks of trucks going into the shoulder. Talking about the Ukrainian War, riding past a military training base where there were some posters about it. Dji Spark drone flying over sunflowers. Very bad Ukrainian roads. Diverged from the highway, to some backroads, which was a bad idea, because the hills became very steep and the roads very bad. I had to push my bike up some very steep hills to the point I was covered in sweat. Came across a horse as well. After another bad uphill I made it to my Airbnb apartment in center Lviv.

Josef from TheOneGoodRoad called me this morning and we talked for 2.5 hours, which threw my plans for the day a little off-guard. Unfortunately my plans fell completely through when I came across a sign which said that the road to the Primieval forest (Bialowieza) was closed. That forced me to ride around the forest and because of the fact that there was only 1 more road going in and out of the forest, I had to cycle the same 40 km twice, which I didn't want to do, I decided to skip the forest for now. I had a nice little hotel in a place called Hajnowka, where I met the cyclists I had seen yesterday again, which was quite funny. Also had some problems with ants eating my cherries.

Start the day in Nida, going to the Tourist Information center to ask if there is a ferry going to the mainland. Turns out there is one in the night, which means Sofie and I have one last full day together. We decided to spend it by taking a look at the Russian-Lithuanian border, then we went to the sand dunes and walked on the sand dunes, and rolled down the sand dunes, which was a lot of fun. We started the day at our campsite in Ventspils. Then we cycled out of town, but stumbled across a road that would turn into dirt, which was indicated by a sign. Also came across a running competition we had to pass by as well. Then we made our way south again. Dji Spark drone flying, had some issues. Eat some ice cream. Bad supermarkets in the middle of nowhere. Trying to find a wildcamping place, luckily we had a lot of light, so we weren't pressed to find a place. Made it to a place with a lot of flies, but it was ok! Shoutout to my multi-use buff, very good as a sleeping mask.

description:
*Sofie is not in the shot too often because she is not a fan of the cameras so much, if you were wondering ;)

So today we woke up on our incredible location along the beach. Probably the best campsite I've ever stayed at. Sofie is not so much of a morning person, so I had some time while she was still sleeping to explore the coast a little bit. There were some swans, a nice island and some great waters! Talked about the sun being up for so long. Then we went cycling towards Kolka. Loads of flies around me when cycling. Reached Kolka, which is the northernmost point I'll be at for a long time. From now on it is mainly going to be cycling south. Then we went to our campsite, talking about the heat and that it was really hot for Sofie. The tent was also a sauna. Took a little swim and at the end I did a little talk about the helmet with the mirror and that it works quite well.

It was a relaxed day because Sofie likes to sleep in and wanted to leave at around noon, which was ok for me because I still had to do laundry (which didn't happen unfortunately) and afterwards I went to Sofie's hostel and together we rode out of the city of Riga towards the coast. We had a good evening together and had some great chats. Afterwards it was time to go to bed.
Not much going on on this first day of cycling but it was a lot of fun!

description:
In this episode I visit Trakai Castle about 1 hour outside of Vilnius. My Airbnb host recommended me to go here, so I did. The castle is a beautiful orange Lithuanian castle, that originates from the Middle Ages. Because the walk from the train station to the castle was quite long and I saw a bike rental shop on the way, I decided to rent a bike for the day! First I took a look at the castle, which was quite beautiful but to get in, you had to pay 7 euros. I decided to keep my money and instead get off the beaten path for a bit. So I cycled a route around the castle to a nearby villa. I sat along the lake for a bit and afterwards I flew the DJI Spark drone, but it had some issues... So I didn't have too many drone shots but for the rest it was quite nice.

description:
This is a short one! I left the hostel in Berlin and went to the bus station to catch my bus to Warsaw, from which I would take another bus to Vilnius, Lithuania! On the bus station I saw Line, featured in some of BicycleTouringPro's videos and a good friend of him, so I said 'hi' and she seemed kind of amazed that some stranger knew who she was :) Afterwards I made it on the bus but the bus was having some technical issues in Poznan, Poland, which took 2.5 hours! I eventually arrived in Warsaw at 9:30 PM at night but was at the opposite part of town where my other bus would leave! So I had to take the city bus to the main bus station for Ecolines and I arrived there 7 minutes after my other bus was supposed to leave.. Somehow it was still there at the gate, the bus driver was about to get in and start driving, but he let me in for some reason! (I think the reason I was lucky is because a guy before me had an argument with the bus driver and actually wasn't allowed on it! I saw him walking away in anger, and the bus driver was shouting at him.. he kind of sacrificed himself for me!)

description:
Subscribe to Tim's channel: https://www.youtube.com/user/flujab999

Shoutout to TheCollegePicker: https://www.youtube.com/user/thecollegepicker

This vlog was kindof split into two parts: 1 Dutch King's Day 2 Meeting up with Tim Cooke. I showed some footage from April 27th when it was King's day in the Netherlands. It's a day full of orange and selling/buying at street markets or flee markets. We sold quite a bit of junk and made about 100 euros from this day, which isn't that bad! (I got another 45 euros from the donation box, thank you all who stopped by and donated, my grandma already donated 20 euros but still ;) I flew my DJI Spark drone around, got some cool shots. Also got quite a bit of the balloon thing, which was a plus because for some reason the video signal became very bad. Then we fast forwarded a week to meeting with Tim Cooke in Katwijk. He is riding around the Netherlands on a recumbent trike. A very relaxed tricycle, something I might want to look into for future tours. I let him try some Dutch herring, he liked it, which was good! Then we went to Noordwijk, had some croquets or whatever you call em in English. Then we went to the flower fields where unfortunately Tim lost his drone... He clicked on the RTH button but then it just flew off into the distance, never to be seen again. It was flying south, so if anyone in Belgium or France found a white drone, please lemme know! Or south of Holland of course.. Anyway we still had a good day despite the tragic loss.. He was actually glad I was there with him, because if he lost his drone himself he would have been sad for the whole trip. I tried to remain positive and in the end we had a terrific day.

title: 5 BIG WINS 2017! This was the BEST YEAR OF MY LIFE!!!
tags: TravelingTice|Travel (TV Genre)|Travel Documentary (TV Genre)|Documentary (TV Genre)|Cycle Sport (Sport)|Bicycle (Product Category)|travel vlogger|VLOG|Bicycle Touring|European Bike Tour|Bike Touring|Overcoming fears|Big wins|2017 reflection|2018|happy new year|this was the best year of my life|5 big wins|5 big wins of 2017|Q&A|website|plans|dreams
description:
If you want to support the tour, you can donate here: https://www.patreon.com/TravelingTice

In this video, I'm talking about the 5 big wins that I had in 2017. The first one is of course the European Bike Tour, my second ever bike tour and the first real successful one. I had done a bike tour before, riding for 4 days through Holland on a recumbent bike (link to those videos: http://bit.ly/2qgVzaD), but it wasn't really a success and I decided to ditch the recumbent bike. The thing just didn't work for me (I'll post another article for that one). I almost didn't want to go on this bike tour, but in the end I did it, and man, I'm glad I did!

The second win had to do with overcoming fears. After my first bike tour failure I was scared, very scared. I almost didn't want to go on the big bike tour anymore because I was so scared, because I thought I was gonna end up lonely and the camping idea was suddenly something terrifying, while I thought it was gonna be the best thing of the trip for 3 years... I spent my days watching Ted Talks about how to be positive and be happy and even started meditating.. but nothing helped! The only solution was to do this trip, and so I overcame my fears and now I feel more enthusiastic, confident and assured than ever before!

The third one is about YouTube. I started YouTube already very long ago, in 2010. But those videos were very different from my current ones. They were about domino! I loved setting up domino stones and toppling them, and I was pretty good at it, I sometimes had setups of 8000 stones! But I sold all those domino stones and at my height, I had 350 subscribers, which I thought was a lot! Now I have 1094 subscribers and it's still going up! On top of that, every time I upload a video, I get at least 7 comments all saying positive words about what I'm doing, which is a huge booster to me! If I didn't do the vlogs, I would've already quit probably after a few days.

The fourth win has to do with my school. This year I graduated high school! That happened in May and I remember I was working harder than I've ever done for school, but with result. Now I have the freedom to do whatever I want and I'm not obliged to go back to school anymore!

The last win is about planning. See, before this trip I really didn't know what my future would look like. There were a hundred possibilities and the plans were changing from day to day. Especially in my depressed period in June I even gave up on the idea of traveling and almost wanted to choose a study and stay home for the next years. Now I know exactly what I want. I want to travel to every single country in the world! And that might be ridiculous, but I now know it's the thing I want to go for, a dream I've kind of always had, it was just hidden under a set of fears. But now those are gone, I can finally start working towards that future, and of course I've got more plans, so stay tuned to hear more about my dreams and aspirations!

At the end I talk about 2 more things that I'm gonna do in 2018: I'm gonna work on my shyness with vlogging in the presence of other people. That is something I've noticed in the vlogs, that whenever I'm with other people, I back down and don't vlog as much anymore. I just have to remember that you guys are watching! It's not just a camera.
The other thing was about my website, where I'm busy working on making it better and better, which I'm doing right now!

description:
Started the day explaining why I didn't vlog yesterday. Was thinking about this Forever Living thing and if I want to continue with it. Cycled to the city center of Helsinki. Took a ferry to Suomen Linna, a big fortress off the coast of Helsinki. The fortress is placed on a couple of islands, and when I was on island E, there was pretty much no tourists and I could see some canons and abandoned fortress dungeons for myself! Then I went back to the main island where there was some more dungeons and little shafts and things to explore. Really recommended to go here if you go to Helsinki. Then I went back to the mainland and went to the Temppeliaukion kirkko, a church made into a rock, but it wasn't as spectacular as I thought and you had to pay 3 bucks to get in.. Then I cycled around the city a little more and visited the Torni Hotel. This hotel has a pretty high tower and I tried to get up to the top. After taking a few elevators I made it to the small top bar where there was a terrace with a pretty nice view over the city. End the day by deciding that I'm not gonna do this Forever Living thing. description:
Today was part 2 of the exploring of Stockholm by my mom and I. Got woken up by an alarm we bought but couldn't turn off... Afterwards we went to a few places including the Skansen Museum, which is an Open Air Museum where there are traditional Swedish houses and people with traditional Swedish clothing. There was also a small little zoo with exotic animals and a lot of native animals to Sweden and the places I rode my bicycle through. I also saw an exhibit of 2 spots I've been to on my route through Sweden, which was pretty nice. It was a very interesting experience. Afterwards we went to the Saluhal which was a hall full of small little bits of food sold by little shops. Then we headed back to our little suburb outside of the center to find a place to eat when the power went off... Everything was black and it was quite a scary moment, luckily I had bought a new headlamp. When the power was back on we went to a place where we ordered something we didn't know the name of, turned out to be quite good. Then we headed back to the Airbnb where me and my mom waved you goodbye.

Then I arrived in Oslo and was gonna take a bus at 11PM to Stockholm, but it turned out there was no way to get my bike on this bus. After a long downhill I finally made it to the city of Geilo where there were some Chinese tourists, I had a coffee and then went to my airbnb apartment where there was no one. So I decided to head back to town first and ask at a bike shop what the road conditions ahead. They said I'll be ok and that I don't need winter tires. description:
This day started out foggy and cold. I made my way towards Hamburg to stay at a hostel. I fly the drone and it has some errors again. On the way I unfortunately got a flat tire and had to fix it, which reminded me of the last time I fixed a flat and struggled at the last bit to the point I had to call a bike shop. This time that wasn’t really an option so I kept on trying and trying to get the tire back into the rim and I almost gave up… but in the end I found the strength and conquered this tire! I did it and I felt very proud. Then I made my way towards the city of Hamburg where I check into the hostel and explore the city in the evening. We Visited Boracay's Most Exclusive Beach
tags: travel|island hopping|boracay|puka beach
description:
Puka Beach is a serene destination in Boracay that boasts a white-sand shore that contains bits of coral. It is also known for its local name Yapak Beach. Over the years, this was known as Puka because Puka shells abound on the beach’s coarse white sand. Unlike other beaches on the island Puka is relatively undeveloped and pristine.

There are some stalls and restaurants on the beach that sell drinks, snacks, souvenirs, and coconuts. But if you plan to hang out here for the whole day, it’s smart to bring your own drinks and food. Aside from swimming, there’s really nothing much to do on Puka beach but to just relax on the sand (soft shells) while getting your much-desired tan.

We got there via boat tour, however a boat tour stop at Puka Beach will give you just enough time to walk the stretch, take photos, and swim a bit. So, it's NOT the best option if you want to  spend a longer time and relax on Puka Beach.

Take lots of pictures and don't forget your sunscreen as it doesn't have an abundant amount of natural shade. Enjoy your Puka beach adventure!

Pigeons can recognize words.

title: LASH LIFT EXPERIENCE + PROCESS | Jessica van heerden
tags: lash lift|lash perm|lashes|lash|lash curl|long lashes|lash lift process|lash perm process|get long curly lashes|jessica|jessica van heerden|jess
description:
Taking you through my lash lift experience and sharing with you the process of getting your lashes lifted or permed. 

•My lash lift was done by Adele at The Brow Spot ((082) 7776921): http://instagram.com/_thebrowspot

📍You can visit their salon here: https://www.google.co.za/search?q=the+brow+spot+fourways&ie=UTF-8&oe=UTF-8&hl=en-za&client=safari

👆🏻SUBSCRIBE to my channel if you like beauty videos like this: http://www.youtube.com/channel/UCIw7Fsv6FLIUAkpqEQUjQ6A?sub_confirmation=1

_______________________________________

THE WHOLE PROCESS 
•Adele used the elleebana one shot lash lift from Australia and belmacil tint.
•Procedure as follow.
•Cleanse the lashes using Belma-Remove non oily) tint and eye makeup remover.
•Gently position the correct size silicone rod on the upper eyelid.
•Place a small amount of glue on the back of the rod to keep the rod in place.
•Hold the rod for 5-10 seconds on the eyelid to ensure adhesion.
•Apply a strip of eyelash glue to the front of the silicone rod.
•Use the Elleebana Lash Lifter tool to gentley roll and place the lashes onto the silicone rod.
•Gently separate any lashes using the hook of the lash lifter and ensure correct lash placement.
•Be sure to adhere only the top lashes to the rod.
•Apply Lash lift lotion using application brush from the root of the lash to half way up the lash.  Do not coat the ends of the lashes.
•Let lift lotion process for 5-10 minutes (depending on the strength of the lashes).
•Remove the lift lotion with a damp cotton tip or eye pad. Take note to be gentle and not distrupt the lash position on the rods.
•Apply setting lotion using application brush, process for 5-7 minutes. 
•Remove the setting lotion with damp cotton pad. As well as all the glue on the lashes.
•Put the tint on for 10min.
•Clean off completely. 
•Lash lift will last btw 6-8 wks and can last as long as 12wks.
•Avoid wetting for 12hrs after the procedure. 
•No other maintenance except gorgeous lifted lashes.
•This works for short and long lashes.

title: Balayge & Strobing | HAIR TRANSFORMATION
tags: Ballayage|Hair transformation|Hair colouring|Brunette to blonde|Hair strobing|Virgin hair|Colouring virgin hair|Tanaz hair|Jessica van heerden|My hair process|Hair care routine|New hair
description:
Strobing the next big hair trend. 
 
Just when Balayage, Tortoiseshell, Pastels and Dip Dyes started feeling main stream we are evolving swiftly into another hot colouring trend – hair strobing aka hair contouring
 
Strobing started out as a make-up technique used to highlight features and illuminate the face and it does exactly the same for your hair. The technique is used on areas to be lifted by lighter shades that contrast with darker shades which give an overall effect of more depth and variation in a subtle way. Strobing allows stylists to truly individualize colour, highlighting and toning specific to each individuals hair colour, face shape and skin tone.
The technique creates focal points enhancing facial features, lighter shades are placed where light would naturally hit the face adding a glow to those areas, this draws attention to your best features, for example, lightening the hair around the temples, gives a lift to cheekbones and brightens the eyes. Strobing is similar to the Ballyage colour technique but has a natural gradual fade.
 
“Bespoke and tailored colour is an art, achieving your perfect colour is an evolution of shading technique which is why it is so important to create an individual path for each client. It is a process that is done with precision and follows an in-depth consultation.” Says Master Stylist Shelene Shaer, “the general rule is to use colour that is two shades darker or lighter than a clients' natural hair colour, creating a wave of light that makes your colour pop and gives locks a glossy highlighted look that frames your face.” 
The good news is that maintenance is less intensive with this hand painting colour method. It allows you to get away with longer periods between colour thanks to the use of wider strips of hair that are closer to your natural colour which results in a softer look which makes your regrowth more manageable.
Strobing is subtle and gives dimension to your hair making it more vibrant and alive.

By Shelene Shaer Master Colourist Tanaz Hair

title: RIDING HORSES IN DRAKENSBERG SOUTH AFRICA
tags: Drakensberg|Drakensberg south africa|Horses|Riding horses|Vlog|Winter|South africa|Follow me|Travel with me|Travel diaries|Holiday|2016
description:
Drakensberg mountains is one of the most beautiful and breathtaking places in South Africa. Check out my instagram for more posts: https://www.instagram.com/jessica_vanheerden/

We spent the week at Midlands Saddle and Trout farm situated high up in the mountains, we had the most beautiful view from our little house we stayed in. Midlands Saddle and trout is part of the First Group Resorts in South Africa. You can find them on instagram https://www.instagram.com/first_group_mgmt/ or visit them here http://www.firstresorts.co.za/Pages/default.aspx


In the beginning of 2016 I booked a week here for Bren and I to celebrate our 5 year dating anniversary, unfortunately Bren moved jobs and couldnt take an entire week off so I invited my family to join me and they loved it so much. We were hoping for snow but snowflakes fell 3 weeks after our visit. We went from the 20th of June and snowfall was end of July so if you want to experience ice mountains make sure to book around end July. We stayed in a spacious 2 bedroom house with 2 luxurious bathrooms, beautiful kitchen, spacious living areas and a breathtaking view. 
You can find them here: http://www.midlandssaddle.co.za/Pages/default.aspx

I would recommend this resort to anyone who loves calm and relaxing getaways. The resort is extremely kids friendly and we had the best horse trail around the resort and up the mountains. 

I cant wait to come back next year and experience the snow with Bren 💕

Bren and I ended up celebrating our 5 year anniversary at a garden farmers market Ive wanted to go to for months. It was such a lovely surprise and you can watch that video here: https://youtu.be/URnch3gRLlw


A big thank you to my brother for filming this, go give him a follow: https://www.instagram.com/piet_vanheerden/

title: OUR 5 YEAR DATING ANNIVERSARY
tags: anniversary|5 years|5 year anniversary date|dating|inlove|love|happy
description:
"As he read, I fell in love the way you fall asleep: slowly, and then all at once."
John Green, The Fault in Our Stars


Bren and I have been dating for 5 years and known each other for 10. We are each other's bestest friends and we share almost everything and everyday together. With him I find happiness in almost everything.. His laugh, way of doing and saying things & his genuine and honest heart of gold. 

I have been wanting to go to this farmers market for weeks now & so he surprised me with a day filled with romantic strolls, the beautiful outdoors, lots of laughter & even more food. We enjoy the little things as long as we are doing them together. 

Each year both of us plan a date, one of us take the day and the other the night. Bren is the most down to earth person you will ever meet. He is not impressed by fancy things at all which balances me out a little bit considering I love anything and everything posh (what girl doesn't right?) so for his portion of the date I surprised him with a at home movie date filled with his favorite foods and lots of cuddles. He was so excited and it made me so happy to see him excited about something I did for him. 

If I have one bit of relationship advice, it would be to make him (or her) your best friend. Laugh together, be silly & enjoy each others company. Stand up for him/her and NEVER talk bad about them behind their back, even if he did something to hurt you. A man/woman is viewed as they have been rated by their partner when he/she is not present.

Love each other fearlessly!

title: MY GRADUATION DAY 2016
tags: graduation|clas of 2016|graduation day|degree|university of johannesburg|south africa
description:
"Education is the most powerful weapon we can use to change the world." - Nelson Mandela.

I graduated on 8 June 2016 with a Bcomm Marketing management degree from the University of Johannesburg, South Africa. 

Coming from a family with no urge to obtain further education it always motivated me to build my foundation with books. Education has always been extremely important to me, but in my 4 years of studies I realised you don't need a degree to be successful in life. Success feeds off hard work, dedication, and commitment to your goal... whatever it may be!

Thank you to my mamma and pappa for this amazing gift of education. Thank you for your hard work and encouragement throughout my studies. Seeing my mother shed a tear of joy just before our family graduation photo was taken made me feel so proud to be her daughter, and then realising she is just as proud to be my mother today. My dad (or as I call him: "pappie") is a very quiet person, but I know he is very proud of his only daughter today.

Last but not least, thank you to my best friend and partner for life. We have studied together, laughed and cried together. Getting a degree is not as easy as everybody thinks, but sharing the experience with you definitely made it worth the wait and I can't wait to share your graduation milestone with you.

Thank you for all of you guys for sharing this beautiful life moment of achievement with me. 

You will never regret following your dreams xxx

tags: n2|nacional 2|mora|alentejo|portugal|wild game|dinner|food|N2|MoraAlentejo|N2Portugal|HiddenGems|TravelPortugal|Migas|Woodwork|GameDinner|Beekeeping|RoadTripPortugal
description:
Mora, Alentejo – More Than Just a Pit Stop on the N2! 🇵🇹

Most people just drive through Mora on Portugal’s famous N2 road, but trust us—you’re missing out! In this video, we take the time have a little wonder around this village.

📍 First stop – we got our N2 passports stamped at the local tourism board, officially marking our journey.

🛠️ Then, things got hands-on! We joined an incredible wood workshop with Jorge Caetano Varandas (Ihttps://www.instagram.com/jorgevarandascaetano/), where we watched him skillfully craft a honey dipper. The craftsmanship was next level!

🐝 Next up, bees! We visited a fee farm (yep, that’s a thing!) and learned all about these fascinating creatures with António Canhoto. Spoiler alert: bees are way cooler than we ever realized.

🍽️ And then… food. We had the chance to attend Mora’s annual Game Dinner, a unique event where local restaurants come together to serve incredible dishes made from wild game. A true foodie’s dream!

🥖 But that’s not all—Mora is currently attempting to break a Guinness World Record for the longest Migas (a traditional dish from Alentejo). We love a Village with big dreams and a passion for good food!

🗿 If you ever visit, don’t miss the Megalithism Museum and the Fluviário (a fascinating freshwater aquarium). Mora may be small, but it’s packed with history, culture, and surprises.

🚗 So next time you’re driving the N2, don’t just pass through—stop and explore!

🚗 Embark on an unforgettable journey with us as we share the harrowing tale of our road trip from Yulara to Leonora along the treacherous Great Central Road. Join us as we faced unexpected challenges, conquered the unforgiving desert, and discovered the true meaning of resilience.

🌵 Day 1: Yulara to Warakurna Roadhouse
Our adventure kicked off with a flat tire and a dead battery, but against all odds, we pushed through and made it to Warakurna Roadhouse, a remote oasis in the heart of the Australian outback.

🔧 Day 2: Warakurna to Warburton Roadhouse
Just when we thought the worst was behind us, we discovered a nail in one of our tires. Stranded in the vast desert, a hero from the roadhouse staff came to our rescue, fixing the tire and giving us a renewed sense of hope.

⏳ Day 3: Stranded in the Desert
With assistance days away, we braved the isolation of the desert at Tjukayirla Roadhouse, battling scorching temperatures of 47 degrees. Our endurance was put to the test, but our determination prevailed.

🌅 Day 4: Tjukayirla to Menzies
Rising with the sun, we continued our journey, passing through Leonora and finally finding solace at Menzies Caravan Park. It was here that we took a much-needed break, reflecting on the challenges that shaped our expedition.

🛌 Relaxation and Reflection in Menzies
Explore the quaint Menzies with us as we take a breather, relishing in the security of a peaceful oasis. Our time here allowed us to decompress and assess the incredible journey we had just navigated.

🔥 Unveiling the Great Central Road Nightmare
Watch our YouTube video to witness the highs, lows, and unexpected twists of our Great Central Road nightmare. Subscribe to our channel for more thrilling travel stories and tips on navigating the road less traveled.

description:
🚗 Embark on an unforgettable adventure with us as we tackle the Great Central Road, Australia's longest shortcut to Perth, Western Australia! 🌐 Our journey kicks off with excitement and anticipation, but little did we know that we were in for a series of unexpected challenges that would test our resilience and resourcefulness.

🔧 The first 200km brought us face-to-face with the harsh reality of the Outback as we encountered our first flat tire. With no prior experience in changing a tire and no one around for miles, we found ourselves in a tight spot. After a bit of fumbling, thanks to Cristiana consulting the manual, we located the elusive jack. The vastness of the uncharted roads became evident as we navigated this hurdle with no phone signal in sight.

🛠️ Wrestling with the stubborn tire, we overcame the odds and pressed on, determined to conquer the Great Central Road. Our next pitstop, Lasseter's Cave, offered a brief respite, showcasing the beauty of the Australian Outback. However, our break turned into another unexpected challenge when we returned to find our car lifeless – a drained battery adding to the adventure!

🕵️‍♂️ Enter Joao, our hero of the day, who identified the issue: a loose cable disconnecting from the battery. As we fixed the problem, we couldn't shake the feeling that perhaps we were navigating through a cursed journey. Undeterred, we pushed forward, determined to make it to our next milestone.

🌄 The journey continued, each kilometer adding to the epic tale of our adventure. We pressed on until we reached the Warakurna Roadhouse, our oasis in the vast desert. As the sun set on the horizon, we reflected on the challenges overcome and the thrill of the unknown that lay ahead.

🌿 Immerse yourself in the sacred beauty of Kata Tjuta in the Australian Outback, a place considered sacred by the Aboriginal people. Discover the spiritual significance of this landscape as we ascend to the towering heights of Mount Olga, which stands almost 200m higher than Uluru at its tallest point.

🔍 For those hungry for facts, learn about the rich cultural heritage of Kata Tjuta, intertwined with the stories and traditions of the Aboriginal people. Uncover the geological wonders that make this site truly one of a kind.

description:
After a long journey through the outback, we've finally made it to Coober Pedy! In this travel video, we'll share our experience of this strange, but beautiful, town on the edge of the Australian desert.

Coober Pedy is a bit of an off the map destination, but that's part of the appeal. If you're looking for a unique travel experience.

Hey hey we made it to the Outback of South Australia, we stoped in Coober Pedy for 3 days, this has to be the strangest town in Australia, but in a positive way we loved it here, we visited the Umoona Opal Mine & Museum, the Serbian Orthodox Church, Josephine's Gallery and Kangaroo orphanage (were we held a baby kangaroo named Daphne) BEST DAY EVER. Terry the owner even played the didgeridoo for us, the place is also a gallery and Cristiana bought a boomerang that was made by the aboriginal.

Coober Pedy is the opal capital of the world, opal is a gem, precious stone, we learned all this at the free museum.
Due to the unusual landscape a lot of movies were recorded here like: Pitch Black (2000), Red Planet (2000), Kangaroo Jack (2003), The Osiris Child (2016), just to name a few.

title: The things you cannot replace

description:
In today's fast-paced and materialistic society, it can be easy to get caught up in the pursuit of material possessions and external validation, often neglecting the more meaningful aspects of life, such as health, family, and mental well-being. Here are some strategies to shift the focus and prioritize what truly matters:

Reevaluate Your Values:

Take some time to reflect on what truly brings fulfillment and happiness to your life. Identify your core values and align your actions with them.
Practice Gratitude:

Cultivate a daily gratitude practice. Take a moment each day to acknowledge and appreciate the blessings in your life, including your health, family, and mental well-being.
Set Boundaries with Technology and Materialism:

Limit your exposure to social media and advertising, as they can perpetuate a culture of materialism and comparison. Focus on real-life experiences and connections instead.
Prioritize Self-Care:

Make time for self-care activities that nourish your physical, emotional, and mental well-being. This can include exercise, meditation, spending time in nature, reading, or engaging in hobbies you enjoy.
Spend Quality Time with Family:

Create designated family time where distractions like phones and work are set aside. Engage in activities that promote bonding, communication, and support.
Promote Open Communication:

Encourage open and honest communication within your family. Create a safe space where everyone feels comfortable sharing their thoughts and feelings without judgment.
Seek Professional Help if Needed:

If you or a family member is struggling with mental health, don't hesitate to seek help from a qualified mental health professional. Taking care of your mental state is essential for overall well-being.
Practice Mindfulness:

Incorporate mindfulness practices into your daily life. Mindfulness can help you stay present, reduce stress, and appreciate the small joys in life.
Give Back to the Community:

Engage in activities that contribute positively to your community. Volunteering and helping others can bring a sense of purpose and fulfillment.
Teach and Lead by Example:

If you have children or younger family members, lead by example and teach them the importance of valuing health, family, and mental well-being over material possessions.
Remember that creating a balanced and fulfilling life requires conscious effort and ongoing commitment. By prioritizing the things that truly matter and letting go of excessive materialism, you can lead a more meaningful and satisfying life for yourself and your family.

description:
Have you ever wondered why people get fined NZ$200 in New Zealand for freedom camping? 
In this video, we explore the reasons why Christchurch is off to a bad start for us. 
We'll look at the history of the city, the effects of the earthquakes, and the current situation given that there's not many tourists and New Zealand is in desperate need of people to work. Join us as we uncover Christchurch and its struggles to get back on its feet.

Now back to the issue - we were fined in Christchurch, New Zealand. We were sleeping on a freedom campsite and a gentleman from the council woke us up at 6 or 7 in the morning to give us a fine of 200 New Zealand dollars and said our van was not self contained, the issue was to do with out self contained sticker being handwritten rather than printed out, but our actual self contained paper work was all good and the council staff didn't want to look at it as it had already issued the fine. After a few minutes trying to understand why we got fined and the gentleman just being rude to us we decided to just take it to the council on Monday as this happened on a weekend.
We didn't want our day to be ruined by this so we decided to take on the city and visit everything we had planned out and like everyone said to us before, Christchurch is a lovely city. 
On the following Monday we went to the council and presented all facts we had and explained our situation, they decided that we were not in the wrong and our fine was forgiven. 
This just goes to show you that sometimes the backpackers are not wrong and were just not given the opportunity to express themselves. This was a not so great start in Christchurch but we didn't let it ruin our weekend (at least not completely ahah).

title: IS THIS New Zealand's BEST road trip? DESERT ROAD
tags: new zealand|desert road|how to travel new zealand|mount doom|tongariro alpine crossing|tongariro national park|tongariro crossing|Van life|van life nz|Mount Ruapehu|Mount Ngauruhoe|Mount Tongariro|road trip new zealand|desert road new zealand|North Island Volcanic Plateau in Waikato|north island new zealand|waikato|turangi new zealand|rangipo desert|Waiouru|Ruapehu District|travel nz in a campervan|travelling to nz 2022|volcanoes|new zealand travel
description:
Did you know that there's a desert road in New Zealand?
There is and it's an amazing road trip, we would risk to say that one of the most beautiful.

The Desert Road is 63km long so not that long to drive, and it crosses the alpine desert and links the small towns of Turangi, on the North Island Volcanic Plateau in Waikato region and Waiouru, in the Ruapehu District. This road gains its name from being completely remote. Rangipo Desert (Te Onetapu) is a barren desert-like environment and indeed felt like we were away from civilisation for thousands of kms.

The views are just spectacular there are few words that can describe what we saw that day and in our opinion it's best done from south to north (that's what we did) because you get to see the beautiful views as soon as you enter the road and if you do it the other way around will have the initial beautiful views of this video behind them. 

These are the views that we get to see 
Mount Ruapehu, 2797 meters (9178 ft) above the sea level. Its elevation allows the only glaciers on the North Island. The last eruption was in September 1996.
Mount Ngauruhoe, 2291 meters (7518 ft). The volcano was very active in the 20th century with more than 40 eruptions. The last one was in 1977. It is an inspiration for the famous Mount Doom of the Lord of the Rings trilogy films. Yeah, the place where the Ring was forged by Sauron himself and should be destroyed by Frodon!
Mount Tongariro, 1978 meters (6494 ft). It is the smallest one of these three. The last eruption was in 2012.

tags: Taupo|thermal hot pool|New Zealand|Huka Falls|Wairakei Terraces|Coolest mc donalds in the world|natural hot springs|Waikato River|new zealand travel|taupo|lake taupo nz|what to do taupo|taupo attractions|lake taupo activities|huka falls new zealand|huka falls nz|lake taupo|huka falls taupo|new zealand things to do|taupo what to do|free things to do in taupo|taupo hole in one|taupo mcdonalds|taupo new zealand
description:
Things to do in Taupo in 2022:

Visit Huka Falls (free entrance)
Get a dip in the Wairakei Terraces Hot Thermal Pools (we have a website to purchase discounted entrances)
Get yourself a cheat meal and go to Mc Donalds (or as they call it in New Zealand - Macca's)

Now a little bit of information about the places we visited:
Huka falls are not simply waterfalls, you can witness the phenomenon of natural hydro power with more than 220,000 litres of water per sec barreling over 11meter high waterfall.
They are located in New Zealands longest river - Waikato River. You can enjoy a hike around the river and see the native forest and the tranquil and bright clear Waikato River.

Wairakei Terraces have recreated a series of hot thermal pools, which have been strategically positioned below silica terraces to take full advantage of the mineral enriched water that has been drawn to the earth’s surface from 1.5 kilometres underground – thereby providing a ‘back in time’ sensation, and an ideal setting for anyone wanting to indulge in something unique, and uniquely relaxing. Usually these places are a bit expensive but we found a website where we bought a discounted entrance 
GrabOne - https://new.grabone.co.nz/activities-events-outdoors/volcanic-geothermal/p/wairakei-terraces-1581
This is not sponsored is simply what we used and we are sharing it here.

Now Mc Donalds
This is in the middle of Taupo and the reason we wanted to go there it's because we could have our meals inside an airplane, I mean who wouldn't want to?
This Mc Donalds also holds the title of one of the coolest in the world. "The site was previously part of a car dealership, the Aeroplane Car Company, and the owner bought a disused DC-3 plane, which sat alongside the building. And when McDonald's purchased the site in 1990, the aeroplane came with it.”
The plane is very visible from the street and you can snap a picture of it without having to go to Mc Donalds.

title: Experience the REAL Maori Village in Rotorua!
tags: rotorua|maori|new zealand|maori village|rotorua new zealand|things to do in rotorua|free things to do in rotorua|rotorua thermal pools|ohinemutu|ohinemutu history|ohinemutu church|tama te kapua haka|kuirau park rotorua|redwood forest rotorua|kuirau park
description:
In this Video we visited the Maori village of Ohinemutu which is located in Rotorua - Ōhinemutu Village was settled by the Ngāti Whakaue iwi (tribe), a sub-tribe of the Te Arawa waka (canoe) journeyed from the Pacific homeland of Hawaiiki to New Zealand around 1350AD. The explorers chose this location for their home due to its setting along the shores of Lake Rotorua and the abundant geothermal energy which was useful for cooking, bathing and heating.
 Ngāti Whakaue gifted the land on which the city of Rotorua was built, and today the historic village, just 10 minutes’ walk from the Rotorua city centre, is still home to a few hundred descendants.
We were greeted by lovely locals that showed us around and even showed us new hot pools that have appeared in the zone and the traditional ovens where Maori cook their Hangi (Hāngī is a traditional New Zealand Māori method of cooking food using heated rocks buried in a pit oven, called an umu.).

After the Maori village it was time to visit Kuirau park. Kuirau Park is free to visit and located within an easy walk from the city centre, just off Pukuatua and Ranolf streets. Parking is also free.
Several walkways take you through the park to see the crater lake, mud pools, hot springs, and a free thermal foot bath, all set in a beautifully manicured setting dotted with flower beds and native flora.
Kuirau Park is also great place to play and picnic, with barbecues, picnic tables, children's playground and toilets. If you visit on Saturday, you'll be lured by the wonderful aromas of the food vendors and the beautiful fresh produce at the farmer's market held every week from 6am to 1pm – perfect for breakfast or lunch!
We had the change to (not see much) due to the amount of steam that was coming from the very hot lakes. The smell is also interesting around Rotorua.

Our last stop in Rotorua was the Redwood forest, a forest with native New Zealand ferns and Californian Redwood Trees.

title: What is Hobbiton Really Like?

description:
Guess what? We visited Hobbiton, one of the most famous places in New Zealand.
Wether or not you are a fan of Lord of the Rings Trilogy or The Hobbit Trilogy you must have heard about the Hobbiton and Hobbits right? It's location? New Zealand!

Now let's get into the information.
Where is the Hobbiton located? 
It's located on a family run farm about 8 kilometres of Hinuera and 10 kilometres of Matamata, in Waikato, New Zealand.

How much does it cost to visit?
We paid, in October 2022, 89 (eighty-nine ) New Zealand dollars per person, this included transport from the main entrance to the actual place, a guided tour and a beer in the Green Dragon Pub (there's a non alcoholic option).

Can you visit Hobbiton by yourself?
No, you can't. Hobbiton is located in a family farm and the only way to get there is by a bus provided by the tour company which is owned by the family.

Where to stay the night?
If you have a vehicle where you can sleep you can check Rankers NZ and CamperMate app for the most up to date places nearby. If you are looking for a homestay or hotel your best bet would be Matamata or a homestay nearby (you can google this as we don't have this information).

Is Hobbiton worth visiting?
Absolutely, it's a magical and beautiful place.

title: The Great Pyramids of Giza during Covid
tags: ancient egypt|egypt|egyptians|ancient egyptians|great pyramid of giza|great pyramid of giza inside|great pyramid of giza facts|great pyramid of giza secrets|egyptian pyramids|pyramids|giza|The Great Pyramid|Pyramid of Menkaure|Pyramid of Khufu|Pyramid of Khafre|Sphinx|Giza Necropolis|Pyramid Complex|menkaure|pyramids of egypt|Tutankhamen|tombs|Ancient Egypt Documentary|Valley of the Kings|Immortal Egypt|egypt2021|egypttourism|cairo|cairo vlog|cairo egypt
description:
We visited the Pyramids of Giza!!!!
Still can't believe this happened.
Egypt's pharaohs expected to become gods in the afterlife. To prepare for the next world they erected temples to the gods and massive pyramid tombs for themselves—filled with all the things each ruler would need to guide and sustain himself in the next world.
Way before the valley of the kings, that was during the new kingdom, in the old kingdom Ancient Egyptians Pharaohs built pyramids as their burial place. 
The largest pyramid here in Giza was built 4.500 years ago as a tomb for the pharaoh Kuhfu from the 4th dynasty.
It’s estimated that 2.3 million blocks of rocks were used to build it.
The second largest pyramid was built for the tomb of pharaoh Khafre son of Kuhfu also from the 4th dynasty 
His necropolis also included the Sphinx, a mysterious limestone monument carved entirely from 1 piece of rock with the body of a lion and a pharaoh's head. 
The Sphinx may stand sentinel for the pharaoh's entire tomb complex.
The third pyramid was built for the tomb of the pharaoh Menkaure also from the 4th dynasty.
Each massive pyramid is but one part of a larger complex, including a palace, temples, solar boat pits, and other features.
There are smaller pyramids within the giza pyramid complex belonging to queens (pharaohs wives), daughters and higher elites, in total there are 9 Pyramids there, 6 small one and the 3 big ones.
The first pyramid built in Egypt was none of these 3 tho, in fact there were quite a few pyramids built before these but they got so much more attention because it’s the largest complex of Pyramids.
It’s still fairly unknown exactly how they built these magnificent buildings some theories even say it was the aliens 😂 we personally think ancient civilisations were so much more advanced than what we probably are today even with all the technology we have we still don’t know how they built it so it proves something.
Many think the pyramids were built by slaves but in fact they were very skilled, paid workers, well fed and there was even a temporary village here somewhere for the workers and their families, upon digging the village it was revealed a highly organised community, rich with resources, that must have been backed by strong central authority.
Somewhere in the 11hundreds a sultan of Egypt decided he wanted to destroy or demolish the pyramids and send workers to start  taken them down starting of course with the smaller one but it was very difficult and after 8 months they were only able to remove a few rocks making the job very expensive so they FORTUNATELY stop but we can still see a few rocks missing there. 
We were staying in downtown Cairo and took an Uber to the Pyramids, it costed us less than 80 Egyptian Pounds and took 30min.
We advise everyone to go in the morning and take some snacks to be able to see everything without rushing, we went after lunch and were left with 4 hours to visit the complex and we felt it was not enough even tho we saw everything we could have easily spend the full day there.
Another advise we can give is take plenty of water because it gets really hot and we didn't see anyone selling water inside the complex.
On the way back to downtown Cairo we got a taxi and negotiated the price - 100 Egyptian Pounds, it took us a little over than 2 hours because the traffic was a nightmare.

description:
The Luxor temple was built by Amenhotep III (1390-52 BC) but completed by Tutankhamun (1336-27 BC) and Horemheb (1323-1295 BC) and then some more elements were added to by Rameses II (1279-13 BC). 
At the back there even is a granite shrine dedicated to Alexander the Great (332-305 BC).
Then for thousands of years, the temple was buried beneath the streets and houses of Luxor. 
Although the mud-brick houses and palaces of Thebes have disappeared, its stone temples have survived. The most beautiful of these is the temple of Luxor. It is close to the Nile and laid out parallel to the riverbank.
The temple has been in almost continuous use as a place of worship right up to the present day. 
During the Christian era, the temple’s hypostyle hall was converted into a Christian church, and the remains of another Coptic church can be seen to the west. 
There were 2 obelisks at the front of the temple but one was removed and exchanged for a clock tower with Paris so the obelisk went to paris and Egypt got a clock tower that is in Cairo.
There is an ancient avenue called avenue of sphinxes that goes from Karnak temple (see previous video) to Luxor Temple, it’s currently being under renovation but one can walk 3km from one temple to another in a straight line along the Nile once the renovation is completed, is thought that there were approximately 1350 sphinxes on this road.
This road was used once a year during the Opet festival when the Egyptians paraded along it carrying the statues of Amun and Mut in a symbolic re-enactment of their marriage. At Luxor temple Amun was magically transformed into Min the god of fertility.
The construction of the Avenue of Sphinxes begun during the New Kingdom and finished during 30th Dynasty rule of Nectanebo I (380-362 BC).
The road was renovated by the Ptolemaic Queen Cleopatra (51-30 BC) and later used by the Romans. Recently 850 sphinx fragmented have been discovered along a section of Sphinx road built Amenhotep III (1390-1352 BC).
