Boracay Island, a tropical paradise in the Philippines, is a dream destination for many travelers, especially those visiting for the first time. Here are some keywords that capture the essence of this stunning island and what first-time visitors should look out for:

White Beach: The iconic stretch of powdery white sand and clear blue waters that Boracay is famous for. It's the heart of the island and a must-visit for any traveler.

Station 1, 2, and 3: These refer to the different sections of White Beach, each with its own unique vibe. Station 1 is known for its upscale resorts, Station 2 is the bustling center with shops and nightlife, and Station 3 offers a more laid-back atmosphere.

Crystal Cove Island: A nearby island known for its stunning coves and crystal-clear waters, perfect for a day trip from Boracay.

D'Mall: The main shopping and dining area on the island, where visitors can find a variety of restaurants, bars, and shops.

Puka Beach: A quieter beach on the northern part of the island, known for its unique puka shells and more relaxed ambiance.

Island Hopping: A popular activity where visitors can explore nearby islands, snorkel, and enjoy the beauty of the surrounding waters.

Willy's Rock: An iconic rock formation located on White Beach, often photographed by tourists.

Bulabog Beach: The opposite side of the island from White Beach, known for its water sports like kiteboarding and windsurfing.

Mt. Luho: The highest point on the island, offering stunning panoramic views of Boracay and the surrounding areas.

Boracay Sunset: The breathtaking sunsets that the island is famous for, best enjoyed from White Beach.

Water Sports: Activities such as parasailing, jet skiing, banana boat rides, and paddleboarding are popular on the island.

Scuba Diving: Boracay is home to several diving spots, including Yapak and Crocodile Island, where divers can explore the vibrant underwater world.

Nightlife: The island is known for its vibrant nightlife, with numerous bars, clubs, and beach parties that come alive after sunset.

Food and Cuisine: Boracay offers a wide range of dining options, from local Filipino cuisine to international dishes. Seafood is a must-try, given the island's location.

Henann Resort: One of the popular upscale resorts on the island, known for its luxurious amenities and prime location on White Beach.

Boracay Ocean Club: Another popular accommodation option, offering a mix of comfort and accessibility to the island's attractions.

Eco-Friendly Initiatives: Boracay has made significant efforts in recent years to promote sustainability and preserve its natural beauty. Initiatives include waste management programs and the restriction of single-use plastics.

Transportation: Getting around the island is easy with options like e-trikes, bicycles, and walking paths.

Beach Activities: Aside from water sports, visitors can enjoy activities like beach volleyball, frisbee, and simply relaxing on the sand.

Spa and Wellness: Boracay offers several spa and wellness centers where visitors can unwind with massages, yoga classes, and other relaxation treatments.

Local Markets: Exploring local markets is a great way to experience the culture and buy souvenirs.

Environmental Conservation: The island has various programs aimed at protecting its natural beauty, including coral reef restoration and beach clean-ups.

Boracay Newcoast: A more recent development area on the island, offering new accommodation and leisure options.

Festivals and Events: Boracay hosts various events throughout the year, including the famous Ati-Atihan Festival and dragon boat races.

I hope this list helps you get a comprehensive overview of Boracay Island for your first visit!

Bantayan Island, located in the Visayas region of the Philippines, is a tropical paradise known for its stunning beaches and laid-back atmosphere. While it may not be famous for its nightlife, there are still some charming spots where visitors can enjoy a relaxing evening.

Nightlife in Bantayan Island: The nightlife on Bantayan Island is relatively low-key, with a few bars and restaurants offering a cozy atmosphere. The town of Santa Fe is the hub of nightlife, where visitors can find a handful of bars and live music venues. Popular spots include Hr Musicbar, known for its live music and dance floor, and Coucou Bar Hotel & Restaurant, which offers a mix of drinks and entertainment. On weekends, these places come alive with more people and livelier events.

Beach Bars: For a more relaxed evening, beach bars like Stumble Inn Beach Club and Kota Beach Resort are great choices. These spots offer a laid-back vibe where visitors can enjoy a drink while watching the sunset over the ocean. The atmosphere is friendly and welcoming, making it easy to strike up conversations with fellow travelers.

Karaoke Bars: Karaoke is a popular activity in the Philippines, and Bantayan Island is no exception. Ato Ni Bai is a well-known karaoke bar where visitors can sing their favorite songs and enjoy a fun night out. It's a great way to bond with friends and experience the local culture.

Handmade Ice Cream: Bantayan Island is home to some delightful handmade ice cream shops. Shake Me is a popular spot offering refreshing ice cream made with fresh fruits. Another favorite is Hello Spank, located in Santa Fe, which serves delicious homemade ice cream in a colorful setting. For a unique treat, Teresito Dragon Fruit Farm offers premium dragon fruit ice cream made from fresh dragon fruit picked from their farm.

Local Cuisine: In addition to ice cream, Bantayan Island offers a variety of local dishes that visitors can enjoy. From seafood to traditional Filipino meals, there are plenty of options to satisfy different tastes. Trying the local cuisine is a great way to immerse oneself in the island's culture.

Relaxing Atmosphere: The overall atmosphere on Bantayan Island is relaxed and laid-back, making it an ideal destination for those looking to unwind and escape the hustle and bustle of city life. Whether it's enjoying a quiet evening at a beach bar or savoring a scoop of handmade ice cream, the island offers a peaceful retreat.

Sunset Views: Watching the sunset over the ocean is a must-do activity on Bantayan Island. The beautiful sunsets provide a stunning backdrop for an evening stroll along the beach or a relaxing drink at a beach bar.

Friendly Locals: The locals on Bantayan Island are known for their warm hospitality and friendliness. Interacting with them can enhance the overall experience, whether it's getting recommendations for the best spots to visit or simply enjoying a conversation.

Quiet Nights: Unlike bustling cities, Bantayan Island offers a quieter nightlife experience. This can be a refreshing change for those looking to relax and enjoy a peaceful evening.

Travel Tips: For a pleasant experience, it's recommended to visit during the dry season, from December to May, when the weather is more favorable. Bringing essentials like sunscreen, hats, and reusable water bottles is also advisable.

Accommodation Options: There are various accommodation options on Bantayan Island, ranging from budget guesthouses to luxury resorts. Staying close to the nightlife spots can make it more convenient to enjoy the evening activities.

Exploring the Island: Besides nightlife, Bantayan Island offers plenty of daytime activities such as island hopping, snorkeling, and exploring local markets. Combining these activities with a relaxing evening can make for a well-rounded trip.

title: Surviving a HUGE rain storm in Antipolo Cebu. Resort adventure and fun in Cebu. vlog #16
description:
vlog #16
We made a late decision to go beach camping overnight.  So we went a few hours from Cebu to the North. We went to Antipolo Coral Beach Resort located about halfway between Asturias and Tuburan but located in Tuburan. We had a wonderful time, endured a massive rain storm but survived with a smile on our faces and a very enjoyable adventure. 

The resort has not been open all that long, everything is fresh and new. Entry is 150php for adults and 100 for children 4yo and up. There is a pool, showers and cr block, a restaurant with plenty of good food and drinks, a billiard table, kayaks and paddle boards for hire. There is no charge to bring your own food with several places available to bbq. Drinks will incur a corkage fee. 

For your stay you can rent one of 3 Beach cottages (700 php each) for the day or 1 self contained room (2000-2500php) is available for overnight, a 2nd room is almost completed with another 2 yet to be built. You can also camp in your own tent for 300 php fee.

https://m.facebook.com/Antipolo-Coral-Beach-Resort-107574018271226/?tsid=0.27947127542047934&source=result

The owners, Dwight and Cheradee are extremely welcoming and friendly and add that little bit extra to your stay.

A big thank you to them and Antipolo Coral Beach Resort.

title: Timang Beach Gondola + Best Lobster in Java  | Gunungkidul Day Trip from Yogyakarta

description:
After the ancient temples of Borobudur and Prambanan, Java reveals a completely different face. We head south — deep into Gunungkidul — where the cliffs drop sharply into the Indian Ocean and the coast feels like the edge of the world. This is a full day trip from Yogyakarta, and it might be the most dramatic one yet.

🌊 IN THIS EPISODE
We ride the hand-pulled gondola over open ocean at Timang Beach — one of the most thrilling things you can do in all of Java. We sit down with Pak Sis for lobster pulled straight from these same waters, served fresh and simply, the way it should be. We find a table on the cliffs at On The Rock Drini, with nothing ahead but sea. And on the drive back to Yogyakarta, we stop at Warung Simbok for a quiet, grounding dinner that feels like the perfect end to a long day on the coast.

⏱️ VIDEO TIMESTAMPS
00:00 - Introduction
01:23 - Pre-Ordering Lunch at the Original Kedai Lobster Pak Sis

18:48 - Authentic Regional Dinner Stop: Warung Simbok Javanese Joglo

📍 LOCATIONS IN THE ULTIMATE GUNUNGKIDUL DAY TRIP ROUTE
📍 Stop 1: Timang Beach (Pantai Timang)
The ultimate high-adrenaline ocean crossing. Ride a rugged 4x4 local jeep shuttle through broken backroads to reach the edge of the cliffs. Here, you’ll face the legendary Timang Beach Gondola—a rustic wooden box pulled entirely by hand over the churning Indian Ocean—or brave the swaying suspension rope bridge to reach Lobster Island.

📍 Stop 2: Original Kedai Lobster Pak Sis
Right after the adrenaline rush, we head to the original shop run by one of the gondola’s founding builders. They serve up incredibly fresh rock lobsters caught right off the island cliffs, cooked in rich garlic butter and signature spicy Timang sauce.

📍 Stop 3: On The Rock Drini (Drini Beach)
A stunning, modern cliffside oceanfront destination perched right over Pantai Drini. 

📍 Stop 4: Warung Simbok (Return Journey Dinner)
On the drive back up the Wonosari-Yogyakarta highway, we stop at this iconic traditional Javanese Joglo house. It's the ultimate place to wind down with authentic local comfort food, famous for its rich traditional Ayam Ingkung (Javanese cooked chicken) and traditional sambal.

💡 TRAVEL TIPS
→ Timang Beach is approximately 2–3 hours from central Yogyakarta — start early
→ Gondola ride: ~IDR 200,000 per person (suspension bridge: ~IDR 150,000)
→ Book Pak Sis before your visit to Timang beach; lobster availability depends on the catch
→ On The Rock Drini is best visited for the view — go at low tide

title: Hiking Sungai Chilling Waterfall: 6 River Crossings & Best Scones in Kuala Kubu Bharu(KKB)
tags: TRT&x%|sungai chiling|hiking at sungai chiling|best hiking near kuala lumpur|kuala lumpur day trips|kuala kubu bharu|batang kali|malaysia travel|hidden cafes|sungai chiling fish sanctuary|sungai chiling waterfall|chiling waterfalls|fish sanctuary|chiling waterfall
description:
Looking for the best nature getaway near Kuala Lumpur? 🌿 In this cinematic travel guide, we’re hiking to the Sungai Chilling Waterfall and Fish Sanctuary in Kuala Kubu Bharu (KKB), Selangor. This trail is famous for its 6 river crossings, crystal-clear waters, and the friendly Kelah fish (Malaysian Mahseer) that swim right up to you!

After our hike, we head to a hidden gem—Kebun Cafe in Hulu Yam Lama—to try their famous Earl Grey scones and enjoy a quiet afternoon overlooking a lush organic farm. Whether you’re a hiker or a foodie, this is the perfect weekend day trip from KL.

📍 Locations Featured:
Sungai Chilling Fish Sanctuary: Located near KKB, open weekends only.
Kebun Cafe (Hoho Farm): A rustic, nature-integrated cafe in Batang Kali/Hulu Yam.

📌 CHAPTERS (Key Moments)
00:00 Nature’s Therapy: Intro to Sungai Chilling

01:37 How to Apply for Sungai Chilling Permits & Fees
02:28 Packing List: Water Shoes & Dry Bags
04:43 Encountering the Kelah Fish (Malaysian Mahseer)

09:42 River Crossing 1 & 2: Finding Your Balance
14:40 River Crossing 3 & 4: Deep Waters & Boulders
20:58 The Final 6th Crossing (Deepest Point!)

30:32 Reviewing the Best Scones in Selangor

🎒 TRAVEL TIPS & RESOURCES
Permits: You must register online via the Selangor Forestry website (Seforest) or at the gantry. Limit is 500 pax/day!

Operating Hours: Saturday & Sunday only (8:00 AM – 6:00 PM). Trail entry often closes by 1:00 PM or 3:30 PM depending on weather.

Gear Used: Filmed entirely on the DJI Osmo Pocket 3 for that cinematic, modern-zen look.

Pro-Tip: No food is allowed on the trail. Plan your meal for after the hike at one of the local KKB or Hulu Yam cafes!

💡 FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)
Q: Do I need a permit for Sungai Chilling Waterfall in 2026?
A: Yes! You must apply for a permit via the Seforest (Selangor Forestry) website. Permits are RM5 per person (online) or RM10 (at the gantry/walk-in if slots are available). Daily visitors are capped at 500 people, so book in advance!

Q: What are the opening hours for the Fish Sanctuary?
A: Sungai Chilling is only open on weekends (Saturday & Sunday) from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Note that you must reach the ranger station to start the hike by 1:00 PM, as the waterfall area starts clearing out after 3:00 PM for safety.

Q: How many river crossings are there to reach the waterfall?
A: There are 6 river crossings in total. The trail is mostly flat, but the final crossing can reach waist or chest height depending on recent rainfall. Always use the provided guide ropes!

Q: Can I bring food and have a picnic at the waterfall?
A: To protect the fish sanctuary and keep the river pristine, no food is allowed past the suspension bridge. You can have a picnic at the designated campsite area near the entrance registration counter.

Q: Where is the best place to eat after hiking in KKB?
A: We highly recommend Kebun Cafe in Hulu Yam Lama (about 30 minutes away). It’s open Friday–Sunday (11 AM – 6 PM) and is famous for its Earl Grey scones and organic farm views.

Q: Is the trail suitable for children?
A: Yes, the trail is relatively easy and flat. However, children will need help with the river crossings as the current can be strong. Life jackets are recommended for younger kids.

Looking for the ultimate Terengganu food guide? Join us on a 10-day road trip from Singapore to explore 10 hidden food gems, authentic local flavors, and a traditional Malay Kampong stay in the East Coast of Malaysia!

In this comprehensive Terengganu travel vlog, we dive deep into the local food scene, from the famous blue Nasi Kerabu at Warung Damia to the "Trader’s Rice" (Nasi Dagang) at Pujangga Cafe and Atas Tol. We also take you off the beaten path to explore the scenic Penarik Beach, the Setiu Wetlands mangrove tour, and the iconic Terengganu Drawbridge.

If you love authentic Malay cuisine, you cannot miss the street food snacks like Sata, Pulut Panggang, and the legendary Keropok Lekor from Ikan Saja. Complete your visit with a traditional kampung stay at Teratak Sekuchi, a unique Airbnb experience right by the South China Sea.

description:
Nestled on the northwestern coast of Malaysia, George Town in Penang offers a delightful fusion of old-world charm and modern attractions. As the capital city of Penang, it boasts a rich history and vibrant culture, which visitors can explore through its various landmarks, food, and art. This article highlights some of the top things to do in George Town to truly experience the essence of this UNESCO World Heritage site.

At the heart of this city lies the historic core, adorned with an array of ornate temples, colonial buildings, and traditional shophouses. One can easily spend hours wandering through the narrow streets, admiring the beautiful architecture and intricate street art. 

To ensure an unforgettable experience in George Town, be sure to explore these top attractions and activities.

1. Pinang Peranakan Mansion
The Pinang Peranakan Mansion is a must-visit for anyone interested in the history and culture of Penang's Peranakan community. This beautifully restored 19th-century building showcases an impressive collection of artifacts, furniture, and artwork that reflects the unique Peranakan heritage.

Opening Hours: Mondays to Sundays, 9.30am to 5.30pm
Admission Fee: MYR 25 per person, inclusive of free guided tour

2. TOP Penang, a premier entertainment and tourist destination in Penang, Malaysia, has captured the hearts of both locals and international visitors. Known for its breathtaking panoramic views, thrilling activities, and mouth-watering cuisine, this well-rounded attraction is synonymous with the best that Penang has to offer.

Situated in the heart of Georgetown, TOP Penang boasts a wide variety of activities that cater to all ages and interests. 

3. Cheong Fatt Tze Mansion
The Cheong Fatt Tze Mansion, also known as the Blue Mansion, is a distinctive and well-preserved 19th-century building. Built in traditional Hakka-Teochew style, it boasts a stunning mix of Eastern and Western architectural elements. Its striking blue hue, adorned with intricate carvings and stained-glass windows, make it a must-visit landmark in George Town.

Guided tours are available for visitors who are interested in learning more about the mansion's history and its former owner, Cheong Fatt Tze. 

4. Street Art in Georgetown
The streets of Georgetown are adorned with interactive street art that has become an integral part of the city's culture and identity. Wander through the narrow alleys and discover murals created by renowned artists like Ernest Zacharevic and local talents. 

5. Clan Jetty
The unique settlement comprises an array of wooden houses, built on stilts and connected by boardwalks, serving as a living heritage site in this UNESCO World Heritage city. 

Established in the 19th century, the Clan Jetty soon became home to a myriad of Chinese clans, each with their own jetty, as a solution to the rising costs and issues surrounding land ownership. Today, six major jetties remain, with the Chew Jetty being the largest and most well known.

On this bike tour, we weave through jungles villages, and learn about local Thai life. Before heading back, stop by the Bangkok Tree House, a very unique boutique hotel that is only accessible by foot or bicycles. It's a refreshing break from the city buzz. Come cycle with us and see a different side of Bangkok!

Discover Hidden Gems & Fall in Love with Every City - Your Ultimate Guide to Unforgettable Journeys: https://www.travelsandroadtrips.com/ 

Bangkok is well known for its glittering skyscrapers and bustling cityscapes. But do you know that Bangkok has a hidden rural side with tranquil lakes and a lush jungle just a short boat ride away? In this video, we explore Bangkok Bang Kachao, known as Bangkok’s green lung, on an afternoon bike tour with Follow Me Bike Tour. 

Besides leading us through lush jungle trails and narrow elevated pathways on bikes, our local guide also shared many interesting insights into the customs and culture of the local Thai people. We enjoyed our bike tour immensely and would highly recommend this tour to anyone seeking a respite from the bustle of city life. 

Explore Bangkok like never before and discover Bangkok's best kept secrets.

description:
Explore Phuket's mesmerizing attractions, from the heartwarming Elephant Sanctuary to the serene Promthep Cape sunset. Dive into sea canoe adventures and uncover the beauty of this island paradise.

Discover Hidden Gems & Fall in Love with Every City - Your Ultimate Guide to Unforgettable Journeys: https://www.travelsandroadtrips.com/ 

If you are an animal lover, we highly recommend visiting Phuket Elephant Sanctuary. You will not get to ride on elephants, bathe with them, or watch them perform there. Instead, you will get to observe rescued elephants in their natural habitat. Phuket Elephant Sanctuary is an ongoing effort to rescue abused elephants from all over Thailand. Do support them when you visit Phuket. 

✅ Contact details:
www.Phuketelephantsanctuary.org 

One of the best days we had in Phuket was the day out at sea with John Gray’s Sea Canoe. We joined their Hong by Star Light tour and enjoyed every moment. The excursion was very well organized and was kid-friendly too. 

✅ Contact details:
www.johngray-seacanoe.com 

Finally, only a visit to Phuket is complete with visiting a few beaches. Due to time constraints, we only had time to visit 2 beaches. Our preferred one has to be Freedom Beach as it is quieter and cleaner. However, its location is rather secluded, and there is a small entrance fee to enter the beach. Patong Beach, by contrast, is really busy and very accessible. Do check them out for yourselves when you are in Phuket.

Join us for a thrilling adventure in Pahang, Malaysia! At Tanah Aina Farrah Soraya, we embarked on a guided jungle trek through vibrant rainforests and refreshing streams. The highlight? A daring leap from a 6-meter platform! This 2-hour trek was filled with challenges and fun, making it one of our top experiences. Dive into the heart of Pahang's nature with us!

Discover Hidden Gems & Fall in Love with Every City - Your Ultimate Guide to Unforgettable Journeys: https://www.travelsandroadtrips.com/ 

During our 2 day 1, night stay at Tanah Aina Farrah Soraya, we participated in this awesome guided jungle trek that brought us through lush rainforest and cold streams in the mountainous ranges of Pahang, and finally, a leap off a 6-meter platform!

The duration of this trek, including time for jumping off the platform and swimming in the natural waterfall, was about 2 hours. This trek is mildly challenging, involving some uphill walks, climbing over rocks, and wading through rocky streams. 

The changing terrains added to the fun, and we both agree that although it was just a short 2 hours, it was one of the best treks we have done so far.

description:
Our first day in PENANG, Malaysia surprised us! 🇲🇾 From George Town's incredible heritage streets and colourful temples to an unexpected FREE fire show on the beach, this wasn't quite the day we had planned! 🔥

After travelling from the Cameron Highlands, we finally arrived in George Town, Penang — a city famous for its history, culture and incredible food.

We started by exploring Armenian Street, searching for the famous street art and discovering some beautiful temples along the way. From there, we visited the historic Clan Jetties, wandered through Little India and explored the Sunday market at Hin Bus Depot.

With the Malaysian heat getting the better of us, we also took a break at our £25-a-night heritage hotel before heading out to Batu Ferringhi Beach for sunset.

And that's where things got interesting...

What started as a relaxed evening by the sea turned into one of the most unexpected experiences of our time in Malaysia, when we stumbled across an incredible fire show that was completely FREE to watch!

The night market wasn't quite what we'd hoped for, but we still managed to finish the day with some delicious food.

So, what did we really think of George Town and Penang on our first visit?

Join us for our first impressions as we explore another amazing part of Malaysia!

💬 Have you visited Penang? We'd love to know your favourite places, food recommendations or hidden gems in the comments!

After weeks travelling around some of the most beautiful islands in the Philippines, we leave Coron behind and head for Manila — and it feels like experiencing a completely different side of the country.

Getting there doesn't exactly go to plan. We tried to save some money by flying from Coron to Manila via Cebu, turning a simple journey into an all-day travel day… before Jason's bag suddenly disappeared at Cebu Airport.

description:
Can you pack 5 EPIC adventures into just 48 hours in Rotorua? 🇳🇿 From plunging down the world's highest rafted waterfall to exploring alien landscapes, this might be our craziest New Zealand itinerary yet!
We’re kicking off our 48 hours in Rotorua with having the stunning Waikite Valley Hot Pools entirely to ourselves after a night of camping. Once we dried off, we explored the extreme volcanic activity at the Wai-O-Tapu Thermal Wonderland—the neon colors here are unreal!
That evening, we experienced an unforgettable Maori Cultural evening at Te Pa Tu, learning the history, performing a Haka, and eating an absolute ton of incredible food. But the next day turned up the adrenaline... We took on the Kaituna River for a Grade 5 white water rafting experience, dropping down the highest rafted waterfall in the world! 🌊 Finally, we calmed our nerves with a visit to a local hatchery to spot the elusive, native Kiwi bird.
If you're planning a New Zealand road trip, Rotorua is an absolute must-visit.

description:
Join us for 72 hours on New Zealand's wettest coast! In this vlog, we take an epic West Coast New Zealand road trip from Makarora to the Pancake Rocks, battling the rain, road closures, and wild weather along the way.
We start the journey with a bit of drama at the Haast Pass, which was closed due to a truck blocking the bridge! Once the road opened, the heavy rain actually worked in our favor—making the waterfalls like Thunder Creek Falls and Fantail Falls absolutely massive.
The weather on the West Coast is unpredictable. We tried to spot Fox Glacier, but the rain had other plans. However, patience paid off! After camping at Franz Josef, the skies cleared the next morning for an epic view of the Franz Josef Glacier.
To wrap up this 3-day adventure, we explore the stunning blue waters of Hokitika Gorge, visit the famous Pancake Rocks at Punakaiki, and find an incredible free camping spot right on the beach at Fox River for sunset.

Sierra Gorda Biosphere Reserve (Querétaro)
Located in the north of the state of Querétaro, the Sierra Gorda Biosphere Reserve represents 32.02% of the total territory of the state.

This Protected Natural Area presents a great physiographic complexity with diverse heights ranging from 300 to 3,100 meters above sea level.

It is one of the best-preserved forested areas in the center of the country and contains one of the northernmost fragments of sub-deciduous tropical forest on the continent.

There are 1,724 reported species of flora and 124 species of fungi. As for fauna, Sierra Gorda has 23 reported species of amphibians, 72 of reptiles, 363 of birds, and 131 of mammals.

In 1987, the Sierra Gorda Queretana was designated a Biosphere Reserve to preserve and rehabilitate its ecosystems, promote and guide the orderly use of the natural components that allow their permanence for future generations, and achieve economic and social development for the inhabitants of the area.

Sierra Gorda Biosphere Reserve (Querétaro)
Located in the north of the state of Querétaro, the Sierra Gorda Biosphere Reserve represents 32.02% of the total territory of the state.

This Protected Natural Area presents a great physiographic complexity with diverse heights ranging from 300 to 3,100 meters above sea level.

It is one of the best-preserved forested areas in the center of the country and contains one of the northernmost fragments of sub-deciduous tropical forest on the continent.

There are 1,724 reported species of flora and 124 species of fungi. As for fauna, Sierra Gorda has 23 reported species of amphibians, 72 of reptiles, 363 of birds, and 131 of mammals.

In 1987, the Sierra Gorda Queretana achieved the category of Biosphere Reserve to preserve and rehabilitate the ecosystems, induce and guide an orderly use of the natural components that allow its permanence for future generations, and achieve economic and social development for the inhabitants of the area.

description:
Phoenix dactylifera, commonly known as the date palm, is a flowering plant species in the palm family Arecaceae, native to the region from the Gulf States to India. It is cultivated for its sweet edible fruit, called dates. The species is widely cultivated across northern Africa, the Middle East, Australia, South and Southeast Asia, Portugal, Spain, the coastal Mediterranean basin, and the desert regions of Southern California. It is naturalised in many tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. P. dactylifera is the type species of the genus Phoenix, which contains 12–19 species of wild date palms.

Experience the beauty of Thailand’s date palm farming at Preecha Date Palm Garden and Coffee Shop in Bang Phlap, Pak Kret District, Nonthaburi. Discover premium fresh dates, learn about date palm cultivation, and enjoy a peaceful garden atmosphere just outside Bangkok. Visitors can explore the lush plantation, taste naturally sweet date fruits, capture stunning farm views, and relax at the garden café. A perfect destination for agriculture enthusiasts, families, photographers, and travelers seeking an authentic farm experience in Nonthaburi. Visit one of Thailand’s most popular date palm gardens and experience the charm of sustainable tropical farming.

Date palms reach up to 30 metres (98 ft) in height, growing singly or in clumps with several stems from a single root system. Slow-growing, they can reach over 100 years of age when maintained properly. Their fruit (dates) is oval-cylindrical, 3 to 7 centimetres (1 to 3 inches) long, and about 2.5 cm (1 in) in diameter, with colour ranging from dark brown to bright red or yellow, depending on variety. Containing 63–64% sugar by mass when dried, dates are consumed as sweet snacks on their own or with confections.

Phoenix dactylifera, commonly known as the date palm, is a flowering plant species in the palm family Arecaceae, native to the region from the Gulf States to India. It is cultivated for its sweet edible fruit, called dates. The species is widely cultivated across northern Africa, the Middle East, Australia, South and Southeast Asia, Portugal, Spain, the coastal Mediterranean basin, and the desert regions of Southern California. Their fruit (dates) is oval-cylindrical, 3 to 7 centimetres (1 to 3 inches) long, and about 2.5 cm (1 in) in diameter, with colour ranging from dark brown to bright red or yellow, depending on variety. Thai New Year or Songkran, also known as Songkran Festival or Songkran Splendours, is the Thai New Year's national holiday. Sierra Gorda Biosphere Reserve (Querétaro)
Located in the north of the state of Querétaro, the Sierra Gorda Biosphere Reserve represents 32.02% of the total territory of the state.

This Protected Natural Area presents a great physiographic complexity with diverse heights ranging from 300 to 3,100 meters above sea level.

It is one of the best-preserved forested areas in the center of the country and contains one of the northernmost fragments of sub-deciduous tropical forest on the continent.

There are 1,724 reported species of flora and 124 species of fungi. As for fauna, Sierra Gorda has 23 reported species of amphibians, 72 of reptiles, 363 of birds, and 131 of mammals.

In 1987, the Sierra Gorda Queretana achieved the category of Biosphere Reserve to preserve and rehabilitate the ecosystems, induce and guide an orderly use of the natural components that allow its permanence for future generations, and achieve economic and social development for the inhabitants of the area.

Patagonia National Park (Spanish: Parque Nacional Patagonia) is a national park in the Aysén Region of Chile. Once a private nature reserve operated as a public-access park; it was donated to the government of Chile by Tompkins Conservation in 2018.

The heart of the park is the Chacabuco Valley, an ecologically significant east-west valley that forms a pass over the Andes Mountains, resulting in a transition zone between the Patagonian steppe grasslands of Argentine Patagonia and the southern beech forests of Chilean Patagonia to the west. It is located between General Carrera Lake to the north and Cochrane Lake to the south and extends to the Argentine border to the east. The park contains a network of trails and campgrounds, as well as a visitor center.

Kinnarees, according to Thai mythology, were half-human, half-bird creatures that lived in Himmapan, a legendary forest in the Himalayas, which separated Heaven and Earth. Roman statues were typically realistic, detailed, and often designed to convey power, prestige, or divine association. They drew heavily from earlier Greek sculpture but leaned more toward verism—a style that emphasized lifelike, sometimes unflattering features, such as wrinkles, scars, and the signs of age, especially in portraits of politicians and military leaders.

Common characteristics include:

Materials: Marble and bronze were the most common, though cheaper works might use plaster or terracotta.

Subjects: Emperors, senators, generals, gods, and mythological figures. Roman portraiture was especially famous for capturing the individuality of the subject.

Function: They weren’t just decorative—statues served political and religious purposes, often displayed in forums, temples, and public squares to reinforce authority or commemorate victories.

Clothing & Poses: Figures might be shown in togas (for civilians), armor (for military leaders), or nude (for gods or idealized forms). Many were posed in contrapposto (a natural weight shift stance), a legacy from Greek art.

Color: Contrary to the white marble we see today, many Roman statues were originally painted in vibrant colors, though the pigments have mostly worn away.

In short, Roman statues combined Greek idealism with a Roman taste for realism and political messaging, creating art that was as much about public image as it was about beauty.

"Life for farmers in Thailand is deeply connected to the land, and clearing it is one of their toughest seasonal tasks. Many farmers still work by hand or with basic tools like machetes, hoes, and fire to clear weeds, bushes, and old crops before planting season. In rural areas, you’ll often see entire families working together under the hot sun, cutting down overgrowth, piling it up, and sometimes burning it to prepare fertile soil. The Old Man Cactus (Cephalocereus senilis) is a striking and iconic cactus native to the arid regions of eastern Mexico. Known for its long, white, hair-like spines that resemble a flowing beard, this cactus can live for decades and is admired for its unique appearance and slow growth. Its “hair” serves as protection from the harsh desert sun, helping to retain moisture and shield the plant from extreme temperatures.

The Old Man Cactus can grow up to 15–20 feet tall in the wild, forming a columnar shape with thick, ribbed stems. It blooms at night, producing small, creamy-white flowers when it reaches maturity, often after decades of growth. Perfect for desert gardens or as a striking indoor ornamental plant, this cactus symbolizes resilience, longevity, and the beauty of the Mexican desert landscape.

Whether you’re a collector of rare succulents or simply fascinated by desert flora, the Old Man Cactus is a must-see plant that captures the imagination with its furry, wise-looking appearance.

The Old Man Cactus is popular as a houseplant because of its striking, almost “cute and funny” look. It’s slow-growing, low-maintenance, and can be a lifelong companion plant.
Scientific name: Cephalocereus senilis

Common name: Old Man Cactus

Family: Cactaceae

Origin: Endemic to Mexico, especially the Hidalgo and Guanajuato regions.

Appearance: Tall, columnar cactus covered with long, white, wool-like hairs resembling an old man’s beard.

Growth & Characteristics

Height: Can grow up to 15 meters (50 feet) in the wild, but much smaller in pots (1–2 meters indoors over decades).

Stem: Cylindrical, ribbed, with sharp yellow spines hidden under the white hairs.

Hair: The long, silky hairs help protect it from harsh sun and cold nights in its native desert habitat.

Flowers: Rare in cultivation. In the wild, it produces pink to red tubular flowers at night, but usually only after decades of maturity..

Care & Growing Conditions

Light: Needs full sun to thrive. Indoors, place near the brightest window.

Temperature: Prefers warmth (18–26°C / 65–80°F). Can tolerate cooler temperatures but not frost.

Watering: Water sparingly. Let the soil dry completely between waterings. Overwatering can cause root rot.

Soil: Requires well-draining cactus or succulent soil mix. Add sand or perlite for extra drainage.

Fertilizer: Feed with cactus fertilizer during the growing season (spring–summer), monthly.

description:

Cleaning Off Food or Dirt

After eating fish, insects, or sea creatures, bits of food, slime, or sand can stick to the beak. Birds use their legs or feet to wipe it off, almost like using a napkin.

Removing Salt or Water Residue

Seabirds often get saltwater on their beaks. Wiping helps remove the salty film that could irritate them.

Comfort or Itch Relief

Sometimes birds scratch their beaks with their legs, the same way we scratch our faces—just to relieve an itch or irritation.

Maintaining Beak Sensitivity

Birds rely heavily on their beaks for feeding and sensing. Keeping the beak clean and free from debris ensures it stays sharp and sensitive.

Feeding Behavior

Some seabirds (like gulls, terns, cormorants, or even ducks) stir up small fish, plankton, or insects by swimming in circles. The movement makes prey easier to catch.

Play & Social Interaction

Birds are intelligent and often engage in play, just like dolphins or monkeys. Spinning around and splashing can be a form of entertainment, especially in young or social birds.

Bathing & Preening

By spinning and splashing water with their beaks, birds clean their feathers, wash off salt, and prepare for preening (oiling their feathers to stay waterproof).

Cooling Down

On hot days, water play helps regulate their body temperature. Dipping their heads and splashing water keeps them cool.

Territorial or Courtship Display

In some species, circular swimming with water play can be part of mating rituals or showing off strength to rivals.

description:
The Silkie chicken is believed to have originated in China more than a thousand years ago. 🐔✨

Historical records trace the breed back to Asia, with references in Chinese writings from the 13th century, and the famous explorer Marco Polo mentioned “a furry chicken” during his travels in Asia in the late 1200s.

From China, Silkies spread through Southeast Asia (particularly in places like India and Java) before making their way to Europe via the Silk Road trade routes. By the 18th century, they were well known in Europe and later introduced to North America.

So, their country of origin is China, but their history is deeply tied to the broader regions of Asia and the Silk Road.

description: The hammered dulcimer is a trapezoidal stringed instrument in which multiple courses of strings are stretched over a wooden soundboard and played by striking them with lightweight mallets, often called hammers. Originating in ancient Mesopotamia and spreading through Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, it has many regional variations such as the Persian santur, the Indian santoor, and the Chinese yangqin. The strings are arranged over small bridges that divide them into different pitch ranges, allowing for a wide melodic range and rich harmonics. Its bright, shimmering tone is well-suited for both rhythmic accompaniment and intricate melodic lines, making it a versatile instrument in folk, classical, and contemporary music traditions worldwide.

Panguipulli – A picturesque town in southern Chile’s Los Ríos Region, known for its stunning “Seven Lakes” area, framed by snow-capped volcanoes, lush forests, and the scenic Lake Panguipulli. It’s popular for ecotourism, hiking, and water activities.

Valdivia – The vibrant capital of the Los Ríos Region, famous for its riverside setting, German-influenced architecture, craft beer culture, and sea lions lounging along the waterfront. It’s a historic port city with a mix of colonial heritage and modern university life.
Rivers Flowing Through Panguipulli’s Waterscape
1. Fuy River
Originating near Puerto Fuy, the Fuy River drains Pirihueico Lake and flows south toward Neltume. There, it converges with the Neltume River to help form Panguipulli Lake. The river runs through the rich Valdivian rainforest and features scenic waterfalls like Salto La Leona and Salto Huilo-Huilo within the Huilo-Huilo Biological Reserve.
.
2. Llanquihue River
Formed by the confluence of the Neltume and Fui rivers, the Llanquihue River travels westward into Panguipulli Lake, contributing a significant portion of the lake’s inflow.
.
3. Enco River
Acting as the primary outlet, the Enco River drains Panguipulli Lake and carries its waters southward into Riñihue Lake. Notably, it flows from the lake’s eastern, more mountainous side—rather than the western lowlands—and winds past the impressive Mocho-Choshuenco volcano. This stretch is a popular destination for rafters and adventurers thanks to its clear, fast-moving waters.

Camphor Clay Pots on Koh Kret: A Glimpse into Tradition
Artisanal Heritage
Koh Kret, located in the Chao Phraya River of Nonthaburi Province, is celebrated for pottery crafted by the Mon community—descendants of migrant Mon people. Pottery is their signature vocation, passed down through generations and woven into local identity.

Distinctive Style & Technique
One notable style feature is red-and-black glazed surfaces and intricate designs characteristic of Mon craftsmanship.
These pots—often used as incense burners or decorative vessels—exhibit elegant perforations and ornate forms that combine functionality with artistry, as beautifully depicted in the images above.

Crafting Process & Community
Visitors to Koh Kret can witness pottery-making up close: artisans molding clay on wheels, engraving patterns by hand, and firing the pieces in traditional kilns. This craft is also championed under Thailand’s “One Tambon One Product” (OTOP) program, promoting local specialties across the country

What to Explore There
Pottery Village Stalls: Along the weekend market path, you’ll find stalls filled with handmade items—plates, cups, teapots, incense burners, and iconic charcoal-heated hotpot sets.

Cultural Immersion: Beyond pottery, you'll experience Mon culture, delicious local foods (like khao chae and Mon-style fritters), and peaceful riverside ambiance.

Worth a Visit?
Absolutely—especially if you're drawn to authentic handmade crafts and cultural experiences. Koh Kret offers a rare opportunity to purchase traditional pottery directly from the makers, supporting the community and acquiring one-of-a-kind souvenirs. As one Redditor noted:

“Koh Kret is famous for pottery, and you can do a basic class there. It’s a day trip … well worth it.”

description:
Roman statues were a blend of artistry, politics, and realism — essentially the ancient world’s Instagram feed, but carved in marble and bronze.

They often depicted gods, emperors, philosophers, generals, or idealized citizens. Unlike the earlier Greek tradition, which leaned toward perfect, youthful forms, Roman sculpture embraced verism — showing wrinkles, scars, and the unique features of the subject, especially in portraits of political leaders. This gave their busts a sense of realism and authority.

Many Roman statues were made of marble (often imported from Greece) or bronze (though bronze works rarely survive because they were melted down in later centuries). The style varied depending on the purpose.
In Buddhist art and mythology, kinnarees (Pali: kinnari, plural kinnarī) are graceful, mythical beings that are half-human, half-bird.

They typically have:

The upper body of a beautiful woman is often depicted with elegant features, long flowing hair, and delicate jewelry.

The lower body of a bird — usually shown with wings and birdlike legs or a feathery tail.

An aura of divine beauty and musical talent — kinnarees are often portrayed playing instruments or dancing in heavenly realms.

Origins & Role in Buddhist Tradition
Roots in Indian mythology: The concept comes from ancient Hindu epics, where kinnaras and kinnaris were celestial musicians serving the gods.

Buddhist adoption: In Theravāda Buddhist literature, they appear in the Jātaka tales (stories of the Buddha’s past lives), especially the Manohara Jātaka, where a kinnaree princess is a central character.

Symbolism: They represent grace, beauty, purity of heart, and devotion. Their gentle nature reflects metta (loving-kindness) and harmony with all beings.

Realms: Kinnarees are said to dwell in the mythical Himavanta forest at the foothills of Mount Meru, a cosmological mountain at the center of Buddhist and Hindu universes.

description:
Kinnaree Manorah was a princess of Thai legend, the youngest of the seven Kinnaree daughters of King Prathum and Queen Jantakinnaree. She lived in the mythical kingdom of Mount Grairat. The Seven Kinnaree appeared as half-woman half half-swan. They could fly or shed their wings to assume human form as they pleased.

In Buddhist mythology and Hindu mythology, a Kinnaree is a paradigmatic lover, a celestial musician, a half-human creature. Their character is clarified in the Adi Parva of the Mahabharata, where they say: We are everlasting lovers and beloved.

Roman statues were typically realistic, detailed, and often designed to convey power, prestige, or divine association. They drew heavily from earlier Greek sculpture but leaned more toward verism—a style that emphasized lifelike, sometimes unflattering features, such as wrinkles, scars, and the signs of age, especially in portraits of politicians and military leaders.

Common characteristics include:

Materials: Marble and bronze were the most common, though cheaper works might use plaster or terracotta.

Subjects: Emperors, senators, generals, gods, and mythological figures. Roman portraiture was especially famous for capturing the individuality of the subject.

Function: They weren’t just decorative—statues served political and religious purposes, often displayed in forums, temples, and public squares to reinforce authority or commemorate victories.

Clothing & Poses: Figures might be shown in togas (for civilians), armor (for military leaders), or nude (for gods or idealized forms). Many were posed in contrapposto (a natural weight shift stance), a legacy from Greek art.

Color: Contrary to the white marble we see today, many Roman statues were originally painted in vibrant colors, though the pigments have mostly worn away.

In short, Roman statues combined Greek idealism with a Roman taste for realism and political messaging, creating art that was as much about public image as it was about beauty.

tags: santiago de chile|santiago chile|visit chile|chile|chile travel|chile travel guide|chile tour|best places in chile|Parish of Santísimo Sacramento|The Church of the Sacramentino|National Votive Temple of the Blessed Sacrament|Church of the Blessed Sacrament
description:
The Church of the Sacramentinos or Parish of Santísimo Sacramento is a catholic temple located in the commune of Santiago, in the capital of Chile, in the corner of Arturo Prat and Santa Isabel. The architect Ricardo Larraín Bravo was in charge of the construction of the work; The design of this temple is inspired by the Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Paris, France. His style is neo-Byzantine.

In 1911, the construction of the crypt began,  which was inaugurated on June 15, 1919.  The following year, the upper part of the church was completed, which was handed over for partial use on March 22, 1931.

Overview & Significance
Name & Location
The church is officially called the Templo Votivo Nacional del Santísimo Sacramento, located at the corner of Arturo Prat and Santa Isabel (or alternatively Avenida Matta region) in Santiago’s central district. 

Religious Order
It's affiliated with the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament, founded by Saint Peter Julian Eymard in Paris in 1856. The first Sacramentinos arrived in Chile in 1908. 

Historical Motivation
Constructed as a national votive offering for Chile’s Centennial of Independence, this temple reflects both spiritual dedication and national pride. 

Architecture & Construction
Design & Architect
Designed by Chilean architect Ricardo Larraín Bravo in a Roman–Byzantine (Neo-Byzantine) style, the structure draws inspiration from the Sacré-Coeur Basilica in Paris. 
Timeline
Construction began around 1912; the crypt opened in 1919, and the upper church was inaugurated for partial use in March 1931. 

Structure & Materials
The building is notable for being the second in Chile to use reinforced concrete, featuring a large 1,500 m² crypt and a soaring central dome over the altar. 

Inside, you'll find parquet flooring, carved lingue wood furnishings (pulpit, confessionals, choir stalls) by Salesian workshop, stained glass from France, an altar from Argentina, and intricately crafted bronze doors with an inscription that reads, “I have chosen this place so that my heart may remain here.”

Roman statues were typically realistic, detailed, and often designed to convey power, prestige, or divine association. They drew heavily from earlier Greek sculpture but leaned more toward verism—a style that emphasized lifelike, sometimes unflattering features, such as wrinkles, scars, and the signs of age, especially in portraits of politicians and military leaders.

Common characteristics include:

Materials: Marble and bronze were the most common, though cheaper works might use plaster or terracotta.

Subjects: Emperors, senators, generals, gods, and mythological figures. Roman portraiture was especially famous for capturing the individuality of the subject.

Function: They weren’t just decorative—statues served political and religious purposes, often displayed in forums, temples, and public squares to reinforce authority or commemorate victories.

Clothing & Poses: Figures might be shown in togas (for civilians), armor (for military leaders), or nude (for gods or idealized forms). Many were posed in contrapposto (a natural weight shift stance), a legacy from Greek art.

Color: Contrary to the white marble we see today, many Roman statues were originally painted in vibrant colors, though the pigments have mostly worn away.

In short, Roman statues combined Greek idealism with a Roman taste for realism and political messaging, creating art that was as much about public image as it was about beauty.

title: The Memorial Pavilion That Honors Thailand's Tragic Queen Sunantha
tags: Bangkok|Thailand|Visit Thailand|Thailand tour guide|Thailand travel guide|Wat Ku|Wat Ku in Pak Kret|best places in Thailand.|Wat Phra Nang Rua Lom|Temples in Thailand|bangkok travel|thailand places to visit|travel thailand|nonthaburi thailand|thailand tourism
description:
Wat Ku is situated near the Chao Phraya River in Bang Pood Subdistrict, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi. The temple construction is of Mon architecture.

Wat Ku or Wat Phra Nang Rua Lom was built in 1752. It was formerly named Wat Lang Suan, but later, on May 31st, 1880, the royal yacht of Queen Sunantha Kumariratana, the first queen consort of King Rama V, passed by Bang Pa In, and the yacht sank, resulting in the deaths of Queen Sunantha Kumariratana and Queen Kannaporn Petchsopang.

Overview & Historical Significance
Origins & Architecture
Wat Ku was founded during the Thonburi era by Phraya Cheng (a Mon leader), reflecting Mon-style architecture and cultural heritage. Inside its old chapel, you'll find intricate mural paintings of the Mon tradition depicting scenes from the Buddha’s life 

Tragic Royal Connection
The temple is most well-known for its link to a sorrowful event: Queen Sunandha Kumariratana, consort of King Rama V, tragically drowned in the Chao Phraya River nearby while pregnant. At the time, strict laws prevented commoners from touching or aiding royalty, which ultimately contributed to the tragedy and were later repealed 

Memorial Pavilion & Relics
On the temple grounds is a memorial pavilion modeled after the Phra Thinang Aisawan Thippaya-Asana at Bang Pa-In Palace, built in remembrance of the Queen. The salvaged royal barge has been preserved in a structure beside the main hall, and a large reclining Buddha statue stands prominently inside the wihan (sanctuary)
.
Temporary Resting Place for Royal Remains
Wat Ku served as the temporary location where Queen Sunandha’s body was brought before being transported to the Grand Palace for lying-in-state. This event contributed to the temple’s name—“Ku,” meaning “to recover” or “to salvage,”—symbolizing both the recovery of the royal vessel and her remains.

It is believed to be most active at dusk and during the night.

description: A sala also known as a Sala Thai, is an open pavilion, used as a meeting place and to give people shade. With etymological roots in the Sanskrit sala, the word in Thai connotes buildings for specific purposes, such as sala klang ('provincial hall'). Most are open on all four sides. They are found throughout Thailand in Buddhist temple areas, or wats, although they can also be at other places. A person who builds a sala at a temple or in a public place gains religious merit. A sala located in a temple is called a salawat. Some temples have large salas where laity can hear sermons or receive religious instruction. These are called sala kan parian, meaning 'pavilion where monks learn for the Parian examination'. The city halls or offices of the province governors are called sala wa kan (ศาลาว่าการ, literally meaning 'government pavilion') or sala klang changwat  literally meaning a 'provincial main pavilion').

The Frauenkirche (IPA: [ˈfʁaʊənˌkɪʁçə], Church of Our Lady) is a Lutheran church in Dresden, the capital of the German state of Saxony. Destroyed during the Allied firebombing of Dresden towards the end of World War II, the church was reconstructed between 1994 and 2005.

The current structure is the third church building to stand at this site. The earliest was founded as a Catholic church before being converted to Protestantism during the Reformation. It was replaced in the 18th century by a larger Baroque Lutheran building. Considered an outstanding example of Protestant sacred architecture, it featured one of the largest domes in Europe. It was originally built as a sign of the will of the citizens of Dresden to remain Protestant after their ruler had converted to Catholicism. Having been reconstructed, it now also serves as a symbol of reconciliation between former warring enemies.

description:
Buda Castle (Hungarian: Budavári Palota, German: Burgpalast) is the historical castle and palace complex of the Hungarian Kings in Budapest. It was first completed in 1265, although the massive Baroque palace today occupying most of the site was built between 1749 and 1769. The complex in the past was referred to as either the Royal Palace (Hungarian: Királyi-palota) or the Royal Castle (Hungarian: Királyi Vár, German: Königliche Burg). The castle now houses the Hungarian National Gallery and the Budapest Historical Museum.

Buda Castle sits on the southern tip of Castle Hill, surrounded by the touristic area known as Várnegyed (Castle Quarter), which is famous for its Medieval, Baroque, and Neoclassical houses, churches, public buildings, and monuments. The hill is linked to Clark Ádám Square and the Széchenyi Chain Bridge by the Castle Hill Funicular. The castle is a part of the Budapest World Heritage Site, so declared in 1987. The original Royal Palace was ruined during World War II; it was rebuilt in a simplified Stalinist Baroque style during the Kádár era.

description:
The Fairmont Le Château Frontenac, commonly referred to as the Château Frontenac, is a historic hotel in Quebec City, Quebec, Canada. The hotel is situated in Old Quebec, within the historic district's Upper Town, on the southern side of Place d'Armes. The Château Frontenac was designed by Bruce Price and was built by the Canadian Pacific Railway company. The hotel is managed by Fairmont Hotels and Resorts.

Opened in 1893, the Châteauesque-styled building has 18 floors; its 79.9-metre (262-foot) height is augmented by its 54-metre (177-foot) ground elevation. It is one of the first completed grand railway hotels and was designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 1981.  The hotel was expanded on three occasions, with the last major expansion taking place in 1993.

description:
The Frauenkirche (IPA: [ˈfʁaʊənˌkɪʁçə], Church of Our Lady) is a Lutheran church in Dresden, the capital of the German state of Saxony. Destroyed during the Allied firebombing of Dresden towards the end of World War II, the church was reconstructed between 1994 and 2005.

The current structure is the third church building to stand at this site. The earliest was founded as a Catholic church before being converted to Protestantism during the Reformation. It was replaced in the 18th century by a larger Baroque Lutheran building. Considered an outstanding example of Protestant sacred architecture, it featured one of the largest domes in Europe. It was originally built as a sign of the will of the citizens of Dresden to remain Protestant after their ruler had converted to Catholicism. Having been reconstructed, it now also serves as a symbol of reconciliation between former warring enemies.

title: This 12th Century Swiss Castle Has an Incredible Secret | Thun Castle
tags: Google Earth Studio|Google|Google Map|List of castles in the world|Most beautiful castle in the world|Swiss canton of Bern|Thun Castle in the city of Thun|Thun Castle|Swiss|castle in Swiss|Thun City|Thun|medieval castle
description:
Thun Castle (German: Schloss Thun) is a castle in the city of Thun, in the Swiss canton of Bern. It was built in the 12th century, today houses the Thun Castle museum and is a Swiss heritage site of national significance.

History
During the Early Middle Ages, there was a small fort and church on the top of the castle hill. The castle was built between 1180 and 1190 by Duke Berthold V of Zähringen, who constructed the still-preserved keep to the level of the Knights' Hall (German: Rittersaal). The 14 m tall Knights' Hall was built as the centerpiece of a monument to Zähringen power. However, the family never lived in the castle, preferring Burgdorf Castle. In 1218 it was inherited by the House of Kyburg, who built the upper levels above the Zähringen castle. A quarrel over who would rule the southern Kyburg lands led, in 1322, to Eberhard II von Kyburg murdering his brother Hartmann II at the castle. To protect his newly acquired land from the Habsburgs Eberhard II then sold them to Bern and was promptly given them back as a fief. The Kyburgs ruled over the region for nearly two centuries until a failed raid by Rudolf II on Solothurn, in 1382, started the Burgdorferkrieg (also Kyburgerkrieg). After several decisive Bernese victories the Kyburgs were forced to concede an unfavorable peace. In 1384 Bern bought Thun and Burgdorf, the most important cities of the Kyburg lands. The castle came under Bernese control and became the seat of their local administration.

description:
The Cathedral Basilica of Christ the King is a Roman Catholic church in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. The cathedral was consecrated on December 19, 1933. It is the seat of the bishop of the Diocese of Hamilton, and the cathedral of the Diocese of Hamilton. The cathedral contains the cathedra (bishop's chair) of the bishop, the Most Rev. Douglas Crosby. The cathedral was raised to the status of a minor basilica in February 2013 by Pope Benedict XVI.

On the south side of the bell tower is the cornerstone blessed by Bishop McNally, builder of the cathedral and fifth bishop of the diocese. It is a stone excavated from the Roman catacombs to symbolize the cathedral's unity with the ancient Christian church, the first generation after Christ. The cathedral is perched atop a hill overlooking Highway 403 leading in towards the rest of Hamilton and one travelling towards Oakville, Mississauga and Toronto. Christ the King Cathedral is close in proximity to the Hamilton-Wentworth Catholic District School Board administration offices, and the offices for the Diocese of Hamilton. The offices for the diocese are located just off to the side of the cathedral, next to the rectory.

Gamlehaugen is a Royal Castle in Bergen, Norway, and the residence of the Norwegian royal family in the city. Gamlehaugen has a history that goes as far back as the Middle Ages, and the list of previous owners includes many of the wealthiest men in Bergen. Today owned by the Norwegian state, the most recent private owner was Christian Michelsen, a politician and shipping magnate who later became the first prime minister of Norway after the dissolution of the union between Sweden and Norway. Michelsen commissioned the construction of the current main building at Gamlehaugen, where he would live for most of the rest of his life.

When Michelsen died in 1925, his closest friends and colleagues started a national fund-raising campaign that brought in enough money to allow the Norwegian state to purchase the property. The large English park was opened to the public the same year, and the ground floor of the house was opened as a museum two years later. Gamlehaugen has been the Norwegian royal family's residence in Bergen since 1927.

According to Elogius Kiburger, the author of the Strättliger Chronicle, in 933 the King of Burgundy, Rudolph II, built the castle. Portions of the current castle curtain walls and main tower were built during the 12th century and by the 13th century, the town of Spiez existed outside the castle walls. By 1280 the castle was listed as an Imperial fief under Vogt Richard de Corbières. In 1289 the Freiherr von Strättligen was co-owner of the castle along with a succession of other noble families. The Palace of the Parliament (Romanian: Palatul Parlamentului), also known as the House of the Republic (Casa Republicii) or People's House/People's Palace (Casa Poporului), is the seat of the Parliament of Romania, located atop Dealul Spirii in Bucharest, the national capital. The Palace reaches a height of 84 m and has a floor area of 365,000 m2 (3,930,000 sq and a volume of 2,550,000 m3. The Palace of the Parliament is one of the heaviest buildings in the world, weighing about 4,098,500 tonnes (9.04 billion pounds), and also being the second-largest administrative building in the world.[3] The building was designed and supervised by chief architect Anca Petrescu, with a team of approximately 700 architects, and constructed over 13 years (1984–97) in modernist Neoclassical architectural forms and styles, with socialist realism in mind. The Palace was ordered by Nicolae Ceaușescu (1918–1989), the president of Communist Romania and the second of two long-ruling heads of state in the country since World War II, during a period in which the personality cult of political worship and adoration increased considerably for him and his family.

description:
The Altenburg is a castle that sits on the tallest of the seven hills of Bamberg, southern Germany, overlooking the town. It is located in Upper Franconia, a region in the state of Bavaria, and dates back to at least 1109.
The first mention of the Altenburg was in 1109, although it is likely that it was built on the spot of an earlier palisade castle.

It first served as what is known in German as a "Fliehburg". This is a castle that was not regularly inhabited but served mainly for city defense as a place where local residents could flee to in times of danger.

In 1553, during the Second Margrave War, the army of Albert Alcibiades, Margrave of Brandenburg-Kulmbach, burned the castle down. Afterward, the castle was used as a prison for a while.

In 1801, the Bamberg physician Adalbert Friedrich Marcus acquired the decaying castle and restored it from the ground up. The author E. T. A. Hoffmann, who was friends with Marcus, felt so drawn to the castle that he frequently stayed for a long time in one of the wall towers during the years 1808 to 1813.

description:
Craigmillar Castle is a ruined medieval castle in Edinburgh, Scotland. It is three miles (4.8 km) southeast of the city center, on a low hill to the south of the modern suburb of Craigmillar. The Preston family of Craigmillar, the local feudal barons, began building the castle in the late 14th century and building works continued through the 15th and 16th centuries. In 1660, the castle was sold to Sir John Gilmour, Lord President of the Court of Session, who breathed new life into the aging castle. The Gilmours left Craigmillar in the 18th century for a more modern residence, nearby Inch House, and the castle fell into ruin. It is now in the care of Historic Environment Scotland as a scheduled monument and is open to the public.

Craigmillar Castle is best known for its association with Mary, Queen of Scots. Following an illness after the birth of her son, the future James VI, Mary arrived at Craigmillar on 20 November 1566 to convalesce. Before she left on 7 December 1566, a pact known as the "Craigmillar Bond" was made, with or without her knowledge, to dispose of her husband Henry Stuart, Lord Darnley.

The Palace of Versailles French: château de Versailles is a former royal residence commissioned by King Louis XIV located in Versailles, about 19 kilometers (12 mi) west of Paris, France.

About 15,000,000 people visit the palace, park, or gardens of Versailles every year, making it one of the most popular tourist attractions in the world.

Louis XIII built a simple hunting lodge on the site of the Palace of Versailles in 1623. With his death came Louis XIV who expanded the château into the beginnings of a palace that went through several changes and phases from 1661 to 1715. It was a favorite residence for both kings and in 1682, Louis XIV moved the seat of his court and government to Versailles, making the palace the de facto capital of France. This state of affairs was continued by Kings Louis XV and Louis XVI, who primarily made interior alterations to the palace, but in 1789 the royal family and capital of France returned to Paris. For the rest of the French Revolution, the Palace of Versailles was largely abandoned and emptied of its contents, and the population of the surrounding city plummeted.

The London Eye, or the Millennium Wheel, is a cantilevered observation wheel on the South Bank of the River Thames in London. It is Europe's tallest cantilevered observation wheel and the most popular paid tourist attraction in the United Kingdom, with over three million visitors annually. It has made many appearances in popular culture.

The structure is 135 metres (443 ft) tall, and the wheel has a diameter of 120 metres (394 ft). When it opened to the public in 2000, it was the world's tallest Ferris wheel. Its height was surpassed by the 160 metres (525 ft) Star of Nanchang in 2006, the 165 metres (541 ft) Singapore Flyer in 2008, the 167 metres (548 ft) High Roller (Las Vegas) in 2014, and the 250 metres (820 ft) Ain Dubai in 2021. Supported by an A-frame on one side only, unlike these taller examples, the Eye is described by its operators as "the world's tallest cantilevered observation wheel". The Eye offered the highest public viewing point in London until it was superseded by the 245-metre-high (804 ft) observation deck on the 72nd floor of The Shard in early 2013.

The London Eye adjoins the western end of Jubilee Gardens (previously the site of the former Dome of Discovery), on the South Bank of the River Thames between Westminster Bridge and Hungerford Bridge beside County Hall, in the London Borough of Lambeth. The nearest tube station is Waterloo.

description:
The Castle, Newcastle, or Newcastle Castle is a medieval fortification in Newcastle upon Tyne, England, built on the site of the fortress that gave the City of Newcastle its name. The most prominent remaining structures on the site are the Castle Keep (the castle's main fortified stone tower, pictured below right), and the Black Gate, its fortified gatehouse.

Use of the site for defensive purposes dates from Roman times, when it housed a fort and settlement called Pons Aelius (meaning 'bridge of (Publius) Aelius (Hadrianus)' - the Roman emperor Hadrian), guarding a bridge over the River Tyne. Robert Curthose, eldest son of William the Conqueror, in 1080 built a wooden motte and bailey-style castle on the site of the Roman fort. Curthose built this 'New Castle upon Tyne' after he returned south from a campaign against Malcolm III of Scotland. Henry II built the stone Castle Keep between 1172 and 1177 on the site of Curthose's castle. Henry III added the Black Gate between 1247 and 1250. Nothing remains above the ground of the Roman fort or the original motte and bailey castle. The Keep is a Grade I listed building and a Scheduled Ancient Monument.

The Castle Keep and Black Gate pre-date the construction of the Newcastle town wall, construction of which started around 1265, and did not include it. The site of the keep is in the center of Newcastle and lies to the east of Newcastle station. The 75-foot (23 m) gap between the keep and the gatehouse is almost entirely filled by the railway viaduct that carries the East Coast Main Line from Newcastle to Scotland.

The Keep and Black Gate are now managed by the Old Newcastle Project under the Heart of the City Partnership as one combined visitor attraction, "Newcastle Castle".

description:
Lumley Castle is a 14th-century quadrangular castle at Chester-le-Street in the North of England, near the city of Durham, and a property of the Earl of Scarbrough. It is a Grade I listed building. It is currently a hotel.
It is named after its original creator, Sir Ralph Lumley, who converted his family manor house into a castle in 1389 after returning from wars in Scotland. However, after being implicated in a plot to overthrow Henry IV, he was imprisoned and ultimately executed, forfeiting his lands to the Earl of Somerset. In 1421 the ownership of the castle reverted to Sir Ralph Lumley's grandson, Thomas.

During the time of John Lumley, 1st Baron Lumley, he altered the windows of the castle to let more light in, installed a new fireplace in the great hall along with a lavabo of black and white marble, adorned by a pelican, which is the crest of the Lumley coat of the arms. On the accession of James VI and I as King of England in 1603, he journeyed from Edinburgh to London to take his new throne. On 13 April, en route from Newcastle upon Tyne to Durham, he stopped briefly at the castle as a guest of Lord Lumley. The King James Suite hotel room commemorates this connection with the king. However, the suite was previously the chapel; the king did not stay at Lumley overnight, instead traveling later that day and staying at Durham Castle.

Lincoln Castle is a major medieval castle constructed in Lincoln, England, during the late 11th century by William the Conqueror on the site of a pre-existing Roman fortress. The castle is unusual in that it has two mottes. It is one of only two such castles in the country, the other being at Lewes in East Sussex. Lincoln Castle remained in use as a prison and court into modern times and is one of the better-preserved castles in England; the Crown Courts continue to this day. It is open to the public most days of the week and possible to walk around the walls from which there are views of the castle complex, cathedral, the city, and surrounding countryside. Displayed within the castle is one of only four surviving exemplars of the Magna Carta of 1215. The castle is now owned by Lincolnshire County Council and is a scheduled monument.

description:
York Castle is a fortified complex in the city of York, England. It consists of a sequence of castles, prisons, law courts, and other buildings, which were built over the last nine centuries on the south side of the River Foss. The now ruined keep of the medieval Norman castle is commonly referred to as Clifford's Tower. Built originally on the orders of William I to dominate the former Viking city of Jórvík, the castle suffered a tumultuous early history before developing into a major fortification with extensive water defenses. After a major explosion in 1684 rendered the remaining military defenses uninhabitable, York Castle continued to be used as a jail and prison until 1929.

The first motte and bailey castle on the site was built in 1068 following the Norman conquest of York. After the destruction of the castle by rebels and a Viking army in 1069, York Castle was rebuilt and reinforced with extensive water defenses, including a moat and an artificial lake. York Castle formed an important royal fortification in the north of England.

In 1190, 150 local Jews were murdered in a pogrom in the timber castle keep; most of them died by suicide in order not to fall into the hands of the mob. Henry III rebuilt the castle in stone in the middle of the 13th century, creating a keep with a unique quatrefoil design, supported by an outer bailey wall and a substantial gatehouse. During the Scottish wars between 1298 and 1338, York Castle was frequently used as the center of royal administration across England, as well as an important military base of operations.

description:
Kenilworth Castle is a castle in the town of Kenilworth in Warwickshire, England, managed by English Heritage; much of it is still in ruins. The castle was founded during the Norman conquest of England; with development through to the Tudor period. It has been described by the architectural historian Anthony Emery as "the finest surviving example of a semi-royal palace of the later middle ages, significant for its scale, form and quality of workmanship".

Kenilworth played an important historical role: it was the subject of the six-month-long siege of Kenilworth in 1266, thought to be the longest siege in Medieval English history, and formed a base for Lancastrian operations in the Wars of the Roses. Kenilworth was the scene of the removal of Edward II from the English throne, the perceived French insult to Henry V in 1414 of a gift of tennis balls (said by John Strecche to have prompted the campaign that led to the Battle of Agincourt), and the Earl of Leicester's lavish reception of Elizabeth I in 1575. It has been described as "one of two major castles in Britain which may be classified as water-castles or lake-fortresses.

The castle was built over several centuries. Founded in the 1120s around a powerful Norman great tower, the castle was significantly enlarged by King John at the beginning of the 13th century. Huge water defenses were created by damming the local streams, and the resulting fortifications proved able to withstand assaults by land and water in 1266. John of Gaunt spent lavishly in the late 14th century, turning the medieval castle into a palace fortress designed in the latest perpendicular style. The Earl of Leicester then expanded the castle during his tenure in the 16th century, constructing new Tudor buildings and exploiting the medieval heritage of Kenilworth to produce a fashionable Renaissance palace.

tags: Google Earth Studio|Google|Google Map|Windsor Castle is a royal residence at Windsor in England|Windsor Castle|Britain|British|England|King Charles|Queen Elizabeth|Castles in England|Most beautiful castle in the world|Visit England|Best royal castle|London|The Tower of London|Arundel Castle|Arundel|english castles|united kingdom|travel guide|google earth studio tutorial
description:
Arundel Castle is a restored and remodeled medieval castle in Arundel, West Sussex, England. It was established by Roger de Montgomery in the 11th century. The castle was damaged in the English Civil War and then restored in the 18th and early 19th centuries by Charles Howard, 11th Duke of Norfolk. Further restoration and embellishment were undertaken in the 1890s by Charles Alban Buckler for the 15th Duke.

Since the 11th century, the castle has been the seat of the Earls of Arundel and the Dukes of Norfolk. It is a Grade I listed building.

History
The original structure was a motte-and-bailey castle. Roger de Montgomery was declared the first Earl of Arundel as the King granted him the property as part of a much larger package of hundreds of manors. Roger, who was a cousin of William the Conqueror, had stayed in Normandy to keep the peace there while William was away in England. He was rewarded for his loyalty with extensive lands in the Welsh Marches and across the country, together with one-fifth of Sussex (Arundel Rape). He began work on Arundel Castle in around 1067.

Between 1101 and 1102 the castle was besieged by the forces of Henry I after its holder Robert of Bellême rebelled.[5] The siege ended with the castle surrendering to the king.  The castle then passed to Adeliza of Louvain (who had previously been married to Henry I) and her husband William d'Aubigny. Empress Matilda stayed in the castle, in 1139.[4] It then passed down the d'Aubigny line until the death of Hugh d'Aubigny, 5th Earl of Arundel in 1243.[4] John Fitzalan then inherited jure matris the castle and honor of Arundel, by which, according to Henry VI's "admission" of 1433, he was later retrospectively held to have become de jure Earl of Arundel.

description:
Königstein Fortress (German: Festung Königstein), the "Saxon Bastille", is a hilltop fortress near Dresden, in Saxon Switzerland, Germany, above the town of Königstein on the left bank of the River Elbe. It is one of the largest hilltop fortifications in Europe and sits atop the table hill of the same name.

The 9.5-hectare (23-acre) rock plateau rises 240 metres (790 ft) above the Elbe and has over 50 buildings, some over 400 years old, that bear witness to the military and civilian life in the fortress. The rampart run of the fortress is 1,800 metres (5,900 ft) long with walls up to 42 metres (138 ft) high and steep sandstone faces. In the centre of the site is a 152.5-metre-deep (500 ft 4 in) well, which is the deepest in Saxony and second-deepest well in Europe.

The fortress, which for centuries was used as a state prison, is still intact and is now one of Saxony's foremost tourist attractions, with 700,000 visitors per year.
