description:
Palacio de La Moneda (Spanish: [paˈlasjo ðe la moˈneða], Coin Palace), or simply La Moneda, is the seat of the President of the Republic of Chile. It also houses the offices of three cabinet ministers: Interior, General Secretariat of the Presidency and General Secretariat of the Government. It occupies an entire block in downtown Santiago, in the area known as Civic District between Moneda (North Side), Morandé (East), Alameda del Libertador Bernardo O'Higgins (South) and Teatinos street (West).

La Moneda, originally a colonial mint (Moneda means coin), was designed by Italian architect Joaquín Toesca.[1] Construction began in 1784 and was opened in 1805,[1] while still under construction. The production of coins in Chile took place at La Moneda from 1814 to 1929.
In June, 1845 during president Manuel Bulnes's administration, the palace became the seat of government and presidential residence. In 1930, a public square —named Plaza de la Constitución ("Constitution Square")— was built in front of the palace. After the presidency ofGabriel González Videla it ceased to serve as a presidential residence.

description:
The Metropolitan Cathedral of Santiago (Spanish: Catedral Metropolitana de Santiago) is the seat of the Archbishop of Santiago de Chile, currently Ricardo Ezzati Andrello, and the center of the archdiocese of Santiago de Chile. Construction of the neoclassical cathedral began in 1748 and ended in 1800; further alterations ordered at the end of the 19th century give it its present appearance.  
The cathedral, located in the city's historic center, faces Santiago's Plaza de Armas and stands near the Palacio Arzobispal de Santiago, the administrative center for the archdiocese. The cathedral is also close to the Parroquia El Sagrario, a Catholic temple and a Chilean national monument.

title: Costanera Center the Amazing earthquake proof building ever built, Chile
tags: Costanera Center (Building Complex)|Chile (Country)|Tourist Destination|Tourism (Interest)|Earthquake (Disaster Type)|chile tourism|chile travel information|chile trip|chile travel packages|chile travel|chile travel advisory|chile travel blog|chile points of interest
description:
The Costanera Center is a business and commercial complex that includes a six-floor shopping mall, the Gran Torre Santiago and three other skyscrapers - two high-end hotels and an office building. The complex is located in the commune of Providencia, Santiago, Chile, and is owned by the holding Cencosud. The tallest of the four buildings, the Gran Torre Santiago, was designed by architect César Pelli and is 300 metres (980 ft) tall, making it the tallest building in Latin America and the second tallest in the Southern Hemisphere after Australia's Q1 on the Gold Coast at 322 metres (1,056 ft) tall. Of the two other buildings in the complex, one will be 170 metres (560 ft) high and the other only four stories.
Construction was put on hold in January 2009 as a consequence of the late 2000s recession, as the developers were concerned that they would not be able to find tenants if completed by the originally proposed date. After the recession reached its end, Cencosud announced the construction would resume on December 16, 2009.
The construction process restarted at the end of 2010. On February 14, 2012, the Gran Torre Santiago reached 300 meters and became the tallest building in South and Latin America.

The tallest of the four buildings, the Gran Torre Santiago, was designed by architect César Pelli and is 300 metres (980 ft) tall, making it the tallest building in Latin America and the second tallest in the Southern Hemisphere after Australia's Q1 on the Gold Coast at 322 metres (1,056 ft) tall. Of the two other buildings in the complex, one will be 170 metres (560 ft) high and the other only four stories.
Construction was put on hold in January 2009 as a consequence of the late 2000s recession, as the developers were concerned that they would not be able to find tenants if completed by the originally proposed date. After the recession reached its end, Cencosud announced the construction would resume on December 16, 2009.
The construction process restarted at the end of 2010. On February 14, 2012, the Gran Torre Santiago reached 300 meters and became the tallest building in South and Latin America.

title: Cementerio General in Santiago, Chile (Final Resting Place)
tags: Cementerio General De Santiago (Location)|Chile (Country)|Santiago (City/Town/Village)|chile tourism|chile travel information|chile trip|chile travel packages|chile travel|chile travel advisory|chile travel blog|chile points of interest
description:
The Cementerio General de Santiago, Chile is one of the largest cemeteries in Latin America with an estimated 2 million burials. The cemetery was established in 1821 after Chile's independence when Bernardo O'Higgins inaugurated the Alameda de las Delicias along the old course of the Mapocho River. O'Higgins set aside more than 85 hectares of land for the foundation of what became a magnificent grounds filled with ornate mausoleums surrounded by palm and leaf trees set amidst lush gardens and numerous sculptures, which have been estimated be 237. The cemetery, which is located northwest of Cerro Blanco, serves as a true urban park for Santiago.

This cemetery is the final resting place for at least 172 of the most influential people in Chile,[1] including all but two of the deceased Presidents of Chile, the exceptions being Gabriel González Videla and Augusto Pinochet. One of the most visited memorials is that of former President Salvador Allende who had been buried in the Santa Ines cemetery at Viña del Mar following his suicide in the 1973 coup d'état. With the democratic changes that began in the 1990s, Allende was exhumed and his remains were transported in a solemn procession through the streets of Santiago to a place of honor in the Cementerio General de Santiago. The cemetery also has a memorial to the people that were 'disappeared' during the regime of Augusto Pinochet that ousted President Allende.

The gatehouse that serves as the main entrance to the cemetery is crowned by a dome, which acts as a terminating vista for La Paz Avenue. This entrance is preceded by the Plaza La Paz, a semicircular plaza whose curved portion is framed by two exposed brick arcades. At the center of the square stands a monument dedicated to the people who died in the Church of the Company Fire. The cemetery can be accessed via Cementerios metro station.

The historical portion of the cemetery was designated as a national monument in 2010, reaching the same status as Patio 29.

description:
Señor de los Milagros/ Lord of Miracles
This religious festival is relatively new in our country and has been established by numerous Peruvian colony resident of the capital. Following the tradition of the same procession held in Lima from 1687, wearing purple robes and a thick white cord around his neck, the guild takes on a stretcher painting a replica of the Lord of Miracles Pachacamilla one hand and on the other that of Our Lady of the Cloud, to the Italian parish of Bustamante Park. During the trip from Santiago Cathedral, the walk is preceded by a large group of sahumadoras and brass band that plays music features.
Lord of Miracles
Mural of the Señor de los Milagros painted in Sanctuary of Las Nazarenas at Lima in Perú
Lord of Miracles (in Spanish: Señor de los Milagros de Nazarenas) is an image painted of Jesus Christ that is venerated in Lima, Peru. The image was painted during the 17th century by an unnamed African taken from what is now Angola to Peru as a slave. Its feast is the main Catholic celebration in Peru and one of the largest processions in the world.

Description and feast
Christ is shown enduring the pain of crucifixion. Above the cross is the Holy Spirit and God the Father. Below and to the right of Jesus is his mother, the Virgin Mary with her heart pierced by a metaphorical sword of sorrow. Kneeling and weeping at the foot of the cross is St. Mary Magdalene.
Its name originated in the 17th century during an earthquake, which destroyed most of the city leaving only that mural standing. This is considered a miraculous occurrence by many living there.
Every year in October, hundreds of thousands of devotees from all races and economic backgrounds participate in a religious procession honouring the image through the streets of Lima. Boulevards are decorated in purple on October 18, 19, and 28 to celebrate the Lord of Miracles.

description:
The Votive Temple of Maipú or Basilica of Our Lady of Carmen is a Catholic church ordered to be built by Captain General and Supreme Director Bernardo O'Higgins , to acknowledge that and to fulfill the mandates that made ​​the Virgen del Carmen , because victory the Army of Chile by the Army of the Andes in the plains of Maipu , which ensured the independence of Chile.

Votive was called because of the votes that made ​​O'Higgins to the Virgin. After its construction decreed May 7 of 1818 , one on 15 November the same year was placed and blessed the first stone of the Chapel of Victory or Votive Church of Maipu. The Canon Madariaga Sunday Errázuriz was the first superintendent of the building until his death in 1819 . In April 1892, one after sixty-four years of intermittent construction due to lack of resources, the old church was solemnly opened. But in 1906 , a violent earthquake and then a tremor necessitated rebuilding the temple. On December 8 of 1942 , the Marian Congress held in Santiago, took sole agreement of this meeting to build a great shrine in Maipu, on the grounds of the former Chapel of the Victoria to honor the Virgen del Carmen.

Thus, the July 16 of 1948 the Archbishop of Santiago , and later Cardinal , Monsignor José María Caro sent begin construction of the new sanctuary. The winning design was the Chilean Juan Martinez Gutiérrez . During the long years of the construction of the current temple, Catholic groups, like young church or clandestine, opposed to the construction of that work, because it was rated a luxury, and proposed giving the money invested in that building for most people poor, both the archdiocese and the rest of the country. This group was led by Leonardo Jeffs gave anonymous and various media interviews.

The work delayed due to lack of resources but finally the 24 October of 1974 , and thanks to Vote O'Higgins National Foundation (which depends on the shrine today), solemnly inaugurated the Votive Temple of Maipú Carmen street, right where it intersects with the April 5th Avenue , next to the avenue Camino Rinconada .

Initially, the project mainly by the government, was to transform this place into a large mausoleum where to rest the remains of the Heroes of the Fatherland and the most notorious, like the Chilean Pantheon in Paris , but the Church owns the land by express grant its owner until the decade of the 40 ', opposed to this initiative and preferred to turn it into a shrine , dedicated to Catholic worship and spiritual care of pilgrims. The Archbishop of Santiago entrusted his attention to the Fathers of Schoenstatt , its first rector the RP Joaquin Alliende.

On November 23 of that year, the Bishops of Chile, presided over by the Cardinal Archbishop of Santiago Archbishop Raul Silva Henriquez consecrated the Temple. This is how the Sanctuary began operating for parishioners to surrender cult to the image of the Virgin of Carmen. .

tags: santa rita casia|church in chile|Santa Rita chile|Rita Of Cascia (Deceased Person)|Chile (Country)|chile tourism|chile travel information|chile trip|chile travel packages|chile travel|chile travel advisory|chile travel blog|chile points of interest
description:
Saint Rita of Cascia (Born Margherita Lotti 1381 - May 22, 1457) was an Italian Augustinian nun, widow, and saint venerated in the Roman Catholic Church. Rita was married at an early age. The marriage lasted for eighteen years, during which she is remembered for her Christian values as a model wife and mother who made efforts to convert her husband from his abusive behavior. Upon the murder of her husband by another feuding family, she sought to dissuade her sons from revenge before their calamitous deaths.

She subsequently joined an Augustinian community of religious sisters, where she was known both for practicing mortification of the flesh[1] and for the efficacy of her prayers. St. Rita is venerated due to various miracles attributed to her intercession, and is often portrayed with a bleeding wound on her forehead, which the Roman Catholic Church states she experienced as a partial stigmata.

The Roman Catholic Church, under the pontificate of Pope Leo XIII, officially canonized Rita on May 24, 1900, while her feast day is celebrated every May 22. At her canonization ceremony, she was bestowed the title of Patroness of Impossible Causes, while in many pious Catholic countries, Rita came to be known to be as patroness for abused wives and heartbroken women.

description:
The Basilica de la Merced is a basilica located in Santiago, Chile. It was founded by the Order of the Blessed Virgin Mary of Mercy and constructed in 1795. It is a Chilean National Monument.
It is Neo-Renaissance in architecture and has a small museum with religious objects and art, including a collection of pieces from Easter Island. The collection includes a rongorongo tablet, one of 29 left in the world,

The brothers (monks) of the Order of Mercy and Mercy, arrived in Santiago de Chile with Pedro de Valdivia in 1541, but seven years later established in Chile, by way of thanks the Governor Rodrigo de Quiroga donated to the Congregation Ermita del Socorro , located on the south side of Avenida Libertador General Bernardo O'Higgins , where it is now the Church of San Francisco .

description:
The Metropolitan Cathedral of Santiago (Spanish: Catedral Metropolitana de Santiago) is the seat of the Archbishop of Santiago de Chile, currently Ricardo Ezzati Andrello, and the center of the archdiocese of Santiago de Chile. Construction of the neoclassical cathedral began in 1748 and ended in 1800; further alterations ordered at the end of the 19th century give it its present appearance. Previous cathedrals in the archdiocese had been destroyed by earthquakes.

The cathedral, located in the city's historic center, faces Santiago's Plaza de Armas and stands near the Palacio Arzobispal de Santiago, the administrative center for the archdiocese. The cathedral is also close to the Parroquia El Sagrario, a Catholic temple and a Chilean national monument.

title: View from san santa lucia hill in Santiago, Chile
tags: Santa Lucía Hill (Location)|Santiago (City/Town/Village)|Chile (Country)|santa lucia chile|chile tourism|chile travel information|chile trip|chile travel packages|chile travel|chile travel advisory|chile travel blog|chile points of interest
description:
Santa Lucía Hill (Spanish: Cerro Santa Lucía) is a small hill in the centre of Santiago, Chile. It is situated between Alameda del Libertador Bernardo O'Higgins in the south, Santa Lucía Street in the west and Victoria Subercaseaux on the east. An adjacent metro station is named after it. The hill has an altitude of 629 m and a height of 69 m over the surrounding area. The hill is the remnant of a volcano 15 million years old.
The hill comprises a 65,300 square metre park adorned with ornate facades, stairways and fountains. At the highest point there is a viewpoint popular with tourists visiting the city.
It was originally called Huelén by the pre-colonization inhabitants. However, the current name comes from the day in which Pedro de Valdivia conquered the hill, on December 13, 1541. That day celebrates "Santa Lucía."
Its first use by its conquerors was as a point of reconnaissance, or a lookout in the years of the Conquista (1541).
In 1816, the Brigadier of the Royal Engineers Manuel Olaguer Feliú, proceeded to draw and build on the Santa Lucía Hill, two forts or castles, one north and another south of the hill, built of stone and lime and able to put eight or twelve cannons each. Besides, Olaguer Feliú drew and built an outbuilding for ammunition depot and to house the garrison.
On one side of the hill, Fort Hidalgo was finished in 1820 as a defensive point. On the other side, the hillside terrain was used as a "cemetery for the dissidents", people who did not follow the then-official Roman Catholic faith, or were considered otherwise unworthy of burial at hallowed grounds. However, the remains buried in the hillside under this fashion were eventually transferred to a secluded section of the General Cemetery, before said cemetery, in turn, was opened to all burials regardless of creed or social condition.
In 1872 Benjamín Vicuña Mackenna decided to conduct a dramatic change to the urban atmosphere of the city of Santiago, among his many works aimed to improve the city, and thus initiated an extensive remodelation of the hill. The works of 1872 consisted of a road which crossed the hill, which at the top accessed a chapel which he also built there, illuminated by the then-novel means of gas. The rest of the hill contains a park with fountains and lookouts. The actual hill is watered by a sophisticated irrigation system. The now iconic yellow and white facade is also a product of Vicuña Mackenna's remodelation.
Vicuña Mackenna was assisted in realizing his designs by the architect Manuel Aldunate, the constructor Enrique Henes, and the stonecutter Andrés Staimbuck.
A few years ago, Santa Lucía hill received an improvement in its illumination system and protections. Also, Fort Hidalgo was restored and reopened to the public. Traditionally, a cannon shot is fired exactly at noon.

description:
The oldest church in Santiago, Iglesia de San Francisco

The San Francisco Church (Spanish: Iglesia de San Francisco) is a Franciscan church on Avenida Libertador General Bernardo O'Higgins, in the downtown of Santiago de Chile. The church, along with the adjacent convent, has the distinction of being the oldest colonial-era building in the country.
The church was consecrated in 1622. The bell tower was destroyed by an earthquake in 1647, while the rest of the building successfully resisted it. In 1730 another earthquake badly damaged the rebuilt tower, which was demolished in 1751. The current bell tower is of Victorian architecture and was constructed in the mid-1800s. Its architect was Fermín Vivaceta and features a distinctive clock.
In the early years of the 20th century, a part of the convent was sold and demolished to build the Barrio París-Londres. The other part is the current home of the Museo Colonial.

description: Chile's first national hero was the conquistador Pedro de Valdivia (1500?–53), who founded Santiago in 1541. The Indian leader Lautaro (1525–57), another national hero, served Valdivia as stable boy and then escaped to lead his people to victory against the Spanish. His exploits are celebrated in the great epic poem La Araucana by Alonso de Ercilla y Zúñiga (1533?–96), a Spanish soldier. Bernardo O'Higgins (1778–1842), a leader of the fight for independence, was the son of the Irish soldier of fortune Ambrosio O'Higgins (1720?–1801), who had been viceroy of Peru. Diego Portales (1793–1837) helped build a strong central government. Admiral Arturo Prat (1848–79) is Chile's most revered naval hero because of his exploits during the War of the Pacific. Arturo Alessandri Palma (1868–1950), who became president in 1921, initiated modern sociopolitical reform. Salvador Allende Gossens (1908–73), the Western Hemisphere's first freely elected Marxist head of state, served three years as Chile's president (1970–73), initiating a broad range of socialist reforms and dying in the throes of a violent military coup in September 1973. The coup's leader was Gen. Augusto Pinochet Ugarte (b.1915), a former commander-in-chief of the army. Outstanding church figures have been Crescente Errázuriz (1839–1931), archbishop of Santiago, and his successor, José Cardinal Caro (1866–1958). Benjamin A. Cohen (1896–1960) was an undersecretary of the United Nations.

description:
Chile Independence Day: September 18

Chile celebrates Independence Day as a public holiday.

Every year on September 18, Chile celebrates the Independence Day to commemorate its freedom from Spanish rule.


History of Chile Independence Day

Ferdinand Magellan was the first European to visit what is now Chile. In 1535, Spain completed its invasion of Peru under Francisco Pizarro. Diego de Almagro, one of Pizarro’s aides, went into Chile to look for gold. The gold-hunting expedition spent nearly three years without any and then later withdrew to Peru.

In 1540, another of Pizarro’s officers, Pedro de Valdivia, led a second expedition into southern Chile. Valdivia succeeded in establishing several settlements despite fierce resistance from the Araucanians. The only Native American people who were not immediately subdued by the Spanish attack were the Araucanians.

In the Spanish colonial era, Chile developed slowly, because it had neither important silver or gold deposits to interest the Spanish nor natives who were willing to do hard labor. Furthermore, it was far from the main centers of Spanish colonization in Peru. Chile supplied Peru with agricultural products, especially wheat.

In 1810, Chile took the opportunity free itself from Spanish rule when they learned that the king of Spain had been forced out by Napoleon I of France . On September 18 of that year. The Santiago town council overthrew the colonial governor of Chile on September 18, 1810. This marked the formal establishment of Chile’s independence from Spain. After four years, the Spanish viceroy of Peru reclaimed Chile. Nevertheless, the yearning for independence was already strong.

title: Costanera Center is the tallest building in South and Latin Amarica
tags: Building (Site Listing Category)|Costanera Center (Building Complex)|Tower|History Of The Tallest Buildings In The World|Costanera center|chile tourism|chile travel information|chile trip|chile travel packages|chile travel|chile travel advisory|chile travel blog|chile points of interest
description:
The Costanera Center is a business and commercial complex that includes a six-floor shopping mall, the Gran Torre Santiago and three other skyscrapers - two high-end hotels and an office building. The complex is located in the commune of Providencia, Santiago, Chile, and is owned by the holding Cencosud. The tallest of the four buildings, the Gran Torre Santiago, was designed by architect César Pelli and is 300 metres (980 ft) tall, making it the tallest building in Latin America and the second tallest in the Southern Hemisphere after Australia's Q1 on the Gold Coast at 322 metres (1,056 ft) tall. Of the two other buildings in the complex, one will be 170 metres (560 ft) high and the other only four stories.
Construction was put on hold in January 2009 as a consequence of the late 2000s recession, as the developers were concerned that they would not be able to find tenants if completed by the originally proposed date. After the recession reached its end, Cencosud announced the construction would resume on December 16, 2009.
The construction process restarted at the end of 2010. On February 14, 2012, the Gran Torre Santiago reached 300 meters and became the tallest building in South and Latin America.

title: Cable car ride to San Cristóbal Hill, Santiago, Chile
tags: Cerro San Cristóbal|Santiago (City/Town/Village)|San Cristóbal Hill (Tourist Attraction)|Cable Car|Chile (Country)|chile tourism|chile travel information|chile trip|chile travel packages|chile travel|chile travel advisory|chile travel blog|chile points of interest
description:
Cerro San Cristóbal (San Cristóbal Hill) is a hill in central-northern Santiago, Chile. It rises 880 m. AMSL and about 300 m. above the rest of Santiago; the peak is the second highest point in the city, 

after Cerro Renca. Cerro San Cristóbal was named by the Spanish-Chilean San Cristóbal family, although its original name is Tupahue (Mapudungun: place of god or gods). The San Cristóbal family held a quarry on the hill's south side, close to the Mapocho River. 

Limestone from the quarry was used in the building of the first containments of the Mapocho River and also in the construction of its bridges. San Cristobal is one of the main hills that make up Santiago's Metropolitan Park.

Cerro San Cristóbal began to be used within academic-scientific purposes in 1903 with the installation of the Mills Observatory, currently known as the Manuel Foster Observatory, twin of the Lick Observatory of the University of California.

On its summit there is a sanctuary dedicated to the Immaculate Conception, with a 22 meter statue of the Blessed Virgin Mary, an amphitheater and a chapel. The statue of the Immaculate Conception measures 14 meters tall, and the pedestal on which it rests is 8.3 meters in height. It weighs 36,610 kilograms.[2] Within the pedestal there is a small chapel in which Pope John Paul II prayed and blessed the city of Santiago on April 1, 1987. The statue is lit up at night by lights placed on its sides, allowing it to be viewed from all over Santiago both day and night.
At the foot of the statue there is an amphitheater for holding masses or other religious ceremonies. Near the statue, there is also a small chapel for praying.

At the foothills of Cerro San Cristóbal are the Chilean National Zoo and a Japanese-style garden, and up there are also two municipal pools, Tupahue and Antilén.

Cerro San Cristóbal houses Santiago's largest public park: the Santiago Metropolitan Park (Parque Metropolitano).

description:
Frankfurt Cathedral (German: Frankfurter Dom, officially Kaiserdom Sankt Bartholomäus) is a Roman Catholic Gothic church located in the centre of Frankfurt am Main, Germany. It is dedicated to Saint Bartholomew.

The cathedral is the largest religious building in the city and a former collegiate church. As former election and coronation church of the Holy Roman Empire, the cathedral is one of the major buildings of the Empire history and was mainly in the 19th century a symbol of national unity.

The present church building is the third church in the same place. Since the late 19th excavated century buildings can be traced back to the 7th century. The history is closely linked with the General history of Frankfurt and the Frankfurt old town because the cathedral had an associated role as religious counterpart of the Royal Palace Frankfurt.

tags: Luang Pu Thuat (Deceased Person)|Songkhla (Administrative Division)|Thailand (Country)|Prem Tinsulanonda (Politician)|luang pu thuat Thailand|Luang pu Thuat songkhla|Thailand tourism|Thailand travel information|Thailand trip|Bangkok travel packages|Bangkok travel|Thailand Trave|Thailand travel advisory|Thailand travel blog|Thailand points of interest
description:
This memorial Statue of Luang Pu Thuat was officially opened at Songkhla on 3rd February 2015 after nearly a year of construction.

Luang Pu Thuat (Thai: หลวงปู่ทวด), also known as Luang Pu Thuad, Luang Por Tuad, Luang Phu Tuad, and various other spellings. Luang Pu Thuat was born in 1582 (2125 BE) and died 1682 (2225 BE) He is a revered Buddhist monk who lived in Siam. He is said to have performed miracle.
Luang Pu Thuat is mentioned in the early regional histories of southern Thailand, but his life is mainly preserved in oral traditions. Stories of the famous monk were passed on by word of mouth for centuries. As a result, it is a mixture of Buddhist elements: early signs, alleged magic, travel, study, meditation and eventual “sainthood.”
His movements throughout the southern Thai peninsula constitute a path of pilgrimage for many of his followers.
Many people in Thailand, Singapore and Malaysia believe that amulets depicting Luang Pu Thuat hold great protective powers granting safety in times of distress, especially saving the lives of believers from seemingly fatal automobile accidents. Phra Archan Tim Dharmataro, abbot of Wat Chang Hai is the pioneer creator of Phra Luang Phor Thuad amulets.

title: The reason why we must try to be Vegetarian
tags: Vegetarianism (Religious Practice)|Quan yin|Goddess of mercry|Guanyin|Vegetarian|Goddess of compassion|Kuanyin
description:
Do you know that this abstinence is only practiced in South-East Asia, particularly Malaysia and Singapore? In China and Tibet, devotees of the Goddess of Mercy are not aware of such restriction. Tell this to a Bhutanese and he will think it is a joke as meat is a staple in their diet despite being a populace comprising of Buddhists mainly.

The Buddha himself is not a vegetarian and did not forbid his disciples from eating beef, or any meat in general. Remember what he preached was the Middle Way, not a practice of extremes. However, since it is part of the teaching to refrain from killing in any form, a vegetarian diet is recommended but this is not imposed. Mahayana Buddhists recognise the consumption of meat to be cruel and devoid of compassion, thus many Mahayana Buddhists are vegetarians. Numbers of Mahayana sutra record Buddha praising the virtue of avoiding meat. But nowhere in the Buddhist scriptures mentioned that beef has to be abstained from completely. So in terms of authentic Buddhist concepts, abstinence from beef is not part of it. There is only the differentiation of vegetarians and non-vegetarians.

The real root of the belief comes from the legend of Miao Shan , who was believed to be a reincarnation of Avalokitesvara. The extract from an online article explains this clearly:
“Many less educated Buddhists especially the elderly would cite a story where Guan Shi Yin was once the third princess Miao Shan in ancient China. In the story, she was a compassionate daughter who even gorged out her eyes to cure the illness of her evil father. In reward for her deed, Buddha gave her a thousand eyes and a thousand arms so that she could continue to help others. Later, she was canonized and worshiped by the common people. This story has many versions but among the illiterate majority this was the source of inspiration for the masses who could not read the scriptures.”
Due to her father’s evil deeds, he was reincarnated many times as a cow and thus, many devotees felt in respect of the Goddess, it is best to avoid consuming beef totally. This story is based on the writings of a Buddhist monk Chiang Chih-ch'i in 1100AD and said to be originated likely from Taoist folklore.

However, that is a legend and not the actual historical origin of Kwan Yin. First known as Avalokitesvara, the name first appeared at to be around 400 AD in India. The concept of Avalokitesvara was subsequently brought to China via Tibet and metamorphosised from a male form to that of a female to 1200 AD. Thus, true devotees of Avalokitesvara or Kwan Yin, do not need to abstain from beef. But as Buddhists, they are encouraged to adopt a vegetarian diet.

Guanyin (in pinyin; previous transliterations Quan Yin, Kwan Yin, or Kuanyin) is an East Asian deity of mercy, and a bodhisattva associated with compassion as venerated by Mahayana Buddhists. The name Guanyin is short for Guanshiyin, which means "Observing the Sounds (or Cries) of the World". She is also sometimes referred to as Guanyin Pusa (simplified Chinese:  traditional Chinese:pinyin: Guānyīn Púsà; literally: "Bodhisattva Guanyin"). Some Buddhists believe that when one of their adherents departs from this world, they are placed by Guanyin in the heart of a lotus, and then sent to the western pure land of Sukhāvatī.

Avalokiteśvara
The name Avalokitasvara was later supplanted by the Avalokiteśvara form containing the ending -īśvara, which does not occur in Sanskrit before the seventh century. The original form Avalokitasvara already appears in Sanskrit fragments of the fifth century. The original meaning of the name "Avalokitasvara" fits the Buddhist understanding of the role of a bodhisattva. The reinterpretation presenting him as an īśvara shows a strong influence of Śaivism, as the term īśvara was usually connected to the Hindu notion of Śiva as a creator god and ruler of the world. Some attributes of such a god were transmitted to the bodhisattva, but the mainstream of those who venerated Avalokiteśvara upheld the Buddhist rejection of the doctrine of any creator god.

In his address, beside from express his sincere congratulations to all students for their accomplishments, and also to their families, teachers and friends who also played an important supporting role in these achievements, he did share his opinion with students regarding the four factors contributing to such success. These are: (1) a good education, (2) good financial support, (3) good physical and mental health and (4) good behaviour. He concluded that, everyone who strives for these things will achieve success, happiness and peace of mind. He mentioned as well that: “… Sri Lanka and Thailand have long enjoyed a close and cordial friendship, especially in religious and academic fields. I hope that our relationship will continue to grow fruitfully for many years to come…”

title: Seoul Station
description:
I'm exhausted. Maybe I pushed myself too hard on this trip. And this humid weather... I just want to go home and rest. But my train isn't for another two hours. 

The café I came into to kill time is packed. It's cramped. I can't even get comfortable enough to close my eyes. I've still got two hours to go.

Then I changed my perspective.

Two hours in a café. What a luxury. How long has it been?

Watching people sit in cafés, slowly enjoying their coffee, I'd wonder when I'd get to do the same. Now I finally have these two hours. I sit quietly and look out the window watching people pass by, sipping my coffee, and simply taking in the air around me.

All this time, why didn't I give myself two hours like this?

This is nice. This time. I'm grateful for it.

title: Oncheoncheon, BUSAN
description:
Cherry blossom season is just around the corner. Every year during blossom season, Oncheoncheon, one of Busan’s most famous cherry blossom spots, hosts the Yeonje Ancient Tombs Fantasy Festival.

This video is from when I visited the festival last year. Under fully bloomed cherry blossoms, I enjoyed performances, hands-on activities, and truly felt the spirit of spring for the whole day.

This year, the 7th Yeonje Ancient Tombs Fantasy Festival will be held again in early April around Oncheoncheon. If you‘re visiting Busan during cherry blossom season, make sure to add this festival to your itinerary!

*The festival takes place at the historic Yeonje Ancient Tombs site and creatively reinterprets the story of the ancient Geochilsan Kingdom through modern fantasy-style performances, parades, and interactive programs. Because it brings real history to life in an imaginative way, it’s called the Fantasy Festival.

description:
Cheomseongdae is a symbol of Silla and a landmark of Gyeongju. It’s an observatory built during the Silla era, over a thousand years ago. A cultural heritage site showing advanced science of its time.

If you come to Gyeongju, this is a must-visit. 

Interestingly, the exact reason it was built isn’t recorded. Some say it was for observing stars, others say to predict the nation’s fate, or to show the authority of the first queen. Anyway, Cheomseongdae represents Gyeongju today.

title: Visiting Gyeongju, Korea
description:
After Seokguram, I walked into Bulguksa. The path felt gentle, almost like an invitation to slow down.
Fallen leaves, quiet steps, and the steady presence of the temple — everything felt balanced. Between the human world and the Buddha’s world, I found myself standing quietly in between. Bulguksa wasn’t loud or overwhelming. It simply stayed there, reminding me of what has lasted for centuries.

석굴암을 지나 불국사로 왔습니다. 길은 부드럽게 이어졌고, 자연스럽게 속도를 늦추게 하네요. 떨어진 단풍, 조용한 발걸음, 변함없이 서 있는 사찰이 조화를 이루고 있습니다. 인간의 세계와 부처의 세계 사이, 그 중간에 조용히 서 있는 기분인데요. 불국사는 크거나 화려하지 않지만 그저 수백 년을 견뎌온 시간의 무게를 담담히 전하고 있습니다.

title: Seokguram Grotto 석굴암
description:
Visiting Gyeongju, Korea

📍 석굴암 Seokguram Grotto

Today, I made my way up the mountain to Seokguram.
The path was quiet, the air felt still, and everything slowed down naturally. Standing there, I couldn’t help but wonder how something so precise and powerful was built so long ago. Hidden behind a simple exterior, Seokguram holds a presence that feels timeless and deeply human. It wasn’t a place to rush through, but a place to pause and reflect.

오늘은 산길을 따라 석굴암으로 향했습니다. 길은 고요했고, 공기는 차분해서 자연스럽게 걸음이 느려졌네요. 이렇게 정교하고 웅장한 공간이 먼 옛날에 만들어졌다는 사실이 새삼 놀라웠습니다. 겉모습은 담담하지만, 그 안에는 시간을 초월한 깊은 기운이 담겨 있더라고요. 석굴암은 지나치는 곳이 아니라, 잠시 멈춰 서서 마음을 바라보게 하는 장소였습니다.

title: A 5 day Seoul itinerary: Day 5
description:
A 5 day Seoul itinerary: Day 5

Fifth day is in the Hongdae area. I've chosen activities that locals often enjoy. Before heading to Hongdae, let's start by visiting Hongjecheon. This place, where an artificial waterfall was recently created, has become a popular spot attracting many visitors. The artificial waterfall is impressive, and behind it, a small hill is covered with numerous blooming flowers, making it a great place to enjoy spring blossoms.

After that, we'll move on to Mangwon Market. Here, you can enjoy some local snacks or have lunch at one of the many small restaurants in Mangwon-dong. 

After lunch, we'll proceed to Yeonnamdong, located near Hongdae. Yeonnamdong, adjacent to Hongdae, is filled with trendy restaurants and cafes. Don't miss walking along Gyeongui Line Forest Park. When you pass Hongdae Station, there's a charming railway track. 

Next, we'll stroll along Hongdae Street. In the afternoon, there are less crowds, making it a perfect time for cafe hopping or visiting street fashion stores for some shopping. 

Moving on to Hapjeong, which is known as a local gathering place with plenty of delicious restaurants and cafes. I recommend having dinner here. 

After that, in the Mangwon area, there is a street adorned with cherry blossoms. It's beautiful during the day, but the evening lighting adds an extra charm, making it more enchanting at night.

Following that, walk on Hongdae Street in the evening. Although you walked through Hongdae Street in the afternoon, the atmosphere changes in the evening. Many people come out for busking, street food stalls emerge, and the place becomes livlier.

title: A 5 day Seoul itinerary: Day 3
A 5 day Seoul itinerary: Day 2
description:
A 5 day Seoul itinerary: Day 2

The second day is all about Gangnam. Unless you're staying in Gangnam, I recommend not to allocate more than a day for Gangnam in a 5-day itinerary due to its distance from other attractions.

If you're an early riser, consider visiting Olympic Park while you're in Jamsil.

Then, move to Seokchon Lake, Lotte Tower, and the outer area of Magic Castle in Jamsil.

Next, visit COEX and Bongeunsa Temple. There are plenty of restaurants here. Have lunch, explore the library, and then visit Bongeunsa Temple located next to COEX.

Following that, if you're visiting during cherry blossom season, take the time to enjoy the cherry blossoms at Yangjaecheon, which is one of the famous places to see cherry blossoms. If it's not cherry blossom season, you might want to skip here because the route is little off.

Next, the real Gangnam around Gangnam Station. This area is more for shopping, dining, or drinking rather than attractions for tourists. Take a stroll along this street to enjoy the local vibe.

Following that, you have the option of going to either Express Bus Terminal (known as Goto) or Sinsa. Goto has the Goto Mall and numerous shopping stores, restaurants, and more gathered indoor. Sinsa, on the other hand, has brand shopping, trendy restaurants, and wine cafes lined up in the streets. It's a trendy and stylish area, so if you're into trends, give it a visit.

title: 2024년 1월 20일
description:
A 5 day Seoul itinerary: Day 1

First, start at Gwanghwamun Square and head up to explore Gyeongbokgung Palace. Taking a leisurely stroll here will take about 2 hours. If you also visit The National Folk Museum of Korea, then it will take about 3 hours in total.

After exploring Gyeongbokgung Palace, head straight to Bukchon Hanok Village. Enjoy a meal and coffee while looking at the traditional Hanok houses.

Next is the optional Ikseondong Hanok Street. While Bukchon Hanok Village focuses more on residential purposes, Ikseondong Hanok Street has more to offer in terms of restaurants, cafes, and shops. 

Moving on, visit Jongmyo Shrine, the royal ancestral shrine of the Joseon Dynasty kings and queens. It takes about 1-2 hours to explore. 

Afterward, head to Gwangjang Market, Seoul’s representative traditional market, where you can enjoy Korean market foods. Look around and have dinner here.

If you still have energy after dinner, I recommend checking out the night admission at Changgyeonggung Palace. It’s the only palace that opens at night, providing a unique experience. It may take around 1 and half hours.

description:
Thailand Real Estate | The New Nominee Crackdown Solution

Thailand is cracking down nationwide on illegal nominee shareholders used to conceal foreign ownership of businesses and property.

Led by the Ministry of Commerce and the Department of Special Investigation (DSI), authorities are investigating and prosecuting foreigners and Thai nominees, with penalties that can include up to three years in prison and fines of up to one million baht.

The crackdown is particularly relevant in major foreign property and tourism markets including Bangkok, Pattaya, Phuket, Hua Hin, Koh Samui and Koh Phangan.

So what does this mean for foreign property owners who may already be using a nominee structure?

Better Than Freehold has developed a solution designed to convert nominee arrangements into a 30-year leasehold structure, with options for renewal, sale and succession.

The company was founded by Andrew Moore, who has decades of property development experience in Koh Samui and a background in financial advisory in the UK.

We sat down with Andrew to find out why Thailand is cracking down on nominee ownership, what it means for foreign property owners, and how Better Than Freehold's structure works.

The proposed solution involves dissolving the nominee company and replacing it with a 30-year lease and associated commercial agreements that can provide rights to extend, sell or transfer the property interest to family members.

The structure separates key roles between four entities:

     * TIN — Thailand Investor Network: A Thai-owned asset-holding company that holds legal title and grants the lease and option agreement.

     * SPH Trustees: A Labuan FSA-regulated offshore trustee that holds the lease, option and security interests on behalf of the investor.

     * Clear Blue Security Agents — CBSA: An independent, Thai lawyer-led security agent responsible for enforcing the structure and managing disputes through arbitration.

     * Siam Venture Capital — SVC: An offshore lending platform providing financing for new buyers and loans for eligible owners converting from nominee structures.

For foreign property owners concerned about Thailand's nominee crackdown, understanding your ownership structure is becoming increasingly important.

Andrew Moore explains how the Better Than Freehold solution works, who it may be suitable for, and what property owners should consider before it's too late.

tags: Ko Samet|Koh Samet|Thailand islands|Thailand travel|Thailand beaches|island near Bangkok|Bangkok weekend getaway|Ko Samet resorts|Ko Samet beaches|Sai Kaew Beach|Ao Prao|Rayong Thailand|Thailand vlog|Thai islands|beach holiday Thailand|Thailand tourism|tropical island|Southeast Asia travel|Thailand expat|beach paradise|Destination Thailand|Travel Asia and Beyond|Perfect Weekend Escape from Bangkok|Koh Samet Thailand|Thailand weekend escapes
description:
Ko Samet is one of Thailand’s most popular weekend escapes thanks to its proximity to Bangkok.

No airports, just a short journey and an island heaven awaits.

Getting to Ko Samet is easy. It’s about a 3 hour drive south of Bangkok or one hour south of Patttaya to the province of Rayong, where you can jump on board a speed boat, a high speed catamaran, or a slower boat, and then when you arrive at the island, there’s a 200 baht fee for the National Park and then you just on to a local taxi and you’re on your way.

Like many little islands in Thailand , Ko Samet began its life as a budget holiday or backpacker retreat. Of course you can still have a low cost holiday here, but also you can have the alternative. This island is now home to some gorgeous 5 star resorts and spas , and some idyllic stays for a romantic getaway. 

Of course it’s also an island that’s great for partying, you’ve got night clubs, beach bars, fantastic little restaurants on the sand, little restaurants in the nearby villages, there’s a lot to see here , there’s never a dull moment on Ko Samet.

In Thailand, Thai people call Ko Samet the island of LOVE. That’s why its so popular with young couples, in fact I think its one of the most romantic places to stay in Thailand.

Bangkok based expats like me, love Samet because its not only close to the city but it has limited island traffic, beautiful beaches and is super relaxed.

One of the great things about Ko Samet is the food. Thai food or seafood on the beach is a must, and of course there are many other dining options on the island, international fare and of course vegan, or vegetarian if you choose.     

Besides convenience, Koh Samet has a bit of something for everyone. Yes you can opt for a high-end resort stay but of major appeal is the bungalow style and 3 star options from as little as US$30 a night. Not bad when you are steps from a beach like this. 

It’s no hard to leave when you know a return to beach bliss is on your doorstep.

So if you’re looking for love or a little piece of paradise here in Thailand , then the island of Ko Samet is waiting.

Make sure to add it to your bucket list here, in the Land of Smiles.

BEST BEACHES: 
Sai Kaew (family-friendly)
Ao Prao (sunset & upscale)
Ao Wong Duean (calmer bays)

NOTE:
- Best time to visit: November–April (dry season)
- Stay overnight for quieter evenings and sunset views; day trips get crowded on weekends/holidays

Koh Kood (also spelled Ko Kood or Koh Kut) is one of Thailand’s quietest and most beautiful islands — known for clear turquoise water, jungle-covered hills, waterfalls, and a much more relaxed atmosphere than places like Phuket or Koh Samui.

People love Ko Kood  because of its uncrowded beaches, long stretches of soft white sand with very little development, crystal-clear water and a slow pace — no nightlife scene compared with Thailand’s party islands. It's ideal for couples, nature lovers, and people wanting to disconnect.

Some standout beaches include:
Klong Chao Beach — probably the island’s most famous beach, with powdery sand and calm water.
Ao Tapao Beach — peaceful and lined with resorts.
Bang Bao Beach — scenic bay with rustic beachfront stays.
Ao Noi Beach — smaller and very secluded.

Ko Kood feels different to other compared Thai Islands by being quieter, greener, more upscale-but-natural and less commercialized.

The ideal season is generally November to April with sunny and dry with calm seas.

Most travellers fly or travel to Trat and then take a ferry or speedboat from Laem Sok Pier to Ko Kood.

description:
Looking for the easiest and cheapest island escape from Bangkok? 🇹🇭

In this video, we travel to Ko Samet Thailand — one of the closest and most affordable beach getaways near Bangkok.

Bangkok is fantastic destination but sometimes and you just need a quick escape. Getting there is simple. From Bangkok, you can take a taxi, or private car and drive about three hours southeast to the coastal town of Rayong.

The best part? You don’t need to fly. 

That means less hassle, less cost, and a much quicker trip from the city.

Once you arrive in Rayong, you’ll head to the pier where you can choose various ferry options depending upon your budget …. and how much time you have. Boats leave from the Ban Phe Pier.
The classic slow wooden ferries take around 40 minutes, while a speedboat will whisk you to the island in 15 minutes for around Baht 300 per person. The large catamaran option takes around 15 to 20 minutes, and around Baht 150 per person.

While Thailand has many more exotic island destinations than Ko Samet, it stands out as one of the best quick island getaways from Bangkok. It appeals for its accessibility. This convenience makes it a favourite for weekend travellers, expats and short-stay visitors.

Another key advantage is that Ko Samet tends to have less rainfall than many other Thai Islands, making it a more reliable option, even in the wet season.

By the way, Don’t forget there is a Baht 200 National Park foreigner fee to pay when you arrive. It’s usually cash only!

It’s the cheapest and easiest island getaway from Bangkok.

And before you know it, you’re arriving at clear blue water, and soft white sand. Suddenly the busy streets of Bangkok feel very far away.

So if you’re visiting Bangkok and need a quick dose of island life, Ko Samet might be the easiest tropical escape you’ll find.

Sometimes paradise is closer than you think.

description:
Bangkok experiences perhaps the World’s Biggest Water Fight! 

A record of 600,000 people partied on Silom Road across 3 days!

Songkran is best known for its massive water fights—people splash water on each other in the streets using buckets, hoses, and water guns. It’s fun, chaotic, and a great way to cool off during Thailand’s hottest time of year 💦

But beyond the party vibe, Songkran actually has deep cultural meaning. Held every year from April 13–15 (often extended in some areas), the water symbolizes cleansing and renewal, washing away bad luck from the past year and welcoming a fresh start. 

Many Thai people visit temples, make merit, pour scented water over Buddha statues, and gently over elders’ hands to show respect and receive blessings.

So it’s really a mix of:

🎉 Fun: street-wide water battles, music, dancing
🛕 Tradition: temple visits, rituals, family time
🌸 Meaning: renewal, respect, and good fortune for the new year

It’s one of Thailand’s most joyful and culturally rich festivals.

description:
BANGKOK HIDDEN GEMS

A RUSSIAN CATHEDRAL in Bangkok? This Place Will Surprise You.

St Nicholas Orthodox Cathedral Bangkok stands out as one of the most unusual and culturally layered religious sites in Thailand. It’s not just a church—it’s a reflection of how Eastern Orthodox Christianity has adapted and taken root in Southeast Asia.

Here’s what makes it genuinely worth a visit

Thailand is overwhelmingly Buddhist, so an active Russian Orthodox church in Bangkok is already distinctive. The cathedral serves a small but diverse community—Russians, Eastern Europeans, and Thai converts—making it one of the key centres of Orthodox Christianity in Southeast Asia.

It also plays a central role in the Russian Orthodox Church’s expansion in the region, marking over two decades of growth in Thailand.

Unlike traditional European Orthodox churches, this cathedral blends:

- Classic Russian elements (onion domes, crosses, iconostasis)
- Subtle Thai architectural influences

Visitors often note how the structure feels like a hybrid—Orthodox in symbolism but adapted to the tropical and cultural context of Bangkok.

This makes it visually different from iconic Orthodox sites in Europe or Russia.
- A full iconostasis (icon wall central to Orthodox worship)
- Hand-painted icons, including some in Thai language
- Traditional liturgical layout with no pews (you stand during services)

Visit if you’re interested in::-
- Unique architecture beyond typical Thai temples
- Religious and cultural contrasts in Southeast Asia
- Authentic, non-touristy experiences in Bangkok

It’s not a “must-see landmark” in the classic sense—but it’s a highly worthwhile niche stop that adds depth to a Bangkok travel itinerary, especially if you appreciate history, culture, or religious architecture.

title: Bangkok in 1 day 🇹🇭 River cruise, Big Buddha & Insane Malls! Would you try this?

description:
Bangkok in 1 day!

1) Take a river cruise to the big famous Buddha
A long-tail canal cruise to Wat Paknam is one one of the best short experiences in Bangkok, combining river culture, local life, and a dramatic reveal of the giant Buddha.
Boat tours combine:
- Bangkok's Chao Phraya River
- Smaller canals (klongs)
- Direct view of the Buddha rising above local neighbourhoods. Height: ~69 m (one of Bangkok’s largest statues)
- Cruise Cost: ~1,500–3,000 THB (private boat)

2) Take a stroll through Lumpini Park.
A walk through Lumphini Park is one of the easiest ways to slow down in central Bangkok—right between Silom and Sukhumvit, yet surprisingly calm given its city-centre location.
- Popular with locals jogging, tai chi, cycling
- Famous for giant monitor lizards (harmless if left alone)
- Central lake with paddle boats
- Bangkok skyline in the background
- Flat, paved paths (perfect 2–3 km loops)

3) Explore the cities huge Malls.
Bangkok’s malls are destinations in themselves—air-conditioned, well-connected, and perfect for a relaxed day mixing shopping, food, and entertainment.

Suggested chilled itinerary:-

Morning
- Start at Siam Paragon (coffee + light browse)
- Walk to Siam Center (quick look at local brands)

Midday
- Head to CentralWorld (lunch + relaxed shopping)
- Optional: quick stop at MBK for bargains

Afternoon → evening
- Travel to ICONSIAM
- Explore SOOKSIAM + luxury floors
- Sunset drinks by the river

4) Visit a concept cafe like Curvistan. A new Porsche-themed venue in Thonglor
Bangkok has gone deep into “concept cafés”—not just coffee, but full lifestyle spaces like Curvistan. Thonglor/Ekkamai is the core zone, but there are strong clusters across the city.

Best café-hopping zones (practical)
a} Thonglor / Ekkamai (best overall)
- 5–15 min between spots
- Dense cluster of concept cafés
- Easy BTS access (Thong Lo / Ekkamai)

b} Soi Nana (Chinatown)
- Old shophouses turned into hip cafés & bars
- Strong contrast: heritage + modern creative scene

c) Ari (emerging scene)
- More relaxed, local feel
- Good mix of indie cafés (less polished than Thonglor)

description:
Witness the breathtakingly beauty of  Wat Arun, otherwise known as the Temple of the Dawn, one of Bangkok's most iconic landmarks. 

Wat Arun sits on the western bank of the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok’s Bangkok Yai district — directly opposite Wat Pho and near the Grand Palace area. Its riverside position makes it a picture-perfect sight from both the water and the opposite bank.

Its centerpiece is a towering central spire, roughly 70–82 meters tall, richly adorned with a mosaic of Chinese porcelain, seashells, and coloured tiles.

The temple remains an active place of worship and Buddhist ritual as well as a major tourist attraction.

Visitors can enjoy panoramic views of the river and surrounding cityscape from parts of the structure 

It is magnificent at sunrise (true to its name) and also very striking at sunset or when illuminated at night.

description:
Bangkok Motor Expo 2025 | MAJOR DUCATI LAUNCH | NEW Dirt-Bike  

IMPACT Challenger, near Don Muang Airport in the north of Bangkok, is widely considered as one of the best and most important large-scale motor exhibitions in Asia.
 
Recently we visited Thailand’s International Motor Expo to check-out DUCATI’s launch of their new dirt-bike and enduro models to Asia ….. particularly the Desmo450 MX.

A notable expansion beyond their sport and street bikes.

It was the centrepiece and drew heavy crowds. This was DUCATI’S boldest technical statement in decades. They hadn’t built a pure dirt-racing motorcycle since the 1971 Ducati 450 R/T, which was produced in very small numbers and disappeared quickly.

When DUCATI began teasing its DESMO 450 MX project in in 2023 , the announcement sparked disbelief in the motorcycle community.

Well …… here it is ….. launching to the Asia market.

📺 About This Video
With a 450cc single-cyclinder 4 stroke engine, it uses Ducati’s signature design with no valve springs to allow the engine to rev faster and reduces engine braking, apparently giving it a very ‘lively throttle” for dirt riding ….. suitable for the experienced.  It’s high revving nature, allows a 11,900 RPM limit, the highest revving engine in its class, allowing riders to shift less, keeping momentum in its tight corners. 

The launch price level was around $15,500 Australian dollars.

Will Ducati’s design language, electronics and cost base naturally fit the lightweight, aggressive, hard hitting MX World? It will be interesting how it compares to the similar KTM, Honda or Yamaha’s in this sector.

Something to contemplate ….. as we choose the most stress-free mode of escaping Bangkok’s late afternoon traffic. Jumping on to the PINK line at the exhibition’s dedicated train station! Muang Thong Thani! An expo that was well worth visiting!

If you’re in Bangkok around mid-February, head to the EM District (Emporium/EmQuartier/Emsphere) during the evenings to enjoy world class Chinese entertainment blending traditional and modern performances.

Expect the huge dragon feature (e.g., a 40 m “Heavenly Dragon”) plus dancers, musicians, and cultural performances aimed at celebrating good fortune and prosperity.

EM District in Bangkok, Thailand is a major upscale lifestyle hotspot — a connected neighbourhood of world-class shopping, dining, entertainment, and cultural experience located along Sukhumvit Road near Phrom Phong BTS Skytrain Station.

EM District isn’t just one mall — it’s a large, integrated retail and leisure district made up of three major destinations:

a) Emporium – One of Bangkok’s original luxury malls, known for high-end fashion brands, gourmet food halls, a luxury cinema, and premium services.

b} EmQuartier – A modern, architecturally striking mall with open garden areas, a waterfall atrium, multi-level dining terraces, and a mix of luxury and lifestyle brands.

c) EmSphere – The newest addition, focusing on innovative retail, entertainment, and dining — including Thailand’s first city-centre IKEA, large event spaces like UOB Live arena, and vibrant food and nightlife zones.

Together, these form a walkable lifestyle precinct with over 650,000 sq.m of space and more than a thousand global and local brands, making EM District one of Bangkok’s most talked-about destinations for shopping, eating, leisure, and events.

description:
HELMET HEROES WORLD RECORD

Helmet Heroes Thailand and Pattaya Police claim a new World Record, educating 7,744 Students on Road Safety in a Single Day.

Founded by Savvy Rick Brown, in a groundbreaking collaboration with the Pattaya Police, Helmet Heroes have set a new Guinness World Record for the Largest Road Safety Lesson. On September 3, 2025, the ambitious initiative successfully delivered essential road safety education to 7,744 students across seven local schools in a single day, significantly surpassing the previous record of 4,178 participants held by Suzuki Philippines Inc.

The event was led by Police Lieutenant Colonel Panupong Nimsuwan and his dedicated team of officers, who conducted training sessions focused on helmet safety and traffic awareness. The partnership highlights a powerful community-focused approach to tackling road safety challenges in the region.

"Helmet Heroes' mission is to provide TIS-certified motorcycle helmets to school communities with road safety education," said Rick Brown. We partner with local merchants to reward helmet usage through our hero reward program. Working with the Pattaya Police has been an amazing collaboration. They understand our vision to educate and protect our local communities."


📺 About This Video
About Helmet Heroes Thailand

Founded by Savvy Rick Brown, Helmet Heroes Thailand is a non-profit organization dedicated to saving young lives by providing TIS (Thailand Industrial Standards) Certified motorcycle helmets and comprehensive road safety education to children throughout Thailand. The organization further incentivizes safe practices through its innovative "Hero Reward Program," which partners with local merchants to offer rewards and discounts for consistent helmet usage.

About the Pattaya Police

The Pattaya Police Department is dedicated to upholding law and order, ensuring public safety, and fostering community well-being in Pattaya, Thailand. Through proactive policing, community engagement, and strategic partnerships, they strive to create a secure environment for residents and visitors alike.

Vibrant Pattaya, with its warm waters and consistent conditions continues to be Thailand’s top racing and training hub, regularly enticing international sailors.
 
The  OK Dinghy has a long history in Thailand. The King Bhumibol raced the class for many years and even built one himself!

The OK Dinghy was designed by Knud Olsen, a Danish naval architect and sailor, in 1956. The name “OK” was chosen from his name, in reverse.

📺 About This Video
Varuna began in 1957 as the Varuna Marine Club. Among the founders were Prince Bhisatej Rajani (in charge of sailing) and Swiss resident Walter Meyer (the first flag commodore).

On 26 April 1965, His Majesty King Bhumibol Adulyadej bestowed royal patronage on the club, which changed its name to the Royal Varuna Yacht Club (RVYC). The king was himself an avid sailor and regularly participated in sailing events with members during this era. 

Initially located near Pattaya’s original beach area, the club moved to its current seaside site on Pratumnak Hill (South Pattaya) in October 1967, chosen for its excellent sailing waters. On 14 September 1968, the king, queen, crown prince, and princesses officially inaugurated the Royal Varuna Yacht Club at this new location. 

Through the following decades, RVYC became central to Thailand’s competitive sailing scene, hosting national and international regattas and events. It has supported the growth of youth sailing, junior training programs, and worked with the Royal Thai Navy and Junior Sailing Squadron of Thailand on training and competitions. 

The Club’s facilities expanded over time, and a modern clubhouse complex with enhanced services was opened in the early 2000s, with the then Crown Prince (now King) participating in the grand opening.

description:
The Tatvani Chiang Rai 

Nestled in the peaceful misty landscapes of Chiang Rai Province, located about 25 minutes from Chiang Rai International Airport, Tatvani is one of the most luxurious private indulgences in Thailand's North.

If seclusion is your dream escape, this super exclusive resort features six unique villas that blend modern design with traditional Thai elements, creating a serene and elegant atmosphere. 

Experiences can include rice planting, picnics or peaceful moments by koi ponds and of course private spa treatments.  

For those seeking adventure or connection with nature, there are opportunities to visit the nearby elephant sanctuary for memorable encounters with the gentle giants. 

A tranquil and authentic escape for travellers looking to unwind and explore the beauty of Northern Thailand while being pampered like a rock star.

📺 About This Video
Chiang Rai is one of the northernmost provinces of Thailand, rich in natural beauty, cultural heritage, and historical significance. While it’s often overshadowed by its more famous neighbor, Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai offers a quieter, more authentic experience, with scenic landscapes, unique attractions, and fascinating local cultures. It's the gateway to the Golden Triangle and a major destination for those seeking to explore Northern Thailand's ethnic diversity and spectacular natural wonders.

Chiang Rai is located in the northern part of Thailand, bordering Laos to the north and Myanmar to the west, known as the Golden Triangle. The Mekong River marks the border with Laos and provides a beautiful setting for the province’s northern region.

The province is known for its mountainous terrain, with lush forests, waterfalls, and rivers. The Phu Chi Fa mountain range offers dramatic views of mist-covered valleys and is popular for sunrise hikes. The land is dotted with tea plantations, farms, and traditional villages.

Chiang Rai enjoys a tropical climate, but due to its higher elevation, it tends to be cooler than much of Thailand. The best time to visit is during the cool season (November to February) when temperatures are more moderate.

description:
HELMET HEROES THAILAND

A project founded by America expat Rick Brown to give helmets away free to Thai children.

Rick was badly injured in a bike accident as a child. He was shocked to see so many children on motorbikes without helmets in Thailand.

Pattaya City Police love the initiative and join in to help.
Sponsors can also add their logos to helmets and help the cause.

Helmet Heroes has now distributed hundreds of helmets to children.

“So we're an organisation that has a mission to protect as many kids as possible with free TIS certified helmets. These are the best helmets we can find in all of Thailand, and we buy them to protect kids from disability or worse"

📺 About This Video
Helmet Heroes of Thailand was born out of personal resilience and a passion for protecting lives. Founded by Rick Brown, his journey began with a traumatic experience of being bullied at the age of 14, which led to a life-altering accident resulting in spinal trauma and PTSD. After rebuilding his life and relocating to Thailand, he identified a critical safety issue: countless children riding motorbikes without helmets.

What started as a modest mission in December 2023 with only three helmets has since grown into a powerful movement. Through partnerships with local police, hundreds of helmets have been distributed, transforming the initial vision into a community-driven safety initiative.
The organisation's goal is simple yet impactful: to educate students, raise awareness about road safety, and prevent the kind of injuries Rick experienced. Each helmet given away is more than just protective gear—it symbolizes hope, resilience, and the belief that one individual can make a significant difference in safeguarding young lives.

Pai Thailand 2025 | Thailand’s Ultimate Backpacker Heaven। Destination Thailand.

Up in the mountains, a 3 hours drive north-west of Chiang Mai, is a secluded small-town haven
where the young-at-heart escape to from every corner of the world.

It’s called PAI. It’s a back-packers dream.  

Located in Mai Hong Son Province, it sits in a valley along the Pai River near the Myanmar border
Surrounded by mountains, hot springs, waterfalls and rice fields.

A town that evokes the elements of a true Thai experience. It still feels original.

Yes, it’s a tourist town but it’s super relaxed and full of young people, many finding their first experience of freedom, in an inexpensive cosmopolitan  environment with less barriers.

In many ways, Pai can be closely seen as an alternative, hippy destination.  
A scooter town, with many adventurers with trepidation experiencing riding for the first time, spontaneously exploring the stunning nearby nature.

Many people visit by van. Prepare your motion tablets if you suffer car sickness! You’ll have to ensure 762 curves from Chiang Mai.

A social town, with around 80 hostels, backpackers can easily save and extend their stay
A typical budget is around $5 to $25 per night.  

The nightly walking street offers excellent variety for the international tourists with quirky café’s, live music. 

An ideal wellness destination.

Every day and every night is a chill day!

Mae Hong Son is a remote, mountainous province in northern Thailand, bordering Myanmar (Burma). Though sparsely populated, it's ethnically diverse and home to hill tribes such as the Shan and Hmong. description:
Wang Pho Viaduct

This stunning piece of railway engineering, a wooden trestle bridge clinging to the side of a cliff, overlooking the Khwae Noi River, was built by Allied prisoners of war and Asian labourers under Japanese rule during WWII. 

Spanning around 400 meters it was constructed in just 17 days in 1943 by prisoners under brutal conditions. 

More than 100,000 lives were lost during the construction of this Thai-Burma railway. 

Tham Kra Sae cave is a natural limestone formation right next to the railway line. During the war, it was used as a shelter and camp for Allied POWs and Japanese soldiers. 

Now, a place of reflection. Quite moving!

title: JUNGLE HOLIDAY tracing the iconic THAI-BURMA RAILWAY | Kanchanaburi
tags: Thailand|Kanchanaburi|Kanchanaburi Thailand|Things to do in Thailand|River Kwai Bridge|Thailand Travel|Kanchanaburi Train|Destination Thailand|Travel Asia and Beyond|JUNGLE HOLIDAY|THAI-BURMA RAILWAY|Wang Pho Viaduct|River Kwai Resotel Resort|Bridge on the River Kwai|thailand travel tips|JUNGLE HOLIDAY tracing the iconic THAI-BURMA RAILWAY | Kanchanaburi|iconic THAI-BURMA RAILWAY|The River Kwai|Railway|World War 2|Thailand Death Railway|Travel|Tham Kra Sae
description:
Whether you are a tourist or an expat, Kanchanaburi is a highly recommended destination to explore. It makes a perfect long-weekend easily accessible from Bangkok.

0:00 Kanchanaburi is a great week-end getaway from Bangkok
0:25 The Bridge on the River Kwai  
1:38 The Tham Kra Sae Train Station
1:56  Death Railway | Wang Pho Viaduct
3:21 River Kwai Resotel Resort

The Bridge on the River Kwai  

Famous for its historic Thai-Burma Railway train route built during the 2nd World War, Kanchanaburi was our weekend getaway from Bangkok, a minimum trip of around 2 and a half hours by car, or even more by train. 
We found a charming, less touristy, authentic holiday destination, with history, and a stunning jungle resort escape on its famous river. Our visit started in the laid-back middle of town, at the most iconic symbol of Kanchanaburi. this bridge. The bridge was part of the Death Railway and was made famous worldwide in the 1957 film "The Bridge on the River Kwai." It’s easy to access, a sombre reminder of the war. Not many trains cross the bridge each day — it's a low-traffic, scenic route, mainly serving tourists and locals. Typically, two to three scheduled trains cross the bridge per day in each direction as part of the Bangkok–Nam Tok line. 
Renting a car gave us more flexibility, and we were quickly further exploring the fascinating province

Tham Kra Sae Train Station 

About 15 kilometres from Kanchanaburi town, the Tham Kra Sae Train Station was a scenic stop on the Bangkok–Nam Tok line, a popular highlight on the Death Railway route. The station is famous for its proximity to the dramatic Wang Pho Viaduct. 

Wang Pho Viaduct

This stunning piece of railway engineering, a wooden trestle bridge clinging to the side of a cliff, overlooking the Khwae Noi River, was built by Allied prisoners of war and Asian labourers under Japanese rule during WWII. Spanning around 400 meters it was constructed in just 17 days in 1943 by prisoners under brutal conditions. More than 100,000 lives were lost during the construction of this Thai-Burma railway. Tham Kra Sae cave is a natural limestone formation right next to the railway line. During the war, it was used as a shelter and camp for Allied POWs and Japanese soldiers. Now, a place of reflection. Quite moving!
 
River Kwai Resotel Resort

Our resort for 2 nights was still 45 minutes up the road.   I highly recommend a GPS route using small windy roads through charming countryside.

We were in for a treat!

TripAdvisor have ranked it as #1 of the resorts in Sai Yok. We could have also arrived by boat on a different type of tour. Situated on the banks of the River Kwai Noi, the River Kwai Resotel is around 60 kilometres out of Kanchanaburi town.  Offering activities such as canoeing, bamboo rafting, biking, cooking classes, cave tours, visiting Mon tribal villages, a spa and even watering herbal and palm gardens.
You definitely can’t get bored. We had found our ideal jungle escape from the bustle of Bangkok.
Riverside relaxation .. and luxury in the forest. And incredible value for money! 
Day trips near the resort include the Sai Yok Noi and Yai Waterfalls, the Lawa Cave and both the Erawan and Sai Yok National Parks. Another attraction not to overlook is Hellfire Pass, a drive around 85 kilometres on the other side of the river. From the museum, you can descend down to the pass and walk on to the the Hellfire Pass Walking Trail, stretching several kilometres through cuttings and embankments to the most notorious section of this railway. 
This holiday took us by car, but we’re sure that using the train would be an adventurous option.
A fascinating 5-hour journey from Bangkok Thonburi Station to Nam Tok Station, and then a 10-minute-long tail ride across the river to the Resotel. Another Thailand experience for the future!

Weddings in Thailand are incredibly popular, especially for couples seeking a beautiful, exotic, and often more affordable destination. Here’s a quick guide to what makes Thailand such a sought-after wedding destination:


🌴 Why Thailand for a Wedding?

Stunning Locations: 
From tropical beaches to lush mountains and luxury resorts.

Affordability: 
High-quality services at a lower cost compared to Western destinations.

Experienced Vendors: 
Planners, photographers, florists, and venues used to hosting international weddings.

Warm Hospitality: 
Thai culture is known for its friendliness and grace.

Legal or Symbolic Ceremonies: 
You can have a legal wedding (with paperwork) or a symbolic one for ease.


💒 Popular Wedding Destinations in Thailand

- Phuket – Beachfront resorts, luxury villas, and dramatic sunsets.
- Koh Samui – Romantic island vibe, perfect for private beach weddings.
- Chiang Mai – Lush countryside, temples, and a more cultural feel.
- Krabi / Railay Beach – Limestone cliffs and crystal-clear water.
- Bangkok – High-end city weddings in rooftop venues or luxury hotels.

💍 Types of Ceremonies Available

- Western-style weddings
- Traditional Thai ceremonies (complete with monks, water blessings, etc.)
- Indian weddings (Thailand is popular for big, multi-day South Asian weddings)
- Same-sex weddings (symbolic, as legal recognition is limited)


📝 Legal Requirements for Foreigners

If you want your wedding to be legally binding:

- You must visit your embassy in Bangkok to get an affidavit.
- Translate and legalize the affidavit with the Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
- Register the marriage at a district office (Amphur).

Many couples skip the legal part in Thailand and do it at home, then have a symbolic ceremony on the beach.

title: What Makes Koh Samui Thailand's MOST BEAUTIFUL Island Getaway?
tags: Thailand|Samui|Koh Samui|Koh Samui Thailand|Samui Paradise|Koh Samui Attractions|Koh Samui Things to do|Things to do in Thailand|What Makes Koh Samui Thailand's MOST BEAUTIFUL Island Getaway|Destination Thailand|Travel Asia and Beyond|Koh Samui Tourism|Thailand Travel|Travel Thailand|Koh Samui Travel|Travel Koh Samui|Koh Samui Thailand's MOST BEAUTIFUL Island
description:
Koh Samui is often hailed as Thailand’s most beautiful island getaway — and honestly, it’s not hard to see why. It's got that perfect blend of lush nature, beachy vibes, and just enough luxury without losing its Thai soul. Here's what really makes Koh Samui stand out:

🌴 1. Stunning Beaches for Every Vibe

Whether you want lively or laid-back, Koh Samui’s beaches deliver:

    Chaweng Beach – White sand, turquoise water, nightlife, and resorts.
    Lamai Beach – A little quieter than Chaweng, great for swimming and relaxing.
    Silver Beach – A small hidden gem, perfect for peaceful sunbathing.
    Maenam Beach – Super chill, less touristy, great for couples and families.

🌅 2. Unreal Sunsets + Tropical Vibes

Head to Big Buddha or Taling Ngam for those epic golden hour views. Koh Samui sunsets are the kind that make you forget to check your phone (unless it’s for a photo, of course)

🧘‍♀️ 3. Wellness + Luxury Retreats

Koh Samui is basically spa-heaven:

    World-class yoga and detox retreats
    Award-winning luxury resorts like Four Seasons or Banyan Tree
    Affordable beachside massages that’ll melt all your stress away

🐘 4. Nature, Waterfalls & Jungle Adventures

    Na Muang Waterfalls are insta-worthy and perfect for a quick hike.
    Zipline through the jungle canopy or go off-roading in a 4x4.
    Visit Secret Buddha Garden in the hills for serene statues and views.

🛕 5. Culture Meets Island Life

It’s not just a beach destination:

    Wat Phra Yai (Big Buddha Temple) – iconic 12-meter golden statue.
    Wat Plai Laem – colorful, quirky, and peaceful.
    You’ll see monks, spirit houses, and Thai traditions woven into daily life.

🐠 6. Amazing Island-Hopping + Diving

    Hop over to Koh Phangan or Koh Tao for more exploring.
    Dive or snorkel around Ang Thong Marine Park – it’s like Avatar meets The Beach.

🍜 7. Food = Fire

    Fresh seafood, authentic Thai curries, tropical fruits, and coconut ice cream everywhere.
    Trendy cafes in Fisherman’s Village or local night markets with street food galore.
    Try pad krapow, mango sticky rice, and a fresh coconut on the beach.

Koh Samui is that rare place where you can party, detox, explore, and just chill out—all in one trip. It’s Thailand’s postcard-perfect island, but with enough personality to keep you coming back.
