description:
This week Destination Thailand features the award winning Veranda Resort & Spa between Hua Hin and Cha Am.

There are some places you know are truly special the moment you arrive......

I'm Raine, and I'm Sam and together we have made our way to the gulf of Thailand to show you the lovely Veranda Hua Hin Cha Am Resort.

The resort, just an easy 2 hour drive south of Bangkok, is located on one of the widest stretches of beachfront between the traditional Thai resort towns of Cha Am and Hua Hin.
This beach side escape has been a favorite Thai royal and aristocratic retreat since the 1920's and it's not hard to see why international visitors can't stay away as well.

The Veranda resort has only 118 rooms all set on several hectares of manicured gardens, huge trees, tropical palms and soothing water features. The resort has been designed with careful consideration of the principals of Feng Shui. Maybe that's why it feels so good to be here....

The resort pool is one of the most inviting you're likely to find anywhere you travel.
The infinity edge blends with the blue of the sea and you'll be tempted to chill out here or on the wooden pool decking all day long.

The beach here is one of the widest in this area.

Food is one of the great joys of travel and that sentiment is even more appropriate here......Breakfast is a buffet that is sinfully tempting.....

The lovely ISEA restaurant on the beach has a modern Thai menu to die for.....
How can you resist dishes like this: Rock Lobster Kow Soy, Lamb Rack with Thai spices, Hua Hin tuna Tartar and crepes with raison crème cheese.  Ahhhh, I'm in heaven......

The resort's sleek and contemporary Thai architecture and design extends from the lovely lobby and right into your room. The deluxe rooms have big beds and luxurious bathtubs and the wide balconies overlook gardens and ponds. Or you can upgrade to a family size Jacuzzi room.

No wonder so many people head here for weddings and honeymoons.

If you are travelling with youngsters, the water slide and the mini shoreline sand pit next to the swimming pool makes for great fun. Or they could play all day in the supervised kid's club. The resort can also arrange a baby-sitting service should you need some down time.
The spa has a good range of face and body treatments that all make the most of Thai herbal ingredients and aromatic oils. 

All this relaxation in paradise is wonderful but if you do want to explore then Hua Hin is right at your doorstep.

The resort offers a free-shuttle service for the 15 minute ride into town.

There are several top golf courses in this part of Thailand, along with fantastic water parks........elephant camps.......local markets......sea and river cruises .....and quaint beachside escapes where you can ride a horse or just chill on the sand .

There are heaps of restaurants and local Spas here too.

Next time you head to Hua Hin or Cha Am, take a break at the lovely Veranda Resort.

title: Novotel Hua Hin Cha-Am Resort & Spa | Luxury Escapes
tags: Novotel Hua Hin Cha Am Beach Resort and Spa|Novotel Hua Hin Cha-am|Novotel Cha Am|Hua Hin Thailand|Cha Am Thailand|Hua Hin beach resort|Cha Am beach resort|Thailand family resort|Thailand beach holiday|Hua Hin travel|Cha Am travel|Thailand resort review|Hua Hin attractions|Black Mountain Water Park|Black Mountain Golf Club|Luxury Escapes|Destination Thailand|Travel Asia and Beyond
description:
"Hi, I'm Samantha from Luxury Escapes and I'm here to show you the lovely Novotel Hua Hin Cha-am Beach Resort and Spa. 

Chilled Cha-am and the more happening Hua Hin have been well-kept secrets in Thailand but it's not hard to see why more and more people are heading to these stunning shores. Thai travelers discovered this beach side destination when it became the retreat for the country's royalty a hundred years ago.

In some ways the skyline here reminds me of Surfers Paradise on the Aussie Gold Coast. The Novotel is located right between Cha-am and Hua Hin so that means it has the best of both worlds. Now this would have to be on the most inviting views in Thailand.  

The impressive lobby entrance opens out onto a huge terrace and draws you down to an inviting lagoon pool. Even if you are right on the beach, a fantastic pool makes all the difference. You can relax at the pool bar ......or join the kids at the water slide.

The resort also has a cool kid's world and plenty of things to keep the whole family amused......like free Wi-Fi and this Espresso zone in the lobby where you can grab an ice-cream or a drink. If you love the mornings, then make sure you watch at least one sunrise from your balcony.....

If you are here to relax then the spa should be next on your list.

When it comes to dining, start the day just right at the Horizon Café, with a yummy buffet breakfast. Grab lunch on the beach or head back here as the sun sets for a romantic meal. Just for me, chef whipped up white prawns marinated in lemongrass with French Ratatouille and a Proscuitto pizza.

This is the sort of place that demands you just chill out and relax but if you do want more spice in your holiday life then this destination delivers.

The Novotel offers a complimentary shuttle service into Hua Hin where you can explore some of the town's best attractions. Golfers will love the vast array of golf greens in this area including the stunning Black Mountain course. If you want to cool down, head to the Black Mountain water park and wave pool.....or try your skill at wake-boarding.

Companies like Mermaid offer both river and sea cruises.......you can visit an elephant camp, take a temple tour, ride a horse on the beach or just enjoy the local shopping.

The charming streets of Hua Hin also overflow with wine bars, fun pubs with ridiculously cheap happy hours and a vibrant selection of restaurants, including great value seafood.
Now that I've discovered all this, I wish I could stay even longer.

title: Care for Dogs - Chiang Mai. Saving dogs from the dinner table!
tags: Thailand|Chiang Mai|Care for Dogs|Dogs|Dog Meat|Charity|Rehabilitation|Diseases|Distemper|Shelter|Rescued|Clinic|Quarantine|Medical|Care|Donations|Stray Dogs|Companion|Canine|Destination Thailand TV|Capital TV Bangkok|Stephen Rhodes|Save the Hill Tribe Dogs Society
description:
Around mid May, Thai police at Nakhon Phanom apprehended a convoy carrying a huge shipment of dogs destined for the dinner tables of Laos, Vietnam and China. They managed to save about a thousand, but the convoy was so large that they couldn't save them all, and it's estimated that trucks bearing many thousand more dogs broke through the road block and transported their victims to their doom. Those left behind were in an awful condition. Care for Dogs Medical Coordinator Pamela Bayer, and Yosita Srikun, their Charity Support Coordinator, rushed to Nakhom Phanom and offered their help.
They spent a week, giving endless numbers of injections, offering lots of love and care to the dogs, and helping to clean the shelter.
 It was a very intense, emotional, and sometimes harrowing experience for the Care for Dogs team. Contagious diseases like distemper were spreading like wild fire through the shelter and taking a horrifying toll on the dogs.
 Pamela and Yosita brought back three dogs to the Care for Dog's shelter -  Pui Pui, Lilly and Malee. It was a hard choice to make, knowing that those left behind faced an un-certain future. Due to the risk of contagious diseases the three rescued dogs are now in a clinic for quarantine and medical care. Care for dogs hopes to find loving homes for Pui Pui, Lilly and Malee and take in more rescued dogs. 
Hopefully Pui Pui, Lilly and Malee will soon be released from quarantine and living at the Care for Dogs shelter in outer Chiang Mai, being pampered and groomed in readiness to meet their new owners.
Currently there are about 190 dogs at the shelter which depends heavily on donations. They use about three twenty kilo bags of dog food per day which ends up costing about 30,000 baht a month.
Stray dogs are often brought to the shelter by kind hearted people who have found them wandering the streets. Adoption depends on the dog's personality and what the new owner is looking for in a pet.
So, if you're looking for a loyal canine companion, why not give a homeless dog a second chance at a new life? Contact Care for Dogs, at this phone number - 0847 525 255 - or check out their website, www.carefordogs.org

title: Her Holiness "Shinso Ito" visits Wat Paknam | Thailand
tags: Thailand|Bangkok|Thonburi|Wat Praknam|Temple|Meditiation|Holiness|Shinso Ito|Head Priest|Shinnyo-en|Buddhist|Japanese|Dai-Sojo|Theravada Buddhism|Shinnyo Buddhism|Charity|Enlightment|Maha-Chulongkorn-Rajavidyalaya|Mahavana Nirvana Sutra|Relics|Her Holiness "Shinso Ito" visits Wat Paknam|Wat Paknam Shinnyo-En|Destination Thailand|Japanese Buddhism|Shinnyo-en faith|Maha-yana Nirvana Sutra|Wat Paknam Bangkok|Thailand VLOG|one of the most stunning Stupas in Thailand
description:
Wat Paknam is located on the Thonburi side of Bangkok and is home to without a doubt one of the most stunning stupas in Thailand. The temple has a large population of monks and nuns and is famous for its methods of meditation -- a practice that has drawn foreign visitors here year after year. 

One of the longest relationships is with Her Holiness Shinso Ito, the Head of the Shinnyo-en Buddhist Community based in Japan. Her family has had a connection with the temple since 1966 when her father received Buddha relics from the Thai temple. On this day, her 71st birthday, she was back to present a reclining Buddha image to the Abbot of Wat Paknam - Somdej Phra Maha Ratcha-mang-kala-jarn. The ceremony was conducted inside the temple's magnificent stupa and the governing body of senior monks from throughout Thailand began with a ritual chant.

Shinso Ito, is the Head Priest of Shinnyo-en and is one of the few women to be granted the title of dai-sojo, the highest priestly rank in Japanese Buddhism. She was also the first woman to conduct such a ritual in Thailand. Her efforts to foster relations with Theravada Buddhism earned her an honorary doctorate from Maha-chulalongkorn-raja-vidya-laya University in 2002.

The Shinnyo-en faith is dedicated to helping people realize greater self-awareness, happiness, and harmony for the good of humanity. Shinnyo Buddhism is inspired by and rooted in the Maha-yana Nirvana Sutra, the last teachings of the Buddha, which emphasize the ability of anyone to achieve enlightenment. Followers undertake works of charity throughout the world including vital assistance during Thailand's recent floods.

Shinnyo-en attracts people from all backgrounds and faiths. Founded in Japan in the 1930s it today has close to a million practitioners worldwide and over a hundred places of training.1500 worshippers were here to witness the unique event, 700 of them had travelled from Japan alone. 

For all, it was a day to remember.
 
For more information visit: www.shinnyoen.org

title: Thailand's Tourist Police promote their 1155 Hotline during Songkran at Khao San Road
tags: Thailand|Bangkok|Songkran|Festival|Tourist Police|1155|Hotline|Emergency|Khao San Road|Cleansing|Renewal|Merit|Celebrate|Immigration Bureau|Safety|Ministry of Tourism & Sports|Somsak Pureerisak|Service|M2F|CentralWorld|Songkran (Thailand)|Destination Thailand TV|Capital TV Bangkok|Raine Grady|Thailand's Tourist Police promote their 1155 Hotline during Songkran at Khao San Road|Destination Thailand|Destination Thailand APP
description:
Besides representing a great deal of cool fun during the hot season, Thailand's Songkran Festival and the throwing of water is believed to bring good luck and prosperity for the Thai New Year. It is a time for cleansing, renewal and making merit. It's also a time to visit family and celebrate a new beginning. For many visitors though it's also a time when accidents happen. In order to guard against this the Tourist Police Division's 35 branches around Thailand linked hands with the country's Immigration Bureau to ensure the safety of tourists during this year's Songkran celebrations. For more than 20 years the Tourist Police Division has been serving and taking care of the safety of tourists who travel to Thailand, including domestic travelers. To ensure tourists got the message, the Commander of the Thai Tourist Police Division Pol.Maj.Gen.Roy Inkapairoj joined forces with the Minister for Tourism & Sports, Somsak Pu-ree-risak -- to walk down Bangkok's Khao Sarn road at the start of the water festival. The parade included a team of tourist police with information on their 1155 hotline and advice on what services tourism police can provide in case of emergency. title: Getting your toes nibbled at Fish Spas in Chiang Mai, Thailand
tags: Thailand|Chiang Mai|Fish Spa|Garra Rufa Fish|Spa|Fish|Tickling|Nip|Exfoliation|Dead Skin|Discover|Experience|Tourism|Destination Thailand TV|Capital TV Bangkok|Book Shop|Tapae Gate|Kotcuasarn Road|Destination Thailand APP|Fish Spas in Chiang Mai|aquarium|travel|thai
description:
In Chiang Mai, Fish spas are springing up like mushrooms.

The owner of this spa, Mrs Aphinphon Sonderquist, spends much of her time reassuring her customers that all is well and that the legions of garra rufa fish, swarming around their feet, mean them no harm and are simply removing dead skin, leaving the feet feeling fresh and healthy. Depending on the size of the fish, the resulting experience can range from a barely perceptible nibble to a fairly significant nip.

Despite the health benefits being extolled by the Chiangmai fish spa operators, some health concerns have been raised. Some people are worried that if the fish feasted on the flesh of a diseased foot, then the disease could be passed on to the next customer. The American government has banned fish spas for this reason. Regulations in the USA require that exfoliation instruments for the removal of dead skin cells, including live fish, either have to be sterilised, or discarded after use. At fifty five baht a fish, they are rather too expensive to throw away and definitely wouldn't survive any form of sterilising process.

And Aphinphon is adamant that there is no risk of disease being spread because:
Garra rufa fish occur in the river basins of the Northern and Central Middle East, mainly in Turkey, Syria, Iraq and Iran. It is protected from commercial exploitation in Turkey due to concerns about over harvesting for export. In the year 2011 there were 1,341 fish spas in Thailand, so it's no wonder the Turks were starting to worry about the numbers of Garra rufa being depleted. While still very popular in Chiangmai, the number of fish spas have dropped off a little and Aphinphon has diversified in that she also offers conventional foot massages for those too faint hearted to confront the terrors of the fish tank. The place was a 2nd hand book shop when she bought it and she still does a fair trade in books. Customers often browse the shelves for an appropriate bit of light reading while they dangle their legs in the water for a one hour session which costs them 99 baht. After an hours reading, they are often hooked and end up buying the book as well.

At the end of what many people regard as an indescribable experience, 
Aphinphon takes a souvenir photograph which is printed on the spot and presented to the participant.

Mrs Aphinphon's book shop and fish spa is located on Kotcuasarn Road, in Chiang Mai, just near the Tapae Gate.

title: Thailand's Tourist Police launch their Smartphone Tourist Buddy APP for holiday-makers
tags: Thailand|Bangkok|Tourist Police|Tourist|Buddy|Application|APP|Mobile|Smartphone|Telephone|Virtual|Assistant|iExhibition|Suvarnabhumi|Service|Download|iPhone|iPad|Android|Register|Information|Hotline|EMIT 1699|Emergency 1155|1699|1155|English|Thai|Destination Thailand TV|Capital TV Bangkok|Raine Grady
description:
Thailand's Tourist Police recently embarked on a major campaign to improve their image and their services for tourists by launching a new application. The "Tourist Buddy Virtual Assistant" was launched at an "i-Exhibition" within Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport. 
The event was created by the country's Tourist Police Commander Pol.Maj.Gen Roy Inkapairoj. The new APP and allows tourists to download the Tourist Buddy into smartphones, iPhones, iPads and Android devices. 
Once tourists register, and this is required if you wish to use the service, they can have access to tourist police information and numbers along with tourist deals. If there's an emergency tourist police can pinpoint the user through the APP and send assistance 24 hours a day.
When help is needed, immediate calls can be made to the Tourist Police 1155 hotline from the application. 
The Tourist Police Division is also co-operating with the Emergency Medical Institute of Thailand. Tourists with medical concerns can also call the EMIT Hotline 1699 for speedy assistance.
The Tourist Police were joined by the EMIT, The Airports organization of Thailand and the Director General of the Ministry of Tourism & Sports in launching the APP. Together the team marched with a traditional Songkran drum parade and handed out Tourist Buddy information to visitors arriving at the International Airport.
The Songkran Exhibition included a hologram message from the tourist police commander and can be watched in several languages. 
Tourism is Thailand's number one revenue earner and it's the Government's goal to increase tourism revenue income to 2 trillion Baht by 2015.
The Tourist Police believe their new Buddy APP will assist tourists in feeling more secure and confident when they travel to Thailand. We are also told it will later be available languages other than English and Thai, as will the Tourist Police website.

title: The Klong Suan 100 year old market on the outskirts of Bangkok
tags: Thailand|Bangkok|Suvarnabhumi Airport|Klong Suan|Market|Klong Suan Market|Thai style|River|Floating Market|Tourism|The Klong Suan 100 year old market on the outskirts of Bangkok|Klong Suan Market Bangkok|Thailand Tourism|Bangkok Markets|Destination Thailand|Thai Food|Thailand Travel|Travel|Chachoengsao Market|Chachoengsao Thailand|Samut Prakarn Thailand|Bangkok historic markets|Thai street food|Canal|Bangkok canals|Bangkok Muslim|Bangkok Traditional market
description:
You'll find Klong Suan 100 year old market outside Bangkok, about 20 kilometers past Suvarnabhumi airport. It's actually more than 150 years old and is a wonderful slice of traditional Thai life. Because of its remote location, Klong Suan has only recently been discovered by international tourists who mostly flock here on the weekends when boatman also arrive on the local waterway to sell their wares. While the floating market is restricted to Saturdays and Sundays, the main market is open every day and is much less crowded. If you take the time to explore you can discover some true treasures. If you love collectable tin toys, then Klong Suan delivers. Some of the vendors here have become famous within Thailand. This bakery is not busy on a weekday, but when the weekends roll in the queue for cakes is non-stop all day. Klong Suan is several hundred meters long and packed with an endless line of tiny old-fashioned wooden shops, where many of the owners still live upstairs. Some have been here since they were born and many of the businesses have been maintained for 3 or more generations. 70 year old Dumrong has been a barber here for all of his working life. His father started the barber shop before he was born. Somchai and Siriporn run one of Klong Suan's most famous candy stores along with their granddaughter Porntip and if you head here with your children this is usually one place in the market that's hard to avoid. 53 year old Penpat runs the coffee shop started by her 80 year old father, Mr Lee, who is one of the most famous vendors at Klong Suan. She is the 7th of his 9 children and oversees the business when Mr Lee takes a rare day off. You can sip on Arabica coffee from Thailand's north and gaze at the array of family photos that decorate the walls.
There is a small museum at Klong Suan that displays all kinds of products sold in the past. Vintage shampoos, washing powder, and old tea and cookie boxes share dusty shelves with antique medicine bottles. It's housed in what was once the residence of one of the market's founders. Klong Suan market is clean and beautifully maintained, so as you explore the wooden walkways, stop for some traditional local food and enjoy the atmosphere of a bygone era, when time definitely moved at a slower and friendlier pace.

RECIPE #1

Salmon carpaccio dressed with tandoori sour cream,
salmon caviar and pickled cucumber salad

Ingredients:
300gm Salmon fillet cut into thin slices
30 gm Tandoori paste
30 ml Sour cream 
5  gm Blank fish eggs
10 gm Salmon caviar 
20 gm Assorted micro herbs 
1 cucumber - peeled and thinly sliced
1 cup yoghurt
1 tablespoons lemon juice
1 tablespoon chopped fresh mint
½ teaspoon white sugar
¼ teaspoon kosher salt
1 ts fleur de sel

Preparation:
Stir together the cucumber, yoghurt, lemon juice, mint, sugar, and salt in a bowl. 
Cover and refrigerate at least 3 hours, preferably overnight.

Arrange the salmon slices in one layer on a large serving plate.

Sprinkle the salmon with the fleur de sel, micro herbs, salmon caviar, spoons of cucumber salad and dots tandoori cream and serve.

By Marshall Orton 

RECIPE #2

Mini poppadom mille-feuille with french foie gras
Scented by mango chutney

Ingredients:
1 Jar of Mango chutney (sweet or spicy)
24 mini Poppadoms
50 ml  Oli 
300 gm Foie gras 
30 ml Cognac 
30 ml Sauternes
3 gm Salt & Pepper
5 Coffee beans 

Preparation:
Cook Poppadoms between a hot pan and a heave pot to keep them thin and straight. Place on paper to drain oil off them.

For the terrine:
Separate the Foie gras lobes. Remove any of the larger veins from the big lobe of foie gras, 
Sprinkle generously with sea salt and white pepper. And add a splash of Cognac & Sauternes 
Place the foie gras into jars, make the fit as tight as possible. 
Marinate in the refrigerator overnight.
The next day, take the terrine out of refrigerator for 1 hour before cooking, and preheat the oven to 200ºF.
Cook the foie gras in the oven in a bain marie for about 45 minutes 
Cooking is complete when you see a thin layer of melted yellow foie gras butter on the surface.
Cover tightly and place in refrigerator for 2 to 3 days to allow the flavors to fully develop.

For plates 
Lay out the crisp Poppadoms and spoon on some terrine then some mango chutney and top with one more Poppadom / repeat this sequence and then great some fresh coffee over them and service.  

By Marshall Orton

title: ASEAN gets serious. An interview with Dr Surin Pitsuwan
tags: Thailand|Bangkok|ASEAN|Indonesia|Malaysia|Singapore|Philippines|Brunai|Myanmar|Cambodia|Laos|Vietnam|Accelerating|Growth|Social Progress|Protection|Stability|Dr Surin Pitsuwan|12th Secretary-General|Capital TV Bangkok|Destination Thailand TV|Raine Grady
description:
The association of SEA nations, or ASEAN has been in existence since 1967 and was founded by Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.
Since then, membership has expanded to include Brunei, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam. Its aims include accelerating economic growth, social progress, cultural development among its members, protection of regional peace and stability, and opportunities for member countries to discuss differences peacefully. 
The area ASEAN covers is massive. 
4.46 million square kilometers which is 3% of the total land area of Earth, with a population of around 600 million people, which is 8.8% of the world's total. 
If ASEAN were a single entity, it would rank as the tenth largest economy in the world.
For many years, ASEAN has been regarded as a lame body or a toothless mouse. Its ASEAN way -- an agreement of "non-interference" in each other's affairs -- meant that for the most part, there were no condemnations of, or sanctions against, or even reactions to alleged human rights violations amongst them from anyone in the group.
Former Secretary General Surin Pitsuwan says its now time for ASEAN to be taken seriously.

title: Harvest time in Thailand's Khao Yai wine region
tags: Thailand|Khao Yai|PB Winery|Grapes|Wine|Harvest|PB Valley|Fertile|Mountains|Singha Beer|Shiraz|Chenin Blanc|French|Spain|Vintage|Great Hornbill Bistro|Great Hornbill Grill|Pizza|International cuisine|Sukhumvit|Soi 39|Capital TV Bangkok|Dr Piya Bhirom-bhakdi|National Park|World Heritage Park
description:
Khao Yai is one of the loveliest regions of Thailand. Its national park is a world heritage site that's blessed with a lush, mountainous landscape that stretches down to fertile valleys where the pioneers of Thailand's wine industry planted their first vines. The PB Valley Khao Yai winery was established in 1989, by entrepreneur and visionary Dr. Piya Bhirom-bhakdi, whose family also founded the Singha Corporation. The first vineyard spread over a total of 20 hectares and was planted with Shiraz for the red wine and Chenin Blanc for the white, featuring French rootstock, and Tempranillo from Spain. With the harvest of 1998, PB Valley Khao Yai Winery celebrated its first milestone. The 1999 vintage proved that quality wine could be successfully produced in Thailand and PB's international awards speak for themselves. Tourists venture here every day for wine tastings and vineyard tours. We were also here to see if this year would be an award winning harvest. From the fields, the harvest goes into the winery where winemaker Joolperra gets to work.
The Great Hornbill Bistro is a sister venue to the Great Hornbill Grill vineyard restaurant at PB Valley.  Located on Sukhumvit soi 39 the bistro's team specializes in modern international cuisine. One of the biggest hits here is the thin crust PB Pizza and you can take classes to learn how to make your own. Some say good wine is wasted without good food. Well, we tend to agree and a bottle of red or white is even more appreciated when you see what's involved to bring it to the table.

title: A city hotel that captures the elegance of 1930's Shanghai in the heart of Bangkok
tags: Thailand|Bangkok|Chinatown|Chinese|Shanghai|Shanghai Mansion|Boutique|Hotel|Chinese Design|Julian Coombs|Romantic|Vintage|Athmosphere|Library|Atrium|Tea Room|Asian Cuisine|Massage|Jazz|Bar|Cotton|Traditional Medicine|Capital TV Bangkok|Raine Grady|Historic|Destination Thailand TV|Destination Thailand|Destination Thailand APP|Yaowaraj Road|Tourism
description:
A visit to Bangkok should include a walk through the fascinating district of Chinatown. It's one of the best Chinatown's in Asia and is a hive of constant commercial activity and a journey through history. Chinese merchants originally moved to this area in the early 1780's when Bangkok was founded. After generations of living here, the Chinese in Chinatown consider themselves Thai, but you'll find that this part of Thailand remains a unique world of its own. One of the most talked about places in the heart of Chinatown, on Yaowaraj Road is the boutique hotel Shanghai Mansion. Built in 1892, this stunning historic property has operated as a boutique hotel since 2006. Since its inception, the Shanghai Mansion has offered guests  a truly unique experience that captures the elegance of 1930's Shanghai. The original architecture has been complimented with a contemporary Chinese design that's the work of architect Julian Coombs. The end result is a collection of romantic oriental rooms, with canopied beds, red leather couches, lanterns and a cool vintage atmosphere. There's a hotel library that offers view over the hotel's inner atrium and lovely water gardens and a Chinese tea room that offers afternoon teas every day. Chinese and other Asian cuisine is on offer and while staying here you should also experience an authentic Chinese massage. From the incredible design that hearkens back to the romance of 1930's Shanghai, a time when great jazz artists were featured in the best clubs in the city to the elegance and intimacy of 1950's underground night clubs in New York, Chicago and Paris. Cotton has found the best Thai jazz artists to do their thing such Siam Swing band playing a classic pop songs (think about Coltrane's "My favorite Things!) Outside, the colors of Chinatown beckon anyone who loves to explore. The Shanghai Mansion is within easy reach of some of Bangkok's most historic sites and you can take walking tours to temples and riverside markets.
You'll finds streets overflowing with gold shops, tea shops, traditional medicine vendors and street food of all flavors. When the sun goes down the journey back through time continues with an evening at the hotels award winning jazz bar Cotton where both international and local jazz musicians can be found. The romance of old Shanghai makes a trip to Bangkok's Chinatown an unforgettable experience.
www.shanghaimansion.com

description:
When you get an invitation to travel to the gorgeous island of Samui, there's really only one answer. Let's go. I was here to explore a brand new resort, but first a quick look around a destination that's rapidly evolving.  If you want to party, then Chaweng beach is the place to head to......
My next stop was the lovely beachfront of Chaweng Noi and the real reason I was here on the island. Starwood Hotels and Resorts were introducing the newest addition to the Luxury Collection brand, the just opened Vana Belle Resort. It's name means beautiful forest and its been thoughtfully designed over a hillside where the native trees and rock formations have been retained. Combine that with stunning views, gorgeous architecture and lavish service and you've got the makings of an enchanting getaway. General Manager Mark O'Sullivan is lucky enough to work here.....
The luxurious pool suites and villas range from 86 to 211 square meters and are so lovely you won't want to go anywhere else for days.The resort features two restaurants and has a unique approach to dining. When any new resort opens in Thailand its customary to bless the property and ensure an auspicious start. The Siri-wattana-bakdi family who own this resort and oversee the Thai Bev/Beer Chang empire, arranged for the placement of a spirit house at the resort entrance.
Installing a spirit house needs a special Brahmin ceremony in order to beg the spirit or 'chao tee' to come and live in it. In the past this ceremony could only be performed by a Brahmin, a hereditary member of a learned caste which originated in India. Today, those who have learned the correct procedure from a Brahmin, including the necessary Pali incantations can officiate at the ceremony. Donned in white, he called for family members and resort workers to join in and make an offering.
The owner's family members told me why this sort of ceremony is so important for a new venture. Vana Belle has now been truly blessed, a fact you'll discover as soon as you head through the landscaped surrounds and into the grounds of a true island paradise.

description: On Sunday afternoons in Bangkok, listen carefully and you might hear the roar of binocular-attached punters as they watch their favorite horse at the races. The city's horse-racing events are held every second Sunday and the venue alternates between the Royal Bangkok Sports Club and the Royal Turf Club. On this day at the Royal Turf club, scores of enthusiasts had packed the stadium for one of the biggest events of the year -- the Million Baht Derby Cup. Horse-racing first began in Thailand over a century ago when King Rama V returned from his state visit to Europe in 1897. Not long after, in 1901 His Majesty bestowed a piece of land to be used as the country's first racecourse, the Royal Bangkok Sports Club. This second venue, The Royal Bangkok Turf Club was established in 1961. Behind the scenes on race days like this, Major General Sompoth is maintaining order and overseeing the stables. As we mentioned, betting on the races is allowed but only at the club and it begins at Baht 50- on a 'win or a place' basis. Horse racing is not a major sport in Thailand but those involved are passionate about the competition. You can also see many foreign visitors track-side on major race days. All eyes were then on the track as the main race, the Derby Cup was about to begin. Then it was time for the prizes and the lucky punters to collect their winnings. A day at the races in Bangkok is an exhilarating experience.

title: The Race of Champions Thailand - The Best Drivers in the World battling in one Stadium!
tags: Thailand|Bangkok|Rajamangala Stadium|Race of Champions|Race|Motorsport|Champions|2012|Formula 1|WRC|Touring|Le Mans|Moto GP|Michael Schumacher|Sebastian Vettel|David Coultard|Romain Grosjean|Mick Doohan|Jorge Lorenzo|ROC Asia|ROC|Charoen-Suka-Wattana|Team India|Team Germany|Tom Kristensen|Easy Kart|Bali Hai|Pattaya|Capital TV Bangkok|Tyler Nyerges|Indycar|X-Games
description:
The 2012 Race of Champions took place at Bangkok's Raja-man-gala Stadium where a special parallel track had to be constructed. The event, which was being staged for the 25th time, was in Thailand for the first time ever and it brought together the world's greatest drivers from motor sport's main disciplines -- including:Formula 1, World Rally, Touring Cars, Le Mans, MotoGP, IndyCar and the X-Games. The 3 days of driving action set champions free to battle head-to-head in identical machines. For F1 fans the star attractions were Michael Schumacher, Sebastian Vettel, David Coultard and Romain Grosjean. For MotoGP lovers - world champions Mick Doohan and Jorge Lorenzo added some two-wheel talent to the mix. A great line-up of top drivers from throughout Thailand, Asia and the world were also here for the challenge. In between races, fans were treated to a wide array of stunt shows and dramatic driving displays. Day one of the racing action began with the Race of Champions Thailand and ROC Asia. Thailand's own race saw a four-way battle between the country's top rally and drift drivers. 49 year old Thai champ Charoen-Suka-Wattana was the ultimate winner. The ROC Asia race was next, and Team India took the glory, much to the delight of the numerous Indian fans in the stadium. Day two was the Race of Nations. The stadium was packed, as legends from many of the world's biggest motor sport series teamed up in pairs, to battle for national pride. They raced a mix of cars -- including the Audi R8 LMS, VW Scirocco, Lamborghini Gallardo Super Trofeo and the Toyota GT86. It was no surprise when Team Germany's Michael Schumacher and Sebastian Vettel added to their incredible run of success by winning their sixth consecutive ROC Nations Cup title. From Go karts, to the world arena and on to events like this. The last hot night in Bangkok was the individual Race of Champions itself. It was a tough competition and Thailand's drivers put on a great performance much to the delight of the crowds. But it was French Formula 1 star Romain Grosjean who stole the show. He overcame Le Mans legend Tom Kristensen and put in a stunning performance to eclipse 15 fellow superstars to win the Race Of Champions.
It was a night to remember and a great chance to get up close to some of the legends of motor sport.....If I practice enough at Easy Kart, maybe one day the champions will be racing against me.

Kaffir lime leaves --16g (16-18no.s)
Ginger -- 20g
Garlic clove - 4 No.s(20g)s 
Patak's Tikka Masala paste -- 50g
Full fat yogurt -- 75g
Salt -- 2g 
Sugar -- 2g
Fresh mint leaves -- 6g (1tsp)
Lime juice -- 10g (2tsp)
Oil -- 10g/2tsp
Chicken Whole -- 1No.
Butter For Basting

For Raw papaya and mango salad:
Raw papaya (peeled and finely shredded) -- 1 No.
Raw mango (finely shredded) -- 1No.
Fresh red chilli finely shredded 2 No's
Lime juice -- 35ml/ 2tbsp
Red chilli powder --0.5g 
Salt --1.5g
Honey --10g/2tsp
Fresh coriander(roughly chopped) -- 5g/1tsp
Oil -- 10g
Mint fresh chopped -- 2.5g/1/2tsp

METHOD

1. Make paste of lime leaves, ginger and garlic using a mortar and pestle or kitchen blender.( you will have to chop the lime leaves first or alternatively use blender).
2. Add Patak's tikka masala paste, yogurt, above paste, salt and sugar in a bowl and mix together like a marinade.
3. Finely chop mint leaves and add to the marinade.
4. Add lime juice and oil and mix well.
5. Add chicken to the bowl and mix together with light hand.
6. Cover the bowl and keep in the refrigerator for minimum of 2 hours.
7. Cook the marinated chicken in the oven at 200°C for 8 -- 9 minutes or under the grill. 
8. Soak raw papaya& mango juliennes and shredded red chillies in ice cold water till they become firm.
9. Make a dressing with lime juice, red chilli powder, salt, mint and honey.
10. When the papaya, chillies and the mango juliennes are firm, drain them ensuring there is no water left in them.
11. Add papaya, mango, chillies and fresh coriander together in a bowl, add the dressing and mix with light hands and without extensive mixing (if extensively handled the salad will go lumpy).
12. Serve chicken tikka on the bed of raw papaya salad and lemon wedges.

title: Exploring Chumphon - Island Hopping and Eco-Holidays
tags: Thailand|Chumphon|Lomprayah Ferry|Koh Lang Ka Jew|Birds Nesting|Sandy Beaches|Rocky Limestone Cliffs|Coral|Fish|Turtles|\Tham Nok Nang Aen|Caves|\Pitak Island\|Eco-tourism|Fishing|Community|Coconut Plantations|Seafood|\Nok Air\|\Capital TV Bangkok\|\Raine Grady\
description:
When it comes to journeying around the waters off shore from Chumpon, in Thailand's South, the best known high-speed ferry service is run by Lomprayah. The company has its own jetty on the edge of town and from here you can set off to explore some of Thailand's most famous island escapes. We cruised past the Chumphon archipelago and then ventured on through turquoise water. Koh Lang Ka Jew is a large bird's nest concession island. It features white sandy beaches and rocky limestone cliffs that beckon to be climbed. Below the gentle waves, the island is surrounded by several ranges of coral reef so it is a popular diving and snorkeling spot. You'll discover plenty of hard and soft corals and a large amount of sea life such as bat fish, trevally, fusiliers, turtles and seasonal whale sharks. On shore you can enjoy the beach.....
... or explore the island's small caves, including Tham Nok Nang Aen, or the swallow cave, which has a stone inscription by King Rama Five. 
Our journey continued on through the waters of the gulf of Thailand to another lovely island escape. Pitak Island has pristine natural surroundings and a focus on eco-tourism.
Its name actually means ghost calling. The fishing community here lives in small houses built on wooden poles in the water and along the shores you'll also see villagers at work in the local coconut plantations. The seafood on offer here is spectacular so make sure you order some BBQ'd and spicy Thai dishes. If you want to stay a bit longer, the home stay is great value and a true rustic introduction to island life in Thailand.
 
There is a lot to see in the enchanting province of Chumpon. Before you pass through this sleepy gateway to the south, make sure you linger here for a little longer. 
You'll have both a warm welcome and some laid-back holiday memories.
 
For more information visit:
www.nokair.com

title: Exploring Chumphon - Royal Shrines and Fancy Loos
tags: Shrine|Marine Memorabilia|\Royal Chumphon\|\Nam Dam Garden\|Fancy toilets|Flushed with success \Nok Air\|\Capital|TV|Bangkok\|\Raine|Grady\|Tourism
description:
Chumphon is located on the Isthmus of Kra, the narrow landbridge connecting the Malay Peninsula with the mainland of Thailand. It might be small, but Chumphon is packed with surprises. One of the main attractions in town is this popular Shrine.
Dedicated to the Admiral prince, whose full name is the lengthy Phra Borom-Mawong Thoe Krom-luang Chumphon Khet Udomsak, the Shrine is shaped like a ship itself and decorated with an interesting array of marine memorabilia.
The site is visited every day by navy crews and fishermen as well as those with family members at sea. Similar Shrines can be found in most coastal locations around Thailand. After an offering is made, if luck is visited on the worshiper, then it's customary to fire off a pistol or several firecrackers.
There is also a museum on site with exhibits focusing on the admiral's biography and items he used throughout his life -- along with a few larger treasures.
You can climb over the torpedo-ship Royal Chumphon for as long as you like.
My next stop was somewhat bizarre. Nai Dam Garden is a popular spot for coffee in Chumpon and the ideal place to take a toilet break. That is because there is nothing but toilets here, of every size and variety. The creators, Pongsak Ching-su-wan-rot and his father, Nai Dam, originally built one of Chumphon's best toilets to serve the needs of visitors who came to see their successful fruit plantation.  A year later, the toilet was named the country's best. Flushed with success, Pongsak was inspired to build more creative loos and this is the result. The coffee shop here takes the theme to a whole new level. There are souvenirs shaped like, well..... use your imagination, and your beverage will be served in a very special cup. If you've gotta go, it may as well be a memorable experience.
www.nokair.com
www.tourismthailand.org/Chumphon

tags: Thailand|Bangkok|Live|Theatre|Community|Bangkok Community Theatre|English|The British Club|B Floor Theatre|Thai|Pridi Banomyong Institute|Thonglor|Oranong Thaisriwong|The Country Wife|Severin Herbert|John|Wright|Jarunun Phantachat|Teerawat Mulvilai|The Other Land|Stephen Thomas|Robin Schroeter|Capital TV Bangkok|Raine Grady
description:
If you love the smell of greasepaint and the roar of the crowd you'll be pleased to know that Bangkok has a thriving Theatre Scene.

Our story begins here at the British Club where the Bangkok Community Theatre is rehearsing for its next production -- the Country Wife.

Bangkok Community Theatre is celebrating 40 years of bringing English Theatre to Bangkok audiences. The group was founded in 1972 when two existing drama groups dating from the 1950's joined hands.
 
The group has entertained local audiences with some of the world's great Theatre Classics and this performance of The Country Wife is sure to be a hit. The William Witcherley restoration comedy was written in the 17th century but its themes of freedom, double standards and hypocrisy remain relevant today.

•         Bangkok Community Theatre - For bookings call: 081 741 0703
•         Or visit: www.bct-th.org
•         Location: The British Club, Silom Soi 18

Meanwhile, the local Thai Theatre Scene is also making a noise. The team at B-Floor Theatre Productions is known for its willingness to tackle controversial subjects.
Thai actress Oranong Thaisriwong took to centre stage recently for a solo performance of Banglamerd -- a play that tackles the issues of freedom of speech and censorship in the land of smiles. Her portrayal was both funny and frightening.

Producer Jaa says this type of Theatre is not only art - it's a vital commentary on contemporary issues.
 
Meanwhile, B Floor Theatre is also preparing for its newest play -- The Other Land.
This contemporary performance is based on a 1996 S.E.A.- Write work that examines the conflict in the South of Thailand. The Other Land is directed by Teerawat Mulvilai, the director of the play "Oxygen" which had rave reviews in New York earlier this year.
 
All of B Floor's productions are subtitled in English. Some of the plays also feature foreign actors who are skilled enough to perform in Thai. Stephen Thomas and Robin Schroeter told me about their roles.
 
The Other Land" will be performed as part of the Diverse Arts Festival by the Pridi Banomyong Institute in Thonglor, Sukhumvit 55

RECIPE

CHICKEN BIRYANI

INGREDIENTS 

                        2 ½ Cups Uncooked Basmati Rice (cleaned and washed
                        400 Grams Chicken Fillet(cut into required size)
                        2 Tbsp Butter
                        1 Cup Onions (sliced)
                        1 Tbsp Garlic(pounded)
                        1 Tbsp Ginger (pounded)
                        4 Cinnamon sticks (about 2 inches long x ¼ inch  thick)
                        5 Pods Cardamons (split open)
                        10 Cloves
                        3 Bay leaves
                        2 Tsp Tumeric Powder and 10 strands of Saffron (Soak                          
                        Saffron in ½ cup of hot water for at least 1 hour before cooking)
                       1 pouch Patak's  Madras Curry Paste
                       1 Tsp Cumin Seeds Powder
                       1 Tsp Sugar
                       1 Tsp Salt 
                       1 ½ Cups Water 
                       1 Cup Coconut Milk
                       ½  Tsp Food color -- Strawberry Red
                        Silver paper-optional

METHOD

1. Heat butter in a large pan
2. Add Cinnamon, Cardamon, Cloves and Bay leaves.Add Garlic,Ginger, Onions and cook until brown.Add in the Patak's paste and cook for at least 5 mins until nice aroma.
3. Add in the chicken fillet and cook well
4. Add dissolved Saffron and Tumeric Powder with Cumin Seed Powder, sugar and Salt.
5. Add Rice, and mix well (off fire)
6. Put the above mixture, Coconut Milk and water into a rice cooker and cook rice.
7. When rice is ready, sprinkle the safe red color powder over the top of the cooked rice 
8. Cover the rice cooker for 5 minutes until the color seeps through
9. Stir the Saffron rice gently
10. Decorate Saffron rice with silver paper and rice is ready to be served

LADY PIE RECIPE

LADY PIE JUMBO PATAKS BUTTER CHICKEN PIE

Ingredients for 4 individual 240 gm jumbo pies or 1 pie in a 23 cm tray
300 gm short crust pastry bottoms
200 gm plain flour
50 gm butter
Pinch of salt
2 to 3 tablespoons of water to mix
200 gm Puff Pastry Tops - difficult to make for the amateur and probably better to buy or to use Short-crust pastry as above. Puff Pastry is available in most
large stores)

Pie Filling

Pataks Butter Chicken Paste  Packet -- 80gm net. serves 4
450  gm diced Chicken
30 gm butter
1 diced onion
60 ml water
2 fresh diced tomatoes
60 ml cream or yoghurt
Chopped coriander to garnish

Method

Short-crust
Pastry- Mix the flour and salt in a bowl, add the butter (cut into cubes) using your fingertips to rub the butter into the flour until mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Gradually add the water stirring it with a knife. Bring together and wrap in cling film and allow to rest for 15 minutes in the fridge. After 15 minutes you are ready to roll out the pastry to either cover 4 individual foil pie trays or 1 x 23 cm foil tray.  

Puff
Pastry -- Place upside down pie tray over ready rolled puff pastry (or short-crust) and cut a circle for 4 the tops mixture (Pie Filling) In a medium sized pan, heat 30gms of butter then add the diced chicken breast and onion, and fry until sealed. Add the contents of the Patak's packet and fry for 2 minutes. Add 60 ml water and 2 fresh diced tomatoes and cook with the lid on for approx 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked. Stir in 60 ml of cream or yoghurt, and garnish with chopped coriander. Allow mixture to cool.

Pie Assembly
Having inserted the bottom short-crust pastry in the bottom of the foil tray, add the mixture (pie filling) evenly between the 4 pie trays (or 1 big tray). Brush the rim of the bottoms of the trays with a little whisked egg then place the Puff Pastry (or Short-crust Pastry) lid/top over the top, pressing the edges together to seal. Brush the tops with whisked egg to glaze then bake in a pre-heated oven of 200 degrees C for 30 minutes, or until golden brown.

title: Nong Nooch Gardens Pattaya - A Scientific Research Center Saving Endangered Plant Species
tags: Thailand|Pattaya|Bangsaray|Nong Nooch Tropical Gardens|Botanical Gardens|Scientific|Research|Propagation|Gene|Bank|Conservation|Cycads|Palms|Orchids|Hybrid Plants|Anders Lindstrom|Botanist|Kampol Tansacha|Capital TV|Raine Grady|Destination Thailand|Destination Thailand TV|Nong Nooch Gardens Pattaya|Thailand Tourism|Pattaya Attractions|Nong Nooch Gardens Pattaya - A Scientific Research Center Saving Endangered Plant Species
description:
The 600 acre Nong Nooch Tropical Garden, just outside Thailand's Resort City of Pattaya is one of the most stunning attractions in the Land of Smiles.

Besides its traditional shows and animal attractions, this is a must-see destination for gardeners and botanists -- both amateur and advanced.

The world loses around one and a half acres of rainforest every second, so the team at Nong Nooch have joined hands with other conservationists to preserve plants and propagate some of the planets highly endangered species.

This garden has evolved into one of the largest collections of living plants in Asia and its diversity is world renowned.

On this day we were venturing behind the scenes to an area of Nong Nooch Gardens that the general public rarely sees. Our guide was Anders Lindstrom who is a world renowned expert in cycads and has worked here since the gardens first opened in 1980.
Besides its vast Palm and Orchid collection, Nong Nooch has one of the world's most impressive collections of Cycads. 

The garden focuses on Southeast Asian, Tropical American and Central African species of Cycads, but a collection of almost every species can also been seen here. In connection with conservation agencies this is an important conservation area for this endangered and ancient plant group and Anders manages a major Cycad gene bank on site.
The efforts of the Nong Nooch team have been recognized and applauded both near and far. This garden is a multiple winner of Thailand's Kinnari tourism awards and in 2010 Nong Nooch won the prestigious gold medal for its display of "Asian Culture & Plants" at the Chelsea Flower show in London -- the most prestigious flower show in the world.

Do yourself a favor and spend a day in the garden at Nong Nooch Tropical Gardens, Pattaya.

www.nongnoochtropicalgarden.com

INGREDIENTS

INGREDIENTS

1          Tablespoon              Butter (salted)
1          Tablespoon              Ginger Chopped
½         Tablespoon              Bird Chillies Chopped
1           Tablespoon             Onions Chopped
1           Tablespoon             Fresh Coriander Chopped
1           Tablespoon             Black and Golden Raisins(mix together)
1           Tablespoon             Sliced Almonds(skin removed)
150       Grams                    Minced Chicken
1           Tablespoon             Patak's Chicken Tikka Masala Paste

1           Tablespoon             Cooking Oil

6. Top the Papadam with chicken mixture and sprinkle with cheese.

tags: Thailand|Bangkok|Indian|Cinema|Colours|of|Passion|Raja|Ravi|Varma|Painter|Nandana|Sen|Actress|Ketan|Mehta|Director|Lekha|Shankar|Event|Organizer|.H.E.|Anil|Wadhwa|Ambassador|to|Capital|TV|Raine|Grady|:Bangkok|Art|Culture|Centre|Diverse Cinema
description:
Lovers of Indian Cinema were recently treated to a special screening in Bangkok of the acclaimed Indian movie Colours of Passion, a look a the life of 19th century Indian painter Raja Ravi Varma. 
Raja Ravi Varma, played by actor Randeep Hooda, came from what is today known as Kerala and achieved recognition for his depiction of scenes from the epics of the Mahab-harata and Ramayana. His paintings are considered to be among the best examples of the fusion of Indian traditions with the techniques of European academic art. He is considered among the greatest painters in the history of Indian art. The film, not the traditional Bollywood song and dance fest, is a sensual story about the muse he loved.

Extra Details:
RANG RASIYA, "COLOURS OF PASSION" from India, was the Opening Film of a new Film Series called 'CINEMA DIVERSE' to bring films and  film-makers from around the world to interact with Thai audiences. This year, the focus is on  films and film-makers from Asia. It's the initiative of  the Director of the BANGKOK ART & CULTURE CENTRE (BACC), Khun  Luckana Kunavichayanont, to extend the image of BACC so that it becomes a centre for quality-cinema, in addition to being an in-demand-arts-centre which it is today.
The movie was curated by the new FilmSForum  movie club, with Pasiree Pana and L.Shankar. Well-known Indian Director KETAN MEHTA and lead-actress NANDANA SEN especially flew down to Bangkok to attend the event courtesy Thai Airways International, who are the top airlines to India with maximum routes to the country.
The event was supported by the Embassy of India and Indian Cultural Centre in particular the culture-loving Indian Ambassador to Thailand, HE Anil Wadhwa. The other Sponsors of the event were Mr HK Agarwal,Executive President of the Aditya Birla Group, Mr Atul Jogani of  Almac and  the Jogani Group, Mr Suchin Sachaphimukh of  Express International, Ms Vinder Balbir of  'Ms Balbir's Restaurant', Rembrandt Hotel Bangkok and Coca Cola.

The next film with be NIKINI VASSA' (AUGUST DRIZZLE) from Srilanka on SAT 28 JULY. The 2011 movie is the first film of young Director ARUNA JAYAWARDANA who has won many awards at festivals around the world.
The Director will attend the event as also the second lead-actress SULOCHANA WEERASINGHE. The event will be supported by the Embassy of Srilanka, who will provide Srilankan food prior to the screening.

For more details,check  www.bacc.or.th

RECIPE

FISH BAKED IN BANANA LEAVES

INGREDIENTS
  
 300  Gram   Boneless Fish Pieces cut into 2 inch 
 1  Teaspoon  Salt
 2  Tablespoon  Patak's Korma Gravy Paste
 2  Teaspoon  Mango Chutney
      Black Pepper Crush for taste
 1/3  Cup   Coconut Milk
      Red Chilies sliced for garnish
                                                Banana leaves and aluminum foil 

METHOD

1.    Place fish in a mixing bowl, add salt and black pepper .
2.    Then add in the remaining ingredients except the banana leaves and foil. Marinate the fish for 30 -- 45 minutes in the refrigerator.
3.    Put a big sheet of aluminum foil on to a baking tray,place pieces of fresh banana leaves on to the foil. Spread marinated fish pieces and top with more layers of banana leaves enough to cover the fish.
4.    Wrap tightly with the foil.
5.    Heat oven temperature to 450 Fahrenheit. Grill in oven for 15- 20 minutes.

title: Mrs Balbir cooks Tandoori Chicken Tikka Salad with Patak's
tags: Thailand|Bangkok|Sukhumvit|Mrs Balbir|Indian Restaurant|Thai Airways|Pataks|Tandoori chicken tikka salad|Tikka|Tesco Supercenter|Central Food Halls|Tops Market|Gourmet Market|Paragon|Emporium|Home Freshmarket The Mall|Foodland|Villa Market|Sodexo|Stuart Winters
description:
Join our celebrity chef Mrs Balbir as she cooks Tandoori Chicken Tikka Salad.
Joining her is the CEO of Sodexo Thailand, Stuart Winters who has been in the Land of Smiles for 7 years. 

"What's cooking with Mrs Balbir" is sponsored by Patak's.
www.pataks.co.uk
www.mrsbalbirs.com

In Thailand, Patak's is available in Tesco Supercenter, Central Food Halls, Tops Market, Gourmet Market at Paragon and Emporium, Home Freshmart The Mall, Foodland and Villa Market.
"Britain's favorite curry brand comes to Thailand"  
 
The Recipe for: TANDOORI CHICKEN TIKKA SALAD                                                 

PART 1:
 
INGREDIENTS 

250  Grams  Boneless Chicken
  1  Tablespoon  Lime Juice
  ¼   Teaspoon  Salt
    1Pinch   Safe food coloring -- Strawberry Red
    1Pinch   Safe food Coloring -- Egg Yellow
  ½  Tablespoon  Garam Masala
  ¼  Teaspoon  Cumin seed Powder
  ½  Teaspoon  Chilli Powder
  ½  Tablespoon  Garlic Chopped
  ½  Tablespoon  Ginger Chopped 
  1 ½   Tablespoon  Thick Hung Yogurt
  ½  Tablespoon  Olive Oil (for Pan fry)
  1  Tablespoon  Patak's Chicken Tikka Masala Paste
                   ½                Tablespoon             Japanese White Wine

METHOD

1. Wash and dry the Chicken well for spices to stick.
2. Sprinkle lime juice, salt and the food colorings.
3. Add in all the remaining ingredients except the Olive oil.
4. Add the Olive oil to a hot pan, cook the chicken for 5 minutes turning sides.
5. Cut into required size and keep aside.


PART 2:
 
SALAD INGREDIENTS

  100  Gram   Pumpkin -sliced 
  100  Gram   Eggplant -sliced
  100  Gram   Button Mushroom -sliced
  100  Gram   Avocado --cut into required size
  150  Gram   Ripe Mango --cut into required size
  50  Gram   Ripe Tomatoes -sliced 
  50  Gram   Spanish Onion -sliced 
  50  Gram   Rocket Salad
       Pinenuts (garnish)
       Parmesan cheese shaving (garnish)
       Olive Oil for pan fry

PART 3:
 
SALAD DRESSING

  ¼  Cup   Lemon Juice 
  ¼  Cup   Red Wine Vinegar
  ½  Cup             Olive Oil
       Crushed Black Pepper
  
METHOD

1.     In a skillet heat Olive oil and pan fry the pumpkin, eggplant, mushrooms until cooked and slightly crisp.In a small bowl beat the salad dressing ingredients and keep it aside.

2.      In another large mixing bowl, add the remaining ingredients including the cooked Tandoori chicken pieces.

3.     Than add in the salad dressing and mix well. Garnish with Pinenuts and Parmesan Shavings. Top with extra pieces of Mango, Avocado and crushed black pepper. Serve.

title: 10 tips for the Thailand holiday you need to know before you go
tags: Thailand|jan travel thailand|thailnd vlog|thailand travel|thailand advices|thailand top 10|thai customs|thailand customs|thai language|thailand tips|thailand travel tips
description:
10 awesome Thailand tips before you go for a holiday in Thailand as a tourist 🇹🇭. In this Thailand vlog, I will give you 10 pieces of advice before you travel to Thailand on a vacation or on a holiday in Thailand. See my Step-by-Step to TDAC: https://youtu.be/-XSYAput-Jc?si=gULd_WXh0l-lQkpg

LINK to my video about using BOLT TAXI in Thailand: https://youtu.be/hKuSuhwClr4?si=1AOzw67d3bLeFjKq

10 Thailand tips 🇹🇭 you need to know before traveling as a tourist in Thailand. I will also give you 2 BONUS TIPS before you travel to Thailand on a holiday. If you have some good advice for other people who need to know more about traveling in Thailand, please feel free to tell us in the comment section below the video.

Topics in the Video:
• Passport expiration date and visa in Thailand.
Minimum 6 months before the expiry date on the day of traveling.
When you arrive at the immigration desk at the airport in Thailand, you have to show your passport, and maybe also your boarding pass.

• Vaccinations before traveling to Thailand.
Ask your doctor which vaccines are necessary when traveling to Thailand.
Remember to bring your medicine if you use any kind of medicine.

• Travel insurance in place before departure to Thailand.
Be sure that your travel insurance covers you in Thailand, as well as during the period you will be in Thailand.

Be sure to have a copy of your travel insurance on your phone and in print.

App from your insurance company on your phone, and the emergency number for your insurance company.

• Currency and payment cards in Thailand.
VISA credit card, at least 1 or 2, Thai cash, or US dollars or Euros. Check the expiry date on your credit cards.
Bring some Thai baht in cash from home.
My experience with ATM machines in Thailand is that you can withdraw up to approximately. 10000 Thai baht per day.

• Climate and clothing in Thailand.
Drink plenty of fluids every day, at least 2 liters, besides alcohol. 
Thailand has a subtropical climate with very high humidity.
Bring long training pants for the flight and a long-sleeved shirt.

• Thai culture and customs in Thailand.
Learn the most commonly used Thai customs
How to say hello and thanks in the Thai language.
Remember always to take off your shoes when you enter temples and other religious places in Thailand.

• Health and safety in Thailand.
There are doctors, dentists, and hospitals everywhere in Thailand. In Addition, there are pharmacies on every corner if you need medicine of any kind.
Remember to buy mosquito spray in Thailand. The mosquito spray kills the mosquitoes in Thailand. Especially when you go out to eat in the evenings in Thailand.

• Transportation in Thailand.
In Thailand, there are plenty of means of transport to choose from.
Buses, taxis, Bolt taxis, Indrive, Baht Bus, Tuk Tuk, Train, and motorbike taxis.
Always ask the official taxis to start the meter, or else they will take a fixed price that is too high.
Or else use the Bolt taxi app, because they always have a price that shows up in the Bolt app (Like UBER taxi).
Remember, the road taxes are not included in the price on the Bolt app.
CHECK MY VIDEO ABOUT USING THE BOLT APP IN THAILAND.
The price is very low for all these types of transport.

• Electronics and charging options in Thailand.
You need a power bank for your phone or tablet.
Always remember to have your rechargeable batteries and power banks in your hand luggage for when you have to go through security at the airport, both ways.

• Travel plans.
Print all your airplane tickets, hotel reservations, etc.
Be sure to keep them in your carry-on baggage  (Hand luggage)

Make a list from home of places you would like to see or visit on your trip to Thailand.

Don’t take day trips every day, but keep day trips to a maximum of every 2 days. These day trips can be very exhausting.

title: JOMTIEN Beach Road Pattaya Thailand on a sunny day
tags: Thailand|jan travel thailand|jomtien|jomtien pattaya|jomtien pattaya thailand|jomtien beach|jomtien beach road|land of smiles|thailand tourism|thailand travel guide|thailand travel
description:
JOMTIEN Beach Road on a sunny day in September 2023.
Jomtien Beach Road is a prominent thoroughfare in the Pattaya area of Thailand, particularly in the Jomtien Beach area. Jomtien is located just south of Pattaya and is known for its more relaxed atmosphere compared to the busier and more vibrant Pattaya Beach.

Here are some key features and aspects of Jomtien Beach Road:

Scenic Coastal Views: The road runs parallel to the coastline, offering beautiful views of the Gulf of Thailand. Jomtien Beach is known for its long and sandy shoreline.

Hotels and Resorts: Along Jomtien Beach Road, you'll find a variety of hotels and resorts catering to different budgets. Some of them offer sea-facing rooms with stunning ocean views.

Restaurants and Cafes: The road is lined with numerous restaurants, cafes, and eateries serving a diverse range of cuisines. Visitors can enjoy Thai seafood, international dishes, and local specialties.

Water Activities: Jomtien Beach is popular for water activities, and there are facilities offering jet skiing, parasailing, and other water sports. Tourists often find opportunities for boat trips and island-hopping excursions.

Nightlife: While Jomtien is generally quieter than Pattaya, there are still nightlife options along the beach road. You can find beachfront bars, pubs, and entertainment venues, though it's not as bustling as Pattaya's Walking Street.

Local Markets: Jomtien has local markets and shops where visitors can buy souvenirs, clothing, and other items. The atmosphere is more relaxed compared to the busier markets in Pattaya.

Family-Friendly Atmosphere: Jomtien is considered more family-friendly than Pattaya, making it a popular destination for travelers seeking a more laid-back environment.

Foot massages are a popular form of relaxation and therapy in Thailand, as well as in many other parts of the world. Traditional Thai foot massages focus on the feet, lower legs, and calves. The practice is based on the concept of energy lines, similar to the principles of acupuncture, and is believed to promote overall health and well-being.

Here's what you can expect from a typical foot massage experience in Thailand:

1. Setting:
Foot massages in Thailand are often done in open spaces in comfortable reclining chairs, allowing you to relax and enjoy the massage while observing the surroundings.

2. Duration:
A standard foot massage session usually lasts between 30 minutes to an hour, although longer sessions are also available.

3. Techniques:
Warm Water Soak: Your feet are soaked in warm water to relax the muscles.
Foot Scrub: A scrub is applied to remove dead skin cells and leave your feet soft.
Pressure Points: The therapist uses their hands, fingers, and a wooden stick to apply pressure to specific points on your feet, corresponding to different organs and areas of the body.
Stretching: The therapist may also incorporate gentle stretching to improve flexibility.
Oil or Lotion: Sometimes, oil or lotion is used to reduce friction during the massage.
4. Benefits:
Relaxation: Foot massages promote relaxation and relieve stress.
Improved Circulation: The massage techniques help in improving blood circulation.
Pain Relief: Foot massages can alleviate foot and ankle pain.
Balancing Energy: Practitioners believe that foot massages help balance the body's energy flow.
5. After the Massage:
After the massage, you might be offered a cup of tea and some fruits, allowing you to further relax before leaving.

Tips for Enjoying Your Foot Massage:###
Communicate: If the pressure is too strong or too light, don’t hesitate to communicate your preferences to the therapist.
Relax: Try to relax and clear your mind during the massage. Deep breathing can enhance the experience.
Hydrate: Drink plenty of water afterward to help flush out toxins released during the massage.
Note:

description:
10 important tips to be prepared for before you travel to Thailand on a vacation.

- Your Passport expiration date has to be at least 6 months before you go.
- VISA for your stay. You get 30 days when you enter Thailand as a tourist.
- You can buy a 60 days tourist VISA from home at the Thai embassy in your home country, and after that you can expand it to 30 more days.
- Vaccines. You do not need to have them, but some vaccines can be nice to have before you travel to Thailand.
- Travel insurance or Health insurance. Check your insurance company before you travel. Always have a copy of your insurance in your carry-on baggage.
- Transport and travel plans - Bus, taxi, or airplane.
- Have all batteries (Max.20 pieces) in your hand baggage- Laptops etc. For the security check at the airport.
- Currency and money. Have some Thai bath with you in your hand baggage. 1 or 2 credit cards. Just to be safe.
- Buy mosquito spay in Thailand. They have the best mosquito spray for their mosquitos in Thailand.
- Electronics and charging devices. They have everything in Thailand electronic shops.
- Make travel plans from home, of what you want to see on your trip to Thailand. Ask the locals in Thailand if it is worth going to see.

Bonus TIPS:
- Lears a few words in the Thai language: Thanks and Hello.
- Make an International Driving license from home. It is very cheap and last for 1 year. For both car or bike.
- Print your airplane ticket (e-ticket), Hotel booking, and insurance, and bring in your hand baggage.

title: Koh Samet Thailand 2022 - A weekend on an island in Thailand
tags: koh samet|koh samet 2022|koh samet thailand|koh samet thailand 2022|thailand tourism|thailand travel|thailand 2022|national park thailand|best national park thailand|thailand island to visit|thailand islands|thailand vlog|thailand video|jan travel thailand|thailand|travel in asia|traveling asia vlog|thailand travel 2022
description:
Koh Samet - the overlooked island with sunshine guarantees sunshine travel. Guide to Thailand. Koh Samet - the overlooked island with a sunshine guarantee

Koh Samet is located as a beautiful, but overlooked, a gem in the Gulf of Thailand just a few hours and a short boat ride from Bangkok. Although the island offers fabulously beautiful sandy beaches and sunshine all year round (most hours of sunshine in all of Thailand), the island has never been really commercial and tourist overrun.

This may be because the island, with only 6 km in length and 3 km in width, is too small to really offer guests more than a few days of sun, relaxation, and drinks on the beach. The latter makes Ko Samet excellent on the other hand! Here you will find some of Thailand's most beautiful and romantic beaches, especially Hat Sai Kaew on the east side, which simply invites you to let go and be seduced by the sunset over the crystal clear blue waters of the Gulf of Thailand.

The island is perfect to escape from the hectic life of Bangkok and spending a few days on the beach and that makes the island very popular among Thais and permanent residents from Bangkok, as well as backpackers and tourists from Pattaya. That is why the island's population rises dramatically over the weekend and so do the prices, so if the budget is a bit tight it is best to avoid Friday to Sunday.

How to get to Koh Samet
Koh Samet is located approx. 200 km south-east of Bangkok of the small fishing village of Ban Phe near Rayong. The easiest way to get to Koh Samet is to buy a complete package from a travel agent in Bangkok, which includes transportation to Ban Phe by minibus or taxi, ferry ticket, and hotel. Here, travelers are then picked up early in the morning and arrive in Koh Samet early in the evening.

Otherwise, it is possible to take a bus to Rayong from Ekamai bus station in Bangkok, but be sure to get a ticket for a 1st or VIP bus with so few stops because otherwise you risk stranding in Rayong late in the evening after the last ferry has sailed. The bus ride takes between 3 and 6 hours depending on how many stops are made. From Rayong, you have to buy a taxi or Tuk-Tuk to Ban Phe where the ferry to Ko Samet sails. When you arrive on the island, a small fee must be paid as the island has the status of a national park. From Na Dan where the ferry arrives on Koh Samet, there are songtaews that run around the island and a few taxis.

Koh Samet is not developed in the same way as the large islands of Phuket, Koh Samui, and Ko Chang. The range of accommodation consists mostly of primitive bungalows and individual hotels. Most accommodation options are located on the two northernmost beaches of Hat Sai Keaw and Ao Hin Kok where there are a number of bungalows that vary greatly in quality from concrete huts to teak huts. There is a very large price difference between rooms with and without air-conditioning - especially on weekends.

An air-conditioned bungalow can easily cost 2000-3000 baht, which is at least 2-3 times more expensive than elsewhere in Thailand. On the northern part of the island, there are several upscale resorts. If you have not booked a hotel in advance, you can usually find a room when you arrive, except if you come on the weekend when it is good to be out early.

Koh Samet er en lille ø som ikke tager meget mere end en dag eller to at udforske. Det er ikke aktiviteterne på Koh Samet som lokker, selv om det er muligt at leje ATV, dirt bikes, vandscooter og cykler for at få et action fix. Derimod er Koh Samet perfekt til et par dovne dage på stranden, fantastisk frisk sea-food på stranden og så cocktails i baren om aftenen.

Koh Samet er som sagt en nationalpark så der er mulighed for at være heldig og se makak-aber og de lokale store edderkopper. Ellers er det de fine strande som er den største attraktion. Der er tale om virkelig flotte hvide sandstrande som er relativt uspolerede og med en fantastisk udsigt til det blå vand i golfen.

Her er der også rigelige muligheder for snorkling i de mange små bugte. Der er natteliv på Koh Samet som andre steder i Thailand, men når solen går ned er der flere hyggelig strandbarer langs østkysten.

title: Exploring Korea: Chungcheongnam-do & Seoul
tags: Seoul|Korea|Chungcheongnam-do
description:
Chungcheongnam-do, or Chungnam, is approximately 56 minutes away from Seoul via KTX. Aside from filming locations and heritage sites, Chungnam is home to several pilgrimate sites and art galleries. Here are more destinations you can visit in Chungnam:

- Oeam Folk Village
- Shinri Holy Place
- Solmoe Holy Ground
- Ami Art Gallery

After you visit Chungnam, here are more tourist destinations in Seoul you might not have heard about yet:

- Gangnam Style Statue
- Byeol-madang Library
- Bukchon Hanok Village
- Kahoe and Myeongdong Cathedrals
- Kakao and Friends Shop
- 943 King's Cross: A Harry Potter-themed cafe
- Zapangi Cafe

For more information, visit english.visitkorea.or.kr

title: Exploring Korea: Daejeon & Chungcheongnam-do
tags: Korea|Daejeon|Chungcheongnam-do
description:
Explore more of Korea in Daejeon & Chungcheongnam-do! 
Strategically located in the center of Korea, Daejeon & Chungcheongnam-do are perfect for your itinerary when you want to wander more of Korea!

Daejeon, Korea's 5th largest metropolis, is approximately 50 minutes away from Seoul via KTX. If you have an extra day, here is what you need to see in Daejeon:

- Daeheung-Dong Catholic Church
- Seongsimdang Bakery
- Daecheon Lake Photo Warehouse
- Uineungjeongi Cultural Street & Skyroad

Chungcheongnam-do, or Chungnam, can be reached at approximately 56 minutes from Seoul via KTX. You can find the filming studio of K-drama, Mr. Sunshine in Nonsan, Chungcheongnam-do! More places to visit here:

- Myeongjae Old House
- Asan Marina Village

For more information, visit our website: english.visitkorea.or.kr

title: NAIK BUS MALAM DI SEOUL??
description:
Kenalan dulu yuk sama Owl Bus, bus malam Seoul yang beroperasi setelah jam reguler bus dan subway yang biasa berakhir. Ada total 140 bus dengan 14 rute yang berbeda. Jadi kalian ga usah khawatir lagi urusan transportasi meskipun jamnya sudah malam ataupun subuh.

Owl Bus berguna banget utk kalian yang:
•⁠ ⁠Ketinggalan subway atau bus terakhir
•⁠ ⁠Ga mau kena tarif taksi yang mahal di larut malam atau subuh
•⁠ ⁠Solo traveller yang mau hemat biaya
•⁠ ⁠Akomodasinya di area Hongdae, Gangnam, Itaewon, atau Dongdaemun

🕚 Jam operasional: 23.00-06.00

🦉 Nomor Owl Bus diawali dengan huruf N yang artinya “Night” diikuti dengan 2 digit angka

🚍 4 rute populer untuk wisatawan: N13 (Gangnam ↔️ Dongdaemun), N15 (Jongno ↔️ Sadang), N26 (Hongdae ↔️ Dongdaemun), N61 (Gangnam ↔️ Yeongdeungpo)

💰 Pembayaran dengan kartu transportasi atau dengan uang cash

title: KOREA ALA SON HEUNG MIN !! Kalau versi chingudeul gimana?
tags: ThisIsMyKorea|WhatsYours|AkuDanKorea|KeKoreaAja|OurHeartsAreAlwaysOpen
description:
Organisasi Pariwisata Korea dengan senang hati mengumumkan kemitraan terbarunya dengan pemain sepak bola kelas dunia Son Heung-min, anggota Tottenham Hotspur sejak 2015 dan pemain Asia pertama dalam sejarah yang mencetak lebih dari 50 gol di Liga Premier.

Dalam upacara pada 6 Juli 2021 di Seoul, Son Heung Min ditunjuk sebagai Duta Kehormatan untuk Pariwisata Korea.

Ketika pariwisata internasional mulai dilanjutkan setelah krisis COVID-19, tidak ada momen yang lebih penting untuk memperkenalkan kembali Korea ke dunia sebagai tujuan wisata yang dinamis dan menarik daripada dengan Son, atau “Sonny”, panggilan akrabnya, di garis depan.

"This is my Korea, What's Yours?"

description:
Today wanted to talk about some local ww2 coastal defenses by visiting a local AA/Artillary site called Puckpool Park / Puckpool Battery. Puckpool is a WW2 British Coastal defense site aimed at preventing a naval invasion of the mainland. It was fitted out with several large-caliber Anti Naval guns, some of the same models as the Dreadnought class Battleship. It also had several anti-air guns and mortars, howitzer and guns of other calibers. The site was never really used as the germans didn't actually get to invade. But should they have tried, the Island battery would have been the first line of defense against an invasion of Portsmouth (the UK's most preeminent naval base and the home of the Royal Navy).

description:
Welcome to Thailand's most vibrant and joyous festival – Songkran! 🎉

Songkran, the Thai New Year, has deep roots in ancient traditions. Originally, it marked the start of the solar year and was celebrated with religious rituals, including the pouring of water over Buddha statues and elders' hands for blessings. 🌞🙏

Today, Songkran is a massive, country-wide water fight! People take to the streets armed with water guns, buckets, and hoses, ready to drench anyone in sight. 💦🔫

It's not just about the fun – water symbolizes purification, washing away bad luck and sins. The festival also brings families together, with traditional rituals and temple visits. 🏠✨

So, if you're in Thailand in mid-April, prepare to get wet and join the world's biggest water fight! Happy Songkran! สวัสดีปีใหม่! 🎊💦

description:

In this episode, we explore the delicate nuances of cross-cultural relationships: the invisible lines between local patronage norms, innocent naivety, and the essential boundaries of mutual respect. Can cultural differences explain away the quiet erosion of trust?

description:
There many things I wish I new before I applied for the Global Korea Scholarship Program!

These things can affect your life in South Korea, that is why I am sharing them with you!

1. ​The Stipend is Tight Due to Rising Costs and Restrictions on Work.

Students are not allowed to work during the language school, making it difficult to manage your finances on the first year.

2. Documents Hell
Getting the Global Korea Scholarship Program means one way ticket to Korea. Meaning, the documents and visa processing within Korea cannot be influenced by NIIED. You will do the visa processing, the reservation, almost all things.

3. Language Requirement can be tough and overwhelming

Level 3 of TOPIK is no easy feat! Many scholars returned to their homeland empty handed. no money, no Scholarship, no degree. This is due to the tough language Requirement. Some schools even require TOPIK 4 OR 5!
