title: Gyeongju - The Golden City of South Korea, the History in Gyeongju
description:
Save this video and locations for your next Gyeongju Trip

1. Luge World  

루지 is a non-powered cart-type amusement ride that uses gravity without a special power device and is an all-season experience sport that can be enjoyed dynamically by anyone of any age and gender by easily adjusting direction and braking through terrain and slopes.

Gyeongju Luge World has two courses, the 1.6km Hwarang Course and the 1.4km Cheonma Course, which are 3km long and sloped, making them great for riding at speed.

When you come down from the luge cart, take in the beautiful view of Gyeongju Bomun Gate at a glance. With Gyeongju Luge World, the pleasure of traveling to Gyeongju is doubled.

Address: 6, Cheonbuknam-ro, Gyeongju-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do 
Tel: 1833-2923
Operating Time: 9:20 - 20:00

2. Woljeonggyo Bridge

The Iljeonggyo and Woljeonggyo Bridges are presumed to be the bridges referred to in a passage of Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms) that reads: “In the second moth of the nineteenth year of King Gyeongdeok’s reign, two bridges, Chunyang and Woljeong, were built over the Muncheon stream on the south side of the palace.” Over time, the name “Woljeong” came to be written as “月精” instead of “月淨,” and the name “Chunyanggyo” was replaced by “Iljeonggyo,” “Hyobulhyogyo” or “Chilseonggyo.” The names appear to have eventually become settled as Iljeonggyo and Woljeonggyo, symbolizing the spirit of the sun and the spirit of the moon, respectively. As for the names “Hyobulhyogyo” and “Chilseonggyo,” they seemed to have emerged during the Joseon period, from folk legends that became associated with the Iljeonggyo Bridge.

Address: 경상북도 경주시 교동 48
Contact number: 054-779-6138
Operating Hours: Open from 9:00 am

3. Shilla-Style Hanbok Rental

Yeogi Hanbok has various hanbok designs for customers to try and wear while exploring different parts of woljeonggyo and the nearby hanok village. The hanbok rental shop has distinct Shill style hanboks that can be worn until 19:00 

Address: 150-6 Hwangnam-dong Gyeongju-si Gyeongsangbuk-do
Contact number 0507-1321-5653
Operating Hour - Open from 11:00 - 19:00

4. Wonder Space

This 5 floor attraction in Gyeongju has  a lot of experiences you can try!
a. 1st floor has the parking lot and entrance to the Wonder Space
b. 2nd floor has the arcade area where you can play different arcade games! 
c. 3rd floor has the noodle factory where you can eat and try different games related to noodles - noodle claw machine
d. 4th floor is the Raiders Arena zone. I wanted to try this floor but we lacked time for this event so I had to just watch other people play and enjoy their laser tag game
e. 5th floor has the photo zones. I enjoyed these photo areas as I can see different locations just by going around the 5th floor.


5. Jungdo Tower

This tower is modeled and inspired from the ancient nine-story wooden pagoda of Hwangnyongsa Temple built during Shilla period.

Address: Jungdo Tower (중도타워), Gyeongju, South Korea Landscape

🌸 Exploring the Hidden Gem of South Korea: Chuncheon City 🇰🇷

Join me on an unforgettable journey through the charming streets of Chuncheon in Kangwondo! Chuncheon-si is one of the major cities in South Korea. I have not been able to explore this part of Korea due to schedule and budget. 

This picturesque city is a true Korean gem waiting to be discovered. From lush parks to delectable street food, we'll immerse ourselves in the vibrant culture and breathtaking landscapes. 🏞️

🎨 Korean Arts: Visit local art galleries and appreciate the rich cultural scene.

Gyms are an integral part of Korean culture, and working out is considered an essential aspect of maintaining a healthy lifestyle. The Korean beauty standard is known for being particularly rigorous, emphasizing the importance of slim figures, clear skin, and symmetrical features.

Many Koreans see going to the gym as a way to achieve this ideal. Fitness classes like pilates, yoga, and aerobics are popular among women, while weightlifting and bodybuilding are more common among men. Korean gyms are well-equipped with modern facilities, high-tech equipment, and experienced trainers who help clients achieve their fitness goals.

In Korea, working out is not just about looking good; it's also about feeling good. Exercise is believed to improve mental health, relieve stress, and boost energy levels. Many Koreans incorporate fitness into their daily routines, even if it's just a quick jog around the park or a few sets of push-ups at home.

While the Korean beauty standard may be difficult to achieve for some, the emphasis on health and wellness is a positive aspect of Korean culture. By promoting physical activity and healthy living, Korean gyms are helping to improve the overall well-being of the population.

description:
Walking at night in Seoul is an experience like no other. As the sun sets, the city comes alive with shimmering neon lights, street vendors selling delicious treats, and the hustle and bustle of the people. It's a place where the past meets the present, where ancient temples stand next to modern skyscrapers, and where tradition blends seamlessly with innovation.

One of the most breathtaking sights in Seoul at night is the Namsan Tower. Standing at 236 meters tall, this tower offers a panoramic view of the entire city. As you make your way up the tower, you'll pass through a forest of trees and a beautiful garden. At the top, you'll be greeted by a stunning 360-degree view of the city.

Another must-visit location for a nighttime stroll is the Cheonggyecheon Stream. This stream is located in the heart of Seoul and runs through the city for over 10 kilometers. At night, the stream is lit up by thousands of LED lights, creating a magical and romantic atmosphere. Walking along the stream, you'll pass by numerous bridges, waterfalls, and even art installations.

For those who love to shop, Myeong-dong is the place to be. This bustling shopping district is home to countless shops, restaurants, and street vendors selling everything from Korean cosmetics to street food. At night, the streets are filled with people, and the lights from the shops and buildings create a vibrant and lively atmosphere.

If you're interested in learning about Korean culture, a nighttime stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village is a must. This traditional Korean village is located in the heart of Seoul and is home to hundreds of hanok, or traditional Korean houses. The village is beautifully preserved and gives visitors a glimpse into what life was like in Korea centuries ago.

Finally, no visit to Seoul is complete without a stroll through Hongdae, the city's hip and trendy neighborhood. This area is known for its vibrant nightlife, street performances, and art galleries. At night, the streets are filled with people, and the energy is electric.

Walking at night in Seoul is an unforgettable experience that everyone should try at least once. Whether you're interested in culture, shopping, or simply taking in the city's sights and sounds, Seoul has something for everyone.

Sinimun Station in Seoul is more than just a subway stop; it's a gateway to the past. Located on Line 1 of the Seoul Metropolitan Subway, this station was originally built in 1900 during the Japanese colonial era. It was the first railway station in Korea and played a significant role in the country's modernization. Today, the station has been beautifully restored to its original design, with antique signs and ticket booths adding to the nostalgic atmosphere. Visitors can step back in time and experience what it was like to travel by train over a century ago. The station also serves as a cultural center, with exhibitions showcasing the history of Korean railways and the country's industrial development. Sinimun Station is a unique and fascinating destination for history buffs and anyone interested in Korea's rich cultural heritage.

Transportation: The cost of transportation varies depending on the mode of transportation. The subway system is efficient and affordable, with a single journey fare starting at KRW 1,350. Taxis and buses are also available, but may be more expensive.

title: Why Studying in Korea can be Stressful for International Students

description:
1. Language Barrier: One of the biggest challenges for international students in Korea is the language barrier. Korean is the primary language of instruction, and even though some universities offer courses in English, many professors and students communicate in Korean. This can make it difficult for non-Korean speakers to understand lectures, participate in class discussions, and complete assignments.

2. Intense Competition: Korean students are known for their intense work ethic and competitiveness, and this can make studying in Korea stressful for international students. The pressure to perform well academically and maintain a high GPA can be overwhelming, particularly if students are not used to this level of competition.

3. Culture Shock: Studying in Korea can be a significant cultural adjustment for international students, particularly those from Western countries. The social norms, customs, and traditions in Korea can be very different from what students are used to, which can lead to feelings of isolation and homesickness.

4. High Cost of Living: The cost of living in Korea can be quite high, particularly in the major cities like Seoul. This can make it challenging for students to manage their expenses, particularly if they are not receiving significant financial support from their families or scholarships. The high cost of living can also make it challenging for students to engage in extracurricular activities or travel around the country.

5. Visa and Immigration Process: The process of obtaining a student visa and navigating the immigration system in Korea can be a stressful experience for international students. There are often complicated requirements and paperwork involved, and the process can be time-consuming and confusing. Additionally, students may be required to renew their visa periodically, which can add an additional layer of stress and uncertainty to their experience.

I had an exciting Thursday and Friday at Gangwondo courtesy of Gogogangwondo and Plus Planner. 

My trip includes a visit to Gangwondo's Healing Sanctuary, the Romyzian Garden, a delicious experience at Jeongseon Market, historical music at Jeongson Arirang Festival, and an extravagant Hotel stay at High 1 Hotel.

If you are wondering how much I spent for this trip, I did not spend anything. In Korea, the government has been generous in proving trips for foreigners to immerse them to the Korean Culture. As a person with interest with Korean History, I take advantage of these opportunities to go to places that I have never been to. 

As I learn about Korea, its history and culture, I am able to share what I learn through my contents, video post in YouTube and contents in IG &  FB.

Completing my Korean Language Classes and attaining Level 3 in TOPIK made me eligible to enroll in my chosen graduate school - Hanyang University School of International Business.

On March 2, 2022, my classes at Hanyang University officially started. The Living-with-Covid set-up was a bit new to a lot of universities, but Hanyang and other Korean Universities have prepared their respective facilities for the students and faculty. 

In this video, you will see how face-to-face classes are conducted at Hanyang University School of Business. Also, I went to the Community center for a document I needed to submit (in relation to my monthly allowance as GKS Scholar). A lot of GKS awardees will be able to relate to this process, especially on the last week of each month. Future scholars should watch in order to prepare themselves and learn about the process.

I must say, I was scared when I first entered the room given that I have a lot of expectations. Fortunately, all my classes today ended peacefully :) Hanyang University Business courses are well-tailored for the needs of MBA Students. Hoping to see you here!

title: Yi-Sun-Sin Shrine, Asan City, South Korea. Learning from the bravery & wisdom of Yi Sun Sin
tags: Blue Crystal Village|SunMoon University|Global Korea Scholarship|Asan-si|South Korea|Foreigner in Korea|Traveling|Filipino|YiSunSin|Korea Admiral|Korean History|Namhae|Travel|History-learning experience|2022Koreaz
description:
Let's go back in time and learn about the Admiral Yi-Sun-Sin. 

He is a Korean Admiral and National Hero who was instrumental in repelling the Japanese fleet that was attempting to invade Korea in the 1950s. 

Based on a website pertaining to his battles, he fought 23 battles against the Japanese naval forces and won every single battle. It was also recorded that in 14 of the 23 battles, all of the invading naval forces sent by Japan were completely destroyed!

After visiting his shrine, we went for a walk near the Asan River!

description:
Last October 25, 2021, I received my second dose of Vaccine (Pfizer). 

In South Korea, everyone is advised to get the vaccine as the government plans the re-opening of the economy by November 2021. Having the vaccine (as well as booster shots) can help in preventing the spread of the virus. 

For the vaccination (for foreigners), the government only requires a passport (if available, present the Registration Card). After presenting necessary identification cards, the medical personnel will assess your current health and perform necessary check-ups and screening tests.

The overall process was just 20 minutes. (15 minutes was for the resting required after taking the vaccine to check if there will be an immediate manifestation of side effects). EFFICIENT!

For other foreigners (students, workers), please help fight the spread of the virus by getting your vaccines, and always wearing your masks!

In my 6 months of living in South Korea, I have been visiting this city to relax and experience different cuisine available in the area. For today, I ate at Rolling Pasta (a pasta restaurant near the Sinsegye Department Store. And I must say, it is one of the best restaurants so far!

Following this, I walked around to show the street life in Cheonan City. Life in South Korea is starting to get back to normal as the vaccination has surpassed the 30Million population ( I will be getting my second dose of vaccine on October 25).

Lastly, I roamed inside Sinsegye Department Store and spotted a bookstore / KPOP merch shop. My nephews and nieces will be ecstatic when they see the different albums, merch, and other posters available in this mall. 

BTS. BLACKPINK. K POP MERCH. GOOD FOOD and more. CHEONAN HAS IT ALL.

Until next time,

Justin.

title: "Day Trip to Koh Kret | Bangkok’s Local Island Adventure!"
tags: Koh Kret|Ko Kret|Koh Kret Thailand|Koh Kret Bangkok|day trip from Bangkok|Bangkok hidden gem|island near Bangkok|pottery village Thailand|things to do in Koh Kret|Koh Kret travel guide|Bangkok day trips|off the beaten path Thailand|local Thai experience|Thai island vlog|Thailand slow life|Thai food tour|Bangkok weekend trip|hidden places in Thailand|cycling in Thailand|Bangkok vlog|bangkok vlog|bangkok 2025|thailand 2025|friendsfromthailand|fft
description:
Koh Kret (or Ko Kret / เกาะเกร็ด) is a charming island in the Chao Phraya River, just north of Bangkok in Nonthaburi Province. It’s perfect for a peaceful half-day or day trip from Bangkok — no beach here, but you’ll find local culture, pottery, food, and slow life vibes. 🌿🚲🍵

Why Visit Koh Kret?
🏺 Pottery Village – Famous for traditional Mon-style pottery. You can watch artisans at work or even try making your own.

🚲 Bike Around the Island – Rent a bicycle and cycle along scenic paths through small villages and riverside homes.

🥢 Local Food – Try rare Mon dishes, giant river prawns, Thai desserts, and more at the weekend market.

🧘‍♀️ Chill, Local Vibes – No cars allowed on the island! It’s a slow-paced, peaceful place.

🛕 Wat Poramaiyikawat – The main temple with a leaning white stupa and a small museum.

🎨 Handicrafts & Souvenirs – Handmade candles, snacks, herbal products, and ceramics.

How to Get to Koh Kret from Bangkok
By Car or Taxi:

Head to Wat Sanam Neua Pier (วัดสนามเหนือ) in Nonthaburi.

Take the short ferry ride (2–5 THB) across the river to Koh Kret.

By Public Transport:

MRT to Nonthaburi Civic Center Station or Pak Kret area

Then grab a taxi or local songthaew to Wat Sanam Neua Pier

By Boat (Fun Option!):

Take the Chao Phraya Express Boat to Pak Kret Pier (N33) (weekend boats only).

Hire a local boat or walk to the ferry pier.

🗓️ Best Time to Visit
Weekends – That’s when the island comes alive with the floating/local market.

Morning – For cooler weather and fewer crowds.

📝 Tips:
Rent a bike for ~40 THB

Wear comfy shoes (some walking or biking involved)

Bring cash (many stalls don’t take cards)

Try the fried flower tempura, herbal drinks, or Thai-style crepes

tags: emsphere|emsphere bangkok|emsphere ikea|emsphere food|em district|Emporium & Emquartier|Emporium|Emquartier|bangkok shopping mall|bangkok mall|mall in bangkok|siam paragon|icon siam|best mall in bangkok|Emsphere bangkok stores|Emsphere bangkok restaurants|luxury mall bangkok|luxuary shopping bangkok|how to get to emsphere|emsphere bangkok food court|central world bangkok|terminal 21|Phrom Phong BTS Station|Emsphere at EM District|bangkok shopping|fft
description:
The Emsphere, the newest shopping mall in Bangkok, is located in the heart of the city, adjacent to BTS Phrom Phong station. It is easily accessible, although the walk from the station may be a bit long. However, the skywalk makes it a breeze.

The lower floors are home to a variety of restaurants, as well as an event space. The restaurants are all quite luxurious and spacious. Upstairs, you'll find fashion, gadgets, and electronics. The interior of the mall is modern and stylish.

The highlight of the mall is the Ikea on the third floor. The store is surprisingly comprehensive, with a wide variety of products. You could easily spend hours browsing the aisles. The Ikea food court is also quite large and inviting.

In addition to the Ikea, the mall also has a showroom for luxury cars and supercars.

The upper floors are reserved for UOB Live, which is not yet open. It is expected to open in early 2024.

Overall, the Emsphere is still under construction. There are still some finishing touches to be done, especially on the ceiling. However, it is already one of the most exciting shopping malls in Bangkok. There are plenty of photo opportunities, and even the bathrooms are stunning.

description:
EAT THAI FOOD and DO CHEAP SHOPPING in one of the largest and tallest Chedi in Thailand.
Nakhon Pathom Temple Festival at Wat Phra Pathom Chedi takes place every year for 9 days in December. 

You’ll find many items and souvenirs on sale, from cheap clothes to children’s toys, and phone cases. 

The market is HUGE. The platform on which the stupa sits is a square structure, and the market encompasses all 4 sides of it. In addition to that, there are many twists and turns that branch out from the main area of the market. You will surely get lost if you aren’t paying attention to where you’re going.

And that’s okay because I got lost too.

Nakhon Pathom is about an hour away from Bangkok by car. 

If you don’t have access to your own car you can take a van at BTS Victory Monument which will take you to a nearby Big C grocery store and you’ll have to take another 5 minute motorbike taxi to get to the temple.

I recommend booking a train  from your current destination to Nakhon Pathom as it is the cheapest option and takes roughly the same time as travelling by car (~1 hour).

description:
Thailand’s ‘floating train’ could be one of the world’s most scenic railway journey.An undiscovered but unique experience.
Only 10 USD for round trip ticket! You will experience one of the best day trip from Bangkok,  ‘Rot Fai Loi Nam’ (floating train) trip from Bangkok to Pa Sak Jolasid Dam in Lop Buri

None of your friends did this! 

Let's us take you there.


details of this train ride here:
It is a weekend train trips to Lop Buri’s Pa Sak Jolasid Dam.
Only available on weekend of Nov-Jan each year.

Ticket prices for the round-trip journey from Bangkok’s Hua Lamphong Railway Station to Pa Sak Jolasid Dam are 560 Baht per person (second-class seat in air-conditioned carriages) and 330 Baht per person (third-class seat in regular carriages). The service is also available for group tours who want a private rail wagon.

Train No. 921 departs from Hua Lamphong at 06.00 Hrs. and stops en route at Samsen, Bang Sue, Bang Khen, Lak Si, Don Mueang, and Rangsit Stations and at Ayutthaya, Saraburi, and Kaeng Khoi Junction.

When it reaches Pasak Jolasid Dam, the train will stop for 20 minutes for tourists to enjoy the scenery and take pictures, and will continue to the last station at Khok Salung, where it will stop for 30 minutes for tourists to enjoy shopping for OTOP products.

Then, it will return to the Dam at 10.35 Hrs. for tourists to have leisure time or lunch, or take local transport to visit the nearby sunflower fields.

The return trip No. 926 departs the Dam at 15.30 Hrs. with the same stops en route to arrive back at Hua Lamphong at 18.50 Hrs.

tags: sampeng market|sampeng market bangkok 2023|sampeng night market|sampeng bangkok|how to get to sampeng|bangkok shopping|bangkok local market|market in bangkok|cheap shopping bangkok|thailand shopping|bangkok wholesale market|thailand travel guide|thailand vlog|bangkok vlog|sampeng lane market|Sampheng Market|Sampheng Night Market|Sampheng|What to buy in Sampeng|Sampeng market opening times|Sampeng market clothes|Sampeng Market opening hours
description:
Sampeng Market in Bangkok, Thailand  is unlike all the tourist markets.It super local, you get the vibe , the food and the people. Even you plan to but nothing, its worth walking around.

A typical traditional open-air market, Sampeng Market is one of Bangkok’s biggest, cheapest and most popular places to buy wholesale products, as well as a slice of ‘real Thailand’, which as a tourist you would love. If you only knew where it was, what to buy and how to get there.

You can reach here by taking mrt to sam yot. Not far from city centre. Sampeng market was in alley, connected block by block. Crowded and mostly local who shop here. 

If you love to buy ladies accessories, you must come here. There sale all kind of earing, hair accessories, textile and this place not many tourist and price are reasonable.

Opening hours of Sampeng Market are from 9 am – 6 pm daily.  This is one of the rare markets in Bangkok that remains open during daytime.  The market is a bit more crowded on weekends.

description:
TUANG DIM SUM bangkok AVOID PEAK LUNCH TIME ( NOON-1PM)

A classic Dim sum!
This restaurant provides variation of dim sum for you. Most of them are really good. It's nothing like luxurious Chinese restaurant dim sum but definitely an everyday meal. All of their food are delicious and set the bar too high for local dim sum shop. The seat here is limited but delivery is available!
Chili paste is one of the secret here! Adding it will add a little kick for those who love spicy.

Tuang is run by Hong Kong-born chef Yip, who was behind the success of Shangri-La Bangkok’s Shang Palace restaurant. While almost everything is a can’t-miss, the most noteworthy dishes include shrimp with rice flour roll (B60) and har gow (steamed shrimp dumpling, B60).

Weekend Market (main area):
• Saturday – Sunday: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM
Friday (some sections open):
• 6:00 PM – 12:00 AM
Please note that individual shop opening hours may vary.

🚆How to Get to Chatuchak Aquarium Fish Market

By BTS Skytrain:

Take the BTS Sukhumvit Line to Mo Chit Station (N8).
Use Exit 1, then walk about 5–10 minutes to the aquarium and pet market section near Chatuchak Weekend Market.

By MRT:

Take the MRT Blue Line to Kamphaeng Phet Station or Chatuchak Park Station.
Kamphaeng Phet Station (Exit 2) is the closest option and only a short walk from the market entrance.

By Taxi or Grab:

From Downtown Bangkok (Sukhumvit, Siam, Silom, or Sathorn), the ride usually takes 20–40 minutes, depending on traffic.
The typical fare is around 250–400 THB (2026), plus any expressway tolls if used.

💡 Travel Tip: Arrive early in the morning, especially on weekends, to enjoy cooler weather, fewer crowds, and the best selection of aquarium fish and aquarium supplies.

🕘 Operating Hours

Use Exit 2 and walk only a few minutes directly into the market area.
This is one of the easiest and most comfortable ways to get there, especially during hot weather.

By BTS Skytrain:
Take the BTS Skytrain to Mo Chit Station.
From there, walk around 10–15 minutes toward Chatuchak Market and follow the signs to the fish market section.
You will pass shopping areas, food stalls, and different sections of the famous weekend market along the way.

By Taxi or Grab:
You can also easily reach the market by Taxi or Grab from central Bangkok.
The trip usually costs around 200–350 THB depending on traffic and your location.
Traffic in Bangkok can be heavy during weekends, so MRT is often the fastest option.

description:
Experience one of the most breathtaking views in all of Bangkok from the iconic Mahanakhon Skywalk, home to Thailand’s highest glass skywalk. The Mahanakhon Skywalk is Thailand’s highest observation deck at 314 meters high, you get a stunning 360-degree panorama of the city, with every skyscraper and landmark stretching out beneath you. Enjoy the incredible views from the Indoor Observation Deck on the 74th floor and the Outdoor Observation Deck on the 78th floor.

If you’re looking for unforgettable sunsets, this is the place. The colors over Bangkok from this height are some of the most spectacular you can see not only in the city but in all of Thailand. As the lights turn on across the skyline, the entire view transforms into a glowing sea of skyscrapers.

Whether you’re visiting for photography, adventure, or simply to enjoy the best views in Bangkok, the Mahanakhon Skywalk is a must-see destination. Don’t miss the chance to walk on the glass floor, feel the height beneath your feet, and take in one of the most impressive rooftop experiences in Asia.

description:
Welcome to today’s virtual walking tour of SEA LIFE Bangkok Ocean World — the largest aquarium and oceanarium in Thailand! 

In this video we will visit the Shark Tunnel — an incredible underwater passage where sharks swim all around and overhead. You’ll also get to see the shark-feeding show, a dramatic highlight of our visit. Expect to meet sharks, rays, seahorses, clownfish, pufferfish, moray eels, and many more fascinating reef inhabitants. 

We’ll explore many different zones: from colorful coral reefs to mysterious rockpools, and from rainforest-themed exhibits to icy penguin habitats. In total, the aquarium houses over 30,000 marine creatures representing more than 400 different species. 

You’ll also see sea turtles gliding through the water, gentle rays gliding along the bottom, and quirky little creatures like seahorses and colorful reef fish. 

Inside this massive underwater world there are 11 immersive zones, each offering a different aquatic habitat and vibe — from coral reefs to rainforest rivers, from deep-sea tanks to touch pools and interactive areas. 

The underwater tunnel is a real highlight — walking under the water surrounded by sharks, rays and schools of fish feels like being inside the ocean itself. 

This is one of the best oceanarium in the World! If you travel to Thailand, this aquarium is really worth visiting!

During our walk we will see shark tunnel, shark walk, jellyfish zone, rainforest adventure zone, coral reefs zone, ocean tunnels, penguin ice playground, otter, seahorse kingdom, tropical ocean zone, shark ship wreck, glass bottom boat and etc... description:
In today's virtual walking tour, we will visit two of the best parks in Bangkok : Thailand's largest rooftop park - NEW Dusit Central Park (Dusit Arun) and Lumphini Park. First we go to Lumphini Park, a large green space in the heart of the city. The park covers about 142 acres. It’s located in the Silom–Rama 4 area and is very accessible. When you arrive you’ll see a big lake, many trees and open lawns for walking or exercising. The lake views show high-rise buildings in the background—nice mix of nature and city. One of the most unusual sights: the monitor lizards — Asian water monitor — live here. There are around 400 of them in the park (they can be quite large, often one to two metres long).The park is very old and one of the oldest parks in Bangkok (also one of the most famous parks in the city and a place many locals know). You will feel history around you when you walk there and see how the city has grown around the park.

After our time in Lumphini, we head to Dusit Central Park — the newest and largest rooftop park in Bangkok. The rooftop park officially opened for visitors on 3 September 2025. This park is part of a huge new mixed-use development at the junction of Silom and Rama 4. The rooftop green space spans 7 rai (about 11,200 m²).  It sits from the 4th to 7th floors of the complex, giving sweeping views over Lumpini Park and the city skyline. It’s designed as a relaxing green oasis, with walking trails, seating zones, and landscapes on top of the building. A lot of young people go there to hang out, walk, take photos or relax. At sunset and at night you can see the city lights and the skyline from the rooftop park — it gives incredible views. It’s just perfect: contrast between the calm of Lumphini and the modern rooftop vibe of Dusit Central Park.

description:
Today we’re celebrating Happy Halloween right in the center of Bangkok — at Siam Square, the most popular place in the city for this festival. Every year this area turns into a huge Halloween street party filled with lights, music, and people in crazy costumes.

The atmosphere here is amazing. You’ll see hundreds of people dressed as zombies, ghosts, movie characters and creative cosplay looks. Everywhere you go, there’s music, dancing, and live performances. Famous Thai artists and dancers perform on big stages surrounded by spooky decorations and glowing lights.

You can walk around and watch mini horror shows, zombie parades, and funny Halloween contests. There are also many themed photo zones, decorations, and horror-movie style corners — everything looks so real and detailed.

This Halloween event at Siam Square runs from Friday to Sunday, and the most exciting part starts around 6 PM, when it gets dark and the lights come on. That’s when the whole place feels magical — the music gets louder, the crowd grows, and the real Halloween spirit begins.

Many shops and restaurants around Siam Square also join the celebration. They decorate their places with pumpkins (pumpkin head halloween), spider webs, and glowing ghosts. You can find Halloween-themed snacks, drinks, and lots of cool souvenirs.

People come here from all over Bangkok — locals, tourists, families, and students — to enjoy this night together. It’s fun, colorful, and a little scary at the same time.

If you’ve never experienced Halloween in Thailand, this is one of the best places to feel it. The mix of Thai culture and international Halloween style makes it truly special.

description:
In today's virtual walking tour in Bangkok, we will visit amazing Benjakitti Forest Park - Bangkok's largest forest park. Benjakitti Forest Park is one of the most beautiful green spaces in the center of Bangkok. The park covers about 720,000 square meters (over 180 acres), making it larger than many older parks in the city. It’s Bangkok’s first forest park, combining trees, wetlands, lakes, and modern design to give a breath of fresh air in the concrete jungle. There’s a large man-made lake, fountains, and water bodies which help both with scenery and cooling the surroundings. Around the lake there are paths for running, walking, cycling — many locals come here early in the morning for exercise. One of the standout features is the elevated skywalk through parts of the park, giving panoramic views over the wetlands, the forest canopy, and Bangkok’s skyline (You can see beautiful panoramic views of Downtown Bangkok, One Bangkok Mall, All Bangkok Skyscrapers, Asok Area and etc). Wildlife is present: you can see birds, sunbirds, doves; there are also warning signs about monitor lizards, so wildlife lovers should keep their eyes open. For photography lovers, this park is a gem — especially around sunrise or sunset when the light reflects off the water and you get silhouettes of trees and the city skyline. The Green Bridge connects Benjakitti Park to nearby Lumpini Park, offering even more walking/cycling options. If you like nature, architecture, design, or just a relaxing place to hang out, this park offers all of that in one.

Bangkok’s Chinatown, known as Yaowarat, is one of the most popular areas in Thailand. It has a long history and has been a center of Chinese culture in Bangkok for more than 100 years. Today it is one of the busiest places in the city, especially at night. The main street is full of food stalls, restaurants, and shops. At night the atmosphere is very lively, with thousands of people walking, eating, and enjoying the street markets. This area is often compared with other top attractions in Bangkok, such as the Grand Palace and Chatuchak Market. Many travelers say a visit to Chinatown is one of the highlights of their trip. description:
In today's video, we will have night walking tour in Chinatown Bangkok – one of the most exciting and flavorful places in the city. Walking along Yaowarat Road, you’ll see a mix of cultures, lights, smells, and street food like nowhere else in Bangkok. This area is famous for its street food, especially in the evening when the road comes alive with food stalls and local restaurants. 

Here are some of the most popular Thai and Chinatown dishes you can try during your visit:
Pad Thai – Stir-fried noodles with shrimp, tofu, peanuts, and a sweet-savory sauce
Hoy Tod – Crispy oyster omelette
Guay Jub – Rolled rice noodles in a peppery soup with crispy pork belly
Dim Sum – Steamed dumplings filled with pork, shrimp, or vegetables
Duck Noodles – Soft noodles with roasted duck in a rich, herbal broth.
Seafood BBQ – Grilled prawns, squid, and crab sold right on the street.
Durian – The famous “king of fruits.” Smelly, soft, sweet – and unforgettable!
Mango Sticky Rice – Sweet mango with coconut milk and sticky rice. A Thai dessert favorite.
You can also try some exotic snacks as scorpions, fried insects, silkworms and bamboo worms.

Famous Places and Restaurants:
T&K Seafood – One of the most famous street seafood restaurants in Chinatown.
Lek & Rut Seafood – Right across from T&K, another great spot for fresh grilled seafood.
Nai Ek Roll Noodles – Known for Guay Jub (peppery rolled noodle soup with pork).
Sweet Time – A dessert stall with colorful Thai sweets, including black grass jelly and coconut puddings.
Yaowarat Toast – Grilled buttery bread filled with custard or chocolate. Super popular for dessert!

Walking here, you’ll see gold shops, herbal stores, Chinese temples, and neon signs everywhere. It’s crowded, it’s loud, but it’s full of life. At night, the whole street turns into a giant open-air food market. Locals and tourists come here to eat, explore, and enjoy the energy of the city. It’s the kind of place where you try something new, take photos every few steps, and just enjoy the moment. In this video you will see Sunday night atmosphere and amazing neon lights in Bangkok. Also around Chinatown you can see I'm Chinatown, Ong Ang Canal, China Gate and etc... 🇹🇭 Enjoy the binaural sounds of city walking through Bangkok! description:

"The Bikers Café Thailand" offers 60 seats in the beautiful Café House and 50 seats outside in the beautiful garden next to a "Klong" surrounded by creative motorcycle artwork and a unique plant world.

They offer coffees in various variations (hot and cold), smoothies, frappes, teas, mocktails, beers, wines, soft and sports drinks, cakes, crepes, ice cream, burgers, steaks, spare ribs, pizzas, spaghettis, chips, chicken nuggets, spring rolls, hot dogs and every day also 30 delicious Thai menus.

Welcome all bikers and of course all non-bikers!

I thought the Geumsan Ginseng Festival was all about ginseng, but there was SO much more to explore! 🌿😲

From trying delicious ginseng foods and discovering red ginseng products to enjoying a relaxing red ginseng foot bath and taking pictures at an 1980s Korean-style retro photo booth, this festival was full of surprises!

You can play traditional Korean games, watch traditional folk dance and music performances, and enjoy live concerts by different singers throughout the festival. 🎶 And the best part? You can even try on Hanbok for free and experience Korean culture in a whole new way! 💚

With so many activities, cultural experiences, delicious food, and live performances, there was never a dull moment!

If you’re visiting South Korea this autumn, this is one festival worth adding to your bucket list! 🙌

222 Gwanganhaebyeon-ro 54beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan

💰 Price per person

You’ll fill out a form at the center, get a locker key for your belongings, and they provide the paddle board, paddle and life jacket.

👕 Need extra stuff?
You can also find accessories like shorts and swim shoes at the center.

🚿 After swimming

Get a waterproof phone cover before going into the water. You can easily find one at a nearby convenience store around Gwangalli.

title: Korean traditional festival in busan🇰🇷💜 #rizinkorea #korea #travel #busan #bts #minivlog
description:
so I couldn’t get BTS concert tickets.

and instead of sitting at home feeling sorry for myself, I went to Gwangalli beach where they were having this festival called Eobang Festival.

honestly? I think we had more fun than the concert people.

this festival is not just a random beach party. it goes back 400 years. there used to be fishermen here who worked alongside the navy and they built this whole community together. Korea has preserved that culture till today and this festival is their way of keeping it alive.

anyway. fast forward to 8pm.

1000 drones lit up the entire sky.

the whole crowd went quiet. nobody was talking. everyone just looked up. that kind of silence at a festival is rare.

then there was a mini concert on one side and a full EDM party on the other side of the same beach. three completely different vibes happening at once.

and then the BTS 13th anniversary drone show.

the entire beach turned purple. that was the moment.

6 years in Korea and this country still finds a way to surprise me.

if you ever come to Busan, this festival needs to be on your list. #minivlog #vlog #kpop

description:
Can you explore the whole of Busan in just one day? I said challenge accepted — and this is what happened! 🚌🇰🇷

For this vlog, I hopped on the Busan City Tour Bus – Green Line and hit all the top coastal & cultural spots in just one day! As a Pakistani living in Korea, I wanted to see Busan like a traveler — fresh sea breeze, cityscapes, quirky streets, and everything in between.

🚏 Here’s where I visited on the Green Line route:
 • Busan Station – the starting and ending point
 • Yeongdodaegyo Bridge / Yurari Square – panoramic views over Yeongdo
 • Huinnyeoul Culture Village – artsy hillside village with sea views
 • Sky Observatory at Yeongdo Haneul Park – city vistas at sunset & sunrise
 • Taejongdae – iconic cliffs, lighthouse, and scenic seaside park
 • National Maritime Museum of Korea – maritime history and modern architecture
 • ARTE Museum – artsy spot showcasing BuTI bus stops
 • Oryukdo Sky Walk / Oryukdo Islets – thrilling glass walkway over blue sea
 • Yonghoman Sightseeing Boat Terminal – coastal ferry hub
 • Peace Park – quiet green zone bordered by the sea
 • Songdo Beach & Cloud Trail – seaside walk with urban beach views
 • Jagalchi‑BIFF Plaza (Yongdusan Park area) – iconic seafood market heart of Nampo-dong

From colorful culture villages and skywalks to ocean-front parks and seafood markets — this vlog takes you through Busan’s true coastal charm in one clean, energetic loop ride.

💡 Thinking of visiting Busan? Or just love seafront city vibes with a desi twist? This video is your virtual ticket to Busan’s best — all in one day!

In this video, I’m sharing my full journey of undergoing SMILE LASIK eye surgery. If you’ve ever wondered what it’s like to get rid of glasses or contact lenses and enjoy clear vision, this vlog is for you!

I decided to have SMILE LASIK because my poor vision was affecting my daily life. In this video, I take you through every step of the process, from my initial consultation at SNU Eye Clinic to the moment I opened my eyes after the surgery and saw the world in a whole new way.

You’ll get an inside look at what happens during the surgery, how I felt before and after, and the amazing results that have changed my life. Whether you’re considering LASIK, SMILE, or any vision correction surgery, this video will give you a real-life perspective on what to expect.

If you have any questions or are thinking about getting the surgery yourself, feel free to leave a comment below. I hope my experience helps you make an informed decision about your vision.

MAMF 

Migrant's Arirang Multicultural Festival (MAMF), one of the largest events involving interracial families and migrant workers, 

The annual festival used as held in Seoul from 2005 to 2010, before moving to the regional city.

One country is selected as a "country of honor" and its culture is introduced during the festival period. This year, it is featuring the PAKISTAN.


"You will be able to enjoy the best Pakistani culture from events arranged by performing groups and artists from the PAKISTAN ," 


The theme of this year's festival is "Eat, Play, Love." The programs include bazaars, art performances, concerts and parades. Visitors can try traditional clothes, food and games.

Main performances include a migrants' song festival, an Asian pop music concert, parades and dance and choir performances.

description:
#kingofthailand #rama9 #thailand 

Back in October 13th of 2016 Thailand lost one of its greatest Kings in history, Bhumibol Adulyadej (ภูมิพลอดุลยเดช) otherly known as King Rama 9. (รัชกาลที่ 9) or (ร.9)

For the Majesty's 1 year anniversary of his passing Oct 13, 2017, I decided to take a motorcycle trip from Bangkok at the Grand Palace to Pai (Mae Hong Son) in honor of King Rama 9 and in every province I stopped the motorbike for a photo and took a picture with the King before making it back to Bangkok for King Bhumibol Adulyadej's cremation & funeral on October 25-27th, 2017 at Sanam Luang, Bangkok. I really just wanted to do something in respect for the King and Thailand as a farang living here in Thailand since 2009 so I decided that immersing myself in the Thai culture and experiencing what the Thai people were going through would be the least I could do. "Riding 4 the KING" was such a powerful, emotional, and inspiring experience that I will never forget, I hold Thailand and King Bhumibol Adulyadej (รัชกาลที่ 9) Rama 9 very close to my heart.

I wasn't going to share this as I felt it was my experience that I was going to keep for myself but after all these years the memories start to fade so I create this mini-documentary / vlog to keep the memory fresh.

RIP Bhumibol Adulyadej (รัชกาลที่ 9) The Peoples KING.

ABOUT KING RAMA 9:
Bhumibol Adulyadej Thai: ภูมิพลอดุลยเดช or ร.9 in short born 5 December 1927 – Died 13 October 2016, conferred with the title King Bhumibol the Great in 1987 (officially conferred by King Vajiralongkorn in 2019), was the ninth monarch of Thailand from the Chakri dynasty, titled Rama IX. Reigning since 9 June 1946, he was the world's longest-reigning current head of state from the death of Emperor Hirohito of Japan in 1989 until his own death in 2016,[5] and is the second-longest reigning monarch of all time, reigning for 70 years and 126 days.[6] During his reign, he was served by a total of 30 prime ministers beginning with Pridi Banomyong and ending with Prayut Chan-o-cha.

After a period of deteriorating health which left him hospitalized on several occasions, Bhumibol died on 13 October 2016 in Siriraj Hospital. He was highly revered by the people in Thailand[14][15] – some saw him as close to divine.[16][17] Notable political activists and Thai citizens who criticized the king or the institution of the monarchy were often forced into exile or to suffer frequent imprisonments.[18] Yet many cases were dropped before being proceeded or were eventually given a royal pardon. His cremation was held on 26 October 2017 at the royal crematorium at Sanam Luang. His son, Maha Vajiralongkorn, succeeded him as King.

description:
#Omicron #NewYears2022 #Covid19Thailand

Home quarantine/isolation in Phuket. I caught the Omicron variant of Covid-19 at the New Years Eve countdown on Patong Beach in Phuket, Thailand. Even though I have been fully vaccinated and given my booster covid shot for the protection of the covid virus. On NYE I went out to celebrate the New Years 2022 at Bangla Road in Patong, I was wearing a mask most of the time and washing my hands and despite me being young-ish and healthy with 3 jabs, the Omicron variant still infected me. 
Symptoms included:
Sore throat (bad)
mucus (bad)
running nose
sneezing
fatigue (moderate)
loss of smell and taste 

Omicron's symptoms were NOT fun to have, I have had worse but it still was very unpleasant to have, yes a bad cold BUT a bad cold normally goes away after a few days of rest, Omicron variant sickness lasted 8+ days with little recovering till day 7. I registered with the Thai GOV/hospital here in Phuket for HOME isolation as my sickness was mild and hospital beds are running low, I also received antiviral meds to help speed up the recovery.

If you are traveling to Thailand please stay safe, many people arriving in the Thailand test & go and Phuket Sandbox are testing positive of the omicron covid variant upon arrival. To the anti Vaxxers, please be extra careful as if you are not Asymptomatic and you get covid19, it can be dangerous, take it from me, someone who has 3 jabs and still the illness was pretty bad, I can imagine what it would have been like if I was not vaccinated,

In this video I break down the real costs of living in Phuket, Thailand for long term EXPATS, in 2022 there are a lot of videos online talking about the cost of living in Thailand but most of them are talking from a backpackers point of view and not a real ex-pat who lives here permanently. 

After settling in to living in Thailand for a few years, the backpacker nomad budget of $1000-$1500 a month will not cut it, when you start a new life and have a wife and kid(s), a business and a house you'll find that you'll need to make more money.

I recommend that you make a minimum of $2500 a month to cover the cost of eating western foods more often, food shopping, renting a house, villa or mortgaging your own home and pay for other expenses like health insurance, work permits, visas, weekend trips around Asia etc etc etc....

Although I recommend $2500 as a minimum, set your goals to make $4000+ a month, this is a roomier, more realistic income to have if you plan on living in Thailand long term.

title: The Cambodian Killing Fields 2009
tags: killing|fields|Cambodia|Pol|Pot|Khmer|rouge|genocide|Phnom|Penh|Danny|Baci|D-Bauchery|Films
description:
On April 17th, 1975 the Khmer Rouge, a communist guerrilla group led by Pol Pot, took power in Phnom Penh, the capital of Cambodia. They forced all city dwellers into the countryside and to labor camps. During their rule, it is estimated that nearly 2 million Cambodians died by starvation, torture or execution.  

The Khmer Rouge turned Cambodia to year zero. They banned all institutions, including stores, banks, hospitals, schools, religion, and the family. Everyone was forced to work 12 - 14 hours a day, every day. Children were separated from their parents to work in mobile groups or as soldiers. People were fed one watery bowl of soup with a few grains of rice thrown in. Babies, children, adults and the elderly were killed everywhere. The Khmer Rouge killed people if they didnt like them, if didnt work hard enough, if they were educated, if they came from different ethnic groups, or if they showed sympathy when their family members were taken away to be killed. All were killed without reason. Everyone had to pledge total allegiance to Angka, the Khmer Rouge government. It was a campaign based on instilling constant fear and keeping their victims off balance.

After the Vietnamese invaded and liberated the Cambodian people from the Khmer Rouge, 600,000 Cambodians fled to Thai border camps. Ten million landmines were left in the ground, one for every person in Cambodia. The United Nations installed the largest peacekeeping mission in the world in Cambodia in 1991 to ensure free and fair elections after the withdrawal of the Vietnamese troops. Cambodia was turned upside down during the Khmer Rouge years and the country has the daunting task of healing physically, mentally and economically

title: Tiger Muay Thai BBQ Beatdown IV - Jan.17th 2009
tags: mma|phuket|BBQ|beatdown|tiger|muay|thai|mike|swick|nevertap|asia|fullmoon|party|thailand|ufc|smoker|fighter|champion|fighters|cage|fighting|danny|baci
description:
Highlights from BBQ Beatdown V included Ngoo Ditty extending his MMA win streak to 4 fights with a spectacular double leg takedown, followed by a cartwheel guard pass and a RNC finish. Professional Female Muay Thai fighter Claire Haigh made her MMA debut against a much heavier male opponent and won a hard fought 3 round decision. After competing during the day at the Nevertap tournament and winning first place in his division, Andreas Hesselback gave up 30lbs to face Professional Muay Thai fighter Nick of the Legacy gym as a late replacement for an injured fighter. The fight was fireworks from beginning to end. After a Ref stoppage to allow the ref to check Nick's broken nose the bout was restarted. During a flurry of punches the heavier fighter landed a crushing right hand following Andreas Hesselback to the mat with hammer fists giving Nick the TKO win in the final minute of the first round. The main bout of the evenning featured two Muay Thai fighters currently ranked in the top 15 Muay Thai fighters in the Country. Singjok Legacy a Lumpinee stadium champion, training under Ole Laursen of the Legacy Gym in Ubon Thailand has competed in MMA Internationally with fights in China and Russia. Bernueng TMT is a WMC world Muay Thai champion who made his debut MMA fight earlier this year in Russia losing a close Decision. Agreeing to a combination of Pride/UFC rules this fight lived up to the hype. Bernueng won the first round on the judges card thanks to a late "Rampage Jackson" style slam, followed by gaining Mount on Singjok. The second round featured several exchanges on the feet, with Bernueng securing a couple more takedowns and attempting a solid Armbar submission, only to be reveresed by Singjok. In the third and final round Singjok tried to rally from behind gaining the mount position over Bernueng and attempting to finish the fight. In the end it was too little too late. Judges Jack Magee, Chad Hamzeh, and Mike Swick all scored the bout 2 rounds to 1, allowing ref Alex Berezovik to raise Bernueng TMT's hand as the winner. Look for a rematch of these two warriors in Ubon later this year. What a great night of fights. Special thanks to TMT for sponsoring the Nevertap Asia grappling tournament. HOW TO MAKE ORIGINAL BANOFFEE PIE AT HOME | HEALTHY BANOFFEE PIE RECIPE

Welcome to our channel! Today, we’re sharing a quick and delicious recipe for homemade banoffee pie, the perfect treat for any occasion! This indulgent dessert combines layers of buttery biscuit base, creamy caramel, fresh bananas, and luscious whipped cream. It’s a crowd-pleaser that’s sure to impress your family and friends. Follow along with our easy step-by-step instructions to create your own irresistible banoffee pie in no time! Don’t forget to like, subscribe, and leave a comment to let us know how yours turned out. Happy baking!

Ingredients:
 • Digestive biscuits
 • Butter
 • Canned condensed milk
 • Bananas
 • Heavy cream
 • Sugar
 • Vanilla extract

Instructions:
 1. Crush digestive biscuits and mix with melted butter to form the base.
 2. Press the biscuit mixture into a pie dish and refrigerate.
 3. Cook condensed milk to make caramel, then spread over the biscuit base.
 4. Slice bananas and layer them over the caramel.
 5. Whip cream with sugar and vanilla extract until stiff peaks form.
 6. Spread whipped cream over the bananas.
 7. Optional: garnish with chocolate shavings or cocoa powder.
 8. Chill in the refrigerator for a few hours before serving.
 9. Enjoy your delicious homemade banoffee pie!

WHAT'S INSIDE THIS BUILDING ?  THE UNTOLD STORIES OF RED BUILDING Chalermprakiat Museum

Read details.....,

The Queen Building, affectionately known as the "Red Building" by the people of Ang Sila, holds a rich historical significance dating back to the reign of King Rama V. Originally constructed to accommodate Chao Chom Mother Dara Rasmi in 1906 B.E., it has since become a symbol of the community's resilience and innovation.

This architectural gem stands as Thailand's first-weekend house, boasting a charming beachfront balcony that offers breathtaking views of the sea. Its unique blend of Thai, Chinese, and Western architectural styles is a testament to the cultural diversity and artistic craftsmanship of the region.

Inside the Maharat Building, or the "White Building" as it's locally known, visitors are treated to a captivating journey through Ang Sila's heritage. Exhibitions showcase the local way of life, highlighting the significance of stone carving, fishing, and the art of weaving Ang Sila Cloth.

One of the most cherished traditions preserved within the walls of the Maharat Building is the intricate process of weaving Ang Sila Cloth. Passed down through generations, this art form combines skillful craftsmanship with unique techniques, such as using cooked rice to soften the yarn and create distinctive fabric patterns like the Pikul Flower.

However, despite its cultural importance, the future of Ang Sila Cloth hangs in the balance, with only a handful of artisans like Grandma Ice preserving its legacy. Without renewed interest and support, this ancient craft risks fading into legend, leaving only a handful of precious pieces woven with love and tradition.

description:
Lately I was 2 weeks in Pai and I will share with you the places I’ve visited and also how I truly feel about them. So that you get an idea about if you would also like it or not. And for each place I’ve been I’ve also a separate video.

We’d visited:
Chinese Village and the Yun Lai Viewpoint
The Pai Walking Street 
Then we went about 50 km North to the Tham Nam Lod Cave    
and to the 1 Dollar Nudel soup and Coffee shop with the 1 Million Dollar View 
The Mo Paeng Waterfall 
The Kho Kuu So Bamboo Bridge
The Pai Canyon
And my favorite I will keep secret till the end

Pai is a beautiful experience. Also the way from Chiang Mai to Pai is very famous for it’s 763 curves and to go there by bike makes really a lot of fun. 
And Pai itself is special. such a lovely vibe. Everyone is so friendly locals are so friendly and talkative and also tourists.  There are so many different People but what they all have in common is their kindness. That alone makes Pai as one of the best places in Thailand.  
It is a place where you really can enjoy yourself.

title: 🔥 Larb Nuea – ลาบเนื้อ -- Thailands würzigster Rindfleischsalat! 🇹🇭
description:
Servus!
#Larbnuea #thaifood  #beefsalad  #thairecipes  #streetfood  #thailandfood  #isaanfood  #AsianCuisine #spicyfood  #Klebreis #authenticthaifood  #foodie #asmr #ลาบเนื้อ  #Lāb neụ̄̂x

Beschreibung:
Frisch, würzig und voller Geschmack – so schmeckt Larb Nuea 🇹🇭🥩
Dieser thailändische Rindfleischsalat kombiniert zartes Rindfleisch mit Limette, Chili, Kräutern und geröstetem Reispulver. Perfekt mit Reis oder einfach pur genießen. Ein echter Klassiker aus dem Isaan!

📍 Authentisch zubereitet wie in Thailand
🔥 Scharf, sauer, frisch – pure Geschmacksexplosion
🥢 Streetfood-Feeling für Zuhause
______________________________________________________________________
🥩 Zutaten (für 2–3 Portionen)

300 g Rindfleisch (mager, frisch) optional Rinderhackfleisch

2 EL Khao Khua (gerösteter Reispulver – siehe Hinweis unten)

1–2 Limetten (Saft)

2–3 EL Fischsauce

1 TL Palmzucker (oder brauner Zucker, optional)

2–5 Thai-Chilis (nach Schärfe, fein gehackt)

3 EL Schalotten (in dünne Ringe geschnitten)

2 EL Frühlingszwiebeln (in feine Ringe)

2–3 EL frische Minzblätter

Koriander (optional)
______________________________________________________________________
🔥 Zubereitung

1. Fleisch braten

Pfanne erhitzen, Rinderhack zugeben und bei mittlerer Hitze ohne Öl gar ziehen lassen, bis es durch ist. Nicht zu stark anbraten – es soll saftig bleiben. (Ich habs vorher kurz angegrillt)

Hitze abstellen.

2. Würzen

Fischsauce, Limettensaft, Palmzucker und Chilis ins Fleisch geben und gut vermischen.

Das geröstete Reispulver (Khao Khua) unterrühren – es gibt nussiges Aroma und bindet leicht.


3. Frische Zutaten zugeben

Schalotten, Frühlingszwiebeln, Minze und Koriander unterheben.

Kurz ziehen lassen, nicht mehr kochen, damit Kräuter frisch bleiben.


4. Servieren

Sofort mit Klebreis (Khao Niew) und frischem Gemüse (Gurke, lange Bohnen, Thai-Basilikum) servieren.
___________________________________________________________________
📝 Hinweis zu Khao Khua (geröstetes Reispulver)

Falls du es nicht fertig hast:

3–4 EL Reis in einer trockenen Pfanne bei mittlerer Hitze goldbraun rösten.

Abkühlen lassen, dann fein mahlen (Mörser oder Mixer).

_____________________________________________________________________
💡 Tipp:
Für extra Aroma kannst du das Rinderhack halb roh, halb gegart lassen – so wird’s in Nordost-Thailand oft serviert (nur mit sehr frischem Fleisch!).

Guten Appetit

Grüße euer Andy Chan

Servus!

In unserem heutigen Video geht es um.
"Original Thaifood: Kochen wie in Thailand" - Tauche ein in die Welt der thailändischen Kochkunst und lerne, wie man traditionelle thailändische Gerichte authentisch zubereitet. Du wirst überrascht sein, wie einfach es ist!
Wünschen dir viel Spaß beim Video und Guten Appetit.

_____________________________________________________________________________________________________
Für 2 Personen (ca. Angaben)

300 g Schweinehackfleisch
2-3 Thai Chilis
1 rote Zwiebel oder Schalotte
2 EL Fischsauce (evtl. auch Sojasauce )
½ Bund Koriander
3-5 Minzblätter
Saft einer halben Limette
Optional 1 TL Zucker
Jasminreis zum Rösten
2 Eier (Spiegelei)
Öl (zum Anbraten)
Jasminreis (Beilage)

Zubereitung:
In einer Pfanne Öl bei mittlerer bis hoher Hitze erhitzen. Die Eier hineinschlagen und braten, bis der Rand knusprig ist und das Eiweiß gestockt ist. Herausnehmen und beiseite stellen. Schalotte, Chili hacken.
Das Schweinehackfleisch in die Pfanne geben und mit einem Kochlöffel in kleine Stücke zerteilen, während es anbrät. Ca. 5 Min. anbraten, bis es goldbraun ist. 
Dann in eine Schüssel geben. Gehackte rote Zwiebel und Chili hinzugeben.
Fischsauce und Limettensaft hinzugeben. Schön vermischen. Gerösteter Reis (Laab) und Koriander hinzugeben. Weiter vermischen und zu guter Letzt einige Minzblätter dazugeben. 
Der  Fleischsalat kann auch kalt gegessen werden. Mit gekochtem Jasminreis und dem Spiegelei servieren. 


Guten Appetit!

Helle Sojasauce, Fischsauce, Austernsauce, dunkle Sojasauce und Zucker in einer kleinen Schüssel vermischen. (ich habs direkthinzugefügt) Die Basilikumblätter nebenbei abzupfen.
Die Schalotten-Chili-Paste hinzugeben und ca. 2–3 Min. braten, bis sie duftet.
Basilikum hinzufügen und kurz unter Rühren braten, bis die Blätter verwelkt sind.
Aus der Pfanne nehmen und mit gekochtem Reis und einem Spiegelei servieren. 

Guten Appetit!
